article_content: More than 100 British nationals have left Gaza this week, and hopes remain that more evacuations will take place on Sunday, according to Deputy Prime Minister Oliver Dowden in a BBC interview. Dowden expressed disappointment over the closure of the Rafah crossing on Saturday but stated that the UK government is working closely with officials to reopen it soon. The Rafah crossing, which links Gaza and Egypt, was open for three days earlier in the week. During that period, dozens of Britons were identified as eligible to leave, with the Palestinian border authority providing lists of those able to present themselves at the border with their passports. On Friday, over 90 British citizens were named, and 88 were on Saturday's list. However, until Mr. Dowden's comments, it was unclear how many actually managed to cross. Alongside foreign passport holders and dependents, some wounded Palestinian residents were permitted to exit Gaza and enter Egypt. On Saturday, however, hundreds of people with foreign passports gathered at the border but were unable to leave. Palestinian border officials told the BBC that movement of foreign passport holders was halted until agreements regarding the secure transfer of injured patients could be reached. No official statement has been made by the authorities yet. Before the war, there were estimated to be around 200 British nationals in Gaza. Dowden said the first priority is reopening the Rafah crossing, expressing optimism about progress. He also emphasized the need for temporary pauses to allow humanitarian aid into Gaza and facilitate the evacuation of British citizens. Among those who have already left are Elizabeth and Maged El-Nakla, the parents of Scotland’s First Minister Humza Yousaf’s wife, Nadia. The couple had been trapped in Gaza since the outbreak of the war while visiting family. Mr. Yousaf acknowledged the conflicting emotions of relief and sorrow, stating on X: 'We are of course elated, but my father-in-law said, "My heart is broken in two," as he had to leave behind loved ones in Gaza.' Dowden urged remaining British citizens in Gaza to contact the Foreign Office for assistance. The Foreign Office noted the situation remains complex and challenging, and diplomatic efforts are ongoing to reopen the crossing in cooperation with international partners. The office remains in contact with British nationals in the region, offering updated information. All Gaza border crossings have been closed since 7 October, following an attack on Israel by Hamas—which the UK designates as a terrorist organisation—that killed more than 1,400 people and resulted in over 240 hostages. In response, the Israeli military launched extensive airstrikes, imposed a 'complete siege' on Gaza, and recently initiated a ground operation in Gaza’s north. The Hamas-run health ministry in Gaza reports that over 9,400 people have been killed. It is believed that 14 Britons died in the 7 October attacks. Dowden stated that three Britons remain unaccounted for, but it is unclear if they are among the hostages. British transplant surgeon Abdelkader Hammad, who lives in Liverpool, was able to leave Gaza via Rafah last Thursday after weeks of being trapped. Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Dr. Hammad described the experience as terrifying, recounting the dangers of explosions, falling debris, and broken glass. He noted feeling fortunate to have UN protection, adding that many in Gaza lack shelter and continue to suffer. He also expressed concern for his colleagues and patients left behind, many of whom, he believes, risk dying due to interrupted medical care. Families of those still trapped in Gaza face ongoing distress. Faras Abuwarda’s wife and five children, aged three to 11, are eligible to leave but remain stranded in northern Gaza, unable to reach Rafah. Mr. Abuwarda, now in Cairo, expressed frustration with the British government's inability to help and described his children's sense of isolation and hopelessness. Similarly, Omar Mofeed from London said his brother and pregnant wife, along with their children, fear traveling through Gaza despite being advised of a safe route. He recounted that, after assurances from the British foreign ministry, civilians attempting this route came under attack. The Israeli military maintains it does not target civilians. Icel Chumlukh described how his wife Lamia, her 13-year-old daughter, and their one-year-old son were told to leave the border despite being on the list, because the daughter was not included—but his wife brought her in hopes of a miracle. He said his son is now traumatised by loud noises, which remind him of airstrikes. The BBC continues to invite those affected by these issues to share their stories through email or the BBC website, encouraging them to provide contact information.
translated_content: Più di 100 cittadini britannici hanno lasciato Gaza questa settimana, e si spera che altre evacuazioni possano avvenire domenica, secondo quanto dichiarato dal vice primo ministro Oliver Dowden in un'intervista alla BBC. Dowden ha espresso delusione per la chiusura del valico di Rafah sabato, ma ha affermato che il governo britannico sta collaborando strettamente con le autorità per riaprirlo al più presto. Il valico di Rafah, che collega Gaza all’Egitto, è rimasto aperto per tre giorni all’inizio della settimana. In quel periodo, decine di britannici sono stati identificati come idonei a partire, con l’autorità di frontiera palestinese che forniva gli elenchi di coloro che potevano presentarsi al confine con il passaporto. Venerdì sono stati nominati oltre 90 cittadini britannici e 88 sono apparsi nella lista di sabato. Tuttavia, fino ai commenti di Dowden non era chiaro quanti fossero riusciti effettivamente a attraversare. Oltre ai titolari di passaporto straniero e ai loro familiari a carico, alcuni palestinesi feriti hanno ottenuto il permesso di uscire da Gaza ed entrare in Egitto. Tuttavia, sabato centinaia di persone con passaporto straniero si sono radunate al confine senza poter partire. Funzionari di frontiera palestinesi hanno dichiarato alla BBC che il movimento dei titolari di passaporto straniero è stato sospeso fino al raggiungimento di accordi sulla sicurezza nel trasferimento dei pazienti feriti. Al momento, non è stata rilasciata alcuna dichiarazione ufficiale dalle autorità. Prima della guerra, si stimava la presenza di circa 200 cittadini britannici a Gaza. Dowden ha detto che la priorità principale è riaprire il valico di Rafah, esprimendo ottimismo sui progressi. Ha anche sottolineato l’importanza di pause temporanee per permettere l’ingresso degli aiuti umanitari e l’evacuazione dei cittadini britannici. Tra coloro che sono già riusciti a partire ci sono Elizabeth e Maged El-Nakla, genitori della moglie del primo ministro scozzese Humza Yousaf, Nadia. La coppia era rimasta bloccata a Gaza dall’inizio del conflitto mentre era in visita ai familiari. Yousaf ha riconosciuto, su X, le emozioni contrastanti di sollievo e dolore: “Siamo ovviamente sollevati, ma mio suocero ha detto: ‘Il mio cuore è spezzato in due’, poiché ha dovuto lasciare i suoi cari a Gaza.” Dowden ha invitato i cittadini britannici rimasti a Gaza a contattare il Foreign Office per ricevere assistenza. Il Foreign Office ha dichiarato che la situazione resta complessa e impegnativa, e che sono in corso sforzi diplomatici per riaprire il valico in collaborazione con partner internazionali. L’ufficio rimane in contatto con i cittadini britannici nella regione per fornire aggiornamenti. Tutti i valichi di frontiera di Gaza sono chiusi dal 7 ottobre, dopo l’attacco di Hamas a Israele—che il Regno Unito considera un’organizzazione terroristica—che ha causato oltre 1.400 vittime e più di 240 ostaggi. In risposta, l’esercito israeliano ha avviato massicci bombardamenti, imposto uno “stato d’assedio totale” e recentemente lanciato un’operazione terrestre nel nord di Gaza. Il Ministero della Salute di Gaza, gestito da Hamas, riporta oltre 9.400 morti. Si ritiene che 14 britannici siano deceduti negli attacchi del 7 ottobre. Dowden ha affermato che tre britannici risultano ancora dispersi, ma non è chiaro se siano tra gli ostaggi. Il chirurgo dei trapianti britannico Abdelkader Hammad, residente a Liverpool, è riuscito a lasciare Gaza tramite Rafah giovedì scorso dopo settimane di attesa. Parlando alla BBC Breakfast, il dottor Hammad ha descritto l’esperienza come terrificante, menzionando esplosioni, detriti, vetri rotti. Si è detto fortunato di essere stato protetto dall’ONU, aggiungendo che molti a Gaza restano senza riparo e continuano a soffrire. Ha espresso preoccupazione per i colleghi e i pazienti lasciati, molti dei quali, secondo lui, rischiano la vita a causa delle cure interrotte. Le famiglie di coloro che sono ancora bloccati a Gaza vivono una grande angoscia. La moglie di Faras Abuwarda e i cinque figli (tra i tre e gli undici anni) sono idonei a partire ma restano bloccati nel nord di Gaza, impossibilitati a raggiungere Rafah. Abuwarda, ora al Cairo, ha espresso frustrazione per l’incapacità del governo britannico di aiutare e ha descritto i figli come frustrati, senza speranza e isolati. Allo stesso modo, Omar Mofeed, da Londra, ha dichiarato che suo fratello e la moglie incinta, insieme ai figli, hanno paura di viaggiare attraverso Gaza nonostante sia stato indicato loro un percorso sicuro. Ha raccontato che, dopo le rassicurazioni ricevute dal ministero degli Esteri britannico, i civili hanno tentato di percorrere questa via ma sono stati attaccati. L’esercito israeliano ribadisce di non prendere di mira i civili. Icel Chumlukh ha descritto come la moglie Lamia, la figliastra tredicenne e il figlio di un anno siano stati invitati a lasciare il confine nonostante fossero nella lista, poiché la figliastra non era compresa—ma la moglie l’ha portata comunque, sperando in un miracolo. Ha raccontato che ora il figlio è traumatizzato dai rumori forti, che gli ricordano i bombardamenti. La BBC continua a invitare coloro che sono coinvolti da queste vicende a condividere la loro storia tramite email o sito web, incoraggiando a lasciare i propri contatti.

article_content: A mysterious mathematical formula appeared on the hoardings of a construction site in Boscombe, Dorset, sparking widespread speculation among local residents. The 20-foot-long chalk graffiti led many to wonder whether the equation was the work of a maths genius or an artistic prankster. Local resident Jonathan Crozier first noticed the enormous equation and speculated that it had been created by a mathematics graduate. Councillor Chris Wakefield openly invited anyone who could solve the puzzle to come forward, expressing his own intrigue and curiosity. Bournemouth mathematics graduate Holly Crosby also attempted to decipher the formula, describing it as advanced and challenging. However, hopes of deciphering the enigmatic equation were dashed when mathematics experts examined the formula and declared it 'meaningless.' Sebastian Rees, from the mathematics department at Manchester University, explained that while some sections might resemble material from A-Level textbooks, the formula as a whole lacked any coherent meaning. Experts agree that, in spite of its impressive appearance, the formula is essentially gibberish.

Anche Holly Crosby, laureata in matematica a Bournemouth, ha tentato di decifrare la formula, definendola avanzata e impegnativa. Tuttavia, le speranze di svelare il mistero sono state deluse quando gli esperti di matematica hanno esaminato la formula e l'hanno definita 'priva di significato'. Gli esperti concordano: nonostante l'aspetto impressionante, la formula è sostanzialmente priva di significato.

article_content: Alok Kumar Choudhary, Managing Director of State Bank of India (SBI), stated on Wednesday that microfinance institutions (MFIs) must pay close attention to data privacy and cybersecurity, given their handling of large volumes of customer data. Speaking at a conference organized by Sa-Dhan, Choudhary said that MFIs also need to focus on building capacity to face future challenges. "Another crucial point is aligning with evolving regulations, especially with the implementation of data privacy laws. The significant amount of data managed by MFIs demands a focused action plan for data privacy," he said. Choudhary highlighted that financial institutions should aim to enhance the ease of transactions through digital means to meet changing customer needs and preferences. "For customers at the bottom of the pyramid, it's vital to understand their needs and make services convenient and accessible," he added. SBI provides substantial credit to MFIs and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) promoting financial inclusion. Discussing SBI's role in the government's financial inclusion efforts, Choudhary stated that the bank has opened 36% of all accounts under the PM Jan Dhan Yojana scheme. Over 500 million bank accounts have been opened under PM Jan Dhan Yojana in the last nine years, with total deposit balances exceeding Rs 2.03 lakh crore. Regarding the Atal Pension Yojana, Choudhary said SBI has enrolled 32% of all subscribers under the scheme. At the same event, SIDBI Chairman and Managing Director S Ramann advised MFIs not to become complacent amid digital disruptions. He warned that new entrants could outpace traditional players if the sector does not keep up with technological changes. Other notable recent news includes Tata Group acquiring Wistron's iPhone assembly facility for $750 million, India surpassing China in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2024, and an ongoing dispute between Religare Enterprises Ltd. and the Burman family regarding company control.

article_content: Small finance banks (SFBs) are currently facing uncertainty as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has not specifically clarified whether microfinance loans are exempt from the recently announced higher risk weightage norms. Both individual banks and industry groups have contacted the RBI for clarification, according to people familiar with the situation. Microfinance loans account for a large share of SFBs’ loan portfolios, with exceptions such as AU Small Finance Bank and Equitas. The source of confusion is that the RBI explicitly exempted microfinance and self-help group loans from higher capital requirements for non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), but did not specify the status for banks, including SFBs. As stated in the RBI’s November 16 circular: 'Consumer credit exposures of NBFCs (outstanding or new) categorized as retail loans—excluding housing, education, vehicle loans, loans against gold jewelry, and microfinance or SHG loans—shall attract a risk weight of 125%.' However, no similar exemption was listed for banks. A managing director of a major SFB commented that if higher risk weights are required for microfinance loans, it would significantly impact the sector in the medium term. Although most SFBs currently maintain a capital adequacy ratio above 20%, well above the 15% minimum requirement, they may need to accelerate medium-term capital raising plans if higher risk weights are enforced. 'We have approached the regulator to seek clarification,' the executive said. A CEO of a bank with significant microfinance exposure argued that microfinance loans support entrepreneurship and thus should not be classified as consumer loans, meaning the additional 25% risk weight would not apply. Although microfinance loans are granted for a range of purposes, including agriculture, small businesses, and consumption, they are typically not classified by end use in current banking systems, according to sector experts. A former State Bank of India executive suggested it is time for lenders to classify these loans more precisely in line with regulatory guidance. Banche individuali e associazioni di settore hanno chiesto chiarimenti alla RBI, secondo fonti informate sulla vicenda. I prestiti di microfinanza rappresentano una parte rilevante dei portafogli delle SFB, salvo eccezioni come AU Small Finance Bank ed Equitas. La confusione nasce dal fatto che la RBI ha escluso esplicitamente i prestiti di microfinanza e self-help group (SHG) dall’innalzamento dei requisiti patrimoniali per le NBFC, ma non si è espressa nello stesso modo per le banche, includendo le SFB. Nella circolare della RBI del 16 novembre si legge: 'Le esposizioni al credito al consumo delle NBFC (esistenti o nuove) classificate come prestiti al dettaglio—esclusi i prestiti casa, istruzione, auto, quelli garantiti da gioielli in oro e di microfinanza/SHG—sono soggette a un peso di rischio del 125%'. Tuttavia, questa esenzione non è specificata per le banche. Un amministratore delegato di una grande SFB ha dichiarato che, se si dovessero applicare pesi di rischio maggiori ai prestiti di microfinanza, l’impatto per il settore sarebbe rilevante nel medio periodo. Anche se molte SFB hanno oggi un ratio di adeguatezza patrimoniale superiore al 20%, ben oltre il minimo di legge del 15%, potrebbero dover accelerare la raccolta di capitale qualora venissero imposti pesi maggiori. 'Abbiamo chiesto chiarimenti al regolatore,' ha aggiunto. Un CEO di una banca con grande esposizione nella microfinanza ha sottolineato che questi prestiti servono a sostenere l’imprenditoria e quindi non dovrebbero essere considerati prestiti al consumo, e il peso di rischio aggiuntivo del 25% non dovrebbe essere applicato. Nonostante i prestiti di microfinanza vengano concessi per molteplici scopi, come agricoltura, piccole imprese e consumo, di solito non sono classificati per uso finale nei sistemi bancari attuali, come osservato dagli esperti del settore. article_content:
At this very moment, in a major Chinese city, a worker is boarding a train home—just one of the 3.4 billion journeys taking place during China’s Lunar New Year, the world’s largest annual human migration. Each year, millions of Chinese travel home to reunite with their families, a pattern that has recurred for the past two decades and helped drive China’s economic growth. However, this progress has come at a significant personal cost, partly due to the ‘hukou’ system—a type of internal passport that divides the population into rural and urban residents. The system denies migrant workers access to social services in the cities where they work.

The discriminatory nature of the hukou system was brought into sharp relief recently, following a fatal bridge collapse in Henan. Reports stated that families with an urban hukou would receive 400,000 yuan in compensation, while those with a rural hukou would get only 180,000 yuan.

Such restrictions on movement and entitlement date back centuries, but were reinstated by the Communist Party after 1949. Han Dongfang from China Labor Bulletin notes that while economic reforms have loosened some hukou restrictions—mainly on movement—barriers to welfare, education, healthcare, and housing benefits persist, especially for the poor.

Few outside China are familiar with the hukou system, but Han says it’s critical to understand, as real reform could benefit both China’s workers and the global economy. If the country’s 200 million migrant workers became regular consumers and taxpayers, the economic benefits would ripple worldwide.

Rob Schmitz, a China-based journalist for Marketplace, describes migrant workers as being treated like illegal immigrants in their own country. In cities like Beijing, these workers make up a third of the population but lack access to basic services like education and healthcare. This most affects their children—often born and raised in the city but forced to return to their parents' original hometowns if they wish to go to college. Many migrant workers leave their children behind, resulting in about 16 million 'floating children' with substandard education and increased vulnerability to violence and abuse, according to China Labour Bulletin.

The Chinese government has pledged hukou reform as part of broader urbanization plans, and a younger, more rights-conscious generation of migrant workers is pushing for faster change. According to labor activists, these workers want to settle in cities with their families and access equal public services. The hope is that, after two decades of mass migration, they can finally put down roots—leaving the hukou system in the past.

In questo momento, in una grande città cinese, un lavoratore sta salendo su un treno per tornare a casa—uno dei 3,4 miliardi di viaggi che avvengono durante il Capodanno Lunare, la più grande migrazione umana annuale al mondo. Ogni anno, milioni di cinesi viaggiano per riunirsi con le famiglie, una tradizione ripetuta negli ultimi vent’anni che ha contribuito alla crescita economica del Paese. Tuttavia, questo progresso ha avuto un costo personale notevole, dovuto in parte al sistema dell’‘hukou’—una sorta di passaporto interno che divide la popolazione tra residenti rurali e urbani. Il sistema nega ai lavoratori migranti l’accesso ai servizi sociali nelle città dove lavorano.

La natura discriminatoria dell’hukou è emersa chiaramente di recente, dopo il crollo mortale di un ponte a Henan. Secondo i resoconti, le famiglie con hukou urbano avrebbero ricevuto 400.000 yuan di risarcimento, contro i 180.000 yuan destinati a quelle con hukou rurale.

Restrizioni così profonde sui movimenti e sui diritti esistono da secoli, ma sono state reintrodotte dal Partito Comunista dopo il 1949. Han Dongfang della China Labor Bulletin nota che, sebbene le riforme economiche abbiano allentato alcune restrizioni—soprattutto sulla mobilità—persistono barriere importati all’accesso a welfare, istruzione, sanità e alloggi, soprattutto per i più poveri.

Pochi al di fuori della Cina conoscono il sistema hukou, ma Han sottolinea quanto sia importante comprenderlo: una riforma vera porterebbe benefici sia ai lavoratori che all’economia globale. Se i 200 milioni di migranti diventassero consumatori e contribuenti regolari, gli effetti sarebbero positivi anche a livello internazionale.

Rob Schmitz, giornalista in Cina per Marketplace, paragona i migranti a immigrati clandestini nel loro stesso paese. A Pechino, ad esempio, rappresentano un terzo della popolazione, ma restano esclusi dall’accesso ai servizi fondamentali come istruzione e sanità. Il problema tocca soprattutto i loro figli—nati e cresciuti in città, ma costretti a tornare nel villaggio d’origine dei genitori per proseguire negli studi. Molti lavoratori lasciano i figli nei paesi d’origine, creando circa 16 milioni di ‘bambini fluttuanti’ che, secondo China Labour Bulletin, ricevono un’educazione scadente e sono più vulnerabili a violenza e abusi.

Il governo cinese ha promesso la riforma dell’hukou nell’ambito dei programmi di urbanizzazione, mentre una nuova generazione di lavoratori migranti, più consapevole dei propri diritti, chiede cambiamenti rapidi. Secondo gli attivisti, questi lavoratori vogliono stabilirsi nelle città con le loro famiglie ed essere inclusi nei servizi pubblici. Dopo due decenni di grande migrazione, sperano finalmente di mettere radici—lasciandosi alle spalle l’hukou.

article_content: First Lady Michelle Obama recently became the center of a debate over breast-feeding after three prominent conservative women criticized her efforts, claiming they contributed to a 'nanny state.' Conservative radio host Laura Ingraham asked Rep. Michele Bachmann, R-Minnesota, about a new IRS decision that allows purchases of breast-feeding equipment to qualify as medical expenses. Ingraham wondered if the First Lady’s promotion of breast-feeding to fight childhood obesity was connected to the IRS decision. Bachmann, known for opposing Obama administration policies, called the move in line with a 'hard left' agenda and indicative of too much government intervention. During an event in New York, Sarah Palin weighed in, joking that Michelle Obama encouraged breast-feeding because milk prices were rising, though she noted her comment was not meant to be taken literally. The debate centers on the IRS’s recent announcement that breast pumps and breast-feeding supplies now count as reimbursable medical expenses under federal tax law. Previously, such purchases were not eligible for reimbursement or tax deductions through health accounts or itemized deductions. IRS and Treasury officials stated the decision was based on legal judgement by the IRS general counsel rather than political considerations. Two days before the IRS announcement, Michelle Obama celebrated one year of her 'Let’s Move' campaign and indicated breast-feeding would be a focus moving forward, emphasizing its link to lower childhood obesity. She also previously spoke about promoting breast-feeding in the Black community, where lower rates are common. While links between breast-feeding and childhood obesity reduction are commonly accepted, the strength of this effect is still debated. The American Academy of Pediatrics lobbied the IRS in 2009 to support breast-feeding equipment deductions, highlighting broad health advantages and a potential role in reducing obesity. A 2005 policy statement and a 2007 Tufts-New England Medical Center study indicated that breast-fed children may face lower risks of obesity in later years. Bachmann’s office clarified her critique was directed at the complexity of the tax code, not specifically at the breast-feeding equipment deduction, calling for broader tax reform. The IRS allows many medical expenses to be deducted, like wigs, acupuncture, artificial teeth, eyeglasses, and devices for hearing impairment. It is difficult to estimate the impact of the new deduction, as insurance providers have their own guidelines, only about one-third of taxpayers itemize, and expenses must reach 7.5% of income to qualify. Congress' Joint Committee on Taxation labeled the IRS announcement as a regulatory decision and has not issued a cost estimate. A 2010 Pediatrics journal analysis estimated that if 90% of U.S. families breast-fed for six months as recommended, it could save the country $13 billion each year and prevent more than 900 infant deaths.

La conduttrice radiofonica conservatrice Laura Ingraham ha chiesto alla deputata Michele Bachmann, repubblicana del Minnesota, riguardo una nuova decisione dell’IRS che consente l’acquisto di attrezzature per l’allattamento come spese mediche. Ingraham si è domandata se la promozione dell’allattamento da parte della First Lady come strumento contro l’obesità infantile fosse collegata alla decisione dell’IRS. Bachmann, nota per opporsi alle politiche dell’amministrazione Obama, ha definito la misura in linea con un’agenda di 'sinistra radicale' e come sintomo di un’eccessiva ingerenza governativa. Durante un evento a New York, anche Sarah Palin ha detto la sua, scherzando sul fatto che Michelle Obama incoraggiasse l’allattamento poiché i prezzi del latte erano in rialzo, precisando però che il suo commento non doveva essere preso alla lettera. Il dibattito ruota attorno all’annuncio recente dell’IRS secondo cui tiralatte e attrezzature per l’allattamento sono ora considerate spese mediche rimborsabili secondo la legge fiscale federale. In precedenza, questi acquisti non erano ammissibili per rimborsi o detrazioni fiscali tramite conti sanitari o deduzioni dettagliate. I funzionari di IRS e del Tesoro hanno affermato che la decisione si basa su una valutazione legale dell’ufficio del consulente generale IRS e non su motivazioni politiche. Due giorni prima dell’annuncio IRS, Michelle Obama aveva celebrato un anno della campagna 'Let’s Move' segnalando che l’allattamento sarebbe stato un punto chiave, evidenziando il suo legame con un minor rischio di obesità infantile. In precedenza, aveva anche promosso l’allattamento nella comunità afroamericana, dove i tassi sono inferiori. Anche se il legame tra allattamento e riduzione dell’obesità infantile è largamente riconosciuto, la forza di questo effetto è ancora oggetto di discussione. L’American Academy of Pediatrics ha fatto pressione sull’IRS nel 2009 per sostenere la deducibilità delle attrezzature per l’allattamento, sottolineando i numerosi benefici per la salute e il possibile ruolo nella riduzione dell’obesità. Una dichiarazione politica del 2005 e uno studio del Tufts-New England Medical Center del 2007 indicano che i bambini allattati potrebbero avere meno rischi di obesità negli anni successivi. L’ufficio della Bachmann ha chiarito che la sua critica era rivolta alla complessità del codice fiscale, non specificamente alla detrazione per attrezzature per l’allattamento, sostenendo la necessità di una riforma più ampia. L’IRS consente la detrazione di molte spese mediche, come parrucche, agopuntura, denti artificiali, occhiali e dispositivi per l’udito. Stimare l’impatto della nuova detrazione è difficile, dato che ogni compagnia di assicurazione ha linee guida proprie, solo circa un terzo dei contribuenti usufruisce delle detrazioni dettagliate e le spese devono raggiungere il 7,5% del reddito. La Joint Committee on Taxation del Congresso ha definito l’annuncio dell’IRS una decisione regolamentare e non ha fornito stime sui costi. Un’analisi del 2010 pubblicata su Pediatrics ha stimato che, se il 90% delle famiglie americane allattasse per sei mesi secondo le raccomandazioni, gli Stati Uniti risparmierebbero 13 miliardi di dollari l’anno e si eviterebbero oltre 900 morti infantili.

article_content: The Airports Authority of India (AAI) has issued a warning about an increase in fake job offers circulating across the country. In an official statement, AAI reported that people have received fraudulent messages through emails and social media, with false information about job vacancies, examination dates, results, and bogus promises of employment in exchange for payment. AAI stresses that only information on its official website (www.aai.aero) should be trusted. Application fees should only be paid via the online registration portal, and no other payments are requested at any stage in the hiring process. The AAI clarified it is not liable for any losses caused by such scams, urging everyone to stay alert and avoid falling for misleading advertisements.

L’AAI ribadisce che solo le informazioni presenti sul sito ufficiale (www.aai.aero) sono attendibili. Le tasse di iscrizione possono essere pagate solo tramite il portale online autorizzato; nessun altro pagamento è richiesto in alcuna fase della selezione. L’AAI precisa di non essere responsabile per eventuali perdite dovute a queste truffe e invita tutti a prestare attenzione e a non farsi ingannare da annunci fuorvianti.

article_content: Building a business is never easy. Success requires not only a strong product, good timing, and a receptive market, but also an element of luck. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, around 20% of new companies fail within their first year, about 48% make it to five years, and just 35% survive a decade. For entrepreneurs aiming to build companies around open-source software, the challenge intensifies. Open Source Initiative-approved licenses allow anyone to use, modify, or distribute the software without restriction. So, how can you build a profitable company when your product is available to all? A 2009 Harvard Business Review study, 'The Founder’s Dilemma,' explores the choices founders face. It concludes that accepting venture capital (VC) funding can accelerate growth but often requires founders to give up some control—a significant trade-off. In the tech industry, VC investors typically provide funding in exchange for equity, expecting potential returns via company sales or public offerings. Research published in the Journal of Financial Economics (2020) found that about 13.7% of companies reach an Initial Public Offering (IPO), while 42.8% achieve some form of exit. Although VC funding injects capital to drive growth, it can also create conflicts between upholding community values and pursuing profit, especially in open-source companies. While open source builds vibrant communities, it is not a business model by itself. Companies face potential backlash if they restrict access to core projects in favor of commercial offerings. In recent years, several VC-backed businesses have abandoned pure open-source models for more restrictive licenses—often trying to capture more market share or outcompete rivals using the same open-source software. However, venture capital is not the only path. Building an open-source business can also mean growing gradually, powered by your own revenues rather than external funding. This approach helps founders retain control and make decisions that prioritize community interests, not just commercial gains. Most successful open-source companies focus on selling value-added services, such as expert support, implementation, or integration. While this service-driven model can be challenging to scale, many firms have embraced the SaaS (Software as a Service) model, where customers pay recurring fees for managed services. These solutions often reduce operational burdens for clients, making them attractive in the market. Yet, open-source SaaS businesses may face competition from others delivering similar offerings at lower prices. To succeed, companies must continuously innovate and provide unique value—such as outstanding service, robust community support, or specialized integrations—to justify their pricing. Companies relying on consulting must prove their commitment to customers by recommending the right solutions, even if that means suggesting alternatives to their own products. Such integrity can foster long-term customer relationships and revenue. Drawing from my company’s experience, I recommend embracing open-source community values. Supporting multiple projects, delivering unbiased advice, and being independent allows you to make decisions that serve customers best. Bootstrapped companies—those without outside investment—can grow sustainably and retain control, even if progress is slower. This approach may avoid conflicts between shareholder interests and community needs. In sum, open-source companies must balance profitability with community engagement. Sustainable, customer-centric growth—even if gradual—can ultimately offer greater independence and long-term success than relentless pursuit of rapid scaling.
translated_content: Costruire un'azienda non è mai facile. Il successo richiede non solo un prodotto di valore, il giusto tempismo e un mercato ricettivo, ma anche una certa dose di fortuna. Secondo il Bureau of Labor Statistics, circa il 20% delle nuove aziende fallisce entro il primo anno, circa il 48% arriva a cinque anni e solo il 35% sopravvive dieci anni. Per gli imprenditori che vogliono fondare aziende basate su software open source, la sfida si fa ancora più intensa. Le licenze approvate dall'Open Source Initiative consentono a chiunque di usare, modificare o distribuire il software senza restrizioni. Come si può quindi creare un'azienda redditizia quando il tuo prodotto è accessibile a tutti? Uno studio Harvard Business Review del 2009, 'The Founder’s Dilemma', esplora le scelte che i fondatori affrontano. Conclude che accettare fondi da venture capital (VC) può accelerare la crescita, ma spesso implica la rinuncia a parte del controllo—a volte un compromesso difficile. Nel settore tecnologico, gli investitori VC tendono a finanziare in cambio di quote societarie, puntando a ritorni attraverso la vendita dell’azienda o l’IPO. Una ricerca pubblicata sul Journal of Financial Economics (2020) ha rilevato che circa il 13,7% delle società arriva all’Offerta Pubblica Iniziale, mentre il 42,8% consegue un exit. Pur dando impulso alla crescita, il capitale VC può creare conflitti tra i valori della community e il profitto aziendale, specialmente nell’open source. Sebbene l’open source costruisca community vivaci, non è di per sé un modello di business. Le aziende rischiano reazioni negative se limitano l’accesso ai progetti fondamentali per favorire offerte commerciali. Negli ultimi anni, molte aziende finanziate da venture capital hanno abbandonato modelli open source in favore di licenze più restrittive—spesso nel tentativo di accrescere la quota di mercato o superare rivali che usano lo stesso software. Il venture capital, però, non è l’unica strada. Potenziare un’azienda open source può anche significare crescere gradualmente sostenendosi sui ricavi, invece che su capitali esterni. Questo aiuta i fondatori a mantenere il controllo e a mettere la community al centro delle decisioni. Le aziende open source di successo offrono servizi a valore aggiunto, come supporto esperto, implementazione e integrazione. Nonostante questo modello sia difficile da scalare, molte hanno puntato sul SaaS (Software as a Service), in cui i clienti pagano canoni ricorrenti per servizi gestiti. Tali soluzioni spesso riducono i carichi operativi dei clienti, risultando particolarmente vantaggiose. Eppure, le aziende SaaS open source devono spesso competere con chi propone offerte simili a prezzi inferiori. Per emergere, bisogna innovare continuamente e offrire valore unico—eccellente assistenza, forte community o integrazioni specializzate—per giustificare prezzi più elevati. Chi si basa sulla consulenza deve mostrare integrità, consigliando le soluzioni migliori anche se non proprie. Questo rafforza le relazioni di lungo termine e la stabilità dei ricavi. Dalla mia esperienza suggerisco: aderite ai valori della community open source. Sostenere più progetti, offrire consulenza imparziale e indipendenza permette di scegliere sempre per il bene del cliente. Se avviata senza fondi esterni, un’azienda può crescere in modo sostenibile e restare padrona del proprio destino, anche se più lentamente. Ciò evita conflitti tra gli interessi degli azionisti e quelli della community. In conclusione, le aziende open source devono bilanciare profitto e impegno nella community. Una crescita sostenibile e orientata al cliente—anche se più lenta—può offrire maggiore indipendenza e successo duraturo rispetto alla sola ricerca di scalabilità rapida.

article_content: The recent detection of a pulse signal on Saturday could represent a significant new development in the ongoing search for Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, which disappeared without trace. Authorities hope this lead differs from previous ones, all of which have failed to locate the aircraft, believed to rest at the bottom of the Indian Ocean. Over the past month, both promising and unsubstantiated leads have illustrated how a large commercial jet could vanish with 239 people aboard. Timeline: March 8: Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 departs Kuala Lumpur International Airport just after midnight, bound for Beijing. The Boeing 777-200 disappears within an hour of takeoff after its last communication with air traffic controllers. Early eyewitness reports from oil rig workers, fishermen, and islanders prove unfounded. March 9: A Vietnamese reconnaissance plane observes oil slicks in the Gulf of Thailand, the last known vicinity of the plane’s communication. These slicks are later identified as shipping fuel oil. Suspected plane debris sightings also turn out to be unrelated. March 14: Malaysian officials reference satellite data as they focus on two vast arcs spanning each side of the equator, releasing maps and expanding the search to nearly 3 million square miles. The northern arc, crossing several countries, is soon dismissed due to lack of evidence and high security in the region; attention shifts to the southern arc toward the southern Indian Ocean, which becomes the main focus. March 18: Thai military data suggest the plane reversed course, flying west toward the Strait of Malacca. Malaysian authorities indicate that evidence points to deliberate diversion of the aircraft back toward the Indian Ocean. Yet, searches in this area yield no results. March 19: A U.S. official tells CNN that, based on search patterns and fuel limits, the aircraft is likely in the southern arc. Australian-led searches begin about 1,600 miles off the country’s western coast. Although aircraft spot objects potentially related to the plane, the distance and vast area complicate efforts. March 22-23: Multinational search operations continue for debris off Australia’s coast, even utilizing satellite imagery. France reports radar data showing floating objects 1,430 miles from Perth. Satellite images reveal numerous objects over a wide area, deepening the mystery. March 26: Search planes identify several objects in the ocean, but these cannot be relocated or confirmed. Multiple international satellites spot similar objects nearby, though none can be conclusively linked to MH370. March 27: The search focus shifts based on new radar analysis, suggesting the aircraft traveled faster and burned fuel more quickly, bringing the search area closer to Australia. March 28-29: New sightings of possible debris bring momentary hope but are ultimately determined to be unrelated. Chinese vessels retrieve objects and deploy marker buoys; most of the items are identified as fishing gear. March 30: Australian teams observe promising items in the water, one measuring 6.5 feet long, but again, none are confirmed as part of the aircraft. Prime Minister Tony Abbott emphasizes the complexity and persistence of the search. April 2-4: Under domestic scrutiny, Malaysia’s Prime Minister Najib Razak vows to continue seeking answers for the victims’ families. Officials express determination, recognizing the search might extend for months or years. The black box’s battery life approaches the 30-day limit, heightening urgency. April 5: Search teams continue in hope the cockpit voice and flight data recorders’ pingers will last long enough to be detected. A Chinese ship, Haixun-01, records a pulse consistent with black box signals—lasting for about ninety seconds—reviving hopes among officials and experts.
translated_content: La recente rilevazione di un segnale a impulsi sabato potrebbe rappresentare un nuovo e significativo sviluppo nella continua ricerca del volo Malaysia Airlines 370, scomparso senza lasciare traccia. Le autorità sperano che questa pista sia diversa dalle precedenti, che finora non hanno permesso di localizzare l’aereo, che si ritiene sia sul fondo dell’Oceano Indiano. Nell’ultimo mese, piste sia promettenti che infondate hanno illustrato come un grande aereo commerciale possa sparire con 239 persone a bordo. Cronologia: 8 marzo: Il volo Malaysia Airlines MH370 parte poco dopo mezzanotte dall’Aeroporto Internazionale di Kuala Lumpur diretto a Pechino. Il Boeing 777-200 scompare entro un’ora dal decollo dopo l’ultima comunicazione con il controllo di volo. Le prime segnalazioni di testimoni oculari da piattaforme petrolifere, pescatori e abitanti di isole si rivelano infondate. 9 marzo: Un aereo da ricognizione vietnamita osserva chiazze di petrolio nel Golfo di Thailandia, dove si trova l’ultima comunicazione nota dell’aereo. Successivamente queste chiazze vengono identificate come olio combustibile per navi. Avvistamenti di presunti rottami si rivelano anch’essi non collegati. 14 marzo: Le autorità malesi citano dati satellitari concentrando la ricerca su due enormi archi ai lati dell’equatore e diffondono mappe che estendono la zona delle ricerche a quasi 3 milioni di miglia quadrate. L’arco settentrionale, che attraversa diversi paesi, viene presto scartato per mancanza di prove e per la sorveglianza nella regione; l’attenzione si sposta sull’arco meridionale verso l’Oceano Indiano meridionale, che diventa il focus principale. 18 marzo: Dati militari thailandesi suggeriscono che l’aereo abbia invertito la rotta, volando verso ovest in direzione dello Stretto di Malacca. Le autorità malesi indicano che le prove puntano a una deviazione volontaria dell’aereo verso l’Oceano Indiano. Tuttavia, le ricerche non danno risultati. 19 marzo: Un funzionario statunitense riferisce alla CNN che, in base ai modelli di ricerca e ai limiti di carburante, è probabile che l’aereo si trovi nell’arco meridionale. Sono avviate ricerche australiane circa 1.600 miglia a ovest del paese. Sebbene si avvistino oggetti che potrebbero essere legati all’aereo, distanza e ampiezza dell’area complicano le operazioni. 22-23 marzo: Proseguono le operazioni multinazionali per i detriti al largo dell’Australia, anche tramite immagini satellitari. La Francia segnala dati radar che mostrano oggetti galleggianti a 1.430 miglia da Perth. Le immagini satellitari rivelano numerosi oggetti su un’ampia area, aumentando il mistero. 26 marzo: Aerei di ricerca individuano diversi oggetti nell’oceano, ma questi non possono essere ritrovati o confermati nei passaggi successivi. Anche più satelliti internazionali rilevano oggetti simili nelle vicinanze, ma non è possibile attribuirli al volo MH370. 27 marzo: Il focus delle ricerche si sposta in base a una nuova analisi radar che suggerisce che l’aereo abbia volato più velocemente e consumato più carburante, avvicinando la zona di ricerca all’Australia. 28-29 marzo: Nuovi avvistamenti di possibili detriti fanno sperare ma si rivelano nuovamente non collegati. Navi cinesi recuperano oggetti e rilasciano boe; la maggior parte dei resti è materiale da pesca. 30 marzo: Squadre australiane osservano oggetti promettenti in acqua, uno di 2 metri circa, ma anche questi non sono confermati come parti dell’aereo. Il primo ministro australiano Tony Abbott sottolinea la complessità e la tenacia della ricerca. 2-4 aprile: Sotto pressione interna, il primo ministro malese Najib Razak promette di continuare a cercare risposte per le famiglie delle vittime. Le autorità ribadiscono la determinazione, riconoscendo che la ricerca potrebbe durare mesi o anni. La batteria del black box si avvicina al limite di 30 giorni, generando urgenza. 5 aprile: Le squadre sperano che i segnali dei registratori di volo durino abbastanza da poter essere rilevati. Una nave cinese, Haixun-01, registra un impulso coerente con i segnali della scatola nera, durato circa novanta secondi, ravvivando le speranze di autorità ed esperti.

article_content: Juventus enter the Serie A winter break level on points with AC Milan after a scoreless draw against third-placed Udinese on Wednesday. Antonio Conte's team stretched their unbeaten streak to 16 league games, keeping pace with Milan, who beat Cagliari 2-0 a day earlier. Claudio Marchisio nearly found the net for Juventus in the eighth minute, hitting the post, while Udinese rarely threatened Juve goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon. Udinese's coach Francesco Guidolin was sent off late in the match. Conte said he would not have believed in July that his team could go undefeated through the end of the year. Lazio missed out on the chance to catch Udinese in the table, drawing 0-0 at home with Chievo. Inter Milan climbed to fifth with a 4-1 win over bottom-placed Lecce. Napoli moved into sixth on goal difference after a 6-1 rout of Genoa, with Edinson Cavani scoring two early goals. Roma joined them on 24 points with a 2-0 win at Bologna. Ninth-placed Palermo let a two-goal lead slip and had to settle for a 2-2 draw at Novara in new coach Bortolo Mutti's first game. Meanwhile, Atalanta's German Denis scored a league-best 12th goal from the penalty spot in a 4-1 victory over Cesena, lifting his team to 11th, while Parma and Catania drew 3-3. In the German Cup, defending champions Schalke were knocked out after losing 3-1 to Bundesliga high-flyers Borussia Mönchengladbach, with Marco Reus scoring twice. Schalke finished with two men sent off: Klaas-Jan Huntelaar and Jermaine Jones. Mainz were also eliminated, losing 2-0 to fourth-division Holstein Kiel. Hertha Berlin progressed, winning 3-1 over Bundesliga rivals Kaiserslautern. In the Spanish Copa del Rey, Villarreal dismissed coach Juan Carlos Garrido after being eliminated by third-division Mirandes, losing 2-0 on Wednesday and 3-1 on aggregate. Atletico Madrid were also upset by third-tier Albacete by the same total, after a 1-0 home defeat. Alcorcon from the second division ousted La Liga's Real Zaragoza, winning 2-0 away and 3-1 on aggregate.

article_content: Rajo Devi Lohan gained international attention when she became the world’s oldest first-time mother at age 69 through IVF. At the time, critics argued that she risked her health and her child’s future. Rajo experienced severe complications after giving birth and nearly died, but she recovered. Now aged 74, Rajo says that her daughter, Naveen, has given her strength and helped her to live longer. Naveen, now five, is often seen hugging her mother in their home in Hissar, a remote village in India. Rajo believes that her wish to see Naveen grow up and get married gives her the will to live, despite ongoing health challenges. She insists that she cannot die until Naveen turns 15 and is married. Living with her husband Ballo and his second, younger wife Umi (also Rajo's sister), Rajo describes Naveen as a gift from God. Although some questioned the ethics and health implications of becoming a mother at her age, Rajo survived her illness and even outlived the doctor who helped her through her IVF treatment. Rajo recalls that after giving birth, her doctor advised bed rest, but being unaccustomed to resting, she continued her work. Although her health deteriorated for a time, she eventually felt better, crediting good care from her doctor who has since passed away. She explains her deep longing for a child and the shared happiness in the village when Naveen was born. The family enjoys strong support from their extended relatives in the close-knit village. Rajo is not worried about Naveen’s future, as Umi, Ballo, and other family members will care for her. As Rajo’s only child, Naveen will inherit all of her mother’s property, including 566,280 square feet of land. Umi, who married Ballo when it seemed Rajo could not have children, also cherishes Naveen. She assures that she will always care for her in Rajo’s absence, providing love and support. Despite her age, Rajo continues to prepare Naveen for school, as Naveen prefers her mother’s attention. Naveen now attends the local village primary school. She is proud of her mother and says she loves her very much, even more than her father.

All’epoca, i critici sostenevano che stesse mettendo a rischio la sua salute e il futuro della figlia. Rajo ha avuto gravi complicazioni dopo il parto e ha rischiato di morire, ma si è ripresa. Ora, a 74 anni, Rajo afferma che la figlia Naveen le ha dato forza e l'ha aiutata a vivere più a lungo. Naveen, che ora ha cinque anni, viene spesso vista abbracciare la madre nella loro casa a Hissar, un remoto villaggio dell’India. Rajo crede che il suo desiderio di vedere Naveen crescere e sposarsi le dia la forza di vivere, nonostante i problemi di salute. Sostiene di non poter morire finché Naveen non compirà 15 anni e si sposerà. Vive con il marito Ballo e la seconda, più giovane moglie Umi (che è anche la sorella di Rajo). Rajo descrive Naveen come un dono di Dio. Sebbene alcuni abbiano messo in discussione l’etica e le implicazioni sanitarie dell’essere madre alla sua età, Rajo è sopravvissuta alla malattia e ha anche superato in longevità il medico che l’ha aiutata durante il trattamento di fecondazione in vitro. Rajo ricorda che dopo il parto, il suo medico le consigliò il riposo a letto, ma non essendo abituata, continuò comunque a lavorare. Anche se la sua salute si è deteriorata per un periodo, alla fine si è sentita meglio, attribuendo i miglioramenti alle cure del suo medico, purtroppo ora deceduto. Racconta il suo grande desiderio di avere un figlio e la felicità condivisa del villaggio alla nascita di Naveen. La famiglia gode del forte sostegno dei parenti nel villaggio unito. Rajo non è preoccupata per il futuro di Naveen, poiché Umi, Ballo e altri familiari si occuperanno di lei. Come unica figlia di Rajo, Naveen erediterà tutte le proprietà materne, tra cui 52.600 metri quadrati di terreno. Umi, che ha sposato Ballo quando sembrava che Rajo non potesse avere figli, è anch’essa affezionata a Naveen. Garantisce che si prenderà sempre cura di lei in assenza di Rajo, offrendo amore e supporto. Nonostante l’età avanzata, Rajo continua a preparare Naveen per la scuola, dato che Naveen preferisce le attenzioni della madre. Naveen ora frequenta la scuola primaria del villaggio. È orgogliosa della madre e dice di volerle molto bene, persino più che al padre.

article_content: A series of 14 consecutive interest rate hikes by the Bank of England has created anxiety and financial strain for mortgage holders, while also boosting the savings of many. In the UK, millions are both borrowers and savers—so the balance between rising mortgage costs and improved savings returns is crucial. Following the Chancellor’s Autumn Statement, newly published documents offer insights into these shifting dynamics. According to the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), this year, increased savings returns have just outpaced the impact of higher mortgage rates, resulting in a slight rise in real household disposable income for 2023. However, this improvement is sandwiched between a decline in disposable income last year and a forecasted fall in 2024. The past year saw most households hit by rapidly rising prices. Looking ahead, around 1.6 million homeowners are set to see their mortgage deals expire, likely forcing them onto costlier loans and causing further strain. While the OBR’s forecasts are not infallible, they do carry significant influence since the OBR independently scrutinizes government economic policy. Interest rates, often discussed alongside tax and pension changes, are set by the independent Bank of England. Rates have risen steadily since December 2021 following years of historic lows. According to the OBR, UK households as a whole have demonstrated some resilience to these increases this year, as elevated savings returns have so far outweighed higher mortgage payments. However, this effect isn’t distributed evenly. Many in the UK have minimal savings, and a total of £260 billion sits in accounts earning no interest. Meanwhile, those not owning homes have still felt the effects, as higher mortgage rates contribute to rising rents. The OBR’s data are averages, though, and may mask deeper inequalities. Importantly, it warns that as more fixed-rate mortgages come up for renewal next year, aggregate debt interest payments will rise. This is predicted to cause a fall in real household disposable income, signaling more financial hardship even if the Bank of England keeps rates at 5.25%. There is some hope for homeowners: competition among mortgage providers has prompted rate cuts, softening the financial blow. According to Aaron Strutt of Trinity Financial, new two-year fixed mortgage rates start at 4.78%, with five-year deals at 4.43%. Borrowers are encouraged to check if better rates are available before their mortgage begins, as lenders often permit switching to cheaper deals. On the other hand, analysts believe savings rates may have peaked, particularly at National Savings and Investments (NS&I). Laura Suter of AJ Bell cautions that NS&I account rates and the Premium Bond prize fund could be cut, as the government-backed provider has already reached its yearly fundraising goal. Politicians have criticized major banks for not improving savings rates for loyal customers, and consumers are advised to search for the best rates. Recent economic measures include proposed National Insurance cuts, an 8.5% rise for the state pension, a 6.7% increase in benefits, and higher minimum wages. According to the Treasury, these policies are designed to help households meet expenses and support economic recovery. A Treasury spokesperson stated, “Average disposable income is around £800 higher than the OBR expected this spring, and the Autumn Statement set out a clear plan to reduce our borrowing and debt to keep inflation falling, helping get mortgage rates back down to affordable levels.” Still, despite slower price rises, many households continue to face financial challenges. For guidance on savings products, individuals can consult the MoneyHelper website.

article_content: A mysterious force known as dark energy might be gradually erasing the universe’s dark matter, potentially leading to a vast, empty cosmos. Researchers from the UK and Italy report new evidence indicating that dark matter—the hidden framework of galaxies—is being diminished by an ever-growing dark energy. Their analysis of recent astronomical data suggests that dark energy increases as it interacts with dark matter, which in turn slows down the formation of cosmic structures. Over time, this process could result in a universe that eventually becomes largely empty and devoid of features. Professor David Wands, Director of Portsmouth’s Institute of Cosmology and Gravitation, explained, 'This study is about the fundamental properties of space-time. On a cosmic scale, this is about our universe and its fate.' He said that if the trends continue—with dark energy strengthening and dark matter 'evaporating'—the result could be a 'big, empty, boring' universe. Dark matter serves as a framework for galaxy formation, while dark energy is thought to drive the expansion of the universe. Findings suggest their interaction is stunting the formation of new cosmic structures. A Hubble Space Telescope image showing evidence for a dark matter ring in galaxy cluster CI0024+17 exemplifies these complex cosmic phenomena. While the universe’s expansion models indicate the presence of dark energy, its exact nature remains unknown. Theories range from dark energy being a property of space itself to being linked to quantum vacuum fluctuations, where 'empty space' teems with transient particles. Scientists estimate that dark energy constitutes about 68% of the universe, dark matter around 27%, and normal matter less than 5%. Dark matter remains invisible, detectable only through its gravitational influence. As the European Space Agency explains, shining a light in a dark room reveals only part of what exists—likewise, much of the universe is unseen but has measurable effects. In 1998, the discovery that the universe’s expansion is accelerating ushered in a paradigm shift in cosmology, making the 'cosmological constant' central to prevailing theories. Now, researchers at Portsmouth and Rome suggest that a better model involves an energy exchange between dark matter and dark energy. Professor Wands said, 'Since the late 1990s, astronomers have been convinced that something is accelerating the universe’s expansion. The simplest explanation was that empty space holds constant energy. However, new data suggest this view doesn’t account for everything—specifically, the slower-than-expected formation of cosmic structures like galaxies and clusters.' Professor Dragan Huterer of the University of Michigan remarked, 'Any fresh development in the study of dark energy is important because so little is known about it. The paper is intriguing, but it’s not unexpected that new models differ from the simplest theories.' This research seeks to clarify the fate of the universe by understanding how dark energy and dark matter might interact over time.

article_content: Ayman Kandeel, a prominent Egyptian actor, reacted aggressively during the filming of a new Egyptian prank show called 'Alhokm Baad Almozawla' ('Judgment After a Prank'). During his appearance, he physically assaulted producers and crew members, as well as the show's female anchor. The program, hosted by actress Iman Mubarak, brings celebrities in under the pretense of an interview for an Arabic-speaking German channel. After a tense discussion about Egyptian-Israeli relations, the crew reveals that the show is supposedly for an Israeli TV station and begins to provoke the guests. Some participants have responded with anti-Israeli remarks, emotional distress, or physical outbursts. For example, actress Dina Abo Elsoud panicked and attempted to escape, fearing she might be kidnapped. In another episode, actress Mayar al-Beblawi made derogatory comments about Israelis and the Holocaust. The show has received international criticism and accusations of promoting anti-Semitic sentiments. Israeli officials have voiced concerns about its impact on Egypt-Israel relations and the peace accord. The show's creators defend it as a candid examination of a sensitive subject in Egyptian society and say celebrities agreed to airing the footage after learning it was a prank. 'Alhokm Baad Almozawla' ranks among the top five Ramadan TV programs in Egypt and has over four million views on YouTube. According to producers, incidents of violence occurred in only three out of 95 episodes. The show reflects Egypt's evolving media landscape since the end of the Mubarak regime, featuring a greater willingness to tackle controversial subjects. Producers argue that the program is an exercise of freedom of expression, and guests have the right to express their views.

article_content: Police agencies across Australia issued alerts on Monday, warning citizens about widespread scam text messages and emails. These fraudulent messages claimed that recipients had only two days to pay $5,000 or face death.  Detective Superintendent Brian Hay of the Queensland Police Service urged the public not to respond, advising, "Delete it immediately and don't panic, because that's what they prey upon."  The scam messages began appearing on mobile phones and email accounts on Sunday. While authorities did not specify the number of recipients, they expressed surprise at the extensive reach of the scheme. "What is extraordinary is the scope of contact across Australia," Hay said. "We've never seen this before."  Although the investigation is ongoing, previous similar hoaxes have been traced to West Africa, particularly Nigeria. The scam message states: 'Sum1 paid me to kill you. Get spared, 48hrs to pay $5000. If you inform the police or anybody, death is promised.' It directs recipients to reply to a Yahoo email address.  Police warn that seniors and those less familiar with the internet are especially vulnerable to such scams. "They rely on your fear to stop you from thinking logically and to make you respond as they want," Hay explained. "It is likely some people have already fallen victim."  This so-called 'hit-man scam' has surfaced in Australia twice in the past two and a half years. Hay emphasized that this is not a random event but the work of organized crime, noting the complexity and preparation involved. "They've done their research, acquired contact lists, and paid for message distribution." He warned that these criminals could strike again if the scam yields profits.

article_content: Next summer, Ibiza holidaymakers may notice an uptick in fake tans and hair extensions on the island's beaches. Enthusiastic fans, inspired by the Essex cast's adventures, flocked to the booking site despite Ibiza's summer party season having ended only a week prior. Locations such as Hacienda Na Xamena gained particular attention after being featured on the program. While most of Ibiza's annual closing parties have finished, a few smaller clubs remain open, and the primary tourist season resumes each May. In this series, the TOWIE cast traded their usual Marbella destination for two weeks of excitement in Ibiza. The show's influence is notable: after a special Marbella episode aired earlier this year, there was a 72% overnight increase in hotel searches for that destination. Stars like Jasmin Walia and Jessica Wright were filmed enjoying the scene at hotspots including Ocean Beach Ibiza, Hotel Es Vive, and Surf House. Lizann Peppard, Hotels.com spokesperson, commented that TOWIE continues to inspire viewers to seek out their own sun-filled holidays, and the site offers Ibiza deals year-round. Although the official tourist season has just finished, these search numbers underline the show's impact. The next episode of 'The Only Way Is Ibiza' airs on October 12 on ITVBe.

article_content: Animal poison control centers in the U.S. are seeing a sharp increase in reports of pets exposed to marijuana, a trend connected to wider legalization. Dr. Caroline Tonozzi, an emergency vet at the University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital, explains that while many cases involve dogs accidentally eating marijuana, some may be due to intentional exposure by pet owners. In Illinois, there are currently no explicit laws against intentionally getting pets high, according to animal rights attorney Suzana Harman. She notes each state has its own animal cruelty statutes, meaning judgments depend on each case’s specifics. While specific prohibitions are not in place, future legislation could address this gap. Experts from the University of Illinois suggest both dogs and cats are at risk from THC, the psychoactive part of cannabis. Dogs tend to eat marijuana directly, while cats may be affected by inhaling the smoke. Symptoms in dogs include poor coordination, urinating involuntarily, drooling, and being less responsive. Cats might behave as if reacting to things they don't see and can have dilated pupils. Although fatal marijuana intoxication in dogs is rare, some deaths have been reported, especially when pets eat marijuana edibles made with chocolate, xylitol, or fatty substances. Dr. Tonozzi advises immediate veterinary assessment if a pet is suspected of ingesting marijuana, especially due to the risk of combined toxicity from edibles. The health dangers to pets from marijuana can include very low heart rates, sedation to the point where swallowing or standing is difficult, and, in extreme cases, coma. Swift veterinary evaluation is essential, with hospitalization and continued monitoring often recommended.

In Illinois, oggi non esistono leggi esplicite che vietino di far assumere marijuana agli animali domestici volontariamente, secondo l’avvocata per i diritti degli animali Suzana Harman. Sottolinea che ogni stato ha le proprie leggi sulla crudeltà verso gli animali, quindi ogni caso viene valutato singolarmente. Sebbene non ci siano ancora divieti specifici, nuove leggi potrebbero essere introdotte in futuro. Gli esperti dell’Università dell’Illinois affermano che sia cani sia gatti possono essere avvelenati dal THC, il principio attivo della cannabis. I cani tendono a mangiare direttamente la marijuana, mentre i gatti rischiano di essere colpiti più spesso dal fumo inalato. Nei cani i sintomi sono perdita di coordinazione, minzione involontaria, salivazione e riduzione della reattività. I gatti possono sembrare rispondere a stimoli che non esistono e avere le pupille dilatate. Anche se i decessi da intossicazione da marijuana nei cani sono rari, sono stati segnalati, soprattutto dopo l’ingestione di edibili contenenti cioccolato, xilitolo o sostanze grasse. La dottoressa Tonozzi consiglia di rivolgersi subito al veterinario se si sospetta che un animale abbia ingerito marijuana, soprattutto per il rischio di tossicità combinata dovuta agli edibles. I pericoli per la salute degli animali includono un battito cardiaco molto basso, sedazione grave che impedisce loro di stare in piedi o deglutire, e nei casi più gravi, coma. È fondamentale avere una valutazione veterinaria tempestiva; spesso serve ospedalizzazione e monitoraggio continuo.

article_content: Thirteen Islamic seminary pupils were shot and killed by armed men during Maulud celebrations in Kusa village, Musawa district of Katsina state, northwest Nigeria, local officials said. The attack took place late Sunday as gunmen on motorcycles stormed the gathering of children commemorating the Prophet Mohammed’s birthday. Twenty others were injured—five treated in Musawa and 15 transferred to a hospital in the state capital, Katsina. Local vigilantes confronted the assailants, preventing further abductions. These criminal gangs, often called 'bandits', operate across northwestern Nigeria and are responsible for raids, kidnappings, and arson in rural communities. Their violence, once tied to disputes between herders and farmers, now primarily involves organized crime. Communities have formed vigilante groups in self-defense, sometimes escalating cycles of retaliation. Katsina police confirmed the attack, stating 18 people were injured and two later died in the hospital, presenting a slight variance in numbers. In 2020, a similar incident saw 80 pupils abducted during a Maulud celebration, who were later rescued. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, inaugurated in May, faces ongoing challenges in curbing armed violence and bolstering national security.

L’attacco si è verificato nella tarda serata di domenica, quando alcuni uomini armati su motociclette hanno assalito il raduno di bambini che celebravano il compleanno del Profeta Maometto. Altri venti sono rimasti feriti: cinque sono stati medicati a Musawa e quindici trasferiti in un ospedale nella capitale dello stato, Katsina. Nel 2020, un evento simile ha visto il rapimento di ottanta studenti durante una celebrazione del Maulud, successivamente liberati. Il presidente Bola Ahmed Tinubu, in carica da maggio, deve affrontare la sfida costante di combattere la violenza armata e rafforzare la sicurezza nazionale.

article_content: WARSAW, Poland — Polish road transport authorities met with their Ukrainian counterparts on Wednesday to address competition issues that have led Polish truckers to block two border crossings, causing days-long delays. Polish truckers claim unregulated activity by rapidly expanding Ukrainian transport companies is harming their business. Since Russia's invasion in February 2022, Ukraine has increasingly relied on import and export by road as air and sea routes remain blocked. Polish truckers are demanding official permits for Ukrainian transport firms. According to Poland's Infrastructure Ministry, imposing such regulations is subject to European Union jurisdiction, as the Poland-Ukraine border is also an EU border. The Polish side is also calling for faster procedures on the Ukrainian side of the border and wants an additional crossing dedicated to empty trucks to ease congestion. Talks were taking place in the eastern Polish city of Chelm between representatives of both countries' transport sectors. Polish truckers continue to restrict truck passage at the Dorohusk and Hrebenne crossings, leading to wait times approaching two weeks. Most of the trucks delayed are Ukrainian.

article_content:
The dense smogs that once blanketed British cities until the 1950s are well-remembered for their health dangers. However, newly revealed photographs from the 1940s and 1950s show that Pittsburgh, a major American industrial city, faced similarly severe air pollution. At its worst, pollution in Pittsburgh could block out the midday sun. This is evident in images preserved in the University of Pittsburgh’s Smoke Control Lantern Slide Collection.

In these photos, residents go about their lives shrouded in thick smog, which obscures the tops of buildings and reduces visibility between city structures, even during daylight. For decades, the serious health hazards posed by coal smoke and industrial pollution were not widely understood. Clouds of pollution regularly enveloped Pittsburgh’s skyscrapers until the city government took steps to curb the burning of coal.

The pollution problem in Pittsburgh dates back well before the twentieth century. Nineteenth-century novelist Anthony Trollope described Pittsburgh as 'the blackest place which I ever saw.' Still, due to the lack of alternative fuels in the 1800s, implementing smoke controls was not feasible. At the time, many people even believed that heavy smoke indicated economic productivity, and some thought coal smoke was beneficial to health and agriculture.

The University of Pittsburgh assembled the photographic collection to chart the development of the city’s smoke control laws. While such laws were first enacted in 1941, World War II delayed their enforcement, allowing smog to persist for more than a decade. Essays from the era, including James Parton’s 1868 account in The Atlantic Monthly, vividly portrayed Pittsburgh’s air quality problems: 'The town lies low… just visible through the mingled smoke and mist, and every object in it is black. Smoke, smoke, smoke — everywhere smoke.'

Archival images show factory chimneys blanketing the city in smoke and reveal how vehicle exhaust further worsened air quality. Although air pollution in Pittsburgh has improved considerably since the 1950s, similar life-threatening smogs continue to impact newly industrialized countries. For example, recent reports note warnings to foreign embassies in Beijing about sharing pollution data, while official forecasts often understate the problem even as residents face heavy haze.

Pittsburgh’s story highlights both the severe environmental cost of rapid industrialization and the positive changes that can result from sustained policy action.

Il problema dell’inquinamento a Pittsburgh è molto più antico del Novecento. Lo scrittore vittoriano Anthony Trollope definì Pittsburgh "il luogo più nero che io abbia mai visto". Fumo, fumo, fumo — ovunque fumo."

Le foto d’archivio mostrano le ciminiere delle fabbriche che coprono la città di fumo e documentano come anche i gas di scarico delle auto peggioravano la qualità dell’aria. La storia di Pittsburgh mette in evidenza il pesante costo ambientale dell’industrializzazione rapida ma anche i progressi possibili grazie a interventi politici mirati e duraturi.

article_content: Iran’s Football Federation has instituted mandatory gender verification for women’s football players after it emerged that four members of the national women’s team were actually men. Medical staff will perform random checks during training sessions, and any player unable to prove she is female will be excluded from the team. Players can rejoin if they officially undergo gender reassignment procedures and receive medical clearance. The decision follows revelations, reported by The Telegraph, that several prominent players, including four national team members, were men who had not completed sex reassignment surgery or had conditions affecting their sexual development. Sex reassignment surgeries have been legal in Iran since 1979 following a religious decree by Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, even though the country enforces strict laws on sexual conduct under Sharia, banning homosexuality and premarital sex. Ahmad Hashemian, the head of the football federation’s medical committee, told IRNA that those who finish necessary surgeries and receive medical approval may participate in women’s football. To date, seven players in the women’s pro-league have had their contracts terminated after gender tests. Football is hugely popular in Iran among both men and women, but women are not permitted to attend men’s matches. Concerns over player gender reportedly surfaced about four years ago when suspicions arose regarding a female team’s goalkeeper.

article_content: Canada’s women’s tennis team achieved a historic milestone in Seville, Spain, on November 12, 2023, by winning their first Billie Jean King Cup title. The Canadian team, including Leylah Fernandez and 18-year-old Marina Stakusic, delivered consecutive singles wins in the final against four-time champions Italy. Fernandez, renowned for her 2021 US Open run, defeated Jasmine Paolini 6-2, 6-3. Earlier, Stakusic kicked off the final with a 7-5, 6-3 triumph over Martina Trevisan. These victories secured Canada an unassailable 2-0 advantage and brought home one of women’s tennis’s most coveted team trophies. The tournament, which began as the Federation Cup in 1963, is now named in honor of Billie Jean King—a champion for equality, a 12-time Grand Slam winner, and a vocal advocate of LGBTQ rights. "It’s an incredible feeling. Representing Canada on such a grand stage means a lot," said Fernandez, expressing her pride. "Winning in front of Billie Jean King makes this experience even more special. We’re looking forward to celebrating together." Canada’s run to the title was dominant, with only one defeat on their path. Their previous best performance in the competition was reaching the semi-finals in 1988. Along with the victory, the Canadian team earned $2.4 million in prize money—a year after their first Davis Cup triumph. The Canadian Olympic Committee praised the team’s spirited and powerful performance throughout the tournament. For Stakusic, currently ranked 258th, the final capped off a breakout week. She scored her first win over a top-50 player by overcoming Trevisan, delivering a forehand winner on her fifth match point. "I’m so grateful and thrilled to have played this week—it’s truly been the highlight of my career so far," Stakusic said.

Fernandez, nota per il suo percorso fino alla finale degli US Open 2021, ha sconfitto Jasmine Paolini 6-2, 6-3. In precedenza Stakusic aveva aperto la finale superando Martina Trevisan 7-5, 6-3. Questi successi hanno assicurato al Canada un vantaggio decisivo di 2-0, permettendo la conquista di uno dei trofei a squadre più prestigiosi del tennis femminile. Il torneo, nato come Federation Cup nel 1963, oggi è dedicato a Billie Jean King—simbolo di parità nei diritti, vincitrice di 12 titoli del Grande Slam e attivista LGBTQ. «È una sensazione incredibile.
