article_content: Lisa Marie Presley expressed concerns to director Sofia Coppola that a new film’s script portrayed her father, Elvis Presley, as 'a predator and manipulative,' according to Variety. Four months before her death in January, Lisa Marie wrote to Coppola to voice her objections. The film in question, 'Priscilla,' tells the story of Priscilla Presley, who met Elvis when she was 14. Priscilla Presley has publicly supported the film, while Coppola told Lisa Marie that Elvis is depicted with 'sensitivity and complexity.' 'Priscilla' is based on Priscilla's 1985 memoir, 'Elvis and Me.' In emails quoted by Variety, Lisa Marie wrote, 'My father only comes across as a predator and manipulative. As his daughter, I don't read this and see any of my father in this character. I don't read this and see my mother's perspective of my father. I read this and see your shockingly vengeful and contemptuous perspective and I don't understand why?' Priscilla serves as executive producer, but Lisa Marie reportedly threatened to publicly oppose both the film and her mother's support for it. 'I am worried that my mother isn’t seeing the nuance here or realizing the way in which Elvis will be perceived when this movie comes out,' Lisa Marie wrote. 'I feel protective over my mother who has spent her whole life elevating my father's legacy. I am worried she doesn't understand the intentions behind this film or the outcome it will have.' Priscilla has contributed to the film as the source of its story, as executive producer, and in interviews, where she’s stated the film accurately reflects her relationship with Elvis. During an interview with Piers Morgan on TalkTV, Priscilla said the film accurately represents her life with Elvis, whom she met at 14 while he was stationed in Germany with the US Army. She referred to it as 'a different time,' and described Elvis as 'unique.' Priscilla denied claims of grooming, saying, 'I didn’t take it as that. I'd never heard the word. Obviously, it’s all new now.' She recalled that Elvis would buy her clothes and take her to the movies while still maintaining boundaries, asserting he was never aggressive or sexual with her until after their marriage when she was 21. Coppola’s representative told Variety that she assured Lisa Marie of her intent to honor both Priscilla and Elvis with 'sensitivity and complexity.' Critics have discussed how modern audiences may react to the film’s portrayal of Priscilla and Elvis’s early relationship. Brian Truitt of USA Today called their early relationship 'a creepy sight for 2023 eyes.' David Rooney of The Hollywood Reporter notes that some viewers might be uncomfortable, but Coppola handles the subject 'nonjudgmentally.' Marlow Stern of Rolling Stone observed that Elvis is shown as gentlemanly, despite the discomfort their courtship may elicit for contemporary viewers. Ben Kenigsberg of The New York Times commented that the power dynamic can seem 'appalling from a contemporary standpoint,' though the film does not present Elvis simply as a villain. 'Priscilla' stars Cailee Spaeny in the title role and Jacob Elordi as Elvis. The film was recently released in the US and will arrive in UK cinemas in January. The release follows last year’s 'Elvis,' which starred Austin Butler and Tom Hanks. Lisa Marie Presley died at age 54 from a cardiac arrest caused by a small bowel obstruction, a complication stemming from previous weight-loss surgery.

article_content: Homeward, a free browser game developed by Wuppos, blends choose-your-own-adventure storytelling with clever inventory management, all set in charming pixel art. Rather than simply getting home, the challenge lies in seeing how much wealth you can gather before the journey ends. Players begin by packing their bag thoughtfully and then set off, making quick decisions about which items to keep or toss as they face mini-adventures along the way. Unlike the often tedious inventory systems in other games, here these choices are entertaining and add to the fun. Homeward is a playful example of how great design can make even routine game systems enjoyable, suggesting that even complex titles could benefit from such streamlined mechanics.

L’obiettivo non è solo tornare a casa, ma scoprire quanto bottino puoi accumulare lungo il viaggio. All’inizio del gioco, i giocatori selezionano con cura cosa mettere nello zaino, per poi affrontare mini-avventure decidendo velocemente quali oggetti conservare o lasciare. Homeward mostra con ironia come anche i meccanismi più semplici possano essere godibili, suggerendo che persino i giochi più complessi potrebbero beneficiare di soluzioni più agili.

article_content: While many visits to Marrakech focus on the iconic Koutoubia mosque and the lively Jemaa el Fna square, the city offers much more beyond these spots. For those willing to explore the side streets near the square, or venture out to the surrounding desert and mountains, Marrakech presents stunning scenery, unforgettable flavors, and luxurious treats. Here are some of the city's highlights. 1. Getting lost in the medina. Wandering through Marrakech's old medina is both enjoyable and, at times, costly, thanks to small shops selling everything from djellaba robes and spices to carpets and colorful ceramics. Haggling is expected and can make buying souvenirs both rewarding and entertaining. A recommended stop is La Porte d'Or, a two-level bazaar packed with rugs and antiques (115 Souk Semmarine, Marrakech; +212 24445454). 2. Strolling through Jardin Majorelle. This 12-acre botanical garden, once owned by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later rescued by fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent, blends Moorish and art deco styles with rare plants. The electric blue villa stands out, and after Saint Laurent's death, his ashes were scattered here. (Jardin Majorelle, Rue Yves Saint Laurent, Marrakech; +212 5243-01894). 3. Sampling Moroccan cuisine. Marrakech is known for dishes like cooked snails, tajines, couscous, and the adventurous sheep's head. Tanjia, a slow-cooked meat dish, is especially popular among locals. Dar Rhizlane Bejgueni, a 40-year-old restaurant in Jamaa el Fna square, is famed for its sandwiches and atmosphere. (Jamaa el Fna square, Marrakech). 4. Relaxing in a Hammam. Visiting a traditional public bath, or Hammam, is an essential Moroccan experience. Being scrubbed by a professional is a revitalizing way to unwind from the busy medina. Les Bains de Marrakech is a popular luxury spa near the medina with individual massage rooms. (2 Derb Sedra, Bab Agnaou, Kasbah, Marrakech; +212 5 24 38 14 28). 5. Exploring palaces and luxury hotels. El Badi Palace, despite being in ruins, highlights the grandeur of the 16th-century sultan's residence, with underground rooms and a museum. Mamounia Palace, a renowned five-star hotel, has hosted celebrities for nearly a century. Namaskar Palace, on the way to the Atlas Mountains, is famed for its oasis-style spa retreat. (El Badi Palace: Ksibat Nhass, Marrakech; +212 661 350878. Mamounia Palace, Arset el Maach, Marrakech; +212 5243 88600. Namaskar Palace, Route de Bab Atlas, 88/69, Province Syba, Marrakech; +212 5 24 29 98 00). 6. Staying in a riad. Traditional Moroccan houses built around central gardens or courtyards, known as riads, are an essential part of the Marrakech experience. Many now blend classic decor with modern touches. El Fenn is a luxury boutique riad with 22 rooms across three courtyards. (Derb Moullay Abdullah Ben Hezzian, Bab el Ksour Medina, Marrakech; +212 524 44 1210). 7. Visiting the Atlas Mountains. Marrakech’s proximity to the Atlas Mountains offers guests a cool retreat from the city’s bustle. Lalla Takerkoust, a town 43 kilometers southwest, is ideal for outdoor activities like quad biking and camel riding. The Ourika valley and the village of Armed provide access to Berber villages and hiking near Morocco’s highest peak, Toubkal. (Roches Hotel: +212 667 64 49 15). 8. Shopping in Bab el Khemis. Slightly off the beaten path, Bab el Khemis is known for its lively souk, especially on Thursdays when it becomes a bustling flea market for vintage carpets, doors, and various treasures. 9. Hot air balloon rides. Marrakech has become a popular spot for balloon flights, offering spectacular views of the Atlas Mountains with clear skies nearly year-round. Ciel d’Afrique is a well-established operator. (+212 524 43 28 43). 10. Adventure at Terres d’Amanar. Just 30 minutes south of Marrakech, Terres d’Amanar offers outdoor activities like climbing, zip lining, horse and camel riding, and Berber bread-making courses on its 173-acre site. (+212 524 438 103).

Ecco alcuni dei punti salienti della città. 1. Perdersi nella medina. Passeggiare nell’antica medina di Marrakech è piacevole e a volte costoso, grazie ai piccoli negozi che vendono di tutto, dai djellaba alle spezie, dai tappeti alle ceramiche colorate. Contrattare è la norma e può rendere l’acquisto di souvenir divertente e soddisfacente. Consigliato: La Porte d'Or, un bazar su due livelli pieno di tappeti e oggetti d’antiquariato (115 Souk Semmarine, Marrakech; +212 24445454). 2. Passeggiare nel Jardin Majorelle. Questo giardino botanico di 12 acri, un tempo di proprietà del pittore francese Jacques Majorelle e poi salvato dallo stilista Yves Saint Laurent, unisce stili moreschi e art déco con piante rare. L’elettrica villa blu risalta e, dopo la morte di Saint Laurent, le sue ceneri furono sparse qui. (Jardin Majorelle, Rue Yves Saint Laurent, Marrakech; +212 5243-01894). 3. Assaporare la cucina marocchina. Marrakech è rinomata per piatti come lumache cotte, tajine, couscous e testa di pecora per i più avventurosi. Dar Rhizlane Bejgueni, un ristorante istituzione da 40 anni nella piazza Jamaa el Fna, è celebre per i suoi panini e l’atmosfera. (Jamaa el Fna, Marrakech). 4. Rilassarsi in un Hammam. Fare shopping a Bab el Khemis. Voli in mongolfiera. Marrakech è ora popolare per i voli in mongolfiera che offrono panorami impareggiabili sull’Atlante, quasi sempre accompagnati da cieli sereni. A soli 30 minuti dalla città, Terres d’Amanar offre arrampicata, zipline, passeggiate a cavallo e cammello, e corsi di pane berbero su un’area di 173 acri. (+212 524 438 103).

article_content: Facebook surprised investors when it announced on Wednesday its acquisition of WhatsApp for $19 billion—a record sum that led to a drop in Facebook's stock price. The deal consists of $12 billion in Facebook shares, $4 billion in cash, and $3 billion in restricted stock units allocated to WhatsApp’s founders and staff, vesting over four years. While some analysts, such as those at Sterne Agee, view the purchase as strategically important, others at Pacific Crest Securities have questioned whether Facebook should have grown organically or moved earlier to reduce the acquisition cost. WhatsApp, founded in 2009, has grown rapidly to over 450 million monthly active users globally, surpassing Facebook’s user growth during its early years. It offers free messaging services to smartphone users, supporting both individual and group conversations, as well as sharing of media and voice recordings. Mark Zuckerberg, CEO of Facebook, described WhatsApp as the fastest-growing app he has encountered and expressed enthusiasm for the acquisition, highlighting both companies' commitment to global connectivity. He confirmed that WhatsApp would continue to operate independently, as Instagram has, and would not introduce advertisements at this stage. In addition, WhatsApp’s co-founder and CEO Jan Koum will join Facebook’s board. Compared to earlier technology acquisitions—such as Google's $12.5 billion purchase of Motorola Mobility and Microsoft's $8.5 billion deal for Skype—Facebook’s acquisition of WhatsApp stands out in scope. The agreement includes a $1 billion break-up fee if the deal does not close, and ensures WhatsApp will remain headquartered in Mountain View, California. Although Facebook’s shares declined by up to 5% following the announcement, they have risen by over 20% since the start of the year. Observers suggest that WhatsApp’s large user base, particularly among younger people, could help Facebook maintain its appeal and strengthen its position in mobile communications. However, experts also note that the technology and social media landscape is fast-changing, with the potential for new competitors to emerge.

CCTV footage shows police officers allegedly helping themselves to biscuits and coffee in the office of suspect David Sharma while he was detained in a police cell, anxious about his future. Sharma, 47, a father of two from Canterbury, Kent, has announced plans to take legal action against police, claiming a breach of his human rights. 

Sharma, who is a director at the Howfield Manor Hotel in Chartham Hatch, Kent, was arrested on suspicion of voyeurism after a complaint suggested hidden cameras were found in the women's toilets at the hotel. He was questioned and held in custody for nine hours before being released without charge; police later informed him he would face no further action. 

According to Sharma, six officers entered his office during the investigation, requested evidence, and seized CCTV equipment along with personal electronics from his home. He says that while he waited in a cold cell (with his coat and shoes taken from him), officers spent about four hours in his office, consuming his coffee and biscuits. Sharma believes this treatment constituted a breach of the Human Rights Act and has sought legal advice. 

Upon review of his hotel's CCTV after his release, Sharma was dismayed to observe the officers relaxing and consuming refreshments during the search. He also commented on the long-term distress the incident caused him, which included sleep difficulties, anxiety, and business losses, such as canceled events at the hotel. 

A spokesperson for Kent Police declined to comment, citing potential legal action pending from Mr. Sharma.

article_content: Financial technology (fintech) has rapidly transformed over the past decade, driven by widespread internet access and the proliferation of mobile devices. This evolution has given rise to a new generation of fintech companies that tackle challenges facing traditional banking through innovative solutions. Among the most significant advancements is blockchain technology. Often linked to the cryptocurrency Bitcoin, blockchain is a distributed database system that enables secure, transparent, and tamper-resistant transactions. Although still emerging, blockchain is already making a mark on the financial sector and could revolutionize how money is transferred, stored, and managed. One of the main benefits of blockchain is its potential to reduce dependence on centralized intermediaries like banks, which have historically managed transactions but can be prone to errors and fraud. By using a decentralized ledger, blockchain could make banking more efficient and secure. Additionally, fewer intermediaries could lead to reduced costs, making financial services more affordable. Blockchain's potential applications are vast and include: 1. Finance and Banking: Blockchain can accelerate transactions, reduce costs, and enhance security. For example, banks may use it to process payments more quickly and securely. 2. Supply Chain Management: Blockchain can track products and materials across the supply chain, by providing better transparency and efficiency. 3. Healthcare: It can be used to securely store and share patient medical records, improving data privacy and overall healthcare efficiency. 4. Elections: Blockchain-based systems could strengthen the security and transparency of voting, helping to reduce fraud and maintain election integrity. 5. Real Estate: Blockchain can streamline real estate transactions such as buying, selling, or renting property and potentially lower associated costs. These examples only scratch the surface of blockchain's potential, as new applications continue to emerge across industries. Blockchain can increase the efficiency and transparency of financial transactions in several ways: - Security: Blockchains are generally more secure due to their decentralized design and encryption. - Speed: Transactions can be settled much faster than through traditional methods. - Cost: Eliminating third-party intermediaries can lower transaction expenses. - Transparency: Blockchain's tamper-proof ledger makes transaction histories accessible to network participants. - Data Quality: Automation and validation help reduce errors. However, blockchain is still in its early stages and substantial hurdles remain—such as scalability issues, regulatory uncertainties, and a shortage of qualified engineers—before widespread adoption in finance is possible. FAQs: 1. What is blockchain in fintech? Blockchain enables direct money transfers between individuals without using a traditional bank or financial service provider. 2. How does blockchain secure financial transactions? Blockchain employs a decentralized, transparent digital ledger that is used extensively in financial services for payments, identity checks, trading, lending, and more. 3. Are fintech and blockchain the same? No. Blockchain is a technology that drives many advancements in fintech, but they are distinct concepts. Both have the power to reshape industries, particularly financial services. Disclaimer: This article was produced by the ET Spotlight Team. The news and editorial staff of ET were not involved in its creation.

article_content: A sign reading "Where is John Galt?" is displayed on a vehicle traveling down Interstate 85 in Atlanta, Georgia, alluding to Ayn Rand's famous novel, 'Atlas Shrugged.' Though the correct phrase is "Who is John Galt?", the reference signals Rand’s resurgence in popularity amidst the economic downturn and federal bailout initiatives. Ayn Rand, known for her advocacy of libertarian, free-market ideas she called Objectivism, is attracting renewed public attention. Wall Street Journal columnist Stephen Moore suggested in January that if 'Atlas Shrugged' were required reading for Congress and the Obama administration, the country's financial troubles might be resolved more quickly. This sentiment reflects growing public interest in Rand’s works. According to Yaron Brook, president of the Ayn Rand Institute, 'Atlas Shrugged' sold more copies in the first four months of 2009 than in all of 2008, when it reached 200,000 sales. For over a month, the novel ranked within Amazon.com's top 50 bestsellers. This is notable for a 1,100-page novel published in 1957 by an author who passed away in 1982. Many see connections between current events—such as the government taking control of banks and the automobile industry, and even firing the CEO of a major corporation—and themes from 'Atlas Shrugged,' according to Brook. There has also been Hollywood interest in adapting the novel, fitting since Rand once worked as a screenwriter. Despite efforts by 'Godfather' producer Albert S. Ruddy and discussions of miniseries in the 1970s and 1990s, substantial adaptations have yet to be realized. Angelina Jolie was reportedly attached to star as Dagny Taggart in 2006, with Russell Crowe and Brad Pitt rumored to be in consideration, but as of early 2009, the film's prospects remain uncertain. 'Atlas Shrugged' chronicles a group of business leaders and individualists who strike in protest of increasing government regulation. Characters such as Dagny Taggart and Hank Rearden attempt to unravel the situation, eventually encountering John Galt, an engineer who inspires others to withdraw in defense of individual freedom. Galt delivers a pivotal, lengthy speech outlining Rand’s philosophical system. Upon its release, the novel was polarizing. Some readers praised its message of self-sufficiency, while many critics disapproved of Rand's political views, atheism, and writing style. Time magazine questioned its literary merit and criticized Rand’s philosophical stance, though it acknowledged her creativity. Despite controversy, the book became a bestseller and remained influential. In a 1991 Library of Congress/Book-of-the-Month Club survey, it ranked second only to the Bible on the list of most influential books. Rand's philosophy, often associated with selfishness and unrestrained capitalism—she was known for wearing a dollar-sign brooch—has attracted a significant following, especially among political conservatives. Supporters include Rush Limbaugh and former Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, who was once part of Rand's circle. Critics, such as economist Heather Boushey of the Center for American Progress, challenge Rand’s belief in completely unregulated capitalism, especially in light of the recent financial crisis. Even Greenspan, once an advocate of laissez-faire economics, has expressed regret over that stance, telling Congress in October that his faith in banks to act in their own self-interest had been misplaced. Brook stresses that, for Rand, rational self-interest involves pursuing one's long-term good without exploiting others—not acting unethically for personal gain. The debate over the balance between individualism and collective sacrifice continues to animate both Rand’s supporters and detractors. This ongoing conversation contributes to the enduring popularity of her works in bookstores—a trend that would likely have pleased the dollar-sign-wearing author.

Questo sentimento riflette il crescente interesse del pubblico per le opere di Rand. Secondo Yaron Brook, presidente dell'Ayn Rand Institute, 'La rivolta di Atlante' ha venduto più copie nei primi quattro mesi del 2009 che in tutto il 2008, quando ha raggiunto 200.000 copie vendute. Per oltre un mese, il romanzo è stato tra i primi 50 bestseller su Amazon.com. Un risultato notevole per un romanzo di 1.100 pagine pubblicato nel 1957 da un'autrice scomparsa nel 1982. Molti vedono collegamenti tra gli eventi attuali—come il controllo governativo di banche e industria automobilistica, e persino il licenziamento dell’amministratore delegato di una grande azienda—e i temi di 'La rivolta di Atlante', secondo Brook. Anche Hollywood ha mostrato interesse per un adattamento cinematografico del romanzo, il che è appropriato dato che Rand era stata sceneggiatrice. Nonostante gli sforzi del produttore de 'Il padrino' Albert S. Ruddy e discussioni su miniserie negli anni '70 e '90, gli adattamenti concreti non si sono ancora realizzati. Nel 2006 si diceva che Angelina Jolie fosse stata scelta per interpretare Dagny Taggart, con i nomi di Russell Crowe e Brad Pitt proposti, ma all'inizio del 2009 il progetto risultava ancora incerto. 'La rivolta di Atlante' racconta di un gruppo di leader d'azienda e individualisti che scioperano per protestare contro una crescente regolamentazione statale. Personaggi come Dagny Taggart e Hank Rearden cercano di comprendere la situazione, incontrando infine John Galt, un ingegnere che ispira altri a ritirarsi in nome della libertà individuale. Galt pronuncia un lungo discorso fondamentale che illustra il sistema filosofico di Rand. Alla sua uscita, il romanzo fu polarizzante. Alcuni lettori ne lodarono il messaggio di autosufficienza, mentre molti critici non approvarono le posizioni politiche, l’ateismo e lo stile della Rand. La rivista Time ne mise in dubbio il valore letterario e criticò la filosofia della Rand, pur riconoscendone l’inventiva. Nonostante le controversie, il libro divenne un bestseller e restò influente. In un sondaggio del 1991 della Library of Congress e Book-of-the-Month Club, occupò il secondo posto tra i libri più influenti, dietro solo alla Bibbia. La filosofia della Rand, spesso associata all’egoismo e al capitalismo senza restrizioni—era nota per indossare una spilla a forma di simbolo del dollaro—ha raccolto molti sostenitori, specialmente tra i conservatori politici. Tra questi, Rush Limbaugh e l’ex presidente della Federal Reserve Alan Greenspan, un tempo vicino alla Rand. I critici, come l’economista Heather Boushey del Center for American Progress, contestano l’idea di Rand di capitalismo completamente deregolamentato, specialmente dopo la recente crisi finanziaria. Anche Greenspan, un tempo sostenitore del laissez-faire, ha poi espresso rammarico sostenendo davanti al Congresso, a ottobre, di aver riposto troppa fiducia nelle banche e nel loro agire nell'interesse proprio. Brook sottolinea che, per Rand, l’interesse personale razionale consiste nel perseguire il proprio bene a lungo termine senza sfruttare gli altri—non nel comportarsi in modo non etico per profitto personale. Il dibattito tra individualismo e sacrificio collettivo continua ad animare sia i sostenitori che i detrattori di Rand. Questa discussione contribuisce alla duratura popolarità delle sue opere, un trend che probabilmente avrebbe reso felice l'autrice dal simbolo del dollaro.

article_content: On his 35th birthday, Virat Kohli equaled Sachin Tendulkar's record by scoring his 49th ODI century in a World Cup match against South Africa. Tendulkar congratulated Kohli and wished him success in surpassing the record soon. Kohli reached his 49th century in 277 innings, while Tendulkar reached his in 452. Kohli currently has the highest number of international runs among active players and is second overall only to Tendulkar. During this World Cup, Kohli has scored 442 runs in seven matches, averaging 88.40, including one century and four half-centuries. Kohli has played 111 Test matches for India, amassing 8,676 runs at an average of 49.29, with 29 centuries and 29 fifties. He is the fifth-highest Indian Test run-scorer and holds the fourth-highest number of Test centuries for India. Globally, he is among the top ten for Test centuries. As India's Test captain, Kohli recorded 40 wins, 17 losses, and 11 draws in 68 matches, making him the country's most successful Test captain. Under his leadership, India topped the World Test Championship rankings for five consecutive years, aided by strong coaching and a formidable pace attack. In other news, the Indian government banned 22 illegal betting and gambling apps, including Mahadev Book Online, which is under scrutiny for bribery allegations involving Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel. A delegation of senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Jordan, the Palestinian Authority, Indonesia, and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation arrived in Beijing on Monday, urging an immediate ceasefire in Gaza. They were welcomed by China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi and began an international diplomatic campaign aimed at halting Israel’s military actions. China has expanded its influence in the Middle East, notably facilitating dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Iran earlier this year.

Recently, China sent a peace envoy to the region and, as the rotating president of the UN Security Council, maintained a strong endorsement of ceasefire efforts. Wang Yi reaffirmed China’s long-standing support for Arab and Muslim countries and its commitment to the Palestinian cause.

Yet experts such as David Roberts of King’s College London stress that China’s practical influence remains limited in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The confrontation intensified following the October 7 Hamas attack that killed 1,200 people in Israel, leading to Israeli airstrikes and a ground offensive that have killed more than 13,000 people in Gaza, including many children, and displaced around 1.4 million residents.

Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud called for an urgent halt to the violence and increased humanitarian aid to Gaza, stating that existing UN measures were not adequate. Israel’s ambassador to China, Irit Ben-Abba, argued that sufficient aid has been provided and that additional international pressure is politically motivated. While China and the U.S. differ in their policies toward the crisis, analysts are skeptical about China’s prospects for a breakthrough. The Beijing meeting came shortly after an Islamic-Arab summit in Riyadh, where leaders urged the International Criminal Court to investigate alleged Israeli war crimes in Palestinian territories.

article_content: Migration is a vital survival strategy for many animal species. Animals migrate to find food, reproduce, reduce competition, escape predators, or avoid harsh winters. During these journeys, whether they are mammals, birds, fish, or insects, migrating animals often encounter parasites in the environments they pass through, but they have developed strategies to limit infection both for themselves and other members of their species. To explore how parasitic infection and migration interact, Professor Sandra Binning of the Université de Montréal and Dr. Allison Shaw of the University of Minnesota reviewed existing empirical studies and created a model to better understand these processes. Decline of Migration While the diversity and complexity of migratory behavior—and its critical role in species survival—have been widely studied, global migration is declining due to climate change and widespread destruction of natural habitats. This trend is altering approaches to migration research. "The solutions to mitigate these losses are well-known—for example, increasing environmental protection, maintaining habitat connectivity, and reducing deforestation," Binning said. "However, we often lack data about the specific factors that promote or hinder migratory behaviors in the first place." Varying Parasite Infestation Over the past decade, Binning and Shaw have developed theories on how parasites affect migration and on 'migratory recovery,' where migration can help animals recover from infection. With the contribution of PhD student Marie Levet, their literature review, now published in Ecology Letters, offers several insights. "Most migration studies focus on end-points such as reproduction or overwintering, but often neglect the journey's stages, which are crucial for understanding infection dynamics during movement," Binning explained. They found diverse results in the literature: "Sometimes, migrating individuals have higher or lower levels of infection than non-migrating members of the same species. In other cases, parasite load changes during migration," Binning noted. Types of Migratory Behavior Their analysis identified a range of migratory behaviors associated with parasite dynamics, both across long and short distances, falling into three principal categories: migratory recovery (migration to recover from infection), migratory escape (migration to leave contaminated environments), and migratory culling (heavily infected individuals fail to reach migration's end, potentially reducing further spread). "For example, large deer and ruminants in Europe and North America migrate to more remote northern areas in summer, helping them escape the ticks that thrive in southern regions, or they move to higher elevations," Binning said. There is also evidence of taxonomic bias: mammals and birds are overrepresented in migration research compared to fish, reptiles, and insects, which often migrate in larger numbers, with the exception of monarch butterflies. Binning emphasized the importance of studying insect migration due to their essential role in food chains. A Predictive Model for Changing Migration Based on the literature, the team developed a unified evolutionary model. "Our model combines mathematics and biology using a complex ecological perspective—considering factors such as migration distance, infection intensity during migration, and proportions of non-migrating individuals," Binning explained. This model helps capture the complexity of migratory patterns among various species and, according to Binning, will be a valuable tool for scientists aiming to predict changes in animal movements, diseases, and environmental conditions in an era of growing ecological challenges.
translated_content: La migrazione è una strategia fondamentale di sopravvivenza per molte specie animali. Gli animali migrano per trovare cibo, riprodursi, ridurre la competizione, evitare predatori o sfuggire agli inverni rigidi. Durante questi viaggi, che coinvolgono mammiferi, uccelli, pesci o insetti, gli animali migratori spesso incontrano parassiti negli ambienti che attraversano, ma hanno sviluppato strategie per limitare le infezioni sia per sé stessi che per gli altri membri della loro specie. Per esplorare come infezioni parassitarie e migrazione interagiscano, la professoressa Sandra Binning dell’Università di Montréal e la dottoressa Allison Shaw dell’Università del Minnesota hanno esaminato studi empirici esistenti e creato un modello per comprendere meglio questi processi. Il declino della migrazione Sebbene la diversità e la complessità dei comportamenti migratori—e il loro ruolo cruciale nella sopravvivenza delle specie—siano stati ampiamente studiati, a livello globale la migrazione è in declino a causa dei cambiamenti climatici e della distruzione diffusa degli habitat naturali. Questa tendenza sta cambiando anche il modo in cui la migrazione viene studiata. “Le soluzioni per contrastare queste perdite sono ben note—come aumentare la protezione ambientale, mantenere la connettività degli habitat e ridurre la deforestazione,” ha dichiarato Binning. “Tuttavia, spesso mancano dati sui fattori specifici che favoriscono o ostacolano i comportamenti migratori.” Variazione delle infestazioni parassitarie Negli ultimi dieci anni, Binning e Shaw hanno sviluppato teorie su come i parassiti influenzino la migrazione e sul ‘recupero migratorio’, dove la migrazione può aiutare gli animali a riprendersi dalle infezioni. Con il contributo della dottoranda Marie Levet, la loro revisione della letteratura, ora pubblicata su Ecology Letters, offre numerosi spunti. “La maggior parte degli studi sulla migrazione si concentra sui risultati finali come la riproduzione o lo svernamento, ma spesso trascurano le fasi del viaggio, che sono fondamentali per comprendere le dinamiche delle infezioni durante lo spostamento,” ha spiegato Binning. Hanno riscontrato dati molto variabili nella letteratura: “A volte, gli individui migratori hanno livelli di infezione più alti o più bassi rispetto ai non migratori della stessa specie. In altri casi, il carico parassitario cambia durante la migrazione,” ha osservato Binning. Tipi di comportamento migratorio La loro analisi ha identificato diversi comportamenti migratori legati alla presenza di parassiti, sia su lunghe che su brevi distanze, suddivisi in tre categorie principali: recupero migratorio (migrazione per guarire da un’infezione), fuga migratoria (migrazione per allontanarsi da ambienti contaminati) e selezione naturale migratoria (gli individui gravemente infetti non riescono a raggiungere la destinazione finale, riducendo così l’ulteriore diffusione). “Ad esempio, i grandi cervidi e ruminanti di Europa e Nord America migrano verso aree più settentrionali durante l’estate per sfuggire alle zecche che prosperano nelle regioni meridionali, oppure si spostano a quote più alte,” ha specificato Binning. C’è anche una distorsione tassonomica: i mammiferi e gli uccelli sono sovrarappresentati nella ricerca sulla migrazione rispetto a pesci, rettili e insetti, che spesso migrano in numero maggiore—con l’eccezione delle farfalle monarca. Binning ha sottolineato l’importanza di studiare la migrazione degli insetti, dato il loro ruolo fondamentale nelle catene alimentari. Un modello predittivo per capire i cambiamenti migratori Sulla base della letteratura, il gruppo di ricerca ha sviluppato un modello evolutivo unificato. “Il nostro modello unisce matematica e biologia con un approccio ecologico complesso, considerando fattori come la distanza migratoria, l’intensità delle infezioni durante la migrazione e la quota di individui non migratori,” ha spiegato Binning. Questo modello aiuta a cogliere la complessità dei modelli migratori tra le diverse specie e, secondo Binning, sarà uno strumento prezioso per gli scienziati che vogliono prevedere in modo più rapido i cambiamenti nei movimenti animali, nelle malattie e nelle condizioni ambientali in un’epoca di sfide ecologiche crescenti.

Ian Brady, known for the infamous Moors murders, appeared publicly for the first time in decades during a mental health tribunal at Ashworth Hospital in Merseyside. Doctors testified that Brady minimized the murders of five children, calling the acts 'petty' compared to those committed in war by soldiers and politicians. He demonstrated no remorse for his crimes.

Now 75 years old and largely unseen since his 1966 life sentence, Brady seeks to be transferred out of the high-security mental hospital and into prison, aiming to control when and how his life ends, following years on a hunger strike. The tribunal is reviewing whether Brady should remain hospitalized due to mental illness or is fit enough to serve his sentence in prison. The session at Ashworth is closed, but proceedings are transmitted by video to Manchester for family members and the media.

Brady, appearing with a feeding tube and wearing sunglasses, took frequent notes and showed little emotion. His presence was unsettling for families observing the hearing; Alan Bennett, whose brother Keith’s remains are still missing, criticized Brady for attention-seeking, while other relatives described the tribunal as a grim spectacle.

Brady and his accomplice, Myra Hindley (who died in 2002), were convicted for the murders of John Kilbride, Lesley Ann Downey, and Edward Evans in the 1960s, later admitting to killing Keith Bennett and Pauline Reade. Some victims’ remains, including Keith Bennett’s, have never been recovered. The tribunal is not re-examining these crimes, but their impact remains significant for the families involved.

Experts provided conflicting opinions about Brady’s mental health. Dr. Cameron Boyd reported Brady declined to confirm if he wished to die, denied being psychotic, and described his behavior as an existential or philosophical exercise. Dr. Adrian Grounds, examining for Brady’s legal team, found no evidence of psychosis but noted signs of a serious personality disorder, including paranoia and manipulation. Brady claimed to have learned to imitate symptoms of mental illness while previously incarcerated.

The proceedings continue, as the tribunal considers Brady’s mental health, potential transfer, and issues of justice for the victims’ families.

article_content: Nearly fifty years after President John F. Kennedy’s assassination, conspiracy theories continue to circulate about the November day in Dallas. Judyth Vary Baker, claiming to have been Lee Harvey Oswald’s girlfriend, adds her account in a memoir. Baker states Oswald did not kill the President and was framed. In her book “Me and Lee,” Baker alleges she worked on a secret project intended to inflict lung cancer on Fidel Castro. At a recent bookstore event in Oregon, she described Oswald as a hero who tried to stop the assassination. Living abroad for safety, Baker is promoting her book with a limited tour and virtual appearances. She says she conducted advanced cancer research in early 1960s New Orleans under Dr. Alton Ochsner and met Oswald during this time. Baker claims the two were romantically involved and that Oswald shared details of a planned attack on Kennedy. She asserts Oswald worked on a secret project led by Dr. Ochsner that allegedly targeted Castro using biological means. According to her, Oswald mentioned the assassination plot days before Kennedy’s death. She contends Oswald was a covert intelligence agent trying to prevent the killing, and that he could not have fired from the Texas School Book Depository. Baker also claims evidence suggests Kennedy was shot from the front and that conspirators acted against Oswald early on. She recalls her last phone call with Oswald, in which he said ‘I love you, Judyth’ before being shot by Jack Ruby. Kennedy’s assassination has sparked numerous conspiracy theories, including claims of multiple shooters and tampered evidence. The 50th anniversary of the event is approaching. Timeline of November 22, 1963 events: 12:29 p.m.: The presidential motorcade enters Dealey Plaza, Dallas. The limousine contains President Kennedy, Jacqueline Kennedy, Governor John Connally, and Nellie Connally. 12:30 p.m.: Witnesses hear three shots. Zapruder’s film captures Kennedy and Governor Connally being shot. Jacqueline Kennedy’s reaction follows. 12:33 p.m.: Oswald leaves the Texas School Book Depository. 12:38 p.m.: The First Lady and President arrive at Parkland Hospital. 1:00 p.m.: Kennedy is pronounced dead. November 24, 1963, 11:21 a.m.: Jack Ruby fatally shoots Oswald at Dallas Police headquarters during a live broadcast.

article_content: On Sunday, July 13, at the Maracana Stadium, years of planning and preparation culminated as Philipp Lahm lifted Germany’s fourth World Cup trophy. Germany excelled throughout the tournament under the adept leadership of coach Joachim Low. In Roy Hodgson’s first major interview since England’s early World Cup exit with just one point, he suggested that the national team is on a similar upward path. Speaking at Wembley, Hodgson stated on Sky Sports News HQ: 'I don’t believe in the talk about certain countries having a set identity in how they play. I don’t think there is a big difference between how we try to play and how Germany plays.' During a friendly at Wembley last November, Toni Kroos had 125 touches and assisted Per Mertesacker’s goal, whereas Wayne Rooney, in a similar role, had just 42. Until Hodgson or his successor admits Germany currently operate at an elite level, it will be difficult for England to close the gap. Hodgson admitted: 'There is a major difference between the German and English lineups at the moment. But in terms of how both sides approach attack and possession, I don’t see a great difference in style or philosophy. Sometimes, unpredictable moments in a game make all the difference.' England’s group-stage defeats to Italy and Uruguay saw them eliminated before many teams had played their second match. England ended the tournament with one point, alongside Japan, Iran, Ghana, and South Korea. Hodgson retained his role with support from FA chairman Greg Dyke. Reflecting on his position, Hodgson said: 'I’ll happily step down when my employers or the players no longer support me. That wasn’t the case this time.' He emphasized the need to look ahead to 2016 and avoid repeat disappointment. Steven Gerrard’s retirement from international football means England will need a new captain, with Wayne Rooney likely to take on the role. Hodgson stated, 'He found it difficult to leave England because he has always enjoyed representing the country.' article_content: Los Angeles, California (CNN) -- Comedian Betty White, currently experiencing a career resurgence at age 88, credited her enduring success in the entertainment industry to "sheer blind luck" during a recent interview. "I'm the luckiest old broad that ever drew a breath," White shared on CNN's "Larry King Live." Her renewed popularity follows her role in a hit Super Bowl commercial in January and several comedic sketches on Craig Ferguson's "Late, Late Show." Fans mounted a successful campaign on Facebook for her to host NBC's "Saturday Night Live," with her episode set to air May 8. White admitted to King that she feels nervous about hosting SNL, sometimes wondering, "What are they doing with me?" She noted she was approached to host SNL three times many years ago but declined, explaining that as a California native, she never felt suited for New York. White began her career in 1949 on a local television program. She went on to star in iconic sitcoms, including "The Mary Tyler Moore Show" and "The Golden Girls." "I think the reason for my longevity is that several generations have gotten to know me over the years—so I've become sort of part of the family," she said. Most recently, she appeared in the box-office hit "The Proposal" alongside Sandra Bullock and Ryan Reynolds. Continuing her streak, White joined the cast of a new TV Land sitcom, "Hot in Cleveland," with Jane Leeves, Wendie Malick, and Valerie Bertinelli. "I'm not hot again, but I'm surprised to still be working," White commented. "I just am amazed, I'm thrilled, and I'm enjoying every moment of it." White has also maintained her work in animal welfare, especially a 46-year partnership with the Los Angeles Zoo, which she considers one of her greatest loves alongside show business. "It's such fun," she remarked. "Why should you stop something you enjoy so much?"

article_content: A series of earthquakes in the Atlantic Ocean over the past week indicate heightened volcanic activity near El Hierro, the smallest island in the Canary Islands. The most significant earthquake, with a magnitude of 5.1, occurred off El Hierro’s coast, causing the island to swell by about three inches. Scientists suggest that an underwater volcanic eruption may be imminent, with the potential to force molten rock to the ocean’s surface, potentially creating a new island in the archipelago. El Hierro was the site of a 5.1-magnitude earthquake on Friday, signaling the possibility of an impending eruption from a nearby underwater volcano. If such an eruption occurs, it could result in new land formations. In 2011, seismic activity off El Hierro’s southern coast led to the appearance of magma and the evacuation of the nearby town, La Restinga. NASA imagery captured seismic activity in this region during that period. If another eruption occurs, all 10,000 residents of El Hierro could need to be evacuated from the 107-square-mile island. El Hierro originated from three volcanic eruptions about 100 million years ago and features a volcano over 6,000 feet high. According to Involcan, more than 550 earthquakes were recorded between Monday and Christmas Day, 30 of which registered magnitudes of 3.0 or higher. Most of these earthquakes and the observed swelling are centered near La Restinga on El Hierro’s south coast. The recent 5.1-magnitude quake is the strongest ever recorded in the region and had an epicenter approximately nine miles deep. El Hierro has more than 500 volcanic cones and endured over 10,000 tremors in the four months leading up to the 2011 eruption, which began with a 4.3-magnitude earthquake and caused magma to spew 60 feet into the air. Significant volcanic activity can create new land; for example, a volcanic eruption in the Pacific Ocean recently formed a new island near Nishinoshima, 620 miles south of Tokyo, in the seismically active 'Ring of Fire.' Continued eruptions recently caused the new island to merge with Nishinoshima. Geologically, the Canary Islands sit on the African Plate, with a magma chamber beneath capable of breaking through as tectonic shifts occur. Speculation exists about an additional, previously undetected fault line running through the archipelago. Volcanic activity, primarily at the convergence of three ridgelines, has caused El Hierro to gradually expand. The island’s last eruption was in 1793. About 50,000 years ago, large earthquakes triggered a substantial landslide that caused part of the island to break off and fall into the Atlantic, forming El Golfo valley and generating a tsunami estimated to have reached the American coast. There has been speculation—never confirmed—that La Palma, another tectonically active Canary Island, could experience a landslide causing a 'mega-tsunami' affecting areas across the Atlantic. This remains a theoretical scenario. By December 2011, volcanic activity at El Hierro had subsided, marked by a decrease in earthquake frequency. Activity increased again briefly in January 2012, but by March authorities declared the threat over. Following the recent earthquake swarm, El Hierro’s monitoring agency has raised the volcanic risk alert level to 'yellow.' Previous yellow alerts, such as one in June 2012, have not led to eruptions. The last eruption anywhere in the Canary Islands was on La Palma in 1971. Maps show the volcano’s location off El Hierro’s coast.
translated_content: Una serie di terremoti nell'Oceano Atlantico nell'ultima settimana indica un'intensa attività vulcanica vicino a El Hierro, la più piccola delle Isole Canarie. Il terremoto più significativo, di magnitudo 5,1, si è verificato al largo della costa di El Hierro, causando un rigonfiamento dell'isola di circa otto centimetri. Gli scienziati suggeriscono che un'eruzione vulcanica sottomarina potrebbe essere imminente, con la possibilità che il magma spinga nuove rocce sulla superficie dell'oceano e crei potenzialmente una nuova isola nell'arcipelago. El Hierro è stata colpita da un terremoto di magnitudo 5,1 venerdì, segnalando la possibilità di una prossima eruzione da un vulcano sottomarino vicino. Se ciò avvenisse, potrebbero formarsi nuove terre. Nel 2011, l'attività sismica al largo della costa meridionale di El Hierro portò all'emersione di magma e all'evacuazione della vicina città di La Restinga. Immagini della NASA hanno documentato l'attività sismica nella zona in quel periodo. Se si verificasse un'altra eruzione, tutti i 10.000 residenti di El Hierro potrebbero essere evacuati dall'isola, che si estende su 277 chilometri quadrati. El Hierro è nata da tre eruzioni vulcaniche circa 100 milioni di anni fa e presenta un vulcano alto oltre 1.800 metri. Secondo l'Involcan, tra lunedì e Natale sono stati registrati oltre 550 terremoti, di cui 30 di magnitudo 3,0 o superiore. La maggior parte di questi terremoti e il rigonfiamento dell'isola si concentra vicino a La Restinga, sulla costa sud di El Hierro. Il recente terremoto di magnitudo 5,1 è il più forte mai registrato nella regione e il suo epicentro era a circa quindici chilometri di profondità. El Hierro conta più di 500 coni vulcanici e ha subito oltre 10.000 scosse nei quattro mesi che hanno preceduto l'eruzione del 2011, iniziata con un terremoto di magnitudo 4,3 e caratterizzata da magma spruzzato fino a 18 metri in aria. Una forte attività vulcanica può creare nuove terre: ad esempio, una recente eruzione vulcanica nell'Oceano Pacifico ha formato una nuova isola vicino a Nishinoshima, circa 1.000 chilometri a sud di Tokyo, nella sismicamente attiva 'Cintura di Fuoco'. Ulteriori eruzioni recenti hanno poi fuso la nuova isola con Nishinoshima. Dal punto di vista geologico, le Isole Canarie si trovano sulla Placca Africana, con una camera magmatica al di sotto in grado di emergere in superficie a seguito di movimenti tettonici. Si ipotizza l'esistenza di una ulteriore faglia mai individuata che attraversa l'arcipelago. L'attività vulcanica, specialmente in corrispondenza della convergenza di tre dorsali, ha portato a una crescita graduale di El Hierro. L'ultima eruzione dell'isola risale al 1793. Circa 50.000 anni fa, forti terremoti causarono una vasta frana che fece staccare parte dell'isola facendola precipitare nell'Atlantico, formando la valle di El Golfo e generando uno tsunami stimato abbia raggiunto le coste americane. Esistono ipotesi—mai confermate—che La Palma, un'altra isola canaria molto attiva dal punto di vista tettonico, possa in futuro subire una frana capace di causare un 'mega-tsunami' che colpirebbe molte aree lungo l'Atlantico. Si tratta comunque di uno scenario teorico. A dicembre 2011, l'attività vulcanica a El Hierro diminuì, rilevata da una riduzione della frequenza dei terremoti. L'attività si intensificò nuovamente per poco a gennaio 2012, ma a marzo le autorità dichiararono terminato l'allarme. Dopo il recente sciame sismico, l'agenzia di monitoraggio di El Hierro ha innalzato il livello di allerta vulcanica a 'giallo'. Precedenti allerta gialle, come quella di giugno 2012, non hanno portato a eruzioni. L'ultima eruzione nelle Isole Canarie risale al 1971 a La Palma. Le mappe mostrano la posizione del vulcano al largo della costa di El Hierro.

Two small Chinese agate figurines, originally valued at just £200, have stunned the art world by selling for an astonishing £180,000. Each figurine, approximately two inches long, depicts boys at play—one with a dog and one with a drum—and is believed to date from the 19th century. They were consigned for sale by an unnamed English antiques dealer with a modest estimate of £200 to £300.

However, following the publication of the auction catalogue, Woolley and Wallis auction rooms in Salisbury, Wiltshire, were inundated with inquiries, particularly from the Far East. On auction day, the room was filled with mainly Chinese bidders, both in person and on the phones. As bidding rapidly soared from hundreds into the tens of thousands, competition narrowed to two determined phone bidders, pushing the hammer price to £150,000—and with fees, the total reached £180,000, 900 times the original estimate. The winning bidder remained anonymous and participated online from China.

Auctioneer John Axford expressed surprise at the high price, suggesting the pieces may be much older than initially assessed, noting the challenge in determining the age of such small carvings. London-based expert John Berwald speculated these rare agate carvings of boys could possibly date as far back as the 18th century, further contributing to their value. He added that intense competition between motivated collectors often leads to such inflated prices.

The sale exemplifies the current boom in demand for historic Chinese art, as affluent collectors in China seek to repatriate cultural treasures. A similar phenomenon was seen last year when a 900-year-old Song dynasty dish set a record by selling for £17 million at auction in Hong Kong after a fierce contest among eight bidders.

Sono state proposte in vendita da un anonimo antiquario inglese con una stima iniziale di £200–£300.

Tuttavia, dopo la pubblicazione del catalogo d’asta, la casa d’aste Woolley and Wallis di Salisbury (Wiltshire) è stata sommersa dalle richieste, soprattutto dall’Estremo Oriente. La vendita riflette la crescente domanda di arte cinese storica, con ricchi collezionisti cinesi desiderosi di riportare a casa pezzi del proprio patrimonio culturale. article_content: A Kwara State Chief Magistrates Court in Ilorin on Thursday granted bail to Abdulazeez Adegbola, also known as Tani Olohun, a traditional religion devotee, after he spent 91 days in the custody of the Federal Correctional Service. Tani Olohun was facing allegations of defamation across four different cases in three separate courts within the state. He had been detained since August 17, 2023, after being arraigned before Magistrate Mohammed Ibrahim on five counts, including criminal conspiracy, inciting public disturbance, disturbing public peace, defamation of character, and intentional insult. The prosecution stated these offenses were contrary to sections 97, 210, 392, and 114 of Nigeria’s penal code law. Additional charges of a similar nature were filed against him in the Kwara State Upper Area Court, presided over by Mr. Sunday Adeniyi. In two further cases, Sheikh Labeeb Lagbaji and Modirasatu Muhammed, represented by Professor Abubakar Aliagan, brought him before Magistrate Mohammed Adam, alleging defamation of Alhaji Labeeb Lagbaji and burning of the Holy Quran. Tani Olohun pleaded not guilty to all charges. He was previously admitted to administrative bail by the Upper Area Court and Chief Magistrate Court on September 20 and October 24, 2023, respectively. On Thursday, Magistrate Adam granted him bail in the sum of N2 million, requiring three sureties of equal sum in two separate cases. Two of the sureties must own landed property within the court’s jurisdiction or in Oyo State, where the defendant claims residency. During the proceedings, Tani Olohun addressed the court, appealing for forgiveness from Ilorin Islamic scholars and Muslims worldwide for his alleged actions, promising not to post negative videos on social media again. His counsel, Mr. Ademola Bank, emphasized his client’s remorse and requested bail on liberal terms. The counsel for the complainants, Taofeeq Olateju and Y.Y Ajibade, did not oppose the application. If the bail conditions are met, Tani Olohun will be released. Mr. Bank acknowledged the bail conditions were stringent but assured efforts would be made to fulfill them.

Tani Olohun era imputato in quattro diversi procedimenti per presunta diffamazione, in tre tribunali distinti dello Stato. Ulteriori accuse simili sono state presentate davanti al Tribunale Superiore dell’Area di Kwara, presieduto dal giudice Sunday Adeniyi. Bank ha riconosciuto la severità delle condizioni ma ha assicurato che proveranno a rispettarle.

article_content: As election season approaches, political activities are ramping up across India, even during the Gandhi Jayanti holiday. While most Indians commemorate Gandhi Jayanti, the day’s political calendar features numerous rallies, yatras, and project inaugurations. Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi, emphasizing his teachings of unity and compassion. On October 2, 2023, the Prime Minister is scheduled to visit Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh. In Rajasthan, Modi will inaugurate and launch development projects worth Rs 7,000 crore, while in Madhya Pradesh, projects totaling Rs 19,260 crore will be launched. In Chittorgarh, Rajasthan, Modi’s program starts at 10:45 am, where he will inaugurate the Rs 4,500-crore Mehsana-Bathinda-Gurdaspur gas pipeline, launch Hindustan Petroleum’s LPG plant in Abu Road, open a new four-lane National Highway 12 section built for Rs 1,480 crore, and inaugurate several railway and tourism projects, including the permanent campus of the Indian Institute of Information Technology in Kota. His visit follows the BJP Central Election Committee (CEC) meeting held in Delhi the previous night, led by Modi. The meeting aimed to finalize candidate lists for the Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh Assembly polls. Former Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje attended the meeting, though the party has not announced its Chief Ministerial candidate for Rajasthan. Days earlier, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and BJP President J P Nadda held meetings with the party’s Rajasthan core group to discuss ticket allotments amid internal disputes. Modi is scheduled to arrive in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, at 3:30 pm to inaugurate projects such as the Rs 11,895-crore Delhi-Vadodara Expressway and lay foundation stones for five road projects worth over Rs 1,880 crore. He will also participate in the housewarming ceremony for 2.2 lakh rural homes built under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, dedicate PMAY Urban homes worth about Rs 140 crore, and lay foundation stones for Jal Jeevan Mission projects in Gwalior and Sheopur, nine Ayushman Bharat health centers, and 50 critical care units in nine cities. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is visiting Amritsar’s Golden Temple on a personal visit amidst growing tension between Congress and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) over the arrest of Congress MLA Sukhpal Khaira in a narcotics case. Gandhi intends to participate in volunteer service at the temple, reportedly planning to help in the kitchen or the langar. He has no political events scheduled. In Chhattisgarh, Congress is organizing day-long 'Bharosa Yatras' in each of the 90 Assembly constituencies to promote Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel’s welfare schemes. Cabinet ministers, MPs, and MLAs will participate, with each march covering 25-30 km and holding public meetings. In Mumbai, the INDIA bloc is observing Gandhi Jayanti with a 'Main Bhi Gandhi' march protesting BJP’s 'divisive politics', starting at 2 pm at Metro Cinema. Trinamool Congress (TMC) is maintaining its protest against the central government regarding delays in MGNREGS rural job scheme funding. TMC MPs and ministers will hold a sit-in at Raj Ghat at 1 pm, followed by a march to Parliament with MGNREGS cardholders to highlight the withholding of state dues. Senior leaders are expected to decide on further plans and address the media. In Haryana, two major political events are planned: former Union Minister Birender Singh will lead a rally in Jind under the 'Birender Singh ke Saathi' banner, aiming to build new social alliances without official BJP symbols. The murder trial of Lian Bin 'Robert' Xie has been suspended after new evidence was submitted. Justice Peter Johnson informed the Supreme Court jury—who had spent several weeks listening to witness statements—that they were being dismissed. The judge noted that the fresh material, which was shared with both the prosecution and defense earlier this month, is substantial enough to potentially change the outcome of the case. He stated that the evidence could significantly reshape the trial’s proceedings.

Xie is accused of murdering his brother-in-law Min Lin, Min’s wife Lily, their two sons Henry (12) and Terry (9), and Lily’s sister Irene on July 18, 2009, in North Epping, near Sydney. Xie maintains his innocence, having pleaded not guilty to all charges. The court has detailed that a new trial date will be scheduled.

article_content: The UK government has unveiled new welfare reforms requiring many unemployed foreign nationals to reach a specific level of English proficiency in order to keep receiving their benefits. Chancellor George Osborne announced a £350 million support package aimed at improving employability, with mandatory English classes for those whose language skills are below the standard of a typical nine-year-old. Individuals who decline to attend these courses risk losing their benefits. Roughly 100,000 jobseekers will be included in the initiative, with about one-third of the funding dedicated to helping claimants achieve Entry Level Two language certification. Osborne described the move as 'reasonable' and highlighted the importance of English for securing employment. Further changes include extending the initial waiting period for Jobseeker's Allowance from three days to seven, requiring claimants to attend jobcentres weekly instead of biweekly, and annual verification of benefit claims. There is also increased emphasis on active job searching, with claimants participating in regular progress reviews and receiving more training in resume writing and interview techniques. These initiatives are part of a broader strategy to reduce public spending by £11.5 billion for 2015-16, redirecting welfare savings towards programs to help the unemployed find work. The policy also stipulates that single parents must begin preparing for employment when their youngest child turns three, though only those with children aged five or older will be penalized for refusing job offers. Political figures have also drawn attention, such as Conservative MP Andrew Selous, who publicly supported the English language requirement but became the subject of online humor after a typo in his tweet. Osborne defended the reforms, stating, 'The first days after losing a job should be spent seeking employment, not navigating benefit claims.' He maintained that these changes will help individuals return to work more rapidly.

Il Cancelliere George Osborne ha presentato un pacchetto di sostegno da 350 milioni di sterline volto a migliorare l’occupabilità, con corsi di inglese obbligatori per chi ha competenze linguistiche inferiori a quelle tipiche di un bambino di nove anni. Chi si rifiuta di frequentare questi corsi rischia la sospensione dei sussidi. Circa 100.000 persone in cerca di lavoro saranno coinvolte nell’iniziativa, con quasi un terzo dei fondi destinato ad aiutare i beneficiari a raggiungere il livello linguistico Entry Level Two. Osborne ha definito la misura 'ragionevole', sottolineando l’importanza dell’inglese per trovare impiego. Altre novità includono l’estensione del periodo di attesa per il Jobseeker’s Allowance da tre a sette giorni, l’obbligo di recarsi settimanalmente ai centri per l’impiego invece che ogni due settimane e la verifica annuale delle richieste di sussidio. Si presta inoltre maggiore attenzione alla ricerca attiva di lavoro, con revisioni periodiche dei progressi e più formazione su come scrivere un curriculum e affrontare i colloqui. Le iniziative fanno parte di una strategia più ampia per ridurre la spesa pubblica di 11,5 miliardi di sterline per il 2015-16, reinvestendo i risparmi del welfare in programmi per aiutare i disoccupati a trovare lavoro. La normativa prevede anche che i genitori single inizino a prepararsi al lavoro quando il figlio più piccolo compie tre anni, ma solo chi ha figli di almeno cinque anni sarà sanzionato se rifiuta offerte di impiego. Alcune figure politiche hanno attirato attenzione, come il deputato conservatore Andrew Selous, che ha dichiarato pubblicamente il proprio sostegno al requisito linguistico, diventando poi oggetto di ironia online a causa di un errore di battitura in un tweet. Osborne ha difeso le riforme affermando: 'I primi giorni dopo aver perso il lavoro dovrebbero essere dedicati a cercare un’occupazione, non a gestire la richiesta dei sussidi.' Ritiene che queste misure aiuteranno le persone a tornare al lavoro più rapidamente.

article_content: Cristiano Ronaldo, World Player of the Year, is displaying replicas of the FA Cup and Premier League trophies he won with Manchester United at his CR7 Museum in Funchal, his hometown. The museum showcases both his individual awards and copies of trophies from his club successes, including Premier League titles from 2007, 2008, and 2009, the FA Cup from 2004, the Champions League from 2008, and the FIFA Club World Cup from 2008. Official FA and Premier League permissions are required for these replicas, but Ronaldo’s representatives have not started the application process. However, neither the FA nor the Premier League plans to pursue action against him. England manager Roy Hodgson has encouraged young players to dream of winning Euro 2020 at Wembley, as UEFA has named the stadium for both semi-finals and the final of the tournament, which will be held across 13 cities. Hodgson highlighted this as a great opportunity for emerging talent. Competition for the ECB chairmanship is intensifying following Yorkshire's strong support for captain Andrew Gale, who faces ECB charges for racist and abusive language directed at Lancashire batsman Ashwell Prince. Yorkshire’s backing is seen as a signal of potential leadership change from Giles Clarke to Colin Graves, who is supported by many counties. The Football Association could face legal action after removing Edward Lord from its Inclusion Advisory Board because he criticized the FA’s response to discrimination. Lord considers the FA’s explanation for his removal defamatory, raising broader concerns about the FA’s handling of diversity. There are ongoing concerns about the lack of diversity on UEFA’s 17-member executive committee, as all current members are white. After FA chairman Greg Dyke returned a £16,400 Parmigiani watch gifted by the Brazilian federation, it was noted that Parmigiani was heavily advertised at the UEFA Euro 2020 venue announcement. Dyke wore a lower-priced watch, while other FA officials, such as Alex Horne and Roy Hodgson, wore expensive timepieces. UEFA chief Michel Platini stated he does not return gifts but will donate the value to charity. BT Sport is working to remove its company logo from Oscar Pistorius’s Twitter profile after his conviction, clarifying that his ambassador contract ended last year. They are contacting his representatives to make the change before his sentencing. The Footballer of the Year awards night is moving from the London Lancaster hotel to The Landmark after last year’s double-booking incident forced organizers to use a different space.

article_content: It was revealed that two senior Labour figures, Lord Mandelson and Alastair Campbell, approached Alan Johnson last autumn to ask whether he would consider replacing Ed Miliband as Labour leader, according to the Financial Times. Both Mandelson and Campbell have denied actively encouraging Johnson to stand, stating that they only sought to clarify ongoing rumors. Amid increasing speculation about Miliband's leadership following a poorly received party conference speech, reports claimed Mandelson and Campbell discussed with Johnson the possibility of him taking over as a way to prevent a second election defeat. Johnson, however, firmly rejected the idea, repeating his refusal both in private and in public. Despite this, suggestions of desperation within Labour grew as Miliband continued to face criticism. Alan Johnson served in the Cabinet for six years and was considered a reliable and popular figure among colleagues, the media, and the public. He was appointed shadow chancellor by Miliband but resigned after three months due to personal reasons, specifically following news of his wife's affair. Some within the party continued to see Johnson as a potential caretaker leader if Miliband's low poll ratings risked Labour's election chances. Miliband's leadership came under further pressure as several prominent business leaders publicly criticised Labour’s economic policies, expressing concerns about the party’s direction. Business figures such as Stuart Rose, Lord Digby Jones, Simon Woodroffe, Luke Johnson, Brent Hoberman, Charlie Mullins, and Boots chief Stefano Pessina voiced fears that Labour under Miliband could damage the UK economy. David Miliband, Ed’s brother and once seen as closer to New Labour supporters, left Parliament after losing to Ed in the leadership contest. Reports suggested that at least 40 Labour MPs supported exploring a leadership change, though numbers were disputed. Recent tensions between Ed Miliband and New Labour figures have been fueled by the party's strained relationship with business—once seen as a cornerstone under Tony Blair. Lord Mandelson insisted that he simply asked Johnson about press rumors and did not encourage a challenge. The Labour Party formally rejected the leadership plot narrative, calling the story 'false and misleading.' On the other hand, Conservative MP Nadhim Zahawi cited the reported leadership discussions as evidence of instability within Labour, stating it showed a lack of confidence in Miliband. The Conservative Party used Labour’s difficulties as an opportunity to present a business-friendly agenda. Business Minister Matthew Hancock announced plans to cut red tape, reduce employment tribunal claims, and offer tax breaks, positioning the Conservatives as committed to supporting enterprise. Lord Levy, former chief fundraiser for Tony Blair, expressed disappointment over the business community's criticism but maintained optimism about Labour's relationship with business under Miliband. He emphasized that productive collaboration with business is essential for any political party.

Sia Mandelson che Campbell hanno negato di aver incoraggiato attivamente Johnson a candidarsi, affermando di essersi limitati a chiarire le voci circolanti. Tra le crescenti speculazioni sulla leadership di Miliband, seguite a un discorso poco apprezzato alla conferenza del partito, è stato riferito che Mandelson e Campbell abbiano discusso con Johnson la possibilità che prendesse le redini del partito per evitare una seconda sconfitta elettorale. Johnson, tuttavia, ha respinto categoricamente l’ipotesi, ribadendo il suo rifiuto sia in privato che in pubblico. Nonostante ciò, sono cresciuti i segnali di disagio nel Labour mentre Miliband continuava a ricevere critiche. Alan Johnson ha fatto parte del governo ombra per sei anni ed era considerato una figura affidabile e popolare tra colleghi, media e pubblico. Fu nominato responsabile delle Finanze ombra da Miliband, ma si dimise dopo tre mesi per motivi personali, a seguito di notizie riguardanti la relazione extraconiugale della moglie. Alcuni membri del partito vedevano ancora Johnson come possibile leader ad interim se i bassi sondaggi di Miliband avessero messo a rischio le possibilità elettorali del Labour. La leadership di Miliband è stata ulteriormente messa sotto pressione quando diversi noti esponenti del mondo imprenditoriale hanno criticato pubblicamente le politiche economiche del Labour, esprimendo preoccupazione per la direzione intrapresa dal partito. Figure come Stuart Rose, Lord Digby Jones, Simon Woodroffe, Luke Johnson, Brent Hoberman, Charlie Mullins e Stefano Pessina (Boots) hanno espresso il timore che il Labour guidato da Miliband potesse nuocere all’economia del Regno Unito. David Miliband, fratello di Ed e considerato vicino ai sostenitori del New Labour, ha lasciato il Parlamento dopo aver perso la corsa alla leadership contro il fratello. Secondo alcune fonti, almeno 40 deputati laburisti avrebbero sostenuto l’ipotesi di un cambio di leadership, anche se il numero è oggetto di discussioni. Le recenti tensioni tra Ed Miliband e le figure di spicco del New Labour sono state alimentate dai rapporti tesi con il mondo delle imprese, storicamente considerato essenziale sotto la guida di Tony Blair. Lord Mandelson ha insistito di aver domandato a Johnson solo delle voci di stampa, senza incoraggiarlo a lanciarsi nella sfida. Il Partito Laburista ha ufficialmente smentito il presunto complotto, definendo la storia 'falsa e fuorviante.' Al contrario, il deputato conservatore Nadhim Zahawi ha colto le notizie sui colloqui sulla leadership come prova di instabilità all’interno del Labour, affermando che ciò dimostra una mancanza di fiducia in Miliband. Il Partito Conservatore ha sfruttato le difficoltà del Labour per promuovere un’agenda a favore delle imprese. Il Ministro delle Imprese Matthew Hancock ha annunciato piani per ridurre la burocrazia, diminuire il contenzioso del lavoro e offrire sgravi fiscali, posizionando i Conservatori come sostenitori dell’impresa. Lord Levy, ex responsabile della raccolta fondi di Tony Blair, ha espresso delusione per le critiche del mondo imprenditoriale ma ha mantenuto fiducia nella possibilità di un rapporto costruttivo tra Labour e imprese sotto Miliband. Ha sottolineato che ogni partito politico deve collaborare in modo produttivo con le aziende.

At least seven people are presumed dead after being swept away by floodwaters while crossing the Muooni River in Makueni County, southeastern Kenya. The incident took place on Thursday evening following intense rainfall, according to local chief Norman Musyoki. Eyewitnesses say the group was stranded on a log in the river before a sudden surge carried them away, as onlookers could do nothing but watch.

The victims were returning home from Nairobi, where they had attended a meeting with First Lady Rachel Ruto. Makueni County is among the areas worst affected by flooding, which has impacted wide regions of Kenya, Somalia, and Ethiopia. Rescue operations led by local officials and the Kenya Red Cross are ongoing, with the exact number of missing individuals still being confirmed, though at least seven are reported to be missing.

The floods, intensified by the El Niño climate phenomenon, have caused widespread devastation—resulting in over 71 deaths and displacing more than 150,000 people across Kenya, according to the Kenya Red Cross. Humanitarian group Oxfam estimates the total death toll in Kenya, Ethiopia, and Somalia to be over 130.

Experts attribute the increasing frequency of extreme rainfall to climate change, which makes such disasters more likely. Despite the crisis, Kenya’s Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has stated that the national government will not provide financial support for flood response.

L’incidente è avvenuto giovedì sera a causa di forti piogge, secondo quanto riferito dal capo locale Norman Musyoki. I testimoni raccontano che il gruppo era bloccato su un tronco nel fiume prima che una piena improvvisa li trascinasse via, mentre gli spettatori guardavano impotenti.

Le vittime stavano tornando a casa da Nairobi, dove avevano partecipato a un incontro con la First Lady Rachel Ruto. La contea di Makueni è tra le zone più colpite dalle inondazioni che hanno devastato ampie parti di Kenya, Somalia ed Etiopia. Le operazioni di soccorso guidate dalle autorità locali e dalla Croce Rossa del Kenya sono ancora in corso e il numero esatto dei dispersi deve ancora essere confermato, anche se almeno sette persone risultano scomparse.

Le inondazioni, aggravate dal fenomeno climatico El Niño, hanno provocato danni estesi: secondo la Croce Rossa del Kenya, oltre 71 persone sono morte e più di 150.000 sono state sfollate in tutto il Paese. L’organizzazione umanitaria Oxfam stima che il bilancio complessivo delle vittime tra Kenya, Etiopia e Somalia superi i 130 morti.

Gli esperti ritengono che i cambiamenti climatici stiano aumentando la frequenza di eventi meteorologici estremi come questo. Nonostante la situazione critica, il vicepresidente del Kenya Rigathi Gachagua ha dichiarato che il governo nazionale non fornirà sostegno economico per gli interventi contro le inondazioni.

article_content: Tata Technologies is preparing to launch its eagerly awaited initial public offering (IPO), accepting public subscriptions from November 22 to 24. The entire IPO is an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders, principally Tata Motors, Alpha TC Holdings, and Tata Capital Growth Fund. Tata Motors will offload 4.62 crore shares, Alpha TC Holdings will sell 97.1 lakh shares, and Tata Capital Growth Fund will divest 48 lakh shares. The offering's total size has been revised from an initial 9.57 crore shares down to 6.08 crore. Ten percent of the shares have been reserved for eligible Tata Motors shareholders.
