article_content: In the cloakroom of the Bristol Hawks gymnastics club, ten pairs of tiny shoes are neatly lined up. They belong to toddlers taking their first steps into a world of tumbling and soaring leaps in the gymnasium below. Not long ago, Claudia Fragapane was among them. Still just 17, she now trains alone on the top floor of a large warehouse-style building in Easton, an inner-city area of Bristol. From the windows, she can see the rooftops of neighboring terraced houses as she bounces across the sprung floor, closely watched by her coaches, Helen Potter and Rory Weaver. Gymnastics still holds the same magic for Fragapane as it did when she first left her shoes at the door more than a decade ago, but now it is a serious pursuit as well. Claudia Fragapane received the SJA Committee Award at the SJA Sports Awards in December 2014, following her performances earlier that year at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. At just 4ft 6in, she is seen as a powerhouse and has been tipped to become Britain's greatest gymnast. This summer, she became the first Englishwoman in 84 years to win four gold medals at the Commonwealth Games, and at the World Gymnastics Championships in China in October, she made four individual finals. 'I've been amazed by it all,' says Fragapane, her words spilling out as quickly as she spins through the air. 'If someone had asked me before, I’d have said, “No way will I do all that.” It’s not so much the feeling of winning I love, but the feeling of doing something to the best of my ability.' In Glasgow, she won gold medals in vault, floor, all-around, and team events. Her achievements have brought a whirlwind of award nominations, and she is considered a favorite to follow in the footsteps of Tom Daley and Wayne Rooney by winning the BBC's Young Sports Personality of the Year. She is shortlisted alongside para-cyclist Sophie Thornhill and golfer Bradley Neil. 'The awards are a nice chance to dress up,' says Fragapane. 'In training, I don’t make an effort at all—I just throw my hair up. We’ve got a rule that we can be as scruffy as we want and nobody will mind.' The focus at her gym is already on the 2016 Rio Olympics. Taking a break between sessions, Fragapane leans against the gym wall as she eats lunch, having spent the morning working on a new, more challenging vault. By Rio, her coaches hope to challenge North Korea’s Hong Un Jong, currently the world’s best in that discipline. Though talk of Olympic medals is kept low-key, Potter—herself a former Great Britain gymnast—says Fragapane has the potential to win four medals in Brazil, where she will still be just 18. 'At the World Championships in Nanning, you could sense countries like Russia were watching us,' says Potter. 'They have seen what we’ve achieved at the Commonwealths and in Europe and now know we’re a legitimate threat.' Fragapane's power, visible in her muscular thighs and shoulders, is more apparent in person. Gone are the days when only athletes with ballerina-like builds, such as Olga Korbut or Nadia Comaneci, could succeed. The reigning world all-around champion, Simone Biles of the United States, is 4ft 7in and compact, much like Shawn Johnson, the 2008 Olympic champion. 'Gymnastics is one of the few sports where being small can be an advantage,' says Potter. 'Claudia excels at multiple somersaults. She might have been a good diver, or suited for Cirque du Soleil.' At 5ft 1in, her father Paolo is the tallest in the Fragapane family, so Claudia is unlikely to grow much taller, a fact she somewhat laments. 'I’d like to grow so people don’t look at me and wonder how old I am, because I have an older-looking face,' says Fragapane. Paolo, who came to England as a schoolboy, and Claudia’s mother Teresa met in Bristol, later discovering both came from Sicilian villages only 40 minutes apart. Now parents to five daughters with Claudia in the middle, Paolo is proud of his family. 'I love my women,' he says, his accent a unique mix of Italian and Bristolian. 'They are all positive people, and Claudia has always been a performer. She’s not a show-off, but we’re not quiet people.' After Claudia's Commonwealth Games triumph, Paolo threw a party at Noah's Ark play centre in Brislington, which he owns with daughter Lorenza, 26. 'We got all the families together, about 300 people. We Italians like big gatherings—I can name relatives up to my third cousin. Back in my home village of Santa Elisabetta, the consulate spread the news about Claudia’s achievements.' While generally easygoing, Paolo insists Claudia should wait before having a boyfriend. 'I don’t get close to the boyfriends. I’d like them to get married or at least be serious before it happens. Claudia’s not having a boyfriend until she’s 35. She says 18, but I say it has to be a prince—a good bloke. But she doesn’t need to know that yet.' Having finished school in the summer, Fragapane trains 35 hours a week in the gym. Her coaches, Potter and Weaver, spend twice as long, including searching for floor music, creating routines, and monitoring competitors. Her floor routine at the World Championships in Nanning included break-dance style moves mixed with traditional, precisely executed tumbles and twists. 'We didn’t plan it as break-dancing,' says Weaver. 'It actually started because she was resting her feet, but it fit the music. Claudia has this cheeky grin she shares with the judges—her sister Chiara is just the same.' Fragapane also coaches a group of young gymnasts twice a week, including her eight-year-old sister Chiara. 'She treats me like a coach,' says Claudia. 'I like that I can relate to them because I’m still competing myself. If they’re tired, I understand and can advise them.' Fragapane is still learning too. At the World Championships, she slipped during her opening tumble but quickly recovered and finished her routine confidently. 'I was trying too hard,' she admits. 'I was tired and my legs were like jelly. I tried to stay positive. As soon as I fell I was disappointed, but I smiled at the judges and tried to give them a good performance. Overall, the competition was impressive considering I was only 16.'
translated_content: Nel guardaroba del Bristol Hawks gymnastics club, dieci paia di minuscole scarpe sono allineate ordinatamente. Appartengono a bambini che stanno muovendo i primi passi in un mondo fatto di capriole e salti nella palestra al piano terra. Non molto tempo fa, anche Claudia Fragapane era tra loro. Ora, a soli 17 anni, si allena da sola all’ultimo piano di un grande edificio in stile magazzino a Easton, una zona interna di Bristol. Dalle finestre vede i tetti delle case a schiera vicine mentre salta sulla pedana molleggiata sotto lo sguardo attento dei suoi allenatori, Helen Potter e Rory Weaver. La ginnastica continua ad avere per Fragapane lo stesso fascino di quando, più di dieci anni fa, ha lasciato le sue scarpe all’ingresso, ma ora è anche un impegno serio. Claudia Fragapane ha ricevuto il SJA Committee Award agli SJA Sports Awards nel dicembre 2014, dopo le sue straordinarie prestazioni di quell’anno ai Giochi del Commonwealth di Glasgow. Alta solo 1,37 m, è considerata una vera forza della natura e viene vista come una possibile futura migliore ginnasta britannica. Quest’estate è diventata la prima donna inglese in 84 anni a vincere quattro medaglie d’oro ai Giochi del Commonwealth, e ai Mondiali di Ginnastica in Cina, a ottobre, ha raggiunto quattro finali individuali. ‘Sono rimasta stupita da tutto questo,’ dice Fragapane, con le parole che escono veloci quanto i suoi giri in aria. ‘Se me lo avessero chiesto prima, avrei detto “non ce la farò mai a fare tutto questo”. Non è tanto la gioia della vittoria che amo, ma quella di riuscire a dare il massimo.’ A Glasgow ha vinto l’oro al volteggio, al corpo libero, nel concorso individuale e nella gara a squadre. I suoi successi le sono valsi una serie di candidature a premi, ed è considerata una delle favorite per vincere il BBC Young Sports Personality of the Year, seguendo le orme di Tom Daley e Wayne Rooney. È in gara insieme alla para-ciclista Sophie Thornhill e al golfista Bradley Neil. ‘I premi sono una bella occasione per vestirsi elegante,’ dice Fragapane. ‘In allenamento non bado all’aspetto—lego solo i capelli e via. Abbiamo una regola: possiamo essere sciatte finché vogliamo, e a nessuno importa.’ L’obiettivo in palestra è già rivolto alle Olimpiadi di Rio 2016. Durante una pausa tra una sessione e l’altra, Fragapane si appoggia al muro della palestra per mangiare il pranzo, dopo una mattinata passata a lavorare su un nuovo volteggio ancora più difficile. Arrivati a Rio, i suoi allenatori sperano di sfidare la nordcoreana Hong Un Jong, attualmente la migliore al mondo su quell’attrezzo. Anche se si parla poco di medaglie olimpiche, Potter—lei stessa ex ginnasta inglese—dice che Fragapane ha il potenziale per vincere quattro medaglie in Brasile, quando avrà ancora solo 18 anni. ‘Ai Mondiali di Nanning, si percepiva che paesi come la Russia ci osservavano,’ dice Potter. ‘Dopo ciò che abbiamo fatto ai Commonwealth e in Europa, ora sanno che rappresentiamo una vera minaccia.’ La potenza di Fragapane, visibile nelle sue cosce e spalle muscolose, appare ancora più evidente dal vivo. Sono finiti i tempi in cui potevano affermarsi solo atlete dal fisico da ballerina, come Olga Korbut o Nadia Comaneci. L’attuale campionessa mondiale all-around, Simone Biles degli Stati Uniti, misura 1,40 m ed è di corporatura compatta, proprio come Shawn Johnson, oro olimpico 2008. ‘La ginnastica è uno dei pochi sport dove essere piccoli può essere un vantaggio,’ spiega Potter. ‘Claudia eccelle nelle evoluzioni multiple. Probabilmente sarebbe stata anche una brava tuffatrice o una protagonista del Cirque du Soleil.’ Il padre Paolo, che con i suoi 1,55 m è il più alto della famiglia Fragapane, sa che Claudia con ogni probabilità non crescerà molto, cosa che lei vive con un po’ di dispiacere. ‘Vorrei crescere ancora, anche solo per evitare che la gente mi chieda quanti anni ho, perché ho un viso più grande dell’età,’ racconta Claudia. Paolo, arrivato in Inghilterra da ragazzo, ha incontrato Teresa, madre di Claudia, a Bristol. Solo dopo hanno scoperto di provenire da paesi siciliani distanti appena 40 minuti. Oggi sono genitori di cinque figlie, Claudia è la terza. Paolo è orgoglioso della sua famiglia: ‘Adoro le mie donne,’ racconta, con un accento che mescola italiano e dialetto di Bristol. ‘Sono tutte persone positive e Claudia è sempre stata una performer. Non è una vanitosa, ma non siamo una famiglia silenziosa.’ Dopo il successo di Claudia ai Commonwealth, Paolo ha organizzato una festa al Noah’s Ark play centre a Brislington, di cui è proprietario insieme alla figlia Lorenza, di 26 anni. ‘Abbiamo riunito tutte le famiglie, circa 300 persone. Noi italiani amiamo le grandi riunioni—so elencare i parenti fino al terzo cugino. Nel mio paese, Santa Elisabetta, il consolato ha addirittura fatto sapere a tutti dei risultati di Claudia.’ Paolo, di indole generalmente tranquilla, su una cosa però è inflessibile: niente fidanzati per Claudia. ‘Non voglio avvicinarmi ai fidanzati. Prima è meglio che si sposino, o almeno che siano davvero seri. Claudia non avrà un fidanzato prima dei 35. Lei dice 18, ma per me dev’essere un principe—una brava persona. Ma per ora, meglio che lei non lo sappia.’ Terminata la scuola questa estate, Fragapane si allena 35 ore a settimana in palestra. I suoi allenatori, Potter e Weaver, lavorano il doppio, anche cercando musiche per i programmi a corpo libero, creando esercizi e monitorando la concorrenza. La sua routine a corpo libero ai Mondiali di Nanning includeva elementi di breakdance, alternati a movimenti tradizionali eseguiti con la massima precisione. ‘Non lo avevamo pensato come breakdance,’ ricorda Weaver. ‘In realtà è nato perché si stava riposando i piedi, ma si incastrava bene nella musica. Claudia ha quel sorriso furbetto che lancia ai giudici—proprio come sua sorella Chiara.’ Fragapane allena due volte a settimana un gruppo di giovani ginnaste, tra cui la sorellina Chiara, di otto anni. ‘Mi tratta come un’allenatrice,’ dice Claudia. ‘Mi fa piacere potermi relazionare alle bambine perché anche io sono ancora in gara. Se sono stanche, lo capisco e posso consigliarle.’ Ma anche Fragapane sta ancora imparando. Ai Mondiali, ha sbagliato il primo elemento della sua routine ma si è rapidamente rialzata, finendo l’esercizio con sicurezza. ‘Stavo cercando di fare troppo,’ ammette. ‘Ero stanca, le gambe erano molli. Ho provato a restare positiva. Appena sono caduta ero delusa, ma ho sorriso ai giudici e ho cercato di divertirli. Tutto sommato, visto che avevo solo 16 anni, il risultato è stato davvero notevole.’

article_content: Two teenagers are being sought by police after a 15-year-old boy was shot in the leg during a drive-by shooting in Liverpool's busy Chinatown district. The boy remains in stable condition in hospital following the incident, which happened around 9:30pm on Friday. According to detectives, shots were fired from a scrambler motorbike ridden by two teenage boys. Police say the suspects, both believed to be about 14 or 15 years old and wearing dark clothing, stopped in Great George Square, produced a firearm, and fired at a group before fleeing the scene toward Hardy Street. Merseyside officers found the 15-year-old shot in his right leg. His injuries are not thought to be life-threatening. Police are reviewing CCTV footage and have sealed off the crime scene while searching for evidence. The rider was described as slim, and the passenger as stocky. Detective Inspector Rob Hill said the victim is being interviewed and that detectives are trying to locate others who were present, as well as the suspects. Police are appealing for information, especially from anyone who may have seen a silver car in the area at the time. Officers are conducting house-to-house inquiries in connection with the case.

Secondo i detective, i colpi sono stati sparati da una moto da cross guidata da due adolescenti. La polizia afferma che i sospetti, entrambi di circa 14 o 15 anni e vestiti con abiti scuri, si sono fermati in Great George Square, hanno estratto un’arma da fuoco e sparato contro un gruppo prima di fuggire verso Hardy Street. Gli agenti di Merseyside hanno trovato il quindicenne colpito alla gamba destra. Le sue ferite non sono considerate potenzialmente letali. Bayern Munich delivered an emphatic 7-1 win over Roma during their Champions League match at Rome’s Stadio Olimpico, but coach Pep Guardiola emphasized that the team still had areas to improve, despite their record-setting victory.

The morning after their triumph, Bayern’s players enjoyed a private audience with Pope Francis, who praised their performance and expressed surprise at the scale of their win. Guardiola, however, cautioned that such results are outliers and insisted that the wide scoreline didn’t truly represent the difference between the two teams. He anticipated that the return fixture would be more challenging.

Goals from Arjen Robben, Mario Gotze, Robert Lewandowski, and an additional strike from Robben put Bayern ahead early, with Thomas Muller converting a penalty. Late goals from Franck Ribery and Xherdan Shaqiri ensured Bayern’s position at the top of Group E with full points. Roma's only goal came from Gervinho.

Speaking to Sky Sports Italia, Guardiola admitted satisfaction with the win but pointed out that Roma threatened in certain moments, especially after the break. He described the win as an exception rather than the norm and recognized Roma’s quality.

Roma manager Rudi Garcia accepted blame for the defeat, acknowledging missteps in his tactical approach. Having experienced a similar heavy loss to Bayern with Lille, Garcia stated that Roma needs growth in aggression and unity to reach the top level in Europe, and remained hopeful for group qualification, given improvement.

Midfielder Daniele De Rossi described the loss as a painful but instructive experience, saying the result did not fully capture the competitive gap between the teams. Goalkeeper Morgan De Sanctis noted the unwavering support of Roma fans, calling the defeat unjustifiable and assuming collective responsibility.

Bayern’s comprehensive performance has made them favorites among bookmakers for the Champions League title, while Roma will focus on bouncing back in their remaining group stage matches.

Gladys, a baby gorilla born at the Gladys Porter Zoo in Texas on January 29, was relocated to the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden after her mother showed little interest in caring for her. At just two months old, Gladys is thriving under the attentive care of a team of ten human surrogates, all trained to imitate the nurturing behaviors of gorilla mothers. The caregivers use creative methods like wearing furry black clothing, making gorilla sounds, and even crawling on all fours to help Gladys learn essential species-specific skills. According to the zoo's primate team leader, Ron Evans, Gladys recently started supporting herself on all fours and is progressing rapidly, eating soft foods like carrots and sweet potatoes along with her bottle feedings.

Ashley O’Connell, another primate specialist who recently became a mother herself, has grown particularly close to Gladys, often carrying her on her back to model natural gorilla behavior. Human caretakers are introducing Gladys to other gorillas, gently encouraging interaction to prepare her eventual integration into a gorilla family. The Cincinnati Zoo, known for its expertise with gorilla infants, is carefully considering four potential adoptive gorilla mothers, aiming for Gladys to join a real gorilla family in a few months. Caregivers describe their work as both a privilege and a serious responsibility, with the ultimate hope that Gladys will successfully bond with an adoptive gorilla mother. Their efforts are especially significant given the critically endangered status of Western Lowland Gorillas.

article_content: According to the U.S. Census Bureau’s 2006 American Community Survey, about 80 percent of Americans — or 223.2 million people — speak only English at home. The other 20 percent — roughly 55.8 million individuals — use a language other than English at home. Adding millions of tourists who visit the United States each year, there is significant demand for workers proficient in more than one language. Bilingual employees are increasingly valuable across a wide array of industries. In nearly every workplace where customer interaction is required — whether in person, over the phone, or online — being able to communicate in another language is a strong asset. Each additional customer served improves both their experience and the employer’s bottom line. States with the highest percentages of residents speaking a language other than English at home include California, New Mexico, Texas, New York, and Arizona. Spanish is the predominant non-English language, with about 34 million speakers nationwide. Many also speak languages such as French, German, Mandarin, Arabic, and others. Bilingual professionals are essential in serving these communities. If you are bilingual or considering learning a second language, numerous industries highly value these skills:  Health Care: Hospitals and clinics treat patients from varied backgrounds. As the U.S. attracts people from all over the world for medical care, healthcare professionals may encounter many languages. Roles: Registered nurse, paramedic, physician's assistant, home health aide.  Hospitality: Hotels, resorts, and spas strive to make guests feel welcome and comfortable. Bilingual staff enhance the visitor experience. Roles: Concierge, resort manager, hotel manager, desk clerk.  Education: American classrooms, from kindergarten through higher education, are increasingly diverse. Educators often work with students from multilingual backgrounds or international programs. Roles: Teacher, ESL instructor, guidance counselor.  Law Enforcement: Officers frequently interview individuals while resolving conflicts or investigating incidents. Bilingual skills can save time and improve outcomes. Roles: Police officer, investigator, security guard, probation officer, corrections officer.  Customer Service: Many businesses serve customers from households where English may not be spoken, as well as tourists. Multilingual employees can assist a broader clientele. Roles: Sales clerk, demonstrator, retail supervisor, computer support specialist, customer service representative.  Social Services: Social workers interact with families, agencies, and schools to promote the well-being of children. Effective communication minimizes barriers. Roles: Family social worker, substance abuse social worker, social work administrator.  Finance: Global transactions make language skills an asset in banking and finance. Roles: Teller, financial advisor, investment banker, accountant.  Communication: Professionals in media and public relations rely on language proficiency to gather information and communicate effectively. Roles: Translator, public relations specialist, journalist, media relations officer.

STUTTGART, GERMANY – OCTOBER 7: Serhou Guirassy of VfB Stuttgart reacts during the Bundesliga match between VfB Stuttgart and VfL Wolfsburg at MHPArena on October 7, 2023, in Stuttgart, Germany. (Photo by Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Getty Images)

In the first eight weeks of the 2023/24 Bundesliga season, one striker looked truly unstoppable—and it wasn’t Harry Kane. Serhou Guirassy of Stuttgart began the campaign in remarkable form, scoring an incredible 14 goals in eight matches. These weren’t just easy finishes, either; many came from outside the penalty area. His goal against Darmstadt—where he spun, dribbled past a defender, and powered the ball inside the near post—was outstanding. He also produced spectacular efforts like his third against Mainz, lifting the ball over a defender and then heading it over the rushing goalkeeper, showcasing the confidence of a player at his peak.

The 27-year-old Guinea international’s hot streak briefly made him the top scorer across Europe’s major leagues before he was sidelined with a hamstring injury. Guirassy’s 14 goals would have already placed him fifth in last season’s Bundesliga scoring charts.

Unsurprisingly, his excellent form has attracted interest from several Premier League clubs, especially due to a release clause in his contract which reportedly allows clubs to sign him for about $18.5 million this winter, rising to $21.5 million in the summer. This is considered a bargain, particularly when compared to the transfer fees paid by Wolverhampton Wanderers for Matheus Cunha, Everton for Beto, and Nottingham Forest (and Newcastle United) for Chris Wood.

Although Guirassy provides several reasons for clubs to consider him, there are also reasons for caution. He has already scored more goals this season than in any previous year—including during his spell in France’s Ligue 1—raising questions about the sustainability of his form, especially since eight games is a relatively small sample size. However, last season he scored 11 goals in 22 matches for Stuttgart—an impressive ratio of one every 150 minutes—suggesting he may have found a club and system that suit him as he reaches his prime years. Still, doubts remain about whether he can replicate this level elsewhere.

Prior to joining Stuttgart, Guirassy reached double digits for league goals just once, scoring 10 goals in 27 games for Stade Rennais in the 2020/21 season. It’s worth noting that strikers moving from the Bundesliga sometimes struggle to match their scoring rates abroad, particularly if they don’t join a leading team in the Premier League.

Stuttgart have been performing well, ranking among the top three Bundesliga teams for possession, passing accuracy, and shots per game. Despite finishing 16th the previous season, they were among the league leaders in shots and remained in the upper half for possession and pass accuracy. Notably, five of Guirassy’s eight matches this season were against the bottom five Bundesliga teams, and this dominance has given him the third-highest shots per 90 minutes in the league. If Guirassy moves, his new club may not offer the same attacking prominence.

Although Guirassy has expressed a desire to remain at Stuttgart this winter, clubs will likely view the release clause as an opportunity. With interest growing, teams may be reluctant to wait until summer, even if they’re unsure whether Guirassy’s current form is sustainable. The release clause means that even if he can’t replicate his Stuttgart performances, he still represents good value.

Dr. Frasier Crane is returning to screens as Paramount+ debuts a revival of the classic sitcom on October 12. Kelsey Grammer reprises his role, making it feel like Frasier never left—this is more a seamless next chapter than a typical reboot.

While many TV shows today obsess over reboots and alternate timelines, this new Frasier stands apart. It captures the heart of the original with its recognizable laugh track, comedic style, and familiar pacing. The revival is unashamedly old-school, maintaining the same spirit, humor, and format that fans loved during its initial 11-season run that ended in 2004.

Longtime viewers may miss key characters: Frasier’s father Martin (played by the late John Mahoney), brother Niles (David Hyde Pierce), and Daphne (Jane Leeves). However, new storylines emerge—especially between Frasier and his estranged son Freddy (Jack Cutmore-Scott), now a firefighter and former Harvard student. The cast also features Eve (Jess Salgueiro), Alan Cornwall (Nicholas Lyndhurst), Olivia (Toks Olagundoye), and David (Anders Keith), adding fresh dynamics while nodding to the original series.

With the action now set in Boston, viewers will notice updated visuals and a reworked theme song. Renowned director James Burrows helms the first two episodes, while Chris Harris and Joe Cristalli serve as showrunners, blending blue-collar charm with sharp wit for a tone that feels classic yet current.

Beloved original cast members Peri Gilpin and Bebe Neuwirth will also appear later in the season, reviving the characters Roz Doyle and Lilith Sternin. Frasier’s gentle humor and self-awareness remain at the core, as new episodes premiere weekly after launching October 12 on Paramount+ and the first two episodes also air on CBS October 17. The series is rated TV-PG.

article_content: Oil prices climbed in early Asian trading on Friday, reversing earlier losses as traders speculated about potential OPEC+ agreements on further production cuts. Brent crude futures rose 29 cents, or 0.4%, to $81.71 at 0213 GMT, after declining by 0.7% in the previous session. U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude slipped 38 cents, or 0.5%, to $76.72 from Wednesday's close. There was no WTI settlement on Thursday because of the U.S. public holiday. Both oil benchmarks are set to post their first weekly gain in five weeks, buoyed by expectations that OPEC+, led by Saudi Arabia, may extend supply cuts to keep markets balanced into 2024. The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies (OPEC+) surprised markets on Wednesday by postponing its ministerial meeting by four days to November 30, as member states struggled to agree on production targets. According to Tony Sycamore, an IG market analyst, an extension of existing output reductions now appears most likely. The unexpected meeting delay initially sent Brent down as much as 4% and WTI down up to 5% during Wednesday's trading. Holiday-related low trading volumes in the U.S. also subdued market activity. Analysts attribute weaker U.S. crude demand to poor refining margins and rising domestic inventories, with ANZ noting that fundamental market developments have been bearish. In China, oil demand growth is projected to decelerate to around 4% in the first half of 2024 due to persistent challenges in the property sector affecting diesel use. On the supply side, non-OPEC production remains robust, highlighted by Brazilian energy giant Petrobras's plan to invest $102 billion over five years, boosting output to 3.2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd) by 2028 from 2.8 million boepd in 2024. In other business updates, Tesla is considering investing up to $2 billion in an Indian factory, contingent on favorable import duties, while India's government may direct the next Finance Commission to place greater emphasis on human development and sustainability goals. Additionally, more women are taking on senior leadership roles in Indian corporations, increasing their presence in high-profile boardroom debates.

article_content: LONDON: Former UK Prime Minister David Cameron has made a significant political comeback by being appointed as Foreign Secretary. Cameron expressed hope that his experience as both a leader and former Prime Minister will help him assist current British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak at a challenging time. On X (formerly Twitter), Cameron wrote, 'The Prime Minister has asked me to serve as his Foreign Secretary and I have gladly accepted. It will be an honour to serve our country alongside our dedicated FCDO staff and to provide the continued leadership and support that they deserve.' Cameron noted that the UK is facing 'daunting' international challenges due to the Israel-Hamas war and the Russia-Ukraine conflict, emphasizing the need to ensure global stability and security. 'At this time of profound global change, it has rarely been more important for this country to stand by our allies, strengthen our partnerships, and make sure our voice is heard,' he stated. Although Cameron has been away from frontline politics for seven years, he believes his experience—having served as Conservative Leader for eleven years and Prime Minister for six—will assist him in supporting the Prime Minister to address these vital challenges. He highlighted Britain's global presence, noting that its citizens live around the world and its businesses trade internationally. 'Working to help ensure stability and security on the global stage is essential and in our national interest. International security is vital for our domestic security,' Cameron said. Cameron praised Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, calling him a 'strong and capable Prime Minister, who is showing exemplary leadership at a difficult time,' expressing his commitment to support Sunak in delivering the security and prosperity the country needs. He also commended former Foreign Secretary James Cleverly and expressed eagerness to collaborate with him in Cleverly's new role as Home Secretary. 'The UK's Foreign Office, our Diplomatic Service, our Intelligence Services, and our Aid and Development capabilities are some of the finest in the world. I know from my time in office that they are staffed by brilliant, patriotic, and hard-working people. They have been well led by James Cleverly, with whom I look forward to working,' said Cameron. This comes after PM Sunak dismissed Home Secretary Suella Braverman following her public criticism of police during pro-Palestine rallies. Braverman’s removal followed mounting pressure over her article in The Times UK, where she accused the Metropolitan Police of being lenient towards certain elements in the demonstrations. After the cabinet reshuffle, James Cleverly was appointed Home Secretary, while David Cameron became Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs, Downing Street announced. Notably, this is only the second time since World War II that a former Prime Minister has returned to cabinet. Cameron had resigned as Prime Minister in 2016 after Britain voted to leave the European Union in a referendum he called.

article_content: NHS trusts in the UK have outsourced the typing of confidential patient letters to India in an effort to cut staffing costs, resulting in hundreds of thousands of sensitive documents being sent overseas. In the past year, at least 650,000 letters containing confidential medical information were sent to India by eight NHS trusts, and it is likely that more have participated. Members of Parliament and medical professionals warn that complex medical terminology might be incorrectly transcribed or translated, potentially leading to serious consequences. Some London-area hospitals, including Great Ormond Street Hospital, have acknowledged using lower-cost secretarial agencies in India for this task. Addenbrooke’s Hospital in Cambridge reportedly stopped sending letters to India after the returned documents were found to be of insufficient quality. The usual process involves doctors dictating referral letters, which are then transcribed by medical secretaries; however, outsourcing involves sending dictations to India for typing, with documents returned weeks later. Figures provided by Labour MP John Spellar show that in 2011/12, West Middlesex University Hospital sent 234,000 letters to India, Great Ormond Street Hospital sent 123,000, and North Middlesex University Hospital sent 137,000. Other trusts sending letters overseas include Kingston Hospital, Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals, the Whittington Hospital, the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, and Barts and The London; Barts ended the practice in July without giving a reason. Several trusts assert that patient confidentiality is preserved, as names and birthdates are removed prior to transfer. Andrew Lansley, former health secretary, confirmed that Addenbrooke's ended its contract with an outsourcing firm due to poor quality. MP John Spellar has raised concerns in Parliament, citing potential safety risks and negative effects on UK employment, stressing that the work could be kept in the UK to support local jobs. Some primary care trusts (PCTs), which oversee GP services, have also outsourced administrative work to India; at least 46 PCTs have signed such contracts. Reports indicate that errors have occurred, including instances where confidential information was sent to the wrong organization.

article_content: An elderly woman who had accumulated a fortune of half a million dollars had her life savings allegedly stolen by her son and daughter-in-law, according to court proceedings. Earlier this month, Ivan Ljunghammar and his wife, Deborah Jean, were charged with first-degree theft after allegedly taking $512,800 from Ivan's 82-year-old mother’s bank account. The couple, residents of Seattle, were granted control over the woman's finances in 2007 when she began experiencing dementia. Seattle detective Pamela St John, who specializes in elder abuse cases, said family members became suspicious that the couple might be exploiting the 82-year-old. The woman, described as lively but unable to manage her finances, currently resides in a dementia care home in Bellevue. The Ljunghammars reportedly withdrew $190,000 from her bank accounts and hired a convicted felon as her caregiver. Detective St John testified in King County court that Ivan Ljunghammar exercised complete control over his mother’s personal and financial affairs, isolated her from family gatherings and vacations, and used her assets to cover his own personal and household expenses. Senior Deputy Prosecutor Page Ulrey filed charges after it was revealed that the son had been renting out his mother's properties for less than market value, using her vehicles, and had obtained power of attorney. The Ljunghammars were expected to enter their plea in the following days and were not being detained in county jail. Adult Protective Services reports that there were 14,577 cases of elder abuse and exploitation reported in Washington state in 2009, with most victims over the age of 60 and most perpetrators being relatives.

article_content:
America is facing major health care challenges as its population ages. In the past decade, the number of Americans aged 65 and older has increased by 6 million, now constituting over 13% of the population. The 'oldest old' age group, those 85 and older, has grown to 6 million, a tenfold rise since the 1950s. Older adults experience higher rates of serious diseases such as heart disease, cancer, stroke, and dementia, which often require specialist care and advanced medical technology.

Recent policy changes, including the Affordable Care Act (ACA or 'Obamacare'), have shifted millions of Americans into government programs like Medicaid and Medicare. According to Heritage Foundation analysts, over 6 million of the 8.5 million newly insured under the ACA by mid-2014 joined Medicaid. Projections indicate that combined Medicaid and Medicare enrollment could rise from 107 million in 2013 to 135 million by 2018, potentially reaching 140 million by 2020, a growth rate outpacing private insurance.

However, increased coverage by government insurance does not always assure access to care or positive health outcomes. A 2013 Merritt Hawkins survey found over half of doctors declined new Medicaid patients, and more than 20% of primary care physicians were not accepting new Medicare patients—far greater than the refusal rate for privately insured patients. In 2012, nearly 10,000 doctors opted out of Medicare, three times the 2009 number. The American Medical Association's 2013 report found that Medicare had notably high rates of claim denials compared to private insurers.

With the increasing complexity of medical care, specialist visits among seniors have grown from 37% to 55% over the past 20 years. 80% of surveyed Americans say that access to the most advanced procedures and technology is 'very important' or 'absolutely essential.' Just 10% believe these advances cost more than they are worth. A Health Affairs study further found that Americans have greater interest in new medical discoveries than people living in Western Europe.

While attention often focuses on a primary care doctor shortage, the Association of American Medical Colleges projects that nearly two-thirds of the expected 124,000 physician shortfall by 2025 will be in specialties. Nonetheless, some policy recommendations have favored primary care and proposed reducing specialist reimbursement by Medicare, potentially deterring entry into these critical fields.

To meet ACA requirements, many insurers have adopted 'narrow networks'—plans with limited coverage for specialists and top hospitals. McKinsey & Company reported that 68% of ACA exchange plans in 2014 featured narrow or very narrow provider networks. As a result, many leading cancer centers—including MD Anderson, Memorial Sloan-Kettering, Barnes Hospital, and the Seattle Cancer Care Alliance—were not covered by most state exchange plans, a trend expected to continue as insurers attempt to contain premium costs.

Some critics argue these trends push American health care toward a more generalist system with fewer choices, potentially limiting access to specialists and the latest technology. While administration officials argue alternatives are lacking, several Republican proposals advocate expanding choice and access through competition. The debate over the future direction of American health care remains active, centered on balancing access, quality, and the role of government.

Sienna was photographed in a babygro emblazoned with the words 'One Day I’m Going to Marry Prince George,' an outfit her grandmother bought from George at Asda. Her mom, Amy Brady, 28, from Firbanks in Jarrow, snapped the picture and shared it with friends and family on Facebook and Instagram.

Unexpectedly, the photo took off after someone reposted it to a hugely popular Prince Harry fan page, turning little Sienna into an online sensation. To date, the image of Sienna has earned over 200,000 likes and more than 5,000 comments, with many admirers mistaking her for the young Prince George himself. Still, there was slight disappointment in the household, as the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge and Prince George did not get in touch. For Sienna, the viral fame went unnoticed as she remained blissfully unaware, more interested in her feedings than her newfound notoriety. The babygro Sienna wore is part of a collection celebrating the birth of Prince George.

article_content: Every July 11, Mongolia comes alive as it celebrates both its independence and the start of Naadam, the country’s beloved festival of traditional sports. For three days, villages, towns, and cities host spirited competitions in wrestling, archery, and horse racing. The grand wrestling championship in Ulaanbaatar admits only nationally ranked wrestlers, but at local levels, men, women, and children—even as young as four—join in the festivities. Wrestlers wear frontless shirts, a custom rooted in a Mongolian folktale: a woman once disguised herself and won, prompting the tradition to prevent such surprises. While Naadam is often called the 'three manly games,' women compete in archery and girls ride as jockeys in horse races. “Everyone loves horse racing in Mongolia; it’s our national sport,” says Battsetseg Erdenekhuu, an adventure tour guide. The festival draws tourists from around the globe, yet Erdenekhuu believes the core competitions still retain their authenticity and deep local significance. “For the main games, it’s still very traditional,” she explains. “The opening ceremony in Ulaanbaatar is a bit more tourist-oriented, with added performances, but the heart of the event remains unchanged.” Across Mongolia, local and regional competitions are open to all, and participants train for up to two months before Naadam. The celebrations are accompanied by traditional foods, with deep-fried meat dumplings called 'khuushuur' being particularly popular. “Naadam without khuushuur isn’t complete,” Erdenekhuu adds. She’s confident the games will continue as a celebration of Mongolia’s nomadic roots, but expresses concern that rapid mining development could alter the way of life that Naadam honors. “The countryside and the festival are still authentic, but city life is changing. I think nomadic traditions will inevitably evolve in the coming years,” she reflects.

Il grande campionato di lotta a Ulaanbaatar è riservato solo ai lottatori con classifica nazionale, ma a livello locale uomini, donne e bambini — anche di appena quattro anni — partecipano alle feste. I lottatori indossano maglie senza parte anteriore, una tradizione nata da una leggenda mongola: una donna si travestì e vinse, portando all’usanza per evitare altre sorprese. Sebbene il Naadam sia spesso chiamato le 'tre discipline virili', le donne gareggiano nel tiro con l’arco e le ragazze fanno da fantine nelle corse dei cavalli. “Tutti amano le corse di cavalli in Mongolia; è il nostro sport nazionale,” racconta Battsetseg Erdenekhuu, guida turistica per avventure. Il festival attira turisti da tutto il mondo, ma secondo Erdenekhuu le competizioni principali rimangono autentiche e di grande valore locale. “Per le gare principali rimane tutto molto tradizionale,” spiega. “La cerimonia d’apertura a Ulaanbaatar è più orientata verso i turisti, con spettacoli aggiuntivi, ma il cuore dell’evento non cambia.” In tutta la Mongolia, le competizioni locali e regionali sono aperte a tutti e i partecipanti si allenano fino a due mesi prima del Naadam. I festeggiamenti sono accompagnati da cibi tipici, con i ravioli fritti ripieni di carne chiamati 'khuushuur' particolarmente popolari. “Un Naadam senza khuushuur non è completo,” aggiunge Erdenekhuu. È convinta che i giochi continueranno a celebrare le radici nomadi del paese, ma teme che il rapido sviluppo minerario possa cambiare lo stile di vita a cui il Naadam rende omaggio. “Le campagne e il festival sono ancora autentici, ma la vita cittadina sta cambiando. Credo che le tradizioni nomadi inevitabilmente evolveranno nei prossimi anni,” riflette.

article_content: Drones, typically associated with the war on terror in countries like Afghanistan and Somalia, are also part of daily life in Aberporth, a small community in West Wales. Once a busy fishing village, Aberporth now hosts Britain’s so-called 'drone centre of excellence.' Its local airport, a former RAF station now privately owned, is the only place in the UK where both military and civilian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can be tested. The airport is surrounded by 500 square miles of restricted airspace, allowing drones to fly safely without the risk of colliding with other aircraft. The UAVs, mainly used for surveillance and missile targeting without putting servicemen's lives in danger, fill the skies above the seaside town. The decision to transform the West Wales Airport into the National Aeronautical Centre, along with the £21 million public investment in a neighboring technology park, has disrupted the tranquility of Aberporth. Some residents and critics raise ethical concerns about drones being used as remote battlefield weapons, especially citing incidents of civilian casualties linked to US operations. Many also believe the investment has not delivered on the promised job creation. While Welsh Government projections stated Parc Aberporth would generate 1,000 jobs, fewer than 40 people are employed at the site, with a dozen more at the airport itself. Noise pollution, privacy, safety, and accidents—including two test drone crashes—have fueled further protests. The Watchkeeper UAV, costing £889 million, is undergoing trials by the Royal Artillery. Fifty-four Watchkeeper drones are intended for surveillance in Afghanistan, transmitting highly detailed images to a control center from up to 1,000 feet in the air. Military officials claim these drones help identify Taliban operations and save the lives of front-line troops. Although the Ministry of Defence says Watchkeeper will remain unarmed—unlike the armed Reaper drones used by the RAF—it can identify targets for possible missile strikes. Locals report the drones, which take off and land at Aberporth up to 25 times daily, are loud enough to be heard even after disappearing from sight. Opera singer Eirian James, who lives nearby, describes the drones' noise as highly unsettling, comparing it to the distress experienced by civilians living in conflict zones. Des Davies, a 68-year-old retired stockbroker, criticizes the project as ‘a white elephant’ and a waste of public money, questioning its economic impact. Mark Williams, Liberal Democrat MP for Ceredigion, acknowledges community concerns over ethics, surveillance, safety, and noise, and notes that visible economic development has not matched the level of public spending.

article_content: A recent study found that 90% of British women have been on a diet at some point in their lives. On average, a woman will lose her body weight more than nine times over the course of her lifetime through repeated dieting. The study revealed that women spend approximately 17 years of their lives on diets. Typically, women start dieting at age 18, go on two diets a year, and lose about 11 pounds each time. The research, carried out by Kevin Dorren, Founder & Head Chef of Diet Chef, highlights significant regional differences. Women in the North West find dieting the hardest, managing just four days on average—the shortest in the UK. By contrast, women in the North East and East Anglia show more willpower, with some maintaining their last diet for about a month. Less than one percent of women stick to a diet for a full year, and a third diet for at least six months annually. Motivations for dieting include health reasons, preparing for summer holidays or weddings, not fitting into clothes, and noticing a muffin top. The primary barriers to successful dieting are a love of food, a lack of willpower, and the perceived expense of healthy foods, with about 20% saying cost is a factor. Additionally, one in three women make comfort purchases—most often shoes—when feeling low about their dieting efforts.

Lo studio ha rivelato che le donne trascorrono circa 17 anni della loro vita seguendo diete. Tipicamente, iniziano a mettersi a dieta a 18 anni, fanno due diete all'anno e perdono circa 5 kg ogni volta. Al contrario, le donne del North East e dell’East Anglia mostrano maggiore determinazione, mantenendo l’ultima dieta per circa un mese. Meno dell’1% delle donne riesce a seguire una dieta per un anno intero, mentre un terzo fa dieta per almeno sei mesi ogni anno. Inoltre, una donna su tre fa acquisti consolatori—principalmente scarpe—quando si sente giù per i risultati della dieta.

article_content: Village greens across Britain may be under threat after a developer succeeded in winning permission to build on Curtis Fields, a cherished stretch of grassland near Weymouth, Dorset. This outcome follows a decade-long legal battle waged by local campaigners who sought to retain the area's protected status. Betterment Properties, the developer, plans to construct approximately 80 homes on the 46-acre plot, which had been registered as a town green since 2001 based on decades of use by local residents.  Despite nine years of campaigning and £100,000 spent, the Supreme Court recently ruled in the developer’s favor, overturning the land's legal protections. Conservation groups warn that the decision could endanger around 4,000 other town and village greens in Britain, as it may make it easier for developers to challenge and remove such protections.  The legal battle began in earnest when Betterment Properties bought Curtis Fields in 2005 and sought to remove its town green status. Local residents formed the Society for the Protection of Markham and Little Francis to oppose the application. However, in 2010, the High Court decided that Curtis Fields should lose its town green designation, ruling that the required 20 years of continuous recreational use had not been established, as much of the land had been used as farmland until the mid-1980s.  The campaigners took their case to the Court of Appeal and ultimately to the Supreme Court, arguing that the developer’s appeal came too late. Both appeals were unsuccessful, with the Supreme Court upholding the lower courts' decisions. The campaigners were left with an additional legal bill of £15,000, which they plan to repay through fundraising efforts.  Organizations such as the Open Spaces Society and Campaign to Protect Rural England supported the campaign, expressing concern about the wider impact of the ruling. Kate Ashbrook, general secretary of the Open Spaces Society, described the decision as a setback for community efforts to protect public greens, warning it could encourage developers to challenge established protections.  The chairman of the campaign group, Gill Taylor, expressed disappointment but maintained that their fight was important to uphold community rights. A spokesperson for Betterment Properties stated that public use of the land would continue as before until development proceeds.  Village greens have held a special place in English rural life for centuries, but it was not until the Commons Registration Act of 1965 that such lands received formal legal protection. Under the Commons Act 2006, any land used openly by the community for at least 20 years can be registered as a town or village green. Once registered, building, interference, or fencing is prohibited, often leading to disputes between communities and landowners.

Christine Fox, the defense expert who inspired the character 'Charlie Blackwood' in the classic 1980s film Top Gun, has become the highest-ranking woman in Pentagon history. On Tuesday, President Barack Obama appointed Fox as the acting deputy defense secretary, following the resignation of Ashton Carter.

Fox, well-known for her expertise in air and maritime defense rather than as a pilot, was selected during the filming of Top Gun to advise Kelly McGillis and the film's producers on accurately portraying her on-screen counterpart. Like 'Charlie' in the movie, Fox was a non-flying military professional. She spent time with the cast and crew of director Tony Scott's film to ensure factual accuracy, once stating to People magazine in 1985, 'I don't know anything about flying airplanes, but I know a lot about the guy in the back seat — his mission, his radar and his missiles.'

Before this appointment, Fox served as the Pentagon's director of cost controls, a position she held until last summer. A spokesperson for the Department of Defense confirmed that Fox would serve as acting deputy secretary until a permanent replacement for Carter is selected.

Defense Secretary Chuck Hagel praised Fox as 'a brilliant defense thinker and proven manager who knows the intricacies of the Department's budget, programs, and global operations better than anyone.' According to a senior defense official quoted by NBC News, Fox is expected to 'hit the ground running like no one else can.' Her trailblazing career continues to set new milestones for women in American military leadership.

article_content: Relations between Taiwan and the Philippines deteriorated in May after a Taiwanese fisherman was killed by the Philippine coast guard. In response, Taiwan recalled its envoy from Manila, suspended applications from Filipinos seeking work in Taiwan, and held naval drills near Philippine waters. The Philippine coast guard stated that on May 9, its crew fired at a Taiwanese fishing boat after it allegedly attempted to ram a Philippine vessel. The Philippines insists the incident happened inside its exclusive economic zone and that the death was unintended. Taiwan, however, claims the coast guard fired multiple shots at the fishing boat in waters claimed by both countries, resulting in the death of 65-year-old fisherman Hung Shih-cheng. The clash arises from overlapping territorial claims in the South China Sea, an area rich in fishing grounds and natural resources, disputed by Brunei, China, Malaysia, the Philippines, Taiwan, and Vietnam. Taiwanese President Ma Ying-jeou called the shooting a 'cold-blooded murder' and criticized the Philippine response as inadequate. Taiwan has demanded a formal apology, compensation, an investigation with punishment for those responsible, and bilateral talks on fishing rights. Among the measures imposed by Taiwan is a travel alert advising Taiwanese citizens not to visit the Philippines. The Philippine government has expressed frustration at Taiwan's stance. Presidential spokesperson Edwin Lacierda said Manila had acted responsibly, sending a personal representative to apologize and offer aid to the fisherman's family. Philippine authorities are investigating the shooting and have warned that Taiwan's measures could hurt both countries' economies. He also urged Taiwanese to avoid harassment of Filipinos living in Taiwan. Garfie Li, spokeswoman for President Ma, rejected Lacierda’s statement that Manila had 'gone the extra mile,' calling it untrue and unacceptable. The United States, an ally of both countries, expressed regret over the incident and urged both sides to cooperate, maintain maritime safety, and avoid escalating tensions. China, which considers Taiwan a breakaway province, expressed support for Taiwan and condemned the shooting, calling for a full investigation and punishment of those responsible. China and the Philippines are also engaged in another territorial dispute in the region.

article_content: Jenny Gusse and Doug Inglis, both experienced backpackers and scientific researchers, died during a tragic grizzly bear attack while hiking in Banff National Park, Canada. The couple, who were avid nature enthusiasts and careful planners, sent a final distress message, 'Bear attack bad,' via a Garmin inReach satellite device just before succumbing to their injuries. The SOS alert was triggered on a Friday night and received both by the authorities and family members. Despite strict adherence to safety protocols, including storing food in a bear-proof bag and carrying bear spray, the couple could not prevent the fatal encounter. A response team found their bodies, along with their dog Tris, at the remote campsite. The bear involved—a non-lactating female over 25 years old in declining physical condition—was shot and killed after it charged the rescue team. Jenny and Doug were highly respected in the scientific community, working together at Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada and having strong ties to the University of Lethbridge. As life partners and colleagues, they devoted themselves to both their research and outdoor adventures. The incident had no witnesses, and Parks Canada stated that it was the first grizzly-caused fatality in Banff for decades. The loss of Jenny and Doug serves as a reminder of the unpredictability of the wilderness, even for the most prepared and experienced individuals. Friends and family members recalled their passion for conservation, their partnership in all facets of life, and the profound impact they had through both their professional work and mentorship. Their deaths underscore the rare but real risks that come with exploring wild spaces.

La coppia, appassionata di natura e attenta nell’organizzazione, ha inviato un ultimo messaggio di emergenza, 'Attacco orso grave', tramite un dispositivo satellitare Garmin inReach poco prima di soccombere alle ferite. L’allarme SOS è stato inviato nella notte di venerdì ed è stato ricevuto sia dalle autorità che dai familiari. Nonostante il rigoroso rispetto dei protocolli di sicurezza, inclusa la conservazione del cibo in una sacca anti-orso e l’uso dello spray anti-orso, la coppia non ha potuto evitare il tragico incontro. Una squadra di soccorso ha trovato i loro corpi, insieme al cane Tris, nell’area campeggio isolata. L’orso coinvolto—una femmina non allattante di oltre 25 anni in condizioni fisiche precarie—è stato abbattuto dopo aver caricato la squadra. Jenny e Doug erano molto rispettati nella comunità scientifica, lavoravano insieme presso Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada e avevano forti legami con l’Università di Lethbridge. Come compagni di vita e colleghi, si sono dedicati sia alla ricerca che alle avventure nella natura. L’incidente è avvenuto senza testimoni e Parks Canada ha affermato che si tratta della prima morte causata da un grizzly a Banff da decenni. La perdita di Jenny e Doug è un richiamo all’imprevedibilità della natura selvaggia, anche per i più preparati ed esperti. Amici e familiari hanno ricordato la loro passione per la conservazione, la loro collaborazione totale e l’impatto profondo che hanno avuto tramite il lavoro e il mentoring. Le loro morti sottolineano i rischi, rari ma reali, dell’esplorazione degli spazi naturali.

article_content: A seven-year-old girl from El Salvador suffering from cancer has finally been released from an immigrant detention center in Texas to receive treatment for her brain tumor after weeks of delay. Nayely Bermudez Beltran and her mother, Sara Beltran Rodriguez, were allowed to leave the Karnes County Residential Center on Wednesday night, responding to pressure from advocacy groups. The release enables Nayely to begin treatment next week. The pair fled violence in El Salvador in July. Upon entering the United States, Beltran informed border authorities of her daughter's urgent medical needs, according to the Houston Chronicle. Despite this, they were transferred to Karnes County Residential Center without Nayely receiving immediate medical attention. Authorities refused to release them or set bail, even though they had a place to stay, as noted by Grassroots Leadership. Previously, Nayely had received chemotherapy for her brain tumor in El Salvador, but her treatment was interrupted due to the family's need to flee. While awaiting answers in detention, Nayely’s health declined, with her mother reporting increased illness and side effects related to her condition. Nayely had also undergone brain surgery for a shunt, and her lawyer warned that a malfunction could be life-threatening or cause brain damage. 'We waited for a month, and no one would take action,' Beltran, 27, said. On August 18, the pair passed a credible fear screening, a critical step toward asylum, but authorities still refused to release Nayely for medical care, according to Grassroots Leadership. Their attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, obtained Nayely’s medical records, which were reviewed by three U.S. doctors. Neurologist Dr. Simon Carlson urged immigration officials to release Nayely, warning that her condition could worsen unexpectedly with severe consequences. 'Urgent care is needed for this child, who risks long-term brain damage or worse without prompt specialist intervention,' Dr. Carlson stated. On Wednesday, the agency finally released the mother and daughter, who then relocated to a shelter in Austin, with assistance from Texans United for Families. Photos outside the shelter showed Nayely and her mother smiling with their lawyer. 'Nayely and Sara just left the Karnes family detention center. They are heading to a welcoming place in Austin, and Nayely has a doctor’s appointment on Tuesday,' read a caption from supporters. The Houston Chronicle reports it is unclear why the agency ultimately changed its mind. Dell Children's Medical Center of Central Texas in Austin has agreed to evaluate Nayely and may cover her medical costs. Beltran and her daughter also have a hearing scheduled for Thursday. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement declined to comment on the specific case.
translated_content: Una bambina di sette anni di El Salvador, affetta da cancro, è stata finalmente rilasciata da un centro di detenzione per immigrati in Texas per ricevere cure per il suo tumore al cervello dopo settimane di attesa. Nayely Bermudez Beltran e sua madre, Sara Beltran Rodriguez, sono state autorizzate a lasciare il Karnes County Residential Center mercoledì sera, in seguito alle pressioni dei gruppi di sostegno. Questo rilascio permetterà a Nayely di iniziare le cure la prossima settimana. Le due sono fuggite dalla violenza in El Salvador a luglio. Appena entrate negli Stati Uniti, Beltran ha informato le autorità di frontiera delle urgenti necessità mediche della figlia, secondo quanto riportato dall'Houston Chronicle. Nonostante ciò, sono state trasferite al Karnes County Residential Center senza che Nayely ricevesse cure immediate. Le autorità si sono rifiutate di rilasciarle o fissare una cauzione, pur avendo un posto dove stare, come segnalato da Grassroots Leadership. In precedenza, Nayely aveva ricevuto la chemioterapia per il tumore al cervello in El Salvador, ma il trattamento era stato interrotto a causa della fuga della famiglia. Durante l'attesa nel centro, la salute di Nayely è peggiorata, con la madre che ha riferito un aumento dei sintomi e degli effetti collaterali. Nayely aveva inoltre subito un intervento chirurgico per un drenaggio cerebrale e la loro avvocata ha avvertito che un eventuale malfunzionamento avrebbe potuto essere fatale o causare danni cerebrali. 'Abbiamo aspettato un mese, e nessuno agiva,' ha dichiarato Beltran, 27 anni. Il 18 agosto, madre e figlia hanno superato il colloquio per il riconoscimento del fondato timore di persecuzione, un passo cruciale verso l'asilo, ma, secondo Grassroots Leadership, le autorità ancora non hanno permesso il rilascio di Nayely per cure mediche. L'avvocata Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch ha ottenuto le cartelle cliniche di Nayely, poi esaminate da tre medici statunitensi. Il neurologo Dr. Simon Carlson ha sollecitato il rilascio, avvertendo che le condizioni della bambina avrebbero potuto peggiorare improvvisamente, con gravi conseguenze. 'Sono necessarie cure urgenti per questa bambina, che rischia danni cerebrali a lungo termine o peggio senza un intervento specialistico immediato,' ha dichiarato il Dr. Carlson. Mercoledì, l’agenzia ha infine rilasciato madre e figlia, che si sono trasferite in un rifugio ad Austin, aiutate da Texans United for Families. Foto fuori dal rifugio ritraggono Nayely e sua madre sorridenti insieme all’avvocata. 'Nayely e Sara hanno appena lasciato il centro di detenzione familiare di Karnes. Ora vanno in un ambiente accogliente ad Austin e Nayely ha una visita dal medico martedì,' si legge in una didascalia dei sostenitori. Secondo l’Houston Chronicle non è chiaro cosa abbia portato l’agenzia a cambiare opinione. Il Dell Children's Medical Center of Central Texas di Austin ha accettato di valutare Nayely e potrebbe coprire i costi delle cure. Beltran e la figlia hanno anche un’udienza fissata per giovedì. Le autorità per l'immigrazione degli Stati Uniti hanno rifiutato di commentare il caso.

article_content: Scientists have finally resolved a visual illusion that first puzzled Galileo over 400 years ago. Galileo observed that Venus appeared larger than Jupiter when viewed with the naked eye, but not through a telescope. Now, researchers have determined that this is an optical illusion arising from the way our eyes perceive lightness and darkness. The illusion, now better understood thanks to work by Jens Kremkow and collaborators in the labs of Jose Manuel Alonso and Qasim Zaidi at the State University of New York College of Optometry, reveals that the edges of bright objects seem blurred. The brain then magnifies this effect, making the entire object appear larger than it actually is. Because Venus is closer to Earth, it appears brighter than Jupiter in the night sky and thus looks bigger, even though Jupiter is physically much larger. This research improves our understanding of how the human brain processes light and dark objects. This study, scheduled for publication in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, also connects to the work of German physicist Hermann von Helmholtz, who in the 19th century described the 'irradiation illusion.' He suggested the illusion arises from how we sense objects, not from the optics of the eye itself. Dr. Alonso explained that the new research demonstrates the illusion results from a non-linear response of the visual system to objects presented on dark backgrounds. The phenomenon also explains why black text on a white page is easier to read. Galileo theorized that this size illusion was caused by the eyes, although he did not know exactly how. He speculated it might be due to light being refracted in the moisture covering the pupil or reflected off the eyelids. Generations of scientists tried to attribute the illusion to optical blur, but that explanation did not fully account for why Venus appeared larger than Jupiter to the naked eye. Helmholtz recognized that a sensory response, rather than an optical one, was responsible for the illusion. The latest findings show that white shapes on a dark background look larger than equal-sized dark shapes on a white background. In the study, researchers recorded electrical signals from neurons in the visual areas of anesthetized cats, monkeys, and humans, discovering that the illusion may originate from the very first stages of vision in the photoreceptors of the eyes. The research not only solves Galileo’s centuries-old puzzle but also deepens our understanding of how our visual system interprets light and dark, and why black-on-white text is preferred for reading.

Ora i ricercatori hanno stabilito che si tratta di un'illusione ottica dovuta al modo in cui i nostri occhi percepiscono la luce e l’oscurità. L'illusione, oggi meglio compresa grazie agli studi di Jens Kremkow e collaboratori nei laboratori di Jose Manuel Alonso e Qasim Zaidi presso il College of Optometry della State University of New York, mostra che i bordi degli oggetti luminosi appaiono sfocati. Il cervello amplifica questo effetto, facendo sembrare l'intero oggetto più grande di quanto sia in realtà. Poiché Venere è più vicina alla Terra, appare più luminosa di Giove nel cielo notturno e quindi sembra più grande, anche se Giove è in realtà molto più grande. Questa ricerca migliora la comprensione di come il cervello umano elabora luce e oscurità. Questo studio, in uscita sui Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, si collega anche agli studi del fisico tedesco Hermann von Helmholtz che nel XIX secolo descrisse la 'illusione d’irradiazione'. Helmholtz suggerì che l’illusione nasce dalla percezione sensoriale e non dall’ottica dell’occhio. Il dottor Alonso ha spiegato che la nuova ricerca dimostra che l’illusione deriva da una risposta non lineare del sistema visivo a oggetti presentati su sfondi scuri. Il fenomeno spiega anche perché leggere testo nero su sfondo bianco sia più semplice. Galileo teorizzò che questa illusione di grandezza fosse causata dagli occhi, anche se non sapeva esattamente in che modo. Ipotesizzò che ciò fosse dovuto alla luce rifratta nell’umidità che copre la pupilla o riflessa dai bordi delle palpebre. Per generazioni gli scienziati hanno attribuito l’illusione alla sfocatura ottica, ma questa spiegazione da sola non giustificava pienamente perché Venere apparisse più grande di Giove a occhio nudo. Helmholtz riconobbe che una risposta sensoriale, più che ottica, era responsabile dell’illusione. Le ultime scoperte mostrano che le figure bianche su sfondo scuro appaiono più grandi di forme scure della stessa dimensione su sfondo chiaro. Nel loro studio, i ricercatori hanno registrato segnali elettrici dai neuroni nelle aree visive di gatti, scimmie e umani anestetizzati, scoprendo che l’illusione potrebbe avere origine già dai primi stadi della visione nei fotorecettori dell’occhio. La ricerca non solo risolve l’enigma di Galileo ma approfondisce anche la nostra comprensione del sistema visivo e ci spiega perché il testo nero su bianco sia preferito per la lettura.

article_content: The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors took significant action Tuesday by advancing a ban on medical marijuana dispensaries in the county's unincorporated areas. The proposal received unanimous support and is set for formal adoption on December 7, taking effect 30 days later. Similarly, the Orange County Board of Supervisors approved an initial reading of an identical ban by a 4-1 vote, with a final decision also scheduled for December 7. According to Los Angeles County Supervisor Michael Antonovich, 'These facilities have a negative impact on communities, attracting crime and other nuisances. That's why more than 100 cities and nine counties in California have passed similar ordinances.' Antonovich added that bans in individual municipalities may push dispensaries into the remaining unincorporated areas, placing an undue burden on those communities. Both measures respond to concerns over the increasing number of illegally operated dispensaries in these unincorporated regions. Officials warn of health and safety risks, noting that unregulated marijuana-infused food products could contain harmful ingredients, disease, or pesticide residues. The bans come shortly after California voters rejected a proposal to legalize marijuana for recreational use, though medical marijuana remains legal statewide. The proposed Los Angeles County ban would affect about 1.5 million people, while Orange County’s would impact around 119,000 residents. In 2006, Los Angeles County modified its zoning laws to allow medical marijuana dispensaries, but officials are now worried about the surge in illegal operations. Los Angeles city has also begun targeting illegal dispensaries through enforcement actions. Almost all Orange County cities prohibit dispensaries, except Laguna Woods. According to Orange County Public Works Director Jess Carbajal, 22 cities have ordinances that ban dispensaries, and nine more have urgent moratoriums in place. The votes took place the same day the National Cannabis Industry Association was established, marking the emergence of the first national trade organization for the cannabis sector and consumers. The association's creation coincided with Arizona voters legalizing medical marijuana, making it the 15th state to do so. Aaron Smith, executive director of the new association, criticized the bans. 'It’s hard to believe that either county would take such an action during tough economic times, turning away jobs and tax revenue while leaving buildings vacant,' Smith said. He acknowledged concerns about illegal operations but argued that better oversight, not bans, would offer a more effective solution.

Qualcomm, a prominent player in the telecommunications industry, has navigated numerous challenges over its history. After overcoming early skepticism about its CDMA technology, the company has adopted certain practices that may impede its growth and key partnerships. Nevertheless, Qualcomm continues to display resilience and adaptability in a dynamic sector. By recognizing and addressing these challenges, the company can further strengthen its relationships and reinforce its leadership position. Currently, Qualcomm faces conflicts with major clients, ongoing disputes with Arm, and scrutiny from international regulators. While it maintains active partnerships with Meta and Microsoft, connections with other leading technology firms remain limited, and even existing collaborations can be complex. Despite these issues, Qualcomm is pushing forward with technological innovations and expanding its influence within the evolving tech landscape. Focusing on better communication and cooperation with key partners will be vital for maintaining stability and securing long-term success. One significant hurdle for Qualcomm is a reputation for arrogance, highlighted by sometimes strained relations with Google over pricing and collaboration on the Pixel phone. Even if this perception is not unique among competitors, it could nevertheless hinder future partnerships. To overcome this, Qualcomm should foster a more collaborative and open approach when engaging with potential partners. By emphasizing dialogue and mutual understanding, Qualcomm can improve its image and cultivate beneficial, long-term alliances. Additionally, critics have targeted Qualcomm’s organizational structure, noting that it established a dedicated sales department only recently. By previously prioritizing supply agreements and specific design wins, Qualcomm may have missed crucial opportunities to form strategic partnerships with major companies such as Apple, Samsung, Meta, Microsoft, Xiaomi, BBK Group, and Google. To address this, Qualcomm needs to make relationship-building and collaboration a central focus for future growth.

Anker’s Soundcore brand has shaken up the audio market with products that offer strong performance and features at prices below those of major brands like Sony, JBL, Marshall, and Apple. The new Motion 300 Bluetooth speaker continues this trend. It combines high-resolution audio capability, waterproof protection (rated IPX7), stereo pairing, built-in speakerphone, and up to 13 hours of playback, all at just $80.

The Motion 300 features a unique flat design using metal and rubber, initially available in black, with blue and green models coming soon. Unlike most portable speakers that are cylindrical or boxy for improved sound spread, the Motion 300 can stand, lay flat, or hang from its removable strap. A gyroscope inside detects its orientation and adjusts sound output accordingly. At 1.8 pounds, it’s heavier and bulkier than some rivals, such as the JBL Flip 6 and Marshall Emberton.

Connectivity is a strong suit thanks to Bluetooth 5.3 and multipoint pairing, enabling you to connect and seamlessly switch between two devices. Its tested wireless range of 180 feet in open space is above average (though below the claimed 328 feet). All controls—including power, pairing, extra bass, playback, and volume—are located on the top (or side) surface and are backlit for ease of use, with adjustable illumination via the Soundcore app. However, there’s no detailed battery status readout—only a white or red light to indicate charge level—so users will need to check their phone or the app directly for specifics.

Audio quality is a standout: the extra bass mode noticeably enriches lower frequencies, and the sound stays well-balanced up to about 60% volume. Pushing beyond that tends to blur vocals and midrange frequencies, a typical issue for compact speakers. Users can fine-tune the audio with the app’s granular EQ settings. Despite offering support for Sony’s LDAC hi-res codec, most casual listeners won’t hear a difference compared to standard Bluetooth codecs, while LDAC does reduce battery life.

A lesser-known but useful feature is the speaker’s call functionality. Although not featured in most marketing materials, the Motion 300 can serve as a speakerphone, thanks to a top-left microphone (when upright); it works best indoors and at short range.

Battery life is competitive, with around 13 hours per charge at moderate volume and with LDAC turned off—comparable to most similarly-sized speakers. The Motion 300, like many rivals, does not float, so extra care is needed around water.

In summary, the Motion 300 is a strong budget choice for those seeking great sound, robust features, and durability for less than $100. Its few drawbacks—extra weight, lack of a detailed battery display, and understated looks—are outweighed by its reliable performance and excellent value.

Il Motion 300 si distingue per un design piatto, realizzato in metallo e gomma, presentato inizialmente in nero, con versioni blu e verde in arrivo. A differenza della maggior parte degli speaker portatili dalla forma cilindrica o rettangolare, il Motion 300 può essere posizionato in piedi, sdraiato o appeso tramite la tracolla rimovibile. Con un peso di 1,8 kg, è più pesante e voluminoso di alcuni concorrenti come il JBL Flip 6 e il Marshall Emberton.

La connettività è un punto di forza grazie al Bluetooth 5.3 e all’accoppiamento multiplo, che consente di collegare e passare facilmente tra due dispositivi. L’autonomia wireless testata raggiunge i 55 metri in campo aperto, sopra la media seppur inferiore ai 100 metri dichiarati da Soundcore. Tutti i comandi—accensione, pairing, extra bass, riproduzione e volume—sono posti sulla parte superiore (o laterale) e retroilluminati; la luminosità è regolabile dall’app Soundcore. Manca però un vero indicatore dettagliato della batteria: solo una luce bianca o rossa segnala il livello di carica, e per dati più precisi si deve consultare lo smartphone o l’app.

La qualità audio è eccellente: la modalità extra bass esalta le frequenze basse e l’equilibrio del suono rimane valido fino circa al 60% del volume; oltre, le medie e le voci perdono chiarezza—problema comune negli speaker compatti. L’equalizzazione si può personalizzare via app. Il supporto al codec LDAC di Sony permette l’audio hi-res, ma la differenza rispetto ai codec Bluetooth standard è impercettibile per la maggior parte degli utenti, oltre a ridurre la durata della batteria.

Una funzione poco pubblicizzata ma utile è il vivavoce integrato. Anche se non messa in risalto, questa possibilità è presente grazie a un microfono situato in alto a sinistra (nell’uso verticale); funziona al meglio in ambienti interni e a breve distanza.

L’autonomia raggiunge circa 13 ore a volume moderato con LDAC disattivato, in linea con altri speaker simili. Come altri modelli, il Motion 300 non galleggia sull’acqua: serve quindi attenzione extra vicino alle piscine.

In conclusione, il Motion 300 è un’ottima opzione economica per chi desidera qualità, funzionalità e resistenza sotto i 100 dollari. I pochi svantaggi—peso maggiore, assenza di indicatore batteria e design sobrio—sono compensati dall’affidabilità e dal valore offerto.
