article_content: The 2014 tennis season has been one of the most unpredictable in recent memory, with fresh champions, several first-time finalists, and tennis legends striving to reclaim past successes. While the four Grand Slam tournaments have concluded, spots in the year-end championships are still being contested in both the men's and women's tours. Before the season's final stretch, it's worth reflecting on the major tournaments and what they've revealed. 1. Sharapova's Rise as a Clay-Court Specialist: Maria Sharapova has proven her abilities across surfaces, but since 2010, she has claimed 10 titles, with only two coming outside of clay. At the Grand Slams, she has won the French Open twice and reached the final in Paris three more times, but hasn't appeared in another Grand Slam final since the 2012 Australian Open. Her run at Roland Garros this year was a bright spot after underperforming in Melbourne, London, and New York. With an extra week between the French Open and Wimbledon next year, Sharapova may be able to prepare better for the grass-court season. 2. The Big Four Face New Challenges: Marin Cilic's victory over Kei Nishikori at the US Open, along with Stan Wawrinka's Australian Open win, marked the first season since 2003 in which two men's singles Grand Slams were won by players outside Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal, Novak Djokovic, or Andy Murray. Injuries to Nadal (wrist) and Murray (back surgery recovery) contributed to this shift. Even Cilic acknowledged that opportunities opened due to the top players' struggles. Whether this signals the end of the Big Four's dominance remains to be seen. 3. Federer's Resurgence: After injury setbacks in 2013, Federer returned to form in 2014, reaching at least the semifinals at three majors and narrowly missing an 18th Grand Slam at Wimbledon. His tactics, including more net approaches, have increased his effectiveness and may extend his career. Although Federer didn't win a major this year, Switzerland is poised for a Davis Cup victory, potentially adding to his already impressive achievements. 4. Nadal Overcomes a Rocky Clay Season: Despite a less dominant clay-court campaign, Nadal captured another French Open crown, defeating Djokovic in the final. His only clay-court title leading up to Roland Garros was in Madrid, where Nishikori retired with injury. Nevertheless, Nadal's winning record at the French Open remains unblemished. Djokovic also experienced a mixed year—winning Wimbledon but falling to Nishikori in the US Open semifinals, affected by challenging conditions. 5. Grand Slam Variety: Eight different singles players won Grand Slam titles this year, a rarity seen only twice previously in the Open Era (1990, 1998). Serena Williams secured her 18th major by triumphing at the US Open, but failed to reach the quarterfinals at the other Slams, opening opportunities for new finalists like Dominika Cibulkova, Simona Halep, Eugenie Bouchard, and a return for Caroline Wozniacki. With end-of-year championships still to be decided, 2014 has proven to be a season of surprises and shifting fortunes.
translated_content: La stagione tennistica 2014 è stata una delle più imprevedibili degli ultimi anni, con nuovi campioni, diversi finalisti inediti e leggende determinate a riconquistare la gloria. Sebbene i quattro tornei dello Slam si siano conclusi, i posti nei tornei di fine anno sono ancora in palio sia tra gli uomini che tra le donne. Prima dello sprint finale della stagione, vale la pena ripensare ai tornei più importanti e a ciò che ci hanno insegnato. 1. Sharapova, regina della terra rossa: Maria Sharapova ha mostrato talento su tutte le superfici, ma dal 2010 ha conquistato 10 titoli, di cui solo due non sulla terra battuta. Negli Slam ha vinto due volte il Roland Garros e raggiunto altre tre finali a Parigi, senza però disputare altre finali Slam dopo gli Australian Open 2012. La sua corsa a Parigi quest'anno è stata il punto più brillante dopo risultati meno brillanti a Melbourne, Londra e New York. Con una settimana extra tra il Roland Garros e Wimbledon nell’anno prossimo, Sharapova potrebbe prepararsi meglio per la stagione sull’erba. 2. I Big Four in difficoltà: La vittoria di Marin Cilic su Kei Nishikori agli US Open, unita al successo di Stan Wawrinka agli Australian Open, ha reso il 2014 la prima stagione dal 2003 in cui due Slam maschili sono stati vinti da giocatori diversi dai Big Four (Federer, Nadal, Djokovic, Murray). Gli infortuni di Nadal (polso) e Murray (riabilitazione dopo l’operazione alla schiena) hanno avuto un ruolo importante. Anche Cilic ha ammesso che alcune opportunità si sono aperte grazie ai problemi dei top player. Se sia davvero la fine del dominio del quartetto, lo scopriremo solo nei prossimi anni. 3. Il ritorno di Federer: Dopo i problemi fisici del 2013, Federer è tornato al meglio nel 2014, centrando almeno le semifinali in tre Slam e sfiorando il 18° titolo a Wimbledon. Le sue nuove strategie a rete aumentano la sua efficacia e potrebbero allungare la sua carriera. Nonostante nessuna vittoria Slam quest'anno, la Svizzera è favorita per la Coppa Davis, che arricchirebbe ulteriormente il suo palmarès. 4. Nadal trionfa nonostante le difficoltà sulla terra: Pur vivendo una stagione sulla terra meno dominante, Nadal ha conquistato ancora il Roland Garros battendo Djokovic in finale. L’unico titolo su terra prima del torneo parigino era arrivato a Madrid, dove Nishikori si è ritirato causa infortunio. Il record di Nadal a Parigi resta perfetto. Anche Djokovic ha vissuto alti e bassi: vittoria a Wimbledon e sconfitta in semifinale agli US Open contro Nishikori, complice il caldo impartito in campo. 5. Tanta varietà negli Slam: Otto campioni diversi hanno conquistato i titoli singolari quest’anno nei Major, evento già capitato solo due volte nell’era Open (1990, 1998). Serena Williams ha vinto il suo 18° Slam agli US Open, ma non ha raggiunto i quarti negli altri tornei, lasciando spazio a nuove protagoniste come Dominika Cibulkova, Simona Halep, Eugenie Bouchard e al ritorno di Caroline Wozniacki. Con i Masters di fine anno ancora incerti, il 2014 si conferma una stagione ricca di colpi di scena.

article_content: Canada has been named the safest country to travel to in 2024, according to a report from Berkshire Hathaway Travel Protection. The “Safest Destinations” report, now in its ninth year, evaluates countries and cities worldwide based on a variety of safety factors. These include protection from terrorism, natural disasters, strong infrastructure, healthcare quality, and the experiences of underrepresented travelers such as people of color and LGBTQ+ individuals. This year, the top three safest countries are Canada, Switzerland, and Norway. Notably, Japan and Brazil have also entered the top 15 list, with Brazil rising from 42nd place last year. For cities, Honolulu (Hawaii), Montreal (Quebec), and Reykjavik (Iceland) rank as the safest. However, Iceland recently declared a state of emergency due to increased seismic activity around the Fagradalsfjall volcano, highlighting that unexpected events may not be fully reflected in the rankings. The report also emphasizes that its findings are predictive and do not account for all possible natural disasters. Berkshire Hathaway Travel Protection’s rankings are compiled using a survey of 1,702 travelers, who must have visited the countries or cities they rated within the past five years. Third-party data from the Global Peace Index, U.S. State Department, and GeoSure Global are also considered, measuring factors like women’s safety, theft, health risks, and basic freedoms. Manchester United, under manager Louis van Gaal, have struggled to meet expectations, with both performance levels and team morale under scrutiny. Preston North End’s experienced striker Kevin Davies has openly criticized United’s recent displays and intends to target their vulnerable defense when the sides meet in the FA Cup fifth round at Deepdale on Monday night.

Following United’s lackluster Premier League win over Burnley, van Gaal warned his team that a repeat performance could see them eliminated from the cup by their League One opponents. Davies, prepping with his teammates ahead of the clash, expressed doubts about the atmosphere at United. He observed that star players seem to lack enjoyment and suggests the team is still adapting to van Gaal's methods despite the club investing over £150 million in new talent last summer.

Fans are growing impatient with van Gaal’s style of play, and Davies senses that the players are not fully comfortable with the new regime. He pointed out Robin van Persie’s subdued celebration in the previous match and Wayne Rooney’s deeper role as evidence of this transitional discomfort. Davies noted that adapting to a new manager and routines—like increased tactical training or more intense sessions—takes time, especially after the long tenure of Sir Alex Ferguson.

United’s expensively assembled squad has not consistently lived up to expectations, and there’s frustration among supporters about the team’s less exciting playing style compared to the past. According to Davies, Manchester United’s defensive issues persist and, were it not for exceptional performances from goalkeeper David de Gea, the club might not be holding onto a top-four league position. He highlighted the rotating defensive line caused by injuries as a key weakness to exploit.

Davies believes United need to strengthen in defense to truly challenge Chelsea and Manchester City for the Premier League title in the future. He expects it will take van Gaal several transfer windows to reshape the squad and believes improvement will come in the next 6 to 12 months.

The article references manager Sam Allardyce’s previous comments about United’s long-ball tactics, and van Gaal’s statistical rebuttal, to which Davies responded lightheartedly. Davies also laments United’s 1999 withdrawal from the FA Cup, viewing it as a blow to the competition's status, but reaffirms the trophy’s significance for him. He hopes Preston can cause an upset on Monday, recognizing the challenge posed by United’s talented lineup but confident in his team’s ability to exploit any weaknesses.

Davies concluded by highlighting the FA Cup’s enduring appeal, his own memorable runs in the competition, and his determination to test himself and his teammates against United’s high-profile players.

article_content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated on Sunday that India is quickly emerging as a major global player in the defence sector and that the capabilities of its security forces are consistently growing. Addressing soldiers after celebrating Diwali with security personnel stationed near the border, Modi emphasized that global circumstances have led to increased expectations from India. Modi, dressed in Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) uniform, said, 'At this important time, it is essential that India's borders are secure and that there is peace in the country. You play a vital role in achieving this.' He added, 'India remains safe as long as our brave soldiers stand guard at the borders like the Himalayas.' Reflecting on the armed forces' contributions after independence, Modi remarked that soldiers have fought in many wars and earned the nation’s respect, achieving victories despite significant challenges. He acknowledged the sacrifices made by soldiers who spend festivals away from their families, expressing the nation’s indebtedness to them. 'During Diwali, one lamp is lit for your safety, and you are remembered in every prayer,' Modi said. Modi shared that for the last 30-35 years, he has celebrated Diwali with security forces in border areas, even before becoming Prime Minister or Chief Minister. He praised the soldiers for risking their lives and remaining the strongest line of defense at the borders. 'For me, any place where our security forces are present is as sacred as a temple,' Modi declared. The prime minister also commended the armed forces for their role in rescue operations during earthquakes and other emergencies, highlighting their bravery in missions such as evacuation operations in Sudan and earthquake relief in Turkiye. He reiterated that wherever Indians face danger, the security forces are always committed to ensuring their safety. 'We are proud of our armed forces and soldiers,' Modi concluded. Elsewhere in India, corporate companies are celebrating Diwali by distributing gift hampers, sustainable products, electronic gadgets, and silver coins to employees, including third-party and blue-collar workers. Legal experts note that several industries, including banks, healthcare, and telecom, are concerned that India’s new data law may restrict their ability to use consumer data for cross-selling products and services. Moody’s Investors Service downgraded its outlook on the US credit rating from ‘stable’ to ‘negative,’ citing large fiscal deficits and reduced debt affordability. This move drew immediate criticism from President Joe Biden’s administration.

article_content: Australian Indigenous leaders say their communities’ 60,000-year connection to the land deserves recognition. The upcoming Australian referendum on a constitutionally enshrined Indigenous Voice to Parliament is the latest step in a long history of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander advocacy for representation. The referendum follows the Uluru Statement from the Heart, a petition from Indigenous leaders seeking to establish a First Nations Voice in Australia’s constitution. This is part of a broader movement for Voice, Treaty, and Truth—processes aimed at recognition, agreement-making, and historical accountability—which have seen limited progress nationwide. Unlike countries such as New Zealand, Australia has not signed treaties with its Indigenous peoples. Indigenous authors of the Uluru Statement emphasize their peoples’ 60,000-year ancestral ties to land as a ‘sacred link’ that should not be erased from history by only two centuries of colonization. As Australians prepare to vote on October 14, the article reviews key milestones in the struggle for Indigenous rights. Murujuga, in Western Australia, is home to an estimated one million ancient petroglyphs, recording animal species—including extinct ones—painted by Indigenous artists since before the last Ice Age. Traditional owners fear modern industrial projects threaten these artworks. The Gunditjmara people have oral traditions describing volcanic eruptions 30,000 years ago; their Budj Bim aquaculture system, over 6,600 years old, received UNESCO World Heritage status in 2019. January 26 marks the 1788 arrival of Captain James Cook and the British First Fleet in Botany Bay, now celebrated as Australia Day, but also protested as ‘Invasion Day’ by many. Key demands for Indigenous representation date back to William Cooper’s 1937 petition to King George VI, seeking parliamentary representation, citizenship, and land rights. Australian federation occurred in 1901, but the British monarch remains head of state via the governor-general. On January 26, 1938, Indigenous activists staged a Day of Mourning, demanding equality and protesting colonial injustices. Although Indigenous Australians gained federal voting rights in 1962, disparities persist, including overrepresentation in the prison system. The Yolngu people’s 1963 bark petitions protested mining on traditional lands. The 1965 Freedom Ride, led by Charlie Perkins, challenged segregation in rural towns. The Aboriginal Tent Embassy, established in 1972 in Canberra, continues as a site of protest. Major demonstrations were held during the 1982 Commonwealth Games and the 1988 bicentennial. The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission (ATSIC), founded in 1995, gave Indigenous peoples formal governmental inclusion before its 2005 abolition. A Voice to Parliament, if constitutionally established, would require a referendum for any future abolition. The band Yothu Yindi’s 1991 protest song ‘Treaty’ followed stalled Treaty commitments by the government. In 1992, the High Court’s Mabo decision overturned the claim of ‘terra nullius’ and recognized limited native title. Yet, these laws do not equate to treaty agreements. On February 13, 2008, Prime Minister Kevin Rudd formally apologized to the Stolen Generations—Indigenous children removed from their families by state policy. That year’s Federal Parliament session opened with a Welcome to Country ceremony. In 2017, the Uluru Statement from the Heart was drafted by delegates at the First Nations National Constitutional Convention and became the catalyst for the planned 2023 Voice referendum, also calling for truth-telling mechanisms. In 2021, Victoria established the Yoorrook Justice Commission, Australia’s first official truth-telling body, recording testimonies on dispossession and resistance. Victoria and Queensland are taking separate steps toward treaties. In 2020, Senator Lidia Thorpe entered parliament wearing a possum skin cloak, marking her pride as the first Aboriginal Victorian Senator. Though most Indigenous people support the Voice, Thorpe argues that Treaty and Truth processes should precede it. The 2023 referendum on an Indigenous Voice to Parliament has prompted significant national debate, with disinformation and racism clouding the campaign. Polls indicate the proposal may not receive broad support.

Il prossimo referendum australiano su una Voice indigena in Parlamento inserita nella Costituzione rappresenta l’ultima tappa di una lunga storia di attivismo e richiesta di rappresentanza da parte degli aborigeni e degli isolani dello Stretto di Torres. Il referendum segue la Dichiarazione di Uluru dal Cuore, una petizione dei leader indigeni per istituire una Voice delle Prime Nazioni nella Costituzione dell’Australia. Questo fa parte di un movimento più ampio per Voice, Treaty e Truth—processi volti al riconoscimento, alla stipula di accordi e alla responsabilità storica—che hanno registrato progressi limitati a livello nazionale. A differenza di Paesi come la Nuova Zelanda, l’Australia non ha mai firmato trattati con i propri popoli indigeni. Gli autori indigeni della Dichiarazione di Uluru sottolineano i loro legami ancestrali di 60.000 anni con la terra come un “legame sacro” che non dovrebbe essere cancellato dalla storia da soli due secoli di colonizzazione. Mentre gli australiani si preparano a votare il 14 ottobre, l’articolo ripercorre tappe fondamentali nella lotta per i diritti indigeni. Murujuga, nell’Australia Occidentale, ospita circa un milione di antichi petroglifi che raffigurano specie animali—anche estinte—dipingendo la storia indigena fin dall’ultima era glaciale. I proprietari tradizionali temono che progetti industriali moderni possano mettere a rischio queste opere. Il popolo Gunditjmara conserva tradizioni orali che descrivono eruzioni vulcaniche risalenti a 30.000 anni fa; il loro sistema di acquacoltura di Budj Bim, vecchio oltre 6.600 anni, ha ottenuto il riconoscimento UNESCO nel 2019. Il 26 gennaio segna l’arrivo nel 1788 del Capitano James Cook e della Prima Flotta britannica nella Botany Bay, oggi celebrato come Australia Day ma anche contestato da molti come 'Invasion Day'. Le richieste di rappresentanza indigena risalgono almeno alla petizione di William Cooper del 1937 indirizzata al re Giorgio VI, nella quale si chiedevano rappresentanza parlamentare, cittadinanza e diritti fondiari. La federazione australiana ebbe luogo nel 1901, ma il monarca britannico resta capo di stato tramite il governatore generale. Il 26 gennaio 1938, attivisti indigeni organizzarono un Day of Mourning chiedendo uguaglianza e protestando contro le ingiustizie coloniali. Anche se gli aborigeni ottennero il diritto di voto federale nel 1962, permangono disparità, tra cui la sovra-rappresentazione nelle carceri. Le bark petitions del popolo Yolngu nel 1963 protestavano contro l’attività mineraria su terre tradizionali. La Freedom Ride del 1965, guidata da Charlie Perkins, contestò la segregazione nelle città rurali. L’Aboriginal Tent Embassy, fondata nel 1972 a Canberra, continua ad essere un punto di protesta. Grandi manifestazioni si svolsero durante i Giochi del Commonwealth del 1982 e il bicentenario del 1988. La Commissione Aborigena e degli isolani dello Stretto di Torres (ATSIC), fondata nel 1995, permise una parziale inclusione nelle decisioni di governo, ma fu abolita nel 2005. Una Voice to Parliament, se inserita in Costituzione, richiederebbe un referendum per una eventuale abolizione futura. La band Yothu Yindi pubblicò nel 1991 la canzone di protesta 'Treaty' dopo la mancata attuazione degli impegni governativi su un trattato. Nel 1992, la sentenza Mabo della Corte Suprema revocò il concetto di 'terra nullius', riconoscendo un titolo nativo limitato. Tuttavia, queste leggi non equivalgono a trattati. Il 13 febbraio 2008, il Primo Ministro Kevin Rudd chiese formalmente scusa alle Stolen Generations—bambini indigeni rimossi forzatamente dalle famiglie per politiche statali. Quell’anno, la sessione parlamentare si aprì per la prima volta con una cerimonia di Welcome to Country. Nel 2017, la Dichiarazione di Uluru dal Cuore fu redatta dai delegati della First Nations National Constitutional Convention e divenne la base per il referendum sulla Voice previsto per il 2023, richiedendo anche meccanismi di verità storica. Nel 2021, lo stato di Victoria ha istituito la Yoorrook Justice Commission, la prima commissione di verità ufficiale australiana, raccogliendo testimonianze su espropri e resistenza. Victoria e Queensland stanno anche seguendo percorsi separati verso trattati. Nel 2020, la senatrice Lidia Thorpe è entrata in Parlamento indossando un mantello di pelle di possum, sottolineando il suo orgoglio come prima senatrice aborigena del Victoria. Sebbene la maggioranza degli indigeni sostenga la Voice, Thorpe sostiene che Treaty e Truth dovrebbero venire prima. Il referendum 2023 sulla Voice indigena al Parlamento ha acceso il dibattito nazionale, tra disinformazione e razzismo. I sondaggi indicano che la proposta potrebbe non ottenere un ampio consenso.

article_content: Determining the exact proportion of computers running Apple’s OS X can be challenging, but it’s clear that OS X has steadily gained ground while Microsoft Windows remains the major player in desktop and laptop operating systems, securing its dominance since the 1990s. Estimates suggest OS X now commands about 6–7% of the desktop market. While Apple’s OS has not overtaken Windows, it has surpassed Linux in the desktop market. Linux remains a strong force on servers but rarely sees mainstream desktop or laptop use. Despite some recent growth, Linux still hasn’t achieved the widespread adoption its advocates have hoped for. One reason for Linux’s limited desktop presence is the fragmentation among its available interfaces, such as GNOME, Unity, and Xfce. In 2010, Canonical replaced GNOME with its own Unity interface in Ubuntu, generating backlash among many Linux users. High-profile figures like Linus Torvalds openly criticized GNOME’s direction and moved to Xfce, prompting similar decisions from distributions like Ubuntu Studio and Debian. Miguel de Icaza, a key Linux developer and original GNOME co-creator, attributes Linux’s struggle partly to technical issues, particularly a lack of consistent backward compatibility in Linux development tools. This situation led many engineers to switch from Linux to other platforms like OS X or turn to web development, where Apple excelled at supporting old and new software side by side. As web technologies evolved, the open source movement’s emphasis shifted from desktop software to web development. Open-source platforms like Apache, Nginx, PHP, Ruby on Rails, Hadoop, and MongoDB now power much of the global internet infrastructure. Steve Ballmer, former Microsoft CEO, even recognized Linux’s power in the server market, and open-source tools drive the majority of online experiences. Today, open source advocates are channeling efforts into promoting transparency and user autonomy on the web. Stormy Peters, previously with the GNOME Foundation and now at Mozilla, is among those focusing on data transparency and user control online. Mozilla’s Persona project, for example, seeks to enhance privacy and security for internet users. The explosion of mobile internet access has further altered the landscape, with many first-time web users coming online via smartphones. Mozilla has responded with initiatives like Boot to Gecko, an open-source mobile OS, and the Mozilla Marketplace, which hosts web apps accessible wherever Firefox can run. Meanwhile, de Icaza’s Mono project continues to expand, enabling Microsoft’s .NET languages to function on platforms including Android and iOS. At the same time, desktop environments like GNOME persist in evolving, aiming to enhance both user and developer experiences with every version.

Secondo le stime, OS X ora detiene circa il 6–7% del mercato desktop. Sebbene il sistema operativo di Apple non abbia superato Windows, ha comunque superato Linux nel mercato desktop. Linux continua a dominare tra i server ma è raramente adottato dal grande pubblico su desktop o portatili. Nonostante una crescita recente, Linux non ha ancora raggiunto la diffusione sperata dai suoi sostenitori. Uno dei motivi della diffusione limitata di Linux sui desktop è la frammentazione tra le sue interfacce grafiche, come GNOME, Unity e Xfce. Nel 2010 Canonical ha sostituito GNOME con Unity su Ubuntu, scelta accolta con molte critiche dagli utenti Linux. Figure di spicco come Linus Torvalds hanno espresso apertamente il proprio dissenso nei confronti di GNOME, passando a Xfce, una decisione seguita anche da distribuzioni come Ubuntu Studio e Debian. Miguel de Icaza, importante sviluppatore Linux e co-creatore di GNOME, attribuisce le difficoltà di Linux anche a problematiche tecniche, in particolare alla scarsa compatibilità retroattiva degli strumenti di sviluppo. Questo ha portato molti ingegneri a migrare verso altre piattaforme come OS X o verso lo sviluppo web, dove Apple eccelleva nel supportare sia software nuovo che legacy. Con l'evoluzione delle tecnologie web, l'attenzione del movimento open source si è spostata dai software desktop allo sviluppo web. Soluzioni open source come Apache, Nginx, PHP, Ruby on Rails, Hadoop e MongoDB ora alimentano una parte fondamentale dell’infrastruttura internet globale. Steve Ballmer, ex CEO di Microsoft, ha perfino riconosciuto il predominio di Linux nel mercato dei server, con strumenti open source che alimentano la maggior parte delle esperienze online. Oggi i sostenitori dell’open source si impegnano a promuovere trasparenza e controllo degli utenti sul web. Stormy Peters, ex GNOME Foundation e attualmente a Mozilla, è tra coloro che si concentrano su trasparenza dei dati e controllo dell’utente online. Ad esempio, il progetto Mozilla Persona mira a migliorare privacy e sicurezza degli utenti della rete. La crescita dell’accesso a internet tramite dispositivi mobili ha ulteriormente cambiato lo scenario, con molti nuovi utenti che si connettono per la prima volta tramite smartphone. Mozilla ha risposto con progetti come Boot to Gecko, un sistema operativo mobile open source, e il Mozilla Marketplace, che propone app web accessibili ovunque ci sia Firefox. Nel frattempo, Mono di de Icaza continua a espandersi, portando i linguaggi .NET di Microsoft su piattaforme come Android e iOS. Parallelamente, ambienti desktop come GNOME continuano ad evolversi, puntando a migliorare sia l’esperienza degli utenti che degli sviluppatori.

article_content: On Saturday, October 7, Singapore experienced a decline in air quality, with pollution levels moving into the unhealthy range. This situation was attributed to haze caused by an increased number of hotspots in Indonesia. As reported by the National Environment Agency (NEA), at 4pm, the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) reached 119 in eastern Singapore and 110 in the central zone. According to the NEA, PSI readings between 101 and 200 are considered unhealthy. Additionally, one-hour PM2.5 readings were elevated, at 90 for the east and 94 for the central region, within the 'elevated' range of 56 to 150.

Secondo quanto riportato dalla National Environment Agency (NEA), alle 16:00 l'indice di inquinamento atmosferico (PSI) su 24 ore era di 119 nella parte est e di 110 nella zona centrale di Singapore. La NEA definisce valori PSI tra 101 e 200 come non salutari. Anche le letture orarie del PM2.5 erano elevate: 90 a est e 94 al centro, valori che rientrano nella fascia 'elevata' tra 56 e 150.

article_content: COLUMBIA, S.C. – The third Republican presidential debate will feature the smallest group of candidates so far, with only five hopefuls taking the stage Wednesday night at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts of Miami-Dade County, according to the Republican National Committee (RNC). To qualify for this debate, candidates needed at least 4% support in either two national polls or in one national poll plus two polls from four early-voting states: Iowa, New Hampshire, Nevada, and South Carolina. All polls used had to be approved by the RNC. Hopefuls also needed at least 70,000 unique donors, including 200 or more from at least 20 different states or territories, and had to sign a pledge agreeing to support the eventual Republican nominee. These stricter requirements have made it increasingly difficult to qualify. Former Vice President Mike Pence suspended his campaign last month rather than fail to make the stage. Here’s where each candidate stands: RON DESANTIS: Florida's governor was once seen as the main challenger to Donald Trump, finishing a distant second in most early and national polls but raising significant funds. DeSantis has moved some staff from Florida to Iowa, focusing his campaign on that key state. This week, he secured the endorsement of Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds. TIM SCOTT: The South Carolina senator has looked to the debates as a chance to boost his campaign, which has struggled compared to some rivals. There was uncertainty about whether he would meet the higher qualification standards for Miami. In a memo to the Associated Press, Scott’s campaign manager highlighted distinctions between Scott, DeSantis, and Haley, questioning how the others could truly contrast with Trump. NIKKI HALEY: Haley, the only Republican woman in the field, has seen increased attention after previous debates and a heightened focus on foreign policy following Hamas' October 7 attack on Israel. She and DeSantis have exchanged criticisms on issues including the Israel-Hamas conflict and China, making this debate a notable opportunity for a direct exchange. VIVEK RAMASWAMY: The newcomer and youngest candidate has often been the target of attacks over his lack of political experience, which, in turn, have helped raise his profile and fundraising. After September’s debate, he asked the RNC to limit the next debate to four participants and raise the donor bar to 100,000, but the party left its criteria unchanged. CHRIS CHRISTIE: As some rivals focus on Iowa, former New Jersey Governor Christie has targeted New Hampshire, positioning himself as Trump’s main critic and arguing that only he directly challenges Trump. He has continued to mention Trump in debates despite Trump’s absence, once calling him 'Donald Duck' on national TV. DONALD TRUMP: The GOP front-runner is skipping his third straight debate, instead holding an event of his own nearby in Hialeah, Florida. Trump says he skips debates because he doesn't want to elevate lower-polling opponents. DOUG BURGUM: North Dakota Governor Doug Burgum, a former software entrepreneur now in his second term, did not meet polling requirements and will miss his first debate. ASA HUTCHINSON: The former Arkansas governor participated in the first debate but missed the last two. He stated his goal was to reach 4% in an early state before Thanksgiving to stay competitive. ___ Reporter Meg Kinnard can be contacted at http://twitter.com/MegKinnardAP

article_content: On Thursday evening, Sam Altman attended a warehouse event in Oakland where he spoke with a group of artists about generative AI. article_content: YouTube has announced updated policies aimed at tackling the growing presence of AI-generated music that imitates real artists' voices and styles. Earlier this year, the AI-composed song 'Heart on My Sleeve', which closely resembled the work of Drake and The Weeknd, gained over 600,000 streams and was even considered for a Grammy nomination. In a blog post, YouTube revealed it will now allow its music partners to request the removal of AI-generated music content that closely mimics an artist’s unique singing or rapping voice. The rapid advancement of generative AI technology has shocked the music world, with high-quality songs that are often indistinguishable from the originals. In one notable case, a fan unknowingly paid over $4,000 on Discord for an AI-generated Frank Ocean track, believing it to be authentic. While YouTube aims to address these issues directly, concerns remain about whether the platform has the necessary tools to enforce its policy effectively. YouTube will reportedly weigh whether news outlets report on generative AI songs and consider analysis or critique of synthetic vocals in its decisions about content takedown. Additionally, YouTube will require creators to clearly disclose when they’ve used AI to alter content, with labels appearing on affected videos. However, these strategies rely heavily on creator honesty and public reporting, potentially allowing problematic songs to go viral before any action is taken. YouTube acknowledges that some bad actors will attempt to bypass these new protections but commits to integrating user feedback and continuously refining safety measures. The company’s policies mark a shift from earlier reported plans to develop a tool allowing users to license artists’ voices for music creation, as negotiations with major labels like Sony Music and Universal Music Group reportedly fell through. Currently, YouTube is leveraging AI classifiers alongside a team of 20,000 Google reviewers to enforce its Community Guidelines, emphasizing improvements in speed and accuracy for content moderation.

article_content: KATHMANDU, Nepal — Survivors of a powerful earthquake that struck northwest Nepal at midnight described sudden, violent shaking, followed by homes collapsing and burying families as the death toll rose to 157 on Saturday. Most victims were crushed by debris when their houses—typically constructed by stacking rocks and logs—crumbled under the force of the tremor late Friday, according to local media. Rescue efforts were complicated by the mountainous terrain, as many villages could only be reached on foot, and roads were blocked by landslides triggered by the earthquake. Soldiers worked to clear the obstructions. The government is working to deliver as much aid as possible to affected areas, Deputy Prime Minister Narayan Kaji Shrestha announced on Saturday. Tents, food, and medicine were airlifted as thousands were left homeless overnight. Bimal Kumar Karki, one of the first people brought to the regional hospital, said, “I was fast asleep when everything started shaking violently. I tried to run, but the whole house collapsed. I tried escaping but was buried up to half my body in debris. I screamed, but all my neighbors were in the same situation, screaming for help. It took about half an hour to an hour for rescuers to find me.” Another injured man, Tika Ram Rana, recovering in the hospital with his head wrapped in bandages, recounted, “I was asleep around 10 or 11 at night when it started shaking and my house caved in. So many houses have collapsed and so many people have been buried.” Besides delivering aid, rescuers focused on searching for more survivors. Local television broadcast footage of troops recovering bodies while others helped to dig out and carry the wounded. The U.S. Geological Survey reported the earthquake had a preliminary magnitude of 5.6 at a depth of 11 miles (18 kilometers). Nepal’s National Earthquake Monitoring and Research Center said the epicenter was Jajarkot, about 400 kilometers (250 miles) northeast of Kathmandu. Officials confirmed at least 105 people dead in Jajarkot district—a mainly agricultural area—and 52 in neighboring Rukum district. Another 184 people were injured. Security personnel, alongside villagers, worked through the night to rescue the dead and wounded from collapsed homes. Authorities warned that the death toll could rise as communications remained down in many areas. More than 100 beds were prepared at the regional hospital in Nepalgunj, with medical teams on standby to treat the injured. Alongside rescue helicopters, small government and army aircraft were used to transport the injured to Nepalgunj. Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal arrived by helicopter with a medical team. Dahal had previously led an armed communist revolt from 1996 to 2006 which began in districts affected by the earthquake. The quake, which occurred while most people were asleep in their homes, was also felt in New Delhi, India, more than 800 kilometers (500 miles) away. Earthquakes are common in Nepal’s mountainous regions. A magnitude 7.8 earthquake in 2015 killed about 9,000 people and damaged around 1 million structures. Neighboring India has offered rescue assistance. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted on social media expressing deep sorrow over the lives lost and damage caused by the earthquake in Nepal, stating, “India stands in solidarity with the people of Nepal and is ready to extend all possible assistance.”
translated_content: KATHMANDU, Nepal — I sopravvissuti a un potente terremoto che ha colpito il nord-ovest del Nepal a mezzanotte hanno descritto violente scosse improvvise, seguite dal crollo delle case che hanno seppellito intere famiglie, mentre il bilancio delle vittime è salito a 157 sabato. La maggior parte delle vittime è rimasta schiacciata sotto le macerie quando le loro abitazioni—solitamente realizzate impilando pietre e tronchi—sono crollate a causa della scossa avvenuta nella tarda serata di venerdì, secondo i media locali. I soccorsi sono stati complicati dal terreno montuoso, poiché molti villaggi sono accessibili solo a piedi e le strade sono state bloccate da frane provocate dal terremoto. I soldati hanno lavorato per liberare le vie ostruite. Il governo sta cercando di fornire il maggior aiuto possibile alle zone colpite, ha annunciato sabato il vice primo ministro Narayan Kaji Shrestha. Tende, cibo e medicine sono stati trasportati per via aerea mentre migliaia di persone sono rimaste senza tetto durante la notte. Bimal Kumar Karki, tra i primi portati all’ospedale regionale, ha detto: “Stavo dormendo profondamente quando tutto ha iniziato a tremare violentemente. Ho provato a scappare, ma tutta la casa è crollata. Ho cercato di uscire ma ero sepolto fino a metà corpo tra le macerie. Ho urlato, ma anche i miei vicini erano nella stessa situazione, gridando aiuto. Ci è voluta circa mezz’ora o un’ora prima che i soccorritori mi trovassero.” Un altro ferito, Tika Ram Rana, ricoverato in ospedale con la testa fasciata, ha raccontato: “Stavo dormendo verso le 10 o le 11 di sera quando ha iniziato a tremare e la mia casa è crollata. Tante case sono crollate e molte persone sono state sepolte.” Oltre alla consegna degli aiuti, i soccorritori si sono concentrati sulla ricerca di altri sopravvissuti. La televisione locale ha trasmesso immagini di truppe che recuperano corpi mentre altri aiutavano a estrarre e trasportare i feriti. Il Servizio geologico degli Stati Uniti ha riferito che il terremoto ha avuto una magnitudo preliminare di 5.6 a una profondità di 18 chilometri (11 miglia). Il Centro nazionale per il monitoraggio e la ricerca sui terremoti del Nepal ha dichiarato che l’epicentro era a Jajarkot, circa 400 chilometri a nord-est di Kathmandu. I funzionari hanno confermato almeno 105 morti nel distretto di Jajarkot—principalmente agricolo—e 52 nel vicino distretto di Rukum. Altre 184 persone sono rimaste ferite. Le forze di sicurezza, insieme agli abitanti dei villaggi, hanno lavorato tutta la notte per salvare i vivi e recuperare i corpi dalle case crollate. Le autorità hanno avvertito che il numero delle vittime potrebbe aumentare poiché le comunicazioni sono ancora interrotte in molte zone. Più di 100 letti sono stati preparati all’ospedale regionale di Nepalgunj, con squadre mediche pronte ad assistere i feriti. Oltre agli elicotteri di soccorso, piccoli aerei governativi e dell’esercito sono stati utilizzati per trasportare i feriti a Nepalgunj. Il primo ministro Pushpa Kamal Dahal è arrivato in elicottero con un team medico. Dahal, in passato, aveva guidato una rivolta comunista armata dal 1996 al 2006, iniziata proprio nei distretti colpiti dal terremoto. La scossa, verificatasi mentre la maggior parte della popolazione dormiva in casa, è stata avvertita anche a Nuova Delhi, India, a oltre 800 chilometri di distanza. I terremoti sono comuni nelle aree montuose del Nepal. Nel 2015, un sisma di magnitudo 7.8 uccise circa 9.000 persone e danneggiò circa 1 milione di strutture. L’India, paese confinante, ha offerto assistenza per i soccorsi. Il primo ministro indiano Narendra Modi ha espresso sui social media il suo profondo dolore per le vite perse e i danni causati dal terremoto in Nepal, affermando: “L’India è solidale con il popolo nepalese ed è pronta a offrire tutta l’assistenza possibile.”

article_content:
Carmen Figueroa, a detective with Arizona’s Department of Public Safety, resigned after it was revealed she was living in the United States without legal status. Figueroa had believed she was born in the U.S., only finding out recently that she was actually born in Sinaloa, Mexico—a fact her family kept from her since childhood. Her undocumented status came to light during her brother’s military-related passport application, which prompted further background checks. 

Arizona law requires all state police officers to be U.S. citizens. Department spokesperson Bart Graves stated Figueroa would have been dismissed for failing to meet this requirement and for possible misrepresentation, had she not resigned. The 42-year-old detective had worked for ten years as a Highway Patrol officer in southern Arizona and became a criminal investigations detective in 2010. Graves noted her exemplary professional record and confirmed the situation would not compromise any ongoing investigations or prosecutions. 

After the discovery, Figueroa was placed on administrative leave with pay and resigned soon afterward as her termination appeared inevitable. Previously, she held positions as a secretary with the federal Bureau of Prisons and in the Pima County court system. When hired by the state police, she provided documents—a Texas birth certificate, a California driver’s license, and a high school diploma—all of which seemed legitimate at the time. Authorities are now reviewing how documents are verified to prevent similar incidents in the future.

La sua situazione è venuta alla luce quando il fratello, militare, ha richiesto il passaporto, facendo emergere la necessità di ulteriori controlli sullo sfondo familiare.

La legge dell’Arizona impone che tutti gli agenti della polizia statale siano cittadini americani. Bart Graves, portavoce del Dipartimento, ha dichiarato che Figueroa sarebbe stata licenziata per mancato rispetto di questo requisito e per possibile dichiarazione falsa, se non si fosse dimessa lei stessa. La detective, 42 anni, ha prestato servizio per dieci anni come agente della Highway Patrol nel sud dell'Arizona ed è diventata detective delle indagini criminali nel 2010. Graves ha evidenziato la sua carriera esemplare e ha confermato che l'accaduto non comprometterà nessuna indagine o processo in corso.

Dopo la scoperta, Figueroa è stata sospesa retribuita e si è dimessa poco dopo, dato che il licenziamento era ormai inevitabile. In passato aveva lavorato come segretaria presso il Bureau of Prisons federale e nel tribunale della contea di Pima. All’assunzione aveva fornito un certificato di nascita texano, una patente californiana e un diploma di scuola superiore, documenti che sembravano regolari all’epoca. Ora le autorità stanno riesaminando le procedure di verifica dei documenti per evitare casi simili in futuro.

article_content: Val Armstrong, a veteran BBC radio presenter from Carlisle, Cumbria, successfully challenged the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) after they inaccurately deemed her fit to work when she was recovering from breast cancer. After being diagnosed with breast cancer for a second time in August 2010, Armstrong underwent a double mastectomy and underwent intense chemotherapy, which left her suffering severe side effects like pain and insomnia. As a result, she was unable to work for two years. Although she had a valid sick note, the DWP placed Armstrong in a work-related activity group, assuming she was close to returning to work. Following a work capability assessment in March 2012, she was given zero points—well below the 15-point requirement for full Employment Support Allowance (ESA). In April, her weekly benefits were cut from £96 to £71, adding financial pressure. Having spent over 30 years at the BBC, Armstrong described the financial and emotional toll, noting that many in her situation might not have family or savings to rely on. With support from her Macmillan Cancer Support adviser, Armstrong appealed the DWP's decision, particularly since she also cared for her mother. After initially being denied again, she studied the rules and found that the DWP hadn't followed proper procedures. Armstrong brought her case to tribunal in April 2013 and won. She received backdated payments and was able to resume her job at BBC Cumbria. She encourages others facing similar situations to stand up for themselves and appeal if they feel unjustly treated. A spokesperson from the DWP stated that decisions are based on the medical evidence provided, but all claimants have the right to appeal.

Dopo essere stata diagnosticata per la seconda volta con un tumore al seno nell’agosto 2010, Armstrong si è dovuta sottoporre a una doppia mastectomia e a sessioni intensive di chemioterapia, che le hanno provocato dolore e insonnia. Questo l’ha costretta ad assentarsi dal lavoro per due anni. Nonostante un certificato medico valido, il DWP l’ha inserita in un gruppo di attività lavorativa, pensando fosse prossima al ritorno. Dopo una valutazione della capacità lavorativa nel marzo 2012, Armstrong ha ricevuto zero punti—ben sotto i 15 necessari per continuare a ricevere il Supporto al Reddito da Lavoro (ESA). Ad aprile, il suo sussidio è passato da 96 a 71 sterline a settimana, aggravando la sua situazione finanziaria. Con oltre trent’anni in BBC, Armstrong ha raccontato le difficoltà economiche ed emotive, osservando che molti non hanno una famiglia su cui contare. Con il supporto della sua consulente di Macmillan Cancer Support, Armstrong ha fatto ricorso contro la decisione del DWP, anche perché si prendeva cura della madre. Dopo un’ulteriore bocciatura, ha studiato le regole e scoperto che il DWP non aveva rispettato le proprie procedure. Nell’aprile 2013 Armstrong ha portato il caso davanti a un tribunale e ha vinto. Ha ottenuto i pagamenti arretrati e ha potuto riprendere il suo lavoro alla BBC Cumbria. Invita chi si trova in difficoltà simili a difendersi presentando ricorso se ritiene di non essere stato trattato correttamente. Un portavoce del DWP ha ribadito che le decisioni si basano sulle prove mediche fornite, ma ogni richiedente ha diritto al ricorso.

North Korea has announced it is ending an agreement aimed at reducing military tensions with South Korea, signaling that relations are deteriorating after Pyongyang successfully launched a spy satellite into orbit for the first time. According to the official Korean Central News Agency, North Korea stated that "our army will never be bound" by the 2018 accord and pledged to "immediately restore all military measures that have been halted." The report added that North Korea plans to deploy more powerful armed forces and new military hardware along the border with South Korea.

In response, South Korea has warned it will punish North Korea "immediately, strongly, and to the end" for any further provocations, according to a Defense Ministry spokesperson. Tensions have increased since North Korea's purportedly successful launch of a spy satellite, bringing leader Kim Jong Un closer to his goal of deploying reconnaissance probes to monitor U.S. forces in the region. Kim oversaw the latest launch, and state media reported that North Korea intends to launch several more satellites in the near future.

Further escalating the situation, North Korea fired a ballistic missile toward the sea east of the Korean Peninsula around 11:05 p.m. Wednesday, but the launch appears to have failed, according to South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff. Missile failures under Kim have been rare, with the last failure occurring about a year ago.

After the satellite launch, South Korea suspended parts of the 2018 deal aimed at reducing border tensions and approved a plan to restore reconnaissance and surveillance activities that were previously halted. South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff assessed that while the satellite did reach orbit, it remains unclear if it is fully operational.

Although officials in Seoul believe the satellite is likely rudimentary, they say it could help North Korea improve missile targeting, including for new systems designed to deliver nuclear strikes against South Korea and Japan, where most U.S. military personnel in the region are based. According to North Korean media, Kim Jong Un has viewed images of U.S. military facilities in Guam taken by the “Malligyong-1” satellite.

Marco Langbroek, a lecturer at the Delft University of Technology, noted that the technical aspects of the launch suggest North Korea is now capable of more complex launch scenarios and has developed a versatile rocket system.

The Group of Seven (G7) foreign ministers condemned North Korea’s ballistic missile launch, stating that it "poses a grave threat to the peace and stability of the region and beyond." The White House also condemned the launch and is working with allies to assess the situation, said National Security Council spokesperson Adrienne Watson. North Korea is prohibited by UN Security Council resolutions from conducting ballistic missile tests, and U.S. officials have warned that technology developed for the space program could be used to advance North Korea's ballistic missile capabilities.

Tesco, the UK's largest supermarket, is preparing to use data from its Clubcard loyalty program to personalize online shopping for each customer. Visitors to Tesco's website will see products recommended based on their previous shopping habits, highlighting items that match whether they typically choose premium or budget options. For instance, customers identified as preferring higher-end goods might see choices like smoked salmon, while those focused on value may notice offers on essentials such as canned beans.

This strategy follows a difficult year for Tesco, which has issued its first profit warning in twenty years amid increasing competition. Personalizing the digital shopping experience is part of Tesco’s attempt to bring back a sense of individualized service similar to that provided by local shops in the past.

Tesco CEO Phil Clarke said the plan is to make the Clubcard digital by tailoring website promotions to suit different customers. A recent test involved using Clubcard data to learn if a shopper prioritized price or quality when searching for mattresses, displaying the most relevant options. This trial achieved a 10% sales increase.

However, the idea is not without controversy. Some fear that shoppers could feel stereotyped or limited by being shown only certain products. Research suggests that shoppers often mix both premium and value items, regardless of their overall spending patterns.

Tesco’s broader digital initiatives include expanding free in-store wi-fi for Clubcard users, allowing smartphone shoppers to locate products and receive suggestions while walking through the store. Additionally, Tesco has experimented with interactive poster displays in subway stations in Korea, where commuters can shop by scanning barcodes and have their groceries delivered to their homes.

The company hopes these new technologies will enhance shopping convenience and restore a sense of personal service, both online and in stores.

Janelly Martinez-Amador, from Antioch, Tennessee, was born with the most severe form of hypophosphatasia, a rare genetic disorder that prevents bone mineralization. As a baby, she was in pain when held, could not move her limbs, and had no visible bones on X-rays. Her parents, Salvador Martinez and Janet Amador, grew concerned when she failed to grow or gain weight, prompting medical consultation. As her condition worsened, Janelly required a ventilator and a tracheotomy because she lacked enough rib structure to support breathing.

Hypophosphatasia is caused by an enzyme deficiency that stops bones from absorbing essential minerals like calcium and phosphorus, making them soft and fragile. It affects about one in 100,000 U.S. births, and, in its most severe form, more than half of affected infants do not survive past their first year. Possible symptoms include deformed limbs or chest, frequent fractures, and early tooth loss.

When Janelly was two years and eight months old, her parents enrolled her in a clinical trial at Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital at Vanderbilt, where she received an experimental enzyme therapy called asfotase alfa via a port in her abdomen. While other children in the study showed early improvement, Janelly’s progress was slow, raising concerns from Dr. Michael P. Whyte, a bone disorder specialist overseeing her care. Despite this, after a year, Janelly started to gain muscle control, and after 18 months, her ribs began to develop.

Over four years since starting treatment, Janelly no longer needs a ventilator, loves to dance, and enjoys music from her stroller. She still uses a wheelchair and remains smaller than peers her age, but her doctors remain hopeful. They plan to assess her cognitive abilities soon and may be able to remove her tracheotomy tube, giving her a chance to speak. Her recovery has inspired her family and medical team, representing a significant achievement in rare disease treatment.

article_content: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) announced on Monday that it will compel inspections of approximately 175 older Boeing 737 jets after a recent Southwest Airlines 737 experienced a fuselage rupture requiring an emergency landing. This emergency directive, to be issued on Tuesday, includes about 80 U.S.-registered 737-300, 737-400, and 737-500 models, primarily run by Southwest, and some 95 jets registered outside the United States. These planes, all of which have logged over 30,000 flights, will be subjected to regular electromagnetic examinations for signs of structural fatigue. Boeing is also preparing a service bulletin that recommends targeted lap joint inspections for certain 737 types, coordinating efforts with the FAA, the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), and Southwest. According to NTSB board member Robert Sumwalt, visual checks of lap joints were standard in the past, but now new advanced testing like electromagnetic scans will be adopted, since earlier assumptions held that these areas were not prone to cracking. Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Jay Rockefeller stressed the importance of maintaining public trust in airline safety and urged the FAA to be meticulous in reviewing aircraft and investigating the cause of these cracks. He appealed for speedy passage of an FAA reauthorization bill to improve inspection processes. Southwest Airlines canceled around 600 flights during the weekend—and 70 more on Monday—to complete the inspections. By Monday afternoon, 67 of 79 grounded planes were checked, with 64 cleared for service. Inspectors found hidden cracks on three aircraft, which will stay off the schedule until Boeing advises on repairs. All inspections are set for completion by late Tuesday, with the airline recommending that customers check flight status or rebook travel on their website. Last Friday, Flight 812 from Phoenix to Sacramento suffered a five-foot fuselage tear, leading to sudden cabin depressurization and a minor injury to a flight attendant. The pilot made an emergency landing at Yuma, Arizona’s military base after flight staff saw daylight through the torn roof. Several passengers recounted their fear as the event unfolded. Southwest compensated affected travelers with full refunds, apologies, and two free round-trip tickets for future use. A similar incident in July 2009 prompted the airline to inspect its whole fleet of 737-300s. Earlier that year, Southwest was fined $7.5 million for flying 46 Boeing 737s without mandatory checks for fuselage fatigue. Sumwalt noted that the jet involved in the latest incident had recently passed all maintenance checks and had clean records; the flight data recorders showed nothing unusual.

La direttiva d'emergenza, prevista per martedì, riguarda circa 80 modelli 737-300, 737-400 e 737-500 registrati negli Stati Uniti—principalmente gestiti da Southwest—oltre a circa 95 aerei registrati all'estero. Questi aeromobili, ciascuno con più di 30.000 voli all’attivo, saranno sottoposti a regolari controlli elettromagnetici per rilevare segni di fatica strutturale. Il pilota ha effettuato un atterraggio d’emergenza alla base militare di Yuma, Arizona, dopo che il personale ha visto la luce del sole entrare dal tetto squarciato. Diversi passeggeri hanno raccontato la loro paura durante quei momenti. Southwest ha risarcito i clienti coinvolti con rimborsi completi, scuse e due biglietti andata e ritorno gratuiti per viaggi futuri. Un episodio simile nel luglio 2009 aveva già spinto la compagnia a ispezionare tutta la flotta di 737-300. All’inizio dello stesso anno Southwest era stata multata di 7,5 milioni di dollari per aver fatto volare 46 Boeing 737 senza i controlli obbligatori alla fusoliera. Sumwalt ha specificato che il jet coinvolto nell’ultimo incidente aveva superato tutti i manutenzioni previste e i documenti erano regolari; le registrazioni del volo non hanno rivelato anomalie.

After the Nintendo Switch launched in 2017, portable gaming devices have seen a boom as companies try to replicate its success. Valve’s Steam Deck has provided the stiffest competition so far, but many challengers have stumbled—often due to software issues. Lenovo’s Legion Go stands out by offering worthy hardware enhancements and an ambitious approach to software challenges.

The Legion Go is most directly comparable to the Asus ROG Ally, yet Lenovo sets it apart with a larger, beautifully crisp display, stronger performance, and efforts to address the pain points of running Windows on handheld devices. Unlike the Switch’s custom OS or the Steam Deck’s Linux-based setup, most competitors—including Legion Go—use Windows, which frequently leads to awkward, non-intuitive user experiences with touch and controller inputs.

Lenovo addresses this by giving each controller a shortcut to the Legion Space app, making it easier to launch games and access settings. However, toggling through the app’s menus with these buttons can be confusing, since it alternates between different overlays rather than going straight to the desired screen.

A key advantage is the right controller’s trackpad. Modeled after the Steam Deck, it allows for more precise navigation, especially helpful when Windows defaults to desktop mode or when traditional controller inputs don’t suffice.

The hardware gets top marks. The controllers not only detach (charging wirelessly when attached) but are sized for larger hands and feature a variety of input options. The right controller is equipped with extra triggers, a scroll wheel, and customizable buttons—though their initial placement might lead to accidental presses until the user adapts, particularly when FPS mode is in use.

Legion Go’s 8.8-inch IPS display features a 2560 x 1600 resolution and 144Hz refresh rate for sharp, fluid visuals. The sturdy, wide-angle kickstand allows for flexible viewing, and two USB-C ports (top and bottom) provide better charging versatility when playing on the go or tabletop.

FPS mode is a standout innovation: attaching the right controller to a magnetic disk transforms it into a mouse-like input device, combining the precision of a mouse with the comfort of a gamepad—a clever solution for shooter games.

While Windows remains a challenge, the Legion Go delivers thoughtful hardware solutions and creative controller options, marking it as a significant step forward in the evolution of portable PC gaming.

article_content: Jim Jordan, a Republican representative from Ohio, is seeking the position of Speaker of the House amid skepticism regarding his ability to secure enough support. Unlike predecessor Kevin McCarthy, who underwent numerous voting rounds, Jordan has received endorsements from prominent party members such as Marjorie Taylor Greene, former President Donald Trump, and Representative Nancy Mace. In a recent closed-door Republican conference, a secret ballot resulted in 152 members supporting Jordan and 55 opposing. To claim the speakership in the full House vote, a candidate can only afford to lose four Republican votes if all members are present. In comments to CNN, Jordan voiced optimism about reaching the 217 votes required and stressed party unity but did not state if he would withdraw if he fails to achieve this target. The Republican caucus continues to navigate internal divisions as they select their next Speaker.

article_content: Fifty years after the groundbreaking original The Exorcist, fascination with the Devil endures—especially around Halloween. While the 1970s classic, directed by William Friedkin, included shocking scenes that unsettled audiences, including the infamous crucifix incident, the latest sequel, The Exorcist: Believer, avoids such controversy, aligning with contemporary sensibilities. As a direct sequel to the 1973 film, Believer carries a greater legacy compared to previous sequels. Directed by David Gordon Green, known for revitalizing the Halloween franchise, the film also brings back Ellen Burstyn in her iconic role, though her appearance is largely symbolic. The plot follows Victor (Leslie Odom Jr.), who loses his pregnant wife in a devastating Haiti earthquake. Thirteen years later, his daughter Angela (Lidya Jewett), now a rebellious preteen, often clashes with him. After a secret séance, Angela and her friend Katherine (Olivia O’Neill) disappear, leaving their parents distraught. Believer stands out for its subtle observations, including differences in parenting styles: Victor looks up a phone number in a schoolbook, while Katherine's mother, Miranda (Jennifer Nettles), has all the numbers saved on her phone. Such details offer insight amidst the film’s supernatural events. Ann Dowd delivers a reassuring performance as Ann, a neighborhood nurse. As the supernatural threat escalates, the story integrates Catholic rites with African mysticism, broadening its spiritual perspective. The film aims to connect with modern viewers by addressing themes of family, community, and faith. Yet, this approach sometimes dilutes its overall impact and leaves it feeling more conventional than the original film. A notable exchange occurs when Ann asks Victor if he believes in God, and he responds, 'I don’t believe in the question.' The Exorcist: Believer is directed by David Gordon Green and stars Leslie Odom Jr., Ann Dowd, Jennifer Nettles, Danny McCarthy, Lidya Jewett, Olivia O’Neill, and Ellen Burstyn. Rating: 2 stars.

The U.S. Senate unanimously passed a bipartisan measure on Thursday to end budget-related furloughs of air traffic controllers, which have caused widespread flight delays this week. The legislation grants the Department of Transportation more flexibility to handle mandatory spending cuts, aiming to reduce disruptions for travelers.

White House spokesman Jay Carney acknowledged that the measure would benefit the traveling public but described it as "a temporary Band-Aid" that does not address the broader economic risks posed by the sequester's automatic, across-the-board cuts. The House is expected to consider the proposal on Friday.

The plan also seeks to safeguard 149 control towers at small and mid-sized airports that are at risk of closure due to budget constraints. Both the furloughs of air traffic controllers and the planned closures of federally supervised, privately run towers have become key points of contention in the ongoing debate over government spending.

Supporters of the aviation industry have argued that these budget cuts will negatively impact business, travelers, and jobs in the sector. More than 600 million people fly with U.S. airlines each year.

The Federal Aviation Administration began furloughing about 15,000 air traffic controllers this week, asserting that there was no flexibility to prevent the furloughs without Congressional intervention. The FAA was required to cut $600 million from its budget under the sequester. On Wednesday alone, staffing shortages resulting from furloughs caused more than 863 flight delays at facilities in major cities including Chicago, New York, Washington, Cleveland, Jacksonville, Los Angeles, Detroit, and Dallas. By comparison, over 2,100 delays were attributed to other causes such as weather.

To manage traffic with current staffing levels, controllers have been required to space planes farther apart at key air traffic centers. The Senate acted quickly to address the issue. "Something rare has happened in Washington; the Senate came together on a bipartisan basis to put common sense before politics," said Senator Jerry Moran, a Republican from Kansas. Senator Susan Collins, a Republican from Maine, expressed concern that ongoing FAA furloughs could jeopardize jobs throughout the travel and hospitality industries.

Earlier in the spring, Congress had passed stop-gap budget legislation easing cuts for several federal departments, including Agriculture, Commerce, Defense, Homeland Security, Justice, and Veterans Affairs.

CNN's Jim Acosta, Dana Bash, and Kevin Liptak contributed to this report.

article_content: A new theory suggests that Malaysia Airlines flight MH370 was hijacked and secretly landed in Kazakhstan at the direction of Russian authorities, according to Jeff Wise, a U.S. science writer. Wise's theory, which he admits is speculative, is based on satellite data from the British telecommunications company Inmarsat, suggesting the plane continued to send signals for seven hours after disappearing. Wise hypothesizes that hijackers manipulated the aircraft's navigation data to make it appear to travel in another direction and possibly landed it at the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, a spaceport leased by Russia. He acknowledges in New York Magazine that he cannot explain why the Russian government would orchestrate such an event and admits his idea is 'crazy.' MH370 disappeared on March 8, 2014, about 40 minutes after departing Kuala Lumpur for Beijing, with 239 people on board. No confirmed debris from the aircraft has been recovered. Wise also notes that three Russian men, two holding Ukrainian passports, were among the passengers. Other aviation experts, including Malcolm Brenner, have analyzed satellite data and believe flight MH370 was deliberately flown off course, potentially by someone in the cockpit. National Geographic is releasing a documentary exploring these theories, and the ongoing official search—led by the Australian Transport Safety Bureau—is focused on the southern Indian Ocean. The search has covered 22,000 square kilometers of seabed but has yet to yield any confirmed wreckage. The Joint Agency Co-ordination Centre, composed of officials from Australia, China, and Malaysia, is considering next steps as the underwater search continues. The disappearance of MH370 remains one of the most puzzling aviation mysteries in history.

article_content: Teachers fulfill numerous roles, from subject experts to community leaders. In today's unequal society, it is especially important to cultivate teachers who are socially aware and critically engaged. Such educators are better equipped to help students address issues like overconsumption, waste, and a culture that values material goods over protecting natural resources. An academic working with trainee teachers and researching social justice education highlights four main approaches for developing responsible global citizens: 1. Look beyond surface problems to their root causes. Social injustice is rooted in unequal power relationships. One useful method is defamiliarization—making the familiar seem unfamiliar to challenge ingrained perspectives. For example, examining economic policies and trade agreements helps students understand their impacts on African nations, highlighting imbalances and the role of Western power. Students are encouraged to visualize globalization's effects. 2. Foster critical empathy. Empathy alone often isn't enough, as it can reinforce power dynamics if not approached critically. Philosopher Nel Noddings introduced the concept of 'critical empathy,' combining empathic accuracy (truly understanding another's feelings) with a sympathetic response (sharing in emotions). During the COVID-19 pandemic, students learned to share and listen to each other's actual experiences, rather than speaking for one another. 3. Build trust and encourage risk-taking. Recognizing the need for change means accepting everyone's role in both problems and solutions. Anthony Giddens' work on trust and risk is central here—effective change requires trust and the courage to step into the unknown. Since 2016, critical service-learning projects in Cape Town, South Africa, have encouraged collaboration between students and local communities to address educational and food insecurity challenges, despite the risks involved. While not all projects succeed, they foster valuable reflection and mutual understanding. 4. Promote critical reflection, even when emotions are mixed. Using the South African film ‘Krotoa,’ based on the true story of a Khoi girl taken by colonial settlers, students explored the emotional impact of colonialism. Deep discomfort triggered intense reflection, encouraging students to rethink their identities and assumptions. Such experiences broaden perspectives and support the idea of ubuntu, emphasizing inclusion and strong communities. By embracing these approaches, teachers can better prepare students for thoughtful participation in global discussions about justice and equality. translated_content: Gli insegnanti svolgono numerosi ruoli, da esperti di materia a leader della comunità. Nella società diseguale di oggi, è particolarmente importante coltivare insegnanti socialmente consapevoli e critici. Questi educatori sono meglio preparati ad aiutare gli studenti ad affrontare questioni come il consumismo, lo spreco e una cultura che dà valore ai beni materiali piuttosto che alla protezione delle risorse naturali. Un’accademica che lavora con insegnanti in formazione e si occupa di educazione alla giustizia sociale evidenzia quattro approcci principali per formare cittadini globali responsabili: 1. Guardare oltre i problemi superficiali e arrivare alle cause profonde. L’ingiustizia sociale si basa su rapporti di potere diseguali. Un metodo utile è la defamiliarizzazione—rendere ciò che è familiare insolito per mettere in discussione prospettive consolidate. Ad esempio, analizzare le politiche economiche e gli accordi commerciali aiuta gli studenti a capire i loro effetti sulle nazioni africane, evidenziando gli squilibri e il ruolo delle potenze occidentali. Gli studenti sono incoraggiati a visualizzare gli effetti della globalizzazione. 2. Coltivare un’empatia critica. L’empatia da sola spesso non basta, perché può rafforzare le dinamiche di potere se non viene affrontata criticamente. La filosofa Nel Noddings ha introdotto il concetto di 'empatia critica,' che combina una precisione empatica (comprendere davvero i sentimenti dell’altro) con una risposta simpatetica (condivisione delle emozioni). Durante la pandemia di COVID-19, gli studenti hanno imparato a condividere e ascoltare le esperienze reali degli altri invece di parlare al posto loro. 3. Costruire fiducia e incoraggiare il rischio. Riconoscere il bisogno di cambiamento significa accettare che tutti sono parte sia del problema che della soluzione. Il lavoro di Anthony Giddens sulla fiducia e il rischio è fondamentale: un cambiamento efficace richiede fiducia e il coraggio di affrontare l’ignoto. Dal 2016, progetti di service-learning critico a Città del Capo, Sudafrica, hanno promosso la collaborazione tra studenti e comunità locali per affrontare problemi legati all’istruzione e all’insicurezza alimentare, nonostante i rischi. Non tutti i progetti riescono, ma favoriscono una riflessione e una comprensione reciproca. 4. Promuovere la riflessione critica, anche quando le emozioni sono contrastanti. Utilizzando il film sudafricano ‘Krotoa’, basato sulla storia vera di una ragazza Khoi presa dai coloni, gli studenti hanno esplorato l’impatto emotivo del colonialismo. Il disagio ha suscitato una profonda riflessione, invitando gli studenti a rivedere identità e supposizioni. Esperienze simili allargano le prospettive e sostengono l’idea di ubuntu, che enfatizza inclusione e comunità forti. Adottando questi approcci, gli insegnanti possono preparare meglio gli studenti a partecipare attivamente ai dibattiti globali su giustizia ed equità. article_content: The Pakistani government has instructed officials not to detain Afghans awaiting relocation to the United States, even as it steps up action against undocumented migrants. Border authorities report that more than 180,000 Afghans have returned to Afghanistan after Islamabad ordered roughly 1.7 million Afghans—those it considers undocumented—to leave or face deportation. Human Rights Watch has warned that Afghans seeking resettlement in the US, UK, Germany, or Canada after fleeing Taliban rule risk being deported when their Pakistani visas expire. Western countries continue to process these resettlements, leaving many families in prolonged uncertainty in Pakistan since the Taliban regained control in 2021. In a letter dated November 2, Pakistan’s Interior Ministry listed 1,150 Afghan nationals sponsored by the US for relocation, advising authorities not to arrest them until further notice. This directive follows a call from the US urging Pakistan to permit Afghan asylum seekers to leave the country, with State Department spokesman Matthew Miller encouraging regional cooperation for humanitarian assistance. Millions of Afghans have sought refuge in Pakistan over the decades, including around 600,000 since the Taliban took power and enforced strict laws. The Pakistani government says deportations are necessary for national welfare and security, highlighting increased attacks it attributes to groups operating from Afghanistan—an accusation the Afghan government denies.

Human Rights Watch ha avvertito che gli afgani che aspettano il reinsediamento negli Stati Uniti, Regno Unito, Germania o Canada, dopo essere fuggiti dal regime talebano, rischiano l'espulsione una volta scaduti i loro visti pakistani. I paesi occidentali stanno ancora gestendo queste procedure, lasciando molte famiglie bloccate in Pakistan da quando i talebani hanno ripreso il potere nel 2021. In una lettera del 2 novembre, il Ministero dell’Interno del Pakistan ha indicato 1.150 cittadini afgani sponsorizzati dagli Stati Uniti per il trasferimento, chiedendo di non arrestarli fino a nuovo ordine. Questa direttiva segue un appello degli USA a permettere agli afgani richiedenti asilo di lasciare il paese, con il portavoce del Dipartimento di Stato Matthew Miller che incoraggia la collaborazione regionale per l'assistenza umanitaria. Milioni di afgani si sono rifugiati in Pakistan negli ultimi decenni, inclusi circa 600.000 dopo la presa del potere dei talebani e l'introduzione di leggi restrittive. Il governo pakistano afferma che le espulsioni sono necessarie per la sicurezza e il benessere nazionali, citando un aumento degli attacchi attribuiti a militanti attivi dall’Afghanistan—un’accusa respinta da Kabul.
