article_content: Senator Elizabeth Warren is leading efforts to increase oversight of bitcoin and cryptocurrency markets. In a recent letter to national security officials, Warren and other lawmakers claimed that terrorist groups raised $130 million through cryptocurrencies to finance attacks in Israel, referencing a Wall Street Journal article. However, Preston Pysh, a retired Army officer and bitcoin advocate, published an article disputing this figure. Data from Chainalysis cited by Pysh indicates that Hamas raised only about $450,000 in cryptocurrency, a small portion of its estimated $300 million annual budget. Additionally, Hamas announced last spring that it had stopped its bitcoin fundraising due to the traceability and transparency of such transactions, which created risks for donors. A Forbes article noted that illicit activity in cryptocurrency accounts for just 1.1% of transactions, with far more illicit activity present in the traditional banking system. In response to congressional concerns, the U.S. Treasury Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) released a proposal expanding data collection requirements for cryptocurrency transactions. This proposal, enabled under the Patriot Act, has ignited debate. Previously, FinCEN targeted individual financial institutions suspected of money laundering, but under the new rules, an entire category of transactions could be classified as a primary money laundering concern. Industry professionals and advocates argue that these broad measures could harm small businesses and innovation in the United States’ crypto sector, potentially forcing companies to close or relocate abroad. Brady Swenson, Co-Founder and Head of Marketing at Swan, said these rules threaten individual privacy and the competitiveness of the United States in the evolving global financial system. He noted that restricting privacy rights to address a small percentage of illicit transactions might be ineffective. Senator Cynthia Lummis of Wyoming sent a letter to the Department of Justice urging a thorough investigation and possible criminal charges against Binance and Tether for alleged involvement in illicit activities. While Lummis emphasized targeting bad actors, not the underlying technology, she also suggested a possible disagreement with FinCEN’s proposed rules. Senator Ted Cruz has not made a public statement on the proposal but has referenced the significance of lifted sanctions on Iran in financing attacks, suggesting crypto played a minor role compared to traditional sources. Experts note that, due to the open and distributed nature of Bitcoin, peer-to-peer transactions are difficult to regulate at the individual level, making enforcement of FinCEN’s proposed rules challenging. Some worry the measures could lead to further centralization of the crypto industry, potentially reducing transparency and innovation, and risking a repeat of past financial failures. The full text of the FinCEN proposal is available on the federal register website for public comment for the next three months. Advocates encourage citizens to provide feedback before the deadline.

Tuttavia, Preston Pysh, ex ufficiale dell’esercito e sostenitore di bitcoin, ha pubblicato un articolo che contesta questa cifra. Secondo esperti del settore e sostenitori, queste misure così ampie potrebbero danneggiare le piccole imprese e l’innovazione nel settore cripto statunitense, costringendo le aziende a chiudere o a trasferirsi all’estero. Gli esperti sottolineano che, per via della natura aperta e distribuita di Bitcoin, le transazioni peer-to-peer sono difficili da regolare a livello individuale, rendendo complicata l’applicazione delle regole proposte da FinCEN. Alcuni temono che tali misure possano portare a una maggiore concentrazione del settore cripto, riducendo trasparenza e innovazione e rischiando di ripetere errori finanziari già visti in passato. article_content: Blue Grimster, 19, was caught fly-tipping after dumping scrap metal and dentures in an alleyway in Blackpool, Lancashire. He had charged Fleetwood residents £70 to remove their unwanted metal and rubbish, but instead of disposing of the waste legally, he left it in a public alley. Blackpool Council installed a covert camera after receiving complaints, capturing footage of a young man unloading a bag from a flatbed truck. Investigators traced the dumped waste to a home on Chatsworth Avenue, where residents recognized the dentures as belonging to a family member. Prosecutor Lee Petrak said the council linked the fly-tipped items to the Fleetwood address after a relative recognized the dentures. Grimster, also known as 'Blue', admitted the offence. His lawyer said he had ceased his waste removal business and his actions disappointed his family. He was sentenced to 60 hours of unpaid community service under the Environmental Protection Act.

article_content: Many people with siblings know how it feels to be in the shadow of a family member's achievements. For Kate Lappin, 32, from Warrington, this was her reality as her younger sister Kim became a successful glamour model. While Kim was outgoing and popular, Kate struggled with her weight and experienced bullying at school. Weighing 22 stone at her heaviest, Kate found comfort in large portions of unhealthy food. The contrast between the sisters became more pronounced as Kim began her modelling career while Kate increasingly felt isolated and insecure. Kate recalled feeling upset as a child when her parents put her and Kim in matching Minnie Mouse outfits, but hers was much bigger. She developed emotional issues around food and became withdrawn, avoiding social events and preferring to be alone. During her teenage years, Kate faced public bullying and low self-esteem. Despite Kim's popularity, she remained protective of Kate, supporting her whenever she was targeted by bullies. A turning point came in early 2010 when their supportive stepfather Dave Easton passed away unexpectedly. Kate became even more withdrawn, and her weight increased further. Motivated by a desire to improve her health and inspired by Kim's success, Kate decided to change her lifestyle. She adopted a vegetarian diet focused on lighter and healthier foods, reducing her portion sizes and introducing regular exercise like gym visits and cycling. In just over a month, Kate lost three stone and eventually dropped over ten stone in total, shrinking from a size 22 to a size 8. Her weight loss significantly boosted her confidence and allowed her to pursue new relationships, including with her partner Darren King. Previously, Kate's diet included multiple rounds of bread with butter and jam for breakfast, extra-large portions of spaghetti bolognese for lunch, and high-calorie takeaways for dinner, with frequent snacking on crisps. Now, her meals are much healthier, featuring fruit, salads, and Quorn-based dishes. Throughout her weight loss journey, Kim has remained supportive, celebrating Kate's achievements and frequently sharing clothes. Kate now enjoys regular gym workouts, long bike rides, and a much healthier lifestyle. Kim expresses pride in Kate's transformation, saying she has always believed in her sister's beauty and is delighted to share their success.

article_content:
The BBC faced backlash after homophobic remarks were made on its live radio show 'Fighting Talk,' targeting presenter Clare Balding. During a segment titled 'Defend the Indefensible', panellists discussed the idea of 'turning' Balding straight and made inappropriate suggestions about her presenting racing coverage topless. The comments were broadcast at 8:30pm on Radio 5 Live, prior to the 9pm watershed, and provoked loud groans from the audience at Liverpool Echo Arena.

Comedian Bob Mills added further offensive remarks, claiming, 'There is no woman that can't be cured,' which were met with audience disapproval. The incident drew swift criticism from Ben Summerskill, CEO of Stonewall, who labelled the remarks 'canteen bullying from the 1960s' and called on the BBC to better train its staff regarding unacceptable on-air content.

The BBC issued an unconditional apology for any offence caused, although the episode remained accessible via iPlayer. This controversy has drawn comparisons to a 2007 scandal involving Russell Brand and Jonathan Ross, which led to widespread complaints and BBC sanctions.

Clare Balding, a respected broadcaster and advocate for gender equality in sports, was leading Channel 4's Epsom Derby coverage that day and has recently signed with BT Sport. She commented previously on the differing standards for how women and men are judged on television, sharing her own experiences with criticism about her appearance.

The BBC stated, 'The comments were made during a segment that is blatantly indefensible. However, we unreservedly apologise to anyone offended by the broadcast.'

I commenti sono stati trasmessi alle 20:30 su Radio 5 Live, prima del limite delle 21:00, suscitando forti disapprovazioni dal pubblico presente alla Liverpool Echo Arena.

Il comico Bob Mills ha aggiunto ulteriori osservazioni offensive, sostenendo che 'non c’è donna che non possa essere guarita', affermazione accolta con disapprovazione dal pubblico. L’episodio ha ricevuto critiche immediate da Ben Summerskill, CEO di Stonewall, che ha definito tali parole 'bulli da mensa degli anni ’60', invitando la BBC a formare meglio il personale sui contenuti inaccettabili in onda.

La BBC si è scusata senza riserve per qualsiasi offesa arrecata, anche se l’episodio era ancora disponibile su iPlayer. La vicenda richiama allo scandalo del 2007 con Russell Brand e Jonathan Ross, che aveva portato a numerose lamentele e sanzioni interne dalla BBC.

Clare Balding, stimata conduttrice e sostenitrice dell’uguaglianza di genere nello sport, quel giorno era impegnata nella copertura dell’Epsom Derby per Channel 4 e ha recentemente firmato con BT Sport. In passato, ha raccontato come le donne e gli uomini siano giudicati diversamente in TV, condividendo le proprie esperienze sulle critiche al suo aspetto.

La BBC ha dichiarato: "I commenti sono stati fatti durante una sezione che, per sua stessa natura, è palesemente indifendibile. Tuttavia, ci scusiamo senza riserve con chiunque sia stato offeso dalla trasmissione."

article_content: Manchester United's recent slump has left fans deeply frustrated, especially following their dramatic 4-3 defeat to FC Copenhagen in the UEFA Champions League. After this loss, Nigerian afrobeat singer Davido (David Adeleke) stirred the conversation online by playfully trolling United supporters on X (formerly Twitter). The Red Devils have now suffered nine defeats across all competitions this season, placing them at the bottom of their Champions League group with qualification hanging in the balance. Under Erik Ten Hag, United are currently eighth in the Premier League, with 18 points from 11 matches. Although United narrowly beat Fulham 1-0 last weekend, their defeat in Copenhagen has intensified concerns about their lackluster form. Davido, referencing United’s struggles, wrote: 'I don’t watch ball like that … but come wetin Man U do so? Every week una dey complain enlighten me pls,' ending with a laughing emoji. Fans responded with resignation and humor. For instance, Albert Nat Hyde remarked, 'We are just one unlucky football club that make rival clubs like Chelsea who do not perform any better sleep well at night.' Another supporter, fatigued by the weekly disappointments, replied: 'Davido, that’s how we watch matches every week. I’m tired,' including a crying emoji. Michaelson Hon added, 'No one can explain, we just feel pains from everywhere every week.' Despite claiming he rarely follows football, Davido's connection to the sport is evident. He visited Old Trafford in October 2021, showing off a No. 7 Ronaldo jersey on a night the Portuguese striker led United to a 3-2 comeback over Atalanta. Davido also performed at the 2022 FIFA World Cup final in Qatar and at this year’s PFA Awards in England.

article_content: Rev Isaac Poobalan, minister at St John's Episcopal Church in Aberdeen, Scotland, has faced online criticism after allowing Muslims from a nearby mosque to use the church's facilities for worship due to lack of space at the mosque. St John's became the first church in the UK to regularly share its building with Muslim worshippers. Hundreds now pray in the church's main hall and chapel every week. After the announcement, some individuals posted hostile messages on the church's Facebook page, criticizing the decision and making derogatory remarks about Islam. Rev Poobalan stated that offering help was guided by the Christian teaching of 'loving your neighbour as yourself', and that he intends to continue the church's relationship with the Crown Street Mosque. Sheikh Ahmed Megharbi of the Syed Shah Mustafa Jame Masjid mosque welcomed the collaboration, calling it special and expressing hope for similar initiatives elsewhere. The Bishop of Aberdeen and Orkney, Dr Robert Gillies, said the partnership could signal a shift in Christian-Muslim relations and inspire global significance on a local scale. The relationship between the church and mosque began a few years ago, with joint prayer events on Christmas Eve 2010 and a memorial on the 10th anniversary of 9/11. While churches in the US have also allowed Muslims to pray in their halls, church leaders believe this is the first long-term arrangement of its kind in the UK.

article_content: Planning Minister Nick Boles has stated that building houses will generate more ‘human happiness’ than protecting agricultural fields. He said the UK Government is determined to accelerate house building despite opposition from countryside groups. Boles warned that communities refusing to support these initiatives risk losing hospitals and high street shops as their populations decline. In an interview with the Daily Mail, Boles acknowledged that rural rights campaigners and Conservative supporters worry about greenfield land being replaced by housing estates. However, he argued that current planning laws are sending Britain 'back to the 19th century,' when only the wealthy could afford their own homes. He stated: 'The overall human happiness created by new homes is much greater than the economic, social, and environmental value of a field used to grow crops such as wheat or rape.' Environmental campaigners strongly criticized the proposed reforms, asserting they would cause further urban sprawl in the countryside. In Boles’s Grantham constituency, 7,000 homes are being built on greenfield land. Defending these plans, Boles argued that maintaining services like hospitals and attracting businesses like M&S and John Lewis depends on growing the town’s population. He revealed intentions to introduce further changes to planning rules to help address the housing crisis. Boles admitted it is difficult for a Conservative MP to argue for more housing on green fields, but described councils that refuse to cooperate as 'deeply irresponsible.' 'Some local authorities are dragging their feet,' he said. 'They believe they can reject applications and blame me. That is deeply irresponsible. They are elected to serve their communities, taking responsibility for both the difficult and easy decisions.' Shaun Spiers, chief executive of the Campaign to Protect Rural England, warned that the government's actions could harm both countryside and town centers. He commented that while housing can increase happiness, it should not require destroying green fields. Spiers argued that poor planning could lead to issues such as inadequate transport, decline of high streets, empty inner cities, and urban sprawl, especially when town center shops are turned into housing.

Mobile devices have become central to how people connect, engage, and complete everyday tasks—whether hailing a ride, shopping online, ordering food, or seeking entertainment. In this mobile-first world, effective brand promotion requires a strong mobile marketing strategy.

Recent insights from Similarweb highlight the dominance of mobile: as of September, 64.95% of web traffic comes from mobile devices, compared to 33.65% from personal computers and just 1.4% from tablets. Brands are fiercely competing for consumer attention on these devices, where individuals now spend an average of 3 hours and 43 minutes per day—much of it on social media, video platforms, messaging apps, gaming, shopping, and information searches.

Mobile marketing encompasses a range of channels, but two stand out for their consistent performance: social media and in-app advertising. These channels continue to deliver strong results and are poised for further growth.

Social Media: At the Heart of Mobile Marketing

Social media platforms are abundant and diverse—offering something for every interest, from curated visual content to breaking news and creative expression. Key players like Meta, TikTok, Snapchat, X, and YouTube are accessible anytime, anywhere. According to Datareportal’s Digital 2023 July Global Statshot Report, users worldwide spend an average of 2 hours and 26 minutes daily on social media and typically engage with about 6.7 different platforms each month. While platform audiences often overlap, users expect each one to deliver unique content and experiences. For example, TikTok users seek entertainment and humor, while X (formerly Twitter) is favored for news updates. Brands must tailor their content and tone to these patterns.

Social media marketing via mobile offers:
- Access to large, diverse audiences.
- Precise targeting to reach narrow audience segments.
- Multiple ad formats to fit varying budgets.
- Advanced analytics for campaign optimization.

Beyond Social: The Power of In-App Advertising

Mobile marketing extends well beyond social networks. In-app advertising refers to ads presented within different mobile apps (excluding social media), including games, utilities, ecommerce, fintech, and entertainment. It is important to distinguish this from OEM (original equipment manufacturer) ads, which appear within system or pre-installed apps—mainly on Android devices.

The global app ecosystem is vast and evolving, with Apple’s App Store offering over 1.8 million apps (12% gaming) and Google Play providing more than 3.6 million apps (13% gaming). Gaming apps, in particular, generate high-quality in-app traffic thanks to users’ engagement and the widespread use of rewarded ad formats. Players often view ads in exchange for benefits like free game access or extra lives, making these placements highly engaging. Other app categories—such as productivity or service apps—also enjoy focused user attention, though typically for shorter sessions.

In-app advertising advantages include:
- Access to large, engaged audiences without ad fatigue.
- Innovative and interactive ad formats.
- High audience fidelity, especially in gaming.
- Opportunities for AI- and ML-driven optimization, increasingly critical amid heightened privacy standards.

Key Differences—and Why They Matter

Social media and in-app traffic differ on several fronts:
- Traffic sources: Social media comprises a handful of widely known platforms; in-app traffic comes from a broader array of ad-supported apps.
- Ad context: Social platforms have distinct tones and content expectations, while apps—especially games—offer a more immersive and creative environment for brand messaging.
- User behavior and consumption habits: Brands must align their advertising approach to each channel’s unique user environment.
Further distinctions include:
- Analytics: Measuring campaign performance requires different metrics for social and in-app campaigns. Applying analytics from one to the other can lead to misleading conclusions.
- Audience data: Social platforms have granular knowledge of their users; in-app environments often rely on probabilistic or algorithmic audience insights.

Conclusion

Mobile marketing is now essential for brands seeking to connect with and expand their audiences. Thriving in this mobile-first era is a smart long-term investment that helps brands stay ahead of the competition. Both social media and in-app advertising deliver strong results, but marketers must understand the distinct strategies and nuances each requires. Success depends on tailoring approaches, leveraging the specific strengths of every channel, and remaining adaptable to evolving digital trends.

I dispositivi mobili sono diventati elementi centrali per il modo in cui le persone si connettono, interagiscono e gestiscono le attività quotidiane, come prenotare un passaggio, fare acquisti online, ordinare cibo o cercare intrattenimento. In questo contesto dominato dal mobile, una strategia di marketing efficace deve concentrarsi proprio su questi dispositivi.

Secondo dati recenti di Similarweb, a settembre il 64,95% del traffico web proveniva da dispositivi mobili, contro il 33,65% dai computer e solo l’1,4% dai tablet. I brand si contendono l’attenzione dei consumatori su questi schermi, dove le persone trascorrono in media 3 ore e 43 minuti al giorno–principalmente tra social, video, messaggistica, giochi, shopping e ricerche.

Il mobile marketing comprende molti canali, ma due si distinguono per risultati: i social media e la pubblicità in-app. Questi canali continuano a offrire ottime performance e sono destinati a crescere.

Social Media: il cuore del mobile marketing

Le piattaforme social sono numerose e variegate, offrendo formule per tutti e per ogni interesse: dalla fotografia alle notizie, fino alla creatività. Meta, TikTok, Snapchat, X e YouTube sono sempre accessibili. Secondo il Digital 2023 July Global Statshot Report di Datareportal, gli utenti trascorrono in media 2 ore e 26 minuti al giorno sui social e usano circa 6,7 piattaforme diverse ogni mese. Anche se i pubblici si sovrappongono, ciascun social network offre un’esperienza e un’emozione differente (es. TikTok per l’intrattenimento, X per le news). I brand devono adeguare contenuti e tono di voce a queste differenze.

Il mobile marketing sui social offre:
- Accesso a un pubblico ampio e variegato.
- Targeting preciso per raggiungere segmenti specifici.
- Varietà di formati pubblicitari adatti a ogni budget.
- Analisi avanzate per ottimizzare le campagne.

Oltre i social: la forza dell’in-app advertising

Il mobile marketing non si ferma ai social. La pubblicità in-app riguarda annunci presenti in tutte le app mobili (esclusi i social), come giochi, utility, e-commerce, fintech e intrattenimento. Da non confondere con la pubblicità OEM, riservata alle app di sistema (preinstallate), soprattutto su Android.

L’ecosistema globale delle app è enorme: l’App Store conta oltre 1,8 milioni di app (12% gaming), mentre Google Play supera i 3,6 milioni (13% gaming). I giochi, in particolare, generano traffico di alta qualità perché gli utenti sono coinvolti e vengono offerti formati pubblicitari premianti. Spesso gli annunci si guardano per ottenere vantaggi come vite extra o bonus, rendendo questi spazi particolarmente efficaci. Anche altre categorie di app, come quelle di produttività o servizi, godono di attenzione mirata, anche se per periodi brevi.

I vantaggi dell’in-app advertising:
- Ampio pubblico coinvolto senza saturazione.
- Formati innovativi e interattivi.
- Alto grado di fedeltà, soprattutto nei giochi.
- Ottimizzazione tramite AI e ML, sempre più importante in tempi di privacy.

Le differenze principali–e perché sono importanti

Social e in-app si distinguono perché:
- La fonte del traffico: pochi grandi social contro una miriade di app supportate dalla pubblicità.
- Il contesto dell’annuncio: i social hanno toni e aspettative precisi, mentre le app–in particolare i giochi–offrono maggiore creatività e immersività.
- Comportamento degli utenti: il contenuto pubblicitario va adattato all’ambiente specifico del canale.
Altri elementi:
- Analitiche: servono metriche e strumenti diversi; confondere i parametri può generare errori.
- Dati sugli utenti: i social hanno conoscenze approfondite sui loro utenti; le app fanno affidamento su stime e algoritmi.

Conclusione

Il mobile marketing è diventato imprescindibile per i brand che vogliono espandere la propria audience e restare competitivi. Social e in-app adv portano risultati concreti, ma è fondamentale saperne gestire le differenze. Personalizzare i messaggi e adattarsi ai trend digitali è la chiave del successo.

Jose Mourinho has acknowledged he cannot prevent Spain from including Diego Costa in their squad for the upcoming Euro 2016 qualifiers, despite Costa's ongoing hamstring problems. The Chelsea manager has been carefully managing Costa’s playing schedule since he returned injured from his last international appearance. Spain is expected to announce their squad for the qualifiers against Slovakia and Luxembourg next week, and Costa remains a key player in their plans.

Prior to Chelsea’s Premier League game against Aston Villa, Mourinho stated: “I’m not the one to decide. Everyone knows what’s happening with Diego. His situation has been an issue for a while, but when the national team calls up a Chelsea player, it’s beyond my control. They have every right to select and play who they want, and our input is limited to sharing medical information—after that, it’s their decision.”

Mourinho confirmed that Costa will start for Chelsea against Aston Villa on Saturday. After missing the midweek Capital One Cup match against Bolton as a precaution, Costa might be rested or put on the bench for Chelsea’s Champions League fixture with Sporting Lisbon, given his sensitive hamstring.

"He’s set to start against Villa," Mourinho said. "The main concern is whether he can complete the match and be fit for Lisbon 48 hours later. Right now, I’m focused on the Villa match—we’ll address the next game when it arrives."

Should Costa need to be rested in the Champions League, Mourinho indicated that Drogba or Remy would be ready to step in. He emphasized that the priority is always to pick the best team to win each match. Costa continues to work diligently on his recovery with the support of the medical and conditioning staff. Although Mourinho says Costa is mentally prepared for every game, his physical condition is not optimal yet, but everyone is doing their best to help him regain full fitness.

article_content: The House ethics committee has accused veteran Rep. Charles Rangel of 13 violations of House rules, involving alleged financial misconduct and actions damaging to Congress’s credibility. Rangel, a Democrat from New York in his 20th term, is charged with using his influence to solicit donations for a policy center at City College of New York named after him. These solicitations reportedly targeted corporate leaders and others with business pending before the House Ways and Means Committee, which Rangel chaired until he stepped down earlier this year due to the investigation. Additional allegations involve income tax violations, failures in financial disclosure, and improper use of government mail services and letterhead. Rep. Mike McCaul, the ranking Republican on the investigating subcommittee, stated that the credibility of the House is at stake. Rangel was not present at the initial public hearing of these charges. He later commented that, although he may have been 'overzealous' in public service, the allegations did not involve 'corruption' or 'self-dealing.' Rangel’s legal team requested dismissal of the charges, arguing he did not abuse his official position or personally benefit. However, the committee’s investigation concluded that errors—including failure to report over $600,000 in financial disclosure documents and use of a subsidized apartment for campaign purposes—violated House rules. The committee also cited Rangel’s repeated solicitations to potential donors, including meetings with AIG and other business leaders, as violations of House rules prohibiting certain gifts and solicitations. Rangel’s attorneys contended all charitable contributions went to City College and there was no evidence of favors or preferential treatment for donors. Nonetheless, the committee’s report suggested these actions could reasonably be seen as influencing Rangel’s official duties, thereby tarnishing the reputation of the House. As the hearing was underway, negotiations reportedly continued on a possible settlement. Rangel acknowledged the difficulty this period has posed for him and his family but expressed confidence they would overcome it. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi emphasized the importance of accountability and high ethical standards in response to the allegations. Party leaders recognized the case’s implications both for the institution and upcoming midterm elections.

There are increasing concerns that the Somerset Levels may experience another round of severe flooding. Powerful storms and winds reaching up to 93 mph have battered the west of England, leading to rising water levels and fears among locals of a repeat of last winter’s devastating floods. According to the British Geological Survey (BGS), Somerset’s groundwater levels for November are the second highest recorded in the past 45 years, following a previous flood peak.

Recent photos show the River Parrett near Bridgwater dangerously close to overflowing, despite having recently undergone a £6 million dredging project designed to help protect the village. In Dawlish, Devon, gaps appeared in the new sea wall, and trains were drenched, reigniting concerns. The sea wall had been reconstructed at a cost of £35 million after it collapsed during storms last February.

The rising water is a familiar threat for local residents, coming less than a year after the area suffered the most damaging floods in living memory. Hundreds of people were forced to leave their homes as widespread flooding cut off roads, isolated villages, and rendered large areas of farmland unusable. Nearly a year later, some homes remain uninhabitable.

Andrew McKenzie of the BGS warned that groundwater levels in Winsham, Somerset, which indicate regional trends, are at record highs for this time of year. He commented: 'If we have a very wet winter, it would create conditions for extensive flooding.'

Despite these concerns, some locals downplay the threat, saying such conditions are not unusual for this time of year. Others, however, remain vigilant, especially in areas like Burrowbridge and Bridgwater, where river levels are especially high.

The Met Office has issued an amber weather warning for strong winds across parts of southwest England and west Wales, cautioning about potential travel disruption. Meanwhile, community members and councils are holding meetings and preparations to manage any future flooding. Ric Pallister, leader of South Somerset District Council, emphasized the ongoing efforts and improvements made since last winter, clarifying that steps have been taken to better protect the region should similar weather occur again.

Crescono le preoccupazioni che le Somerset Levels possano affrontare un nuovo ciclo di gravi alluvioni. Potenti tempeste e venti fino a 150 km/h hanno colpito l'ovest dell'Inghilterra, causando l'innalzamento dei livelli dell'acqua e suscitando timori tra i residenti di una possibile ripetizione delle devastanti alluvioni dello scorso inverno. Secondo il British Geological Survey (BGS), i livelli delle falde acquifere nel Somerset per il mese di novembre sono i secondi più alti registrati negli ultimi 45 anni, dopo il picco delle precedenti inondazioni.

Recenti foto mostrano il fiume Parrett vicino a Bridgwater pericolosamente vicino a straripare, nonostante sia stato recentemente dragato grazie a un progetto da 6 milioni di sterline per proteggere il villaggio. A Dawlish, nel Devon, sono apparse delle crepe nel nuovo muro marino e i treni sono stati bagnati dalle onde, riaccendendo le preoccupazioni. Il muro era stato ricostruito a un costo di 35 milioni di sterline dopo il crollo durante le tempeste di febbraio scorso.

Il rischio di alluvione è una minaccia ormai familiare per i residenti, a meno di un anno dalle peggiori inondazioni della memoria locale. Centinaia di persone furono costrette ad abbandonare le proprie case mentre l'acqua tagliava fuori le strade, isolava i villaggi e rendeva inutilizzabili ampie aree agricole. Quasi un anno dopo, alcune abitazioni sono ancora invivibili.

Andrew McKenzie del BGS ha avvertito che i livelli delle falde a Winsham, Somerset — considerati un indicatore regionale — sono a livelli record per questo periodo dell'anno. Ha commentato: «Se dovessimo avere un inverno molto piovoso, si creerebbero condizioni per alluvioni estese».

Nonostante queste preoccupazioni, alcuni residenti minimizzano la minaccia, affermando che tali condizioni sono normali per la stagione. Altri però rimangono vigili, soprattutto in località come Burrowbridge e Bridgwater, dove i livelli dei fiumi sono particolarmente alti.

Il Met Office ha emesso un'allerta meteo arancione per venti forti in diverse zone del sud-ovest dell'Inghilterra e del Galles occidentale, avvertendo di possibili disagi ai trasporti. Nel frattempo, cittadini e autorità comunali si stanno organizzando per affrontare eventuali nuove inondazioni. Ric Pallister, leader del South Somerset District Council, ha sottolineato gli sforzi in corso e i miglioramenti adottati dopo l'inverno scorso, chiarendo che sono state prese misure per proteggere meglio la regione in caso di condizioni meteo simili.

article_content: Katie Couric has left the cold, snowy streets of New York City for the sunny shores of Barbados. The acclaimed journalist was recently seen vacationing with her husband, financier John Molner. The couple enjoyed time together on the sand, shared affectionate moments, and swam in the ocean. Couric, currently Yahoo's Global News Anchor, has been mentioned as a possible replacement for NBC's Brian Williams, who is under scrutiny over disputed claims related to the SEAL team involved in the mission that killed Osama Bin Laden in Iraq. Couric previously anchored the CBS Evening News and has held prominent roles at NBC, CBS, and ABC. Couric and Molner, who married in June at her East Hampton home, were photographed together at the exclusive Sandy Lane resort in Barbados, known for its private beaches, three golf courses, and luxury spa. Their activities included snorkeling, boating, and enjoying drinks on the beach. This Caribbean trip follows the cancellation of Couric's talk show, 'Katie,' in 2014 after two seasons. Couric remains a respected figure in the media, with her name often considered for top news anchor roles. Couric rose to prominence during her fifteen years as anchor of NBC's 'Today,' earning her the reputation as 'America's Sweetheart.' She left in 2006 to lead 'CBS Evening News,' reportedly earning $15 million a year—the highest salary for a journalist at the time—which included contributions to '60 Minutes.' A landmark moment in her career was her 2008 interview with vice presidential candidate Sarah Palin, who struggled to name the magazines she read regularly. The interview gained significant media attention, and Palin later claimed Couric was biased against her. After her time at CBS, Couric became a special correspondent for ABC, contributing to 'Nightline,' '20/20,' and filling in on shows such as 'Good Morning America,' 'The View,' and 'Live with Kelly.' In 2012, she launched 'Katie,' her talk show on ABC, which was canceled after two seasons. On a personal note, Couric and Molner each have two daughters from previous marriages. Couric's first husband, John Monahan, died in 1998 from colon cancer. Couric has discussed how important companionship and father figures are for her children. While vacationing in Barbados, Couric and Molner enjoyed snorkeling, boating, and relaxing by the sea at the Sandy Lane resort.

article_content: Thirteen-year-old Rose Matrie lives in a house marked by the 2010 earthquake in Haiti, which devastated the nation and left many families struggling. Light enters through a narrow crack in the wall—a constant reminder of that disaster. Despite these hardships, Rose has big dreams. 'I want to go to a big school to develop my talents,' she says. Her mother covered the crack with a large chalkboard, allowing Rose to do her homework outside. Her teacher praises her as very bright, especially in literature. 'When I let my imagination go, I think of extraordinary things,' Rose adds. Rose's father lost his job after the earthquake, while her mother works as a seamstress, but there is little demand for her skills. Like many in Haiti, the family struggles to afford school fees for Rose and her five siblings. Public schools in Haiti meet only about 20% of the need for basic education in rural areas, and private school costs remain high compared to household income, as noted by Plan International USA. Plan International USA works with local governments and schools to expand access to quality education. The organization builds classrooms and facilities, trains educators, and provides school supplies, textbooks, and uniforms to children in need. 'This is so those costs aren't passed on to families as a barrier to attendance,' explains Ann Wang, a communications specialist at Plan. When school costs are reduced or eliminated, more children like Rose have the chance to attend and fulfill their potential. You can help support girls’ education in Haiti by donating to campaigns such as Girl Rising’s 10x10 Fund for Girls' Education or Plan International USA's 'Because I am a Girl' campaign, which funds global projects for girls' education. The 'Gifts of Hope' program lets you symbolically donate items like uniforms, school supplies, or vaccinations. Plan International USA also offers online resources for students and teachers to learn about the challenges many girls and women face worldwide. For more ways to support girls’ education globally, resources and actions are available through CNN’s Impact Your World and 10x10. For additional details about CNN Films' 'Girl Rising' project and CNN's Impact Your World, visit their websites.

article_content: Ben Flower, a Wigan Warriors prop, faces disciplinary action from the Rugby Football League (RFL) after punching St Helens player Lance Hohaia during Saturday’s Grand Final at Old Trafford. The incident happened just two minutes into the match, with Flower shown a red card after first knocking Hohaia down and then striking him again while he was on the ground. Flower, 26 and a Wales international, has been charged with a Grade F offence, the RFL’s most serious disciplinary category, carrying a minimum eight-match suspension. St Helens have chosen to let the RFL handle the matter and are unlikely to seek criminal charges. Although the club contacted Greater Manchester Police for advice, CEO Mike Rush said they would wait for the league’s decision before considering any further steps. This approach echoes broader concerns within sport, as highlighted by former Wales international Jonathan Davies, that involving police in on-field incidents could set a difficult precedent. Lance Hohaia was also disciplined, receiving a Grade B charge for allegedly hitting Flower with his forearm, which could bring a one or two-match ban. Despite these events, St Helens triumphed in the Grand Final against a Wigan side reduced to 12 men following Flower’s sending off.

L’incidente è avvenuto dopo soli due minuti di gioco: Flower ha ricevuto il cartellino rosso dopo aver mandato a terra Hohaia e averlo colpito di nuovo mentre era già a terra. Nonostante questi eventi, i St Helens hanno trionfato nella Grand Final contro un Wigan rimasto in 12 dopo l’espulsione di Flower.

Oscar-nominated director Maite Alberdi’s latest documentary, The Eternal Memory, has drawn widespread international attention and secured multiple new distribution agreements ahead of its UK debut at the London Film Festival. Both Dogwoof and MTV Documentary Films confirmed that the film, following a period of intense bidding, will be released in Mexico this autumn via Cinemex. Additional new deals include Mediawaan (France), PIFFL (Germany and Austria), Golden Scene (Hong Kong and Macau), and DDDream (China). Dogwoof is set to launch the film in the UK and Ireland on November 10, with a variety of other global theatrical releases lined up for this winter and early 2024. These include partners such as Edge Entertainment (Nordic and Baltics), Madman (Australia and New Zealand), I Wonder Pictures (Italy), Periscoop (Benelux), Lev (Israel), Synca (Japan), Restart (Former Yugoslavia), and Spain’s B-Team.

The Eternal Memory premiered at the Sundance Film Festival this year, where it was honored with the Grand Jury Prize. The documentary provides a moving portrait of the enduring love story between Augusto, one of Chile’s most renowned cultural commentators diagnosed with Alzheimer’s eight years ago, and his partner of 25 years, Paulina, a popular actress. As Augusto’s memory fades, both he and Paulina face the daily challenges of the disease, relying on their deep bond, affection, and humor to navigate life’s difficulties.

MTV Documentary Films acquired international rights to the film earlier this year. The documentary is a collaboration between Micromundo and Fabula, with Maite Alberdi directing and producing alongside Juan De Dios Larraín, Pablo Larraín, and Rocío Jadue; executive producers include Marcela Santibañez, Daniela Sandoval, Nicholas Hooper, Julie Goldman, Christopher Clements, Chandra Jessee, and Rebecca Lichtenfeld. 

After picking up the top award at Sundance, The Eternal Memory went on to screen at Berlinale, where it was a runner-up for the Panorama Audience Award, as well as CPH: DOX and the San Sebastian Film Festival. Maite Alberdi is soon set to receive the prestigious Robert and Anne Drew Award for Documentary Excellence at DOC NYC. Previous recipients of the honor include Steven Bognar and Julia Reichert.

article_content: ATLANTA, Georgia (CNN) — Kristin Davis, star of 'Sex and the City,' launched her new fashion line at Belk department stores in Atlanta, wearing a green plaid A-line skirt from her collection, paired with a black patent leather belt and gladiator stiletto sandals. Her ensemble combines sweetness and boldness, reflecting her character Charlotte York with hints of Carrie Bradshaw’s flair. Davis's upbeat personality and sharp style echo the fashion-forward essence of the show, known for its high-end costumes by designer Patricia Field. Unlike the show's pricey attire, Davis’s goal is to make chic clothing more accessible and affordable for everyday women, following a growing trend of celebrity-designer collaborations for budget-conscious shoppers. Her collection emphasizes versatility and inclusivity, aiming to help women of various body types feel confident and stylish. Davis highlights 'a strong shoe' as the foundation of any look, noting that gladiator heels are a favorite from her line. She credits Patricia Field with helping her define her style philosophy: stick with what works. During development, Davis relied on feedback from family members to ensure her dresses, shoes, and swimsuits flatters different shapes. Her objective is to design for real women—not just actresses. Davis hinted that the upcoming 'Sex and the City' movie sequel, arriving May 2010, may showcase the famed friendship group grappling with more realistic clothing budgets. Her top style advice: 'Green is the color,' she says, adding that saving money is always stylish. Inspired by the event, the author leaves to explore Atlanta in a pair of Davis’s affordable gladiator stiletto sandals.

article_content: Mehreen Faruqi, Deputy Leader of the Australian Greens, has taken a firm public stand in Parliament by calling for an immediate ceasefire in the Israel-Gaza conflict. Faruqi asserts that parliamentarians have a duty to speak out during times of grave injustice, and she has led her colleagues in protests such as boycotting Question Time to express solidarity with those advocating for peace. Despite their 11 Senate seats, the Greens have found their efforts blocked by both the Labor government, headed by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and the Liberal-National opposition. Faruqi strongly criticizes these major parties for resisting a Senate vote on a ceasefire, suggesting they are ignoring both the devastation in Gaza and the large-scale public demonstrations happening nationwide. Throughout Australia, thousands have rallied each weekend to demand an end to violence in Gaza and increased government support for a ceasefire. Faruqi notes that Australia's abstention from a United Nations vote on a humanitarian truce signals a disconnect between government action and the wishes of many citizens, framing it as a betrayal of public trust. Regarding Australia's international involvement, Faruqi draws attention to the country's secretive military exports to Israel over recent years, and argues that by not halting these exports, Australia indirectly contributes to the civilian suffering in Gaza. She urges for greater accountability and an immediate suspension of such arms deals. Although the Greens' influence in Parliament is limited by numbers, Faruqi emphasizes their ongoing commitment to represent those calling for justice and peace for Palestine. She argues that persistent advocacy and parliamentary pressure are essential to pushing the government toward a more humane and just foreign policy.

Quanto al coinvolgimento internazionale, Faruqi punta l’attenzione sulle esportazioni militari segrete dell’Australia verso Israele negli ultimi anni, affermando che non sospendere queste esportazioni significa contribuire indirettamente alle sofferenze dei civili a Gaza. article_content: Racing legend Lester Piggott has listed his uniquely designed Eve Lodge Stables in Newmarket, Suffolk, for £1.25 million. Designed by Piggott in 1985, the property spans more than five acres and offers an indoor arena, paddocks, 95 horse boxes, and a three-bedroom manager’s house. There are also four semi-detached, two-bedroom cottages and direct access to ‘The Gallops’ training grounds at Newmarket racecourse. At its peak, Eve Lodge Stables housed 97 horses and produced 34 winning racehorses. The property is currently leased to trainer James Toller and horse handler Gill Duffield. The decision to sell comes as Piggott and his wife Susan no longer require the facility. Gemma Bailey of Bidwells, the estate agents marketing the property, described the training yard as ‘immaculate’ and in a prime location for the horse training industry, expressing hope for significant interest. Piggott designed the stables with inspiration from a visit to Colin Hayes’ Lindsay Park establishment in Adelaide, Australia, focusing on a jockey’s perspective for detail. A prominent flat-race jockey, Piggott’s illustrious career spanned 48 years, earning him 11 champion titles, 30 Classic wins (including a record nine in The Derby), and 4,493 wins in Britain, a record surpassed only by Sir Gordon Richards and Pat Eddery. He won The Oaks six times, the St Leger eight times, and secured 116 Royal Ascot victories. Two years after becoming a trainer, Piggott was convicted for tax evasion and served just over a year in prison. Upon release, he returned to racing and trained 34 winners at Eve Lodge Stables. Piggott and his wife have two daughters: Maureen, a former eventer, and Tracy, a sports presenter for RTE in Ireland.

article_content: MUGELLO, Italy – Italian rider Valentino Rossi’s resurgence continued on Saturday as the five-time MotoGP champion secured pole position at his home race in Mugello. Rossi gave a thumbs up after taking his first pole of the season. The 29-year-old, who has faced challenges since his last title win in 2005, now leads the field on his Fiat Yamaha following victories in the past two races. Rossi clocked a lap time of 1 minute 48.130 seconds to earn his first pole position of the season, ahead of Dani Pedrosa in second and fellow Italian Loris Capirossi in third. This marks the 50th pole of his career and 40th in MotoGP. "We’ll try to keep this winning streak going. I was worried after practice because we had some problems, but the team made changes and the bike is faster now," said Rossi. "My last pole was such a long time ago – I can’t even remember when it was, so I’m very happy. With Loris behind me and two Italians on the front row, the crowd will be very special here." Rossi leads Repsol Honda rider Dani Pedrosa and his own Yamaha teammate Jorge Lorenzo by three points in the championship, with reigning champion Casey Stoner trailing by a further 28 points on his Marlboro Ducati. Rossi’s pole time was more than 0.8 seconds faster than the previous record set by Spain’s Sete Gibernau two years ago on a more powerful, 990cc bike, as opposed to the current 800cc machines. In fact, the top seven qualifiers all beat Gibernau’s previous lap time.

article_content: Keurig is recalling more than 7 million single-serve coffee machines after reports that some units spewed hot liquid and caused injuries. The recall affects Keurig's Mini Plus brewers, model number K10, manufactured between 2009 and 2014. Keurig received approximately 200 reports of hot liquids spraying from these machines, including 90 cases involving burn-related injuries. Customers who own the affected brewers can contact Keurig to receive a free repair kit. The company advises users to keep an arm's length distance from the machines and avoid brewing more than two cups in quick succession while awaiting the kit. About 6.6 million affected brewers were sold in the U.S. and 564,000 in Canada. The machines retailed for around $100 at stores such as Kmart, Kohl's, Target, and Walmart, as well as online. The recalled brewers have model number K10 and an identification number starting with '31' printed on the bottom. Keurig Green Mountain Inc., based in Waterbury, Vermont, manufactures the brewers. Suzanne DuLong, Keurig’s vice president of corporate communications, told The Wall Street Journal that the issue was reported to the Consumer Product Safety Commission and Health Canada last month. Keurig says it acted immediately when the problem was identified, with the recall timing determined by the Commission. There have been no lawsuits filed over injuries. Keurig recorded a $10 million charge for remedies in its fiscal year 2014. The company’s shares dropped by $3.08 (2.2%) to $136.70 after news of the recall.

Following Liverpool's narrow 3-2 victory at QPR, both manager Brendan Rodgers and captain Steven Gerrard openly criticized the team's subpar performances this season. Rodgers acknowledged that Liverpool often fails to reach its full stride, while Gerrard insisted the team needs improvement across the board.

Even in victory, Liverpool’s defense appeared vulnerable. Center backs Dejan Lovren and Martin Skrtel had trouble containing QPR’s forwards, allowing a late equalizer by Eduardo Vargas before ultimately securing the win. Defensive lapses, coupled with only one clean sheet so far, have caused concern—especially with Real Madrid visiting Anfield in the Champions League.

Real Madrid travel to Liverpool in excellent form, scoring 40 goals in just 13 matches and recording consecutive 5-0 wins. The attack—led by Cristiano Ronaldo, who already has 15 goals from seven league games—also features James Rodriguez, Karim Benzema, and Javier Hernandez. The absence of Gareth Bale due to a muscle injury may provide slight relief for Liverpool, but Real still boasts an array of offensive threats, including Toni Kroos and Luka Modric.

Goalkeeper Simon Mignolet’s inconsistent displays have come under scrutiny, with recent criticism following a match against Everton. Liverpool’s defensive weaknesses, evident in both domestic and European matches, make facing Real Madrid’s prolific attack seem particularly challenging.

Recent Real signings, such as Rodriguez and Kroos, have made a swift impact, while loan arrival Hernandez has found new life at the club. Benzema is likely to return from illness too, giving coach Carlo Ancelotti even more attacking options.

Although Liverpool memorably defeated Real Madrid 4-0 at Anfield five years ago, current performances suggest a much tougher test awaits in the upcoming clash.

article_content: In search of more durable and sustainable building materials, scientists are looking to the ancient world for new ideas. While structures built by Roman, Mayan, and Chinese engineers have survived for thousands of years, much of today’s concrete infrastructure lasts only 50 to 100 years. Researchers are investigating ancient techniques by analyzing fragments of centuries-old structures, examining historical documents, and recreating old recipes. They have discovered unexpected ingredients such as tree bark, volcanic ash, rice, beer, and even urine. These natural additives may allow ancient concretes and plasters to resist damage, strengthen over time, and even heal their own cracks. Modern concrete, made mainly from Portland cement (a combination of heated limestone and clay), is strong and suitable for large projects but lacks the endurance of ancient materials. With growing concerns about climate change, and given that cement production accounts for more than 7% of global CO2 emissions, there is increasing motivation to find greener construction methods. Carlos Rodriguez-Navarro, a cultural heritage researcher at Spain's University of Granada, argues that traditional knowledge from the Mayans or ancient Chinese could help modern construction become more sustainable. Roman concrete is particularly famous, with structures like the Pantheon and aqueducts still standing today. Records suggest Romans combined burnt limestone and volcanic sand with gravel and water. Recent research from MIT’s Admir Masic suggests that lime chunks scattered in Roman concrete allow water to reactivate them, triggering chemical reactions that repair cracks. Marie Jackson of the University of Utah found that volcanic rocks in Roman concrete may react over time to seal cracks. At Copán, a Maya site in Honduras, lime sculptures and temples have lasted more than 1,000 years in a tough tropical climate. Rodriguez-Navarro’s team showed that mixing tree extracts from chukum and jiote trees with lime plaster creates a material that mimics the toughness of seashells, as organic molecules bond with the minerals. Studies of ancient buildings have revealed many organic ingredients in mortars and plasters, such as sticky rice starch in China's Great Wall and the Forbidden City, along with additions like milk, beer, and dung in other civilizations. In India, builders tailored their materials using herbs for humidity resistance, sugar for salt protection, and rice-husk bricks for earthquakes. While some ancient methods were likely discovered through trial and error, many reflect intentional adaptation to local environments. By reviving and updating these recipes, today’s builders hope to create longer-lasting and more eco-friendly structures.

I ricercatori stanno studiando le tecniche antiche analizzando frammenti di vecchie strutture, consultando documenti storici e ricreando antiche ricette. Hanno scoperto ingredienti inaspettati come corteccia d'albero, cenere vulcanica, riso, birra e persino urina. Questi additivi naturali potrebbero aver permesso ai calcestruzzi e agli intonaci antichi di resistere ai danni, rafforzarsi col tempo e persino autoriparare le crepe. Il cemento moderno, composto principalmente da cemento Portland (una miscela di calcare e argilla riscaldati), è robusto e adatto a grandi opere, ma manca della resistenza dei materiali antichi. Con la crescente preoccupazione per il cambiamento climatico, e considerando che la produzione di cemento rappresenta oltre il 7% delle emissioni globali di CO2, cresce l'interesse verso metodi di costruzione più ecologici. Carlos Rodriguez-Navarro, ricercatore sul patrimonio culturale presso l'Università di Granada, sostiene che le conoscenze tradizionali dei Maya o degli antichi cinesi potrebbero aiutare la costruzione moderna a essere più sostenibile. Il calcestruzzo romano è celebre, e strutture come il Pantheon e gli acquedotti esistono ancora oggi. Recuperando e migliorando queste ricette, i costruttori di oggi sperano di ottenere edifici più longevi e sostenibili.

Lars Hedegaard, a noted Danish author and critic of Islam, narrowly survived an assassination attempt at his home in Frederiksberg, Copenhagen. The 70-year-old answered his door to a man posing as a delivery person, who then drew a firearm and fired, just missing Hedegaard’s head. Hedegaard managed to fight back, causing the attacker to lose his weapon and flee. 

Police, who are searching for a suspect described as a 'foreign' man aged between 20 and 25, confirmed an active investigation is underway. Hedegaard was shaken by the incident, but physically unharmed. 

As leader of both the Free Press Society in Denmark and its international counterpart, Hedegaard has often raised concerns about threats to press freedom, especially from extremist groups. He was acquitted in 2012 of hate speech charges stemming from comments on Islam. 

Denmark’s Prime Minister Helle Thorning-Schmidt strongly condemned the attack, stressing the danger it poses to freedom of expression. Other critics of Islam, such as Dutch lawmaker Geert Wilders and Swedish artist Lars Vilks—both subjected to threats for their views—publicly supported Hedegaard. 

This incident is part of a wider pattern of threats and violence against Scandinavian critics linked to the 2005 Danish cartoon controversy, which sparked international protest. Earlier cases include a 2010 axe attack on a cartoonist and a foiled 2012 plot against the newspaper behind the Muhammad caricatures, forcing several high-profile figures to live under police protection.

Hedegaard è riuscito a reagire, facendo cadere l’arma dell’aggressore, che è quindi fuggito.

La polizia, attualmente alla ricerca di un sospetto descritto come uomo “straniero” tra i 20 e i 25 anni, ha confermato che le indagini stanno proseguendo. Hedegaard, pur profondamente scosso, non è rimasto ferito.

In qualità di leader della Free Press Society danese e della sua diramazione internazionale, Hedegaard ha spesso denunciato minacce alla libertà di stampa, soprattutto da parte di gruppi estremisti. Nel 2012 era stato assolto dall’accusa di incitamento all’odio per alcune dichiarazioni sull’Islam.

La premier danese Helle Thorning-Schmidt ha condannato energicamente l’attacco, sottolineando il rischio che corre la libertà di espressione. Altri critici dell’Islam, come il politico olandese Geert Wilders e l’artista svedese Lars Vilks—entrambi più volte minacciati per le loro posizioni—hanno espresso solidarietà a Hedegaard.

Questo episodio si inserisce in una sequenza di minacce e atti violenti contro critici scandinavi legati alla controversia delle vignette danesi del 2005, che scatenò proteste a livello internazionale. Tra i precedenti: un’aggressione con un’ascia ai danni di un vignettista nel 2010 e un attentato sventato nel 2012 contro il giornale autore delle caricature, costringendo diverse personalità a vivere sotto protezione.

article_content: London (CNN) -- The chief executive of Barclays, one of the world's largest banks, resigned Tuesday following a scandal, the bank said. Bob Diamond’s resignation is effective immediately. Diamond has been a controversial figure, known for supporting significant bonuses for bankers. "It's about pay for performance," he told CNN earlier this year, referring to bonuses as "rewards for success." Barclays also announced the resignation of Chief Operating Officer Jerry del Missier, just hours after Diamond’s departure. Chairman Marcus Agius had resigned on Monday, but returned on Tuesday to serve as chief executive after Diamond’s exit. Barclays' reputation has been damaged by a scandal involving the manipulation of Libor, the benchmark rate at which banks lend to each other. Libor affects consumer interest rates on credit cards, mortgages, and student loans. Former investment banker Ralph Silva emphasized the scandal’s impact on the public, noting that changes in Libor influence various consumer and pension rates. The chairman of the Financial Services Authority, Adair Turner, criticized the actions as examples of "cynical greed" and said the scandal had caused significant harm to the banking industry's reputation. Diamond is scheduled to testify before the British Parliament’s Treasury Committee about the scandal on Wednesday. Last week, Barclays was fined more than $450 million by UK and US regulators for rate-fixing during the financial crisis. Several other major global banks are also under investigation. Deutsche Bank, Royal Bank of Scotland, Credit Suisse, UBS, Citigroup, and JPMorgan Chase have all confirmed they are being probed, while Bank of America declined to comment on reports of an investigation. UK Chancellor George Osborne welcomed Diamond's resignation, calling it the right decision, and said that banks should focus on supporting the economy rather than being mired in scandals. Prime Minister David Cameron announced a full parliamentary inquiry into the Libor scandal and banking industry standards. Diamond’s resignation followed that of Chairman Agius, who reversed his decision and will serve as executive chairman while leading the search for a new chief executive. Barclays is ranked as the world’s 15th largest bank and the UK’s second most profitable, according to The Banker magazine. In 2011, Diamond’s total compensation was £6.3 million ($7.92 million), including a salary, bonuses, and share options, with the annual bonus deferred over three years. In his resignation statement, Diamond expressed disappointment at the damage to Barclays’ reputation and praised the company’s management team. Agius recognized Diamond’s contributions over 16 years, stating that he built Barclays Investment Bank into a global leader. The $450 million fine followed Barclays’ admission that some trading desks deliberately under-reported interest rates as part of Libor, which is set daily in London among major banks. Bank of England Governor Mervyn King recently criticized the culture in British banking, highlighting “deceitful” methods used to increase profits. CNN's Paul Armstrong, Jim Boulden, Isa Soares, Nick Thompson, and Maureen Farrell contributed to this report.

Lori Webb, a Utah mother, believes her 19-year-old son Chandler's sudden death was caused by rare complications from a routine flu vaccine. Chandler, reportedly healthy and active, began experiencing severe headaches and vomiting the day after he received his first flu and tuberculosis vaccinations on October 15, which he got in preparation for a Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints mission. His condition worsened quickly, leading to hospitalization at Intermountain Medical Center in Murray, Utah, where after a week, he fell into a coma. Despite thorough testing by his medical team, including six neurologists, doctors were unable to determine the root cause of his illness. Chandler remained on life support for nearly a month before passing away on November 19; the official cause was swelling of the brain.

Lori, sharing emotional moments such as giving her son a final haircut and reading familiar childhood stories, has made Chandler's story public, including hospital photos intended to raise awareness of potential vaccine risks. Health authorities, however, reiterate that serious reactions to flu shots are exceptionally rare. The Utah Department of Health notes no official records of flu vaccine deaths in the state; nationally, about 130 million people are vaccinated annually with only about 140 reporting severe side effects. Still, Chandler’s case remains unexplained, leaving his family grieving and awaiting results from a brain biopsy in the hope of answers. The incident has renewed discussions about vaccine safety amid enduring family heartbreak.

article_content: In response to growing investor participation in India's capital markets, market institutions have introduced the Investor Risk Reduction Access (IRRA) platform to help protect investor positions during technical outages at brokers' systems. The platform, launched by leading stock exchanges, aims to safeguard short-term trading positions, especially those held by large-scale investors, in the event of significant system disruptions at brokerage firms. “No system is infallible, and there's always some risk of failure. With IRRA, we want to ensure that investors' trading positions are protected, even in such cases,” said SEBI chairperson Madhabi Puri Buch during the platform's launch event. Over the past five to seven years, the adoption of advanced technology has allowed SEBI to accelerate measures for the protection of investor assets. As more people participate in the markets, greater efforts have been made to ensure investor safety. According to Buch, these technological advancements and various new tools have strengthened India's standing in global markets, setting the stage for future economic growth and realization of the country’s market potential. Last month, the BSE, National Stock Exchange, Multi Commodity Exchange, Metropolitan Stock Exchange, and National Commodity Derivatives Exchange conducted a soft launch of the IRRA platform. While acknowledging the role of short-term trading, Buch advised individual investors to maintain long-term perspectives and avoid the pitfalls of derivatives trading. “There is a 90% probability that investors will lose money in the F&O segment. However, a long-term approach to investing offers better opportunities for wealth creation,” she observed. SEBI has recently introduced several measures to bolster investor protection. Standard procedures have been updated; now, in the event of a technical outage, stock exchanges must notify brokers and other financial infrastructure institutions within 15 minutes. Separately, the government is reviewing the legality of transferring unclaimed sums from the Sahara-Sebi Refund Account into the Consolidated Fund of India, retaining the option for future investor claims. Additionally, Apple is targeting the production of nearly ₹1 trillion worth of iPhones in India during the current fiscal year, after boosting capacity at manufacturer partners and already surpassing ₹60,000 crore in output in the first seven months. In another development, Nawaz Modi, the estranged wife of Gautam Singhania, is seeking three-quarters of the industrialist’s reported $1.4 billion net worth for herself and their two daughters as part of their separation settlement.

article_content: Scotland Yard has intensified its search for a fugitive monk accused of child abuse by releasing, for the first time, a clear photograph of Laurence Soper, the 68-year-old former Abbot of Ealing Abbey and ex-head of St Benedict's School. The photo, taken about ten years ago, will soon appear on police and Catholic media websites to aid the global search. Faith Today magazine will circulate Soper’s photograph and alert monasteries worldwide. Widely regarded as the most senior British Catholic implicated in recent abuse scandals, Soper disappeared 18 months ago following his arrest. Soper worked at St Benedict’s School, a £12,000-a-year private institution, for nearly 30 years before relocating to Rome in 2001 to serve as treasurer at the Benedictine Order’s headquarters at St Anselmo. He was arrested and questioned by police in September 2010 after allegations from a former pupil, but authorities allowed him to keep his passport and did not photograph him, asking through his solicitor for his return to London. Instead, after leaving St Anselmo in March 2011, Soper vanished, skipping bail. Police now acknowledge they do not know whether he remains in Italy. Soper is among five individuals named in Lord Carlile’s independent report into decades of abuse at St Benedict's. Two former teachers at the school have already been imprisoned. Additional concerns have surfaced about Soper’s tenure as part-time chaplain at Feltham Young Offender Institution from 1988 to 2000, with Ealing Abbey confirming he was questioned by police during that period. In the mid-1990s, Scotland Yard also investigated allegations of a paedophile ring visiting boys at Feltham. An Ealing Abbey spokesperson stated that all attempts to reach Soper have failed and urged anyone with information about his whereabouts to contact authorities, acknowledging the community’s frustration and difficulty moving on while Soper evades justice. The Abbey fully supports the renewed appeal.

L'immagine, scattata circa dieci anni fa, apparirà presto sui siti web della polizia e dei media cattolici per agevolare la ricerca a livello globale. La rivista Faith Today diffonderà la fotografia di Soper e informerà i monasteri in tutto il mondo. Considerato il più alto esponente cattolico britannico coinvolto nei recenti scandali di abusi, Soper è scomparso 18 mesi fa dopo il suo arresto. Soper ha lavorato per quasi trent’anni alla St Benedict’s School, una scuola privata con una retta di 12.000 sterline l’anno, prima di trasferirsi a Roma nel 2001 come tesoriere presso la sede centrale dell’Ordine Benedettino a Sant’Anselmo. È stato arrestato e interrogato dalla polizia nel settembre 2010 dopo le accuse di un ex alunno, ma le autorità gli permisero di tenere il passaporto e non lo fotografarono, chiedendo tramite il suo avvocato un suo ritorno a Londra. Invece, dopo aver lasciato Sant’Anselmo nel marzo 2011, Soper è scomparso, violando la libertà su cauzione. La polizia ora ammette di non sapere se sia ancora in Italia. Soper è tra i cinque menzionati nel rapporto indipendente di Lord Carlile sugli abusi avvenuti per decenni alla St Benedict's e due ex insegnanti della scuola sono già stati condannati. Sono emerse ulteriori preoccupazioni riguardo al periodo in cui Soper fu cappellano part-time presso il Feltham Young Offender Institution dal 1988 al 2000; Ealing Abbey conferma che fu interrogato dalla polizia anche allora. A metà degli anni Novanta, Scotland Yard aveva già indagato su presunte reti di pedofili a Feltham. Un portavoce di Ealing Abbey ha dichiarato che tutti i tentativi di contattare Soper sono falliti e ha invitato chiunque abbia informazioni sulla sua posizione a rivolgersi alle autorità, riconoscendo la frustrazione della comunità e la difficoltà di andare avanti finché Soper sfugge alla giustizia. article_content: Despite an offer from Embassy Group to buy back WeWork Inc.'s 27% stake in WeWork India, the US-based coworking company has so far declined. However, sources suggest that ongoing negotiations may eventually lead to an agreement. Embassy Group, holding 73%, remains in talks with WeWork Inc., and a potential deal could happen within the next few quarters if discussions continue smoothly.  WeWork India, a profitable and fast-growing segment of the company’s international business, operates independently while utilizing the global WeWork brand through its association with WeWork Inc. Since WeWork Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US, WeWork India has stated that its operations remain unaffected by the parent company's insolvency.  In 2020, WeWork Inc. invested $100 million for a 27% stake in WeWork India, valuing it at over $500 million. That investment allowed WeWork India to strengthen its market position and expand amid intense competition in the coworking sector.  As of April–September 2023, WeWork India reported revenue of Rs 831 crore (a 40% year-on-year increase) and EBITDA of Rs 532 crore (up 90% from the previous year). The company expects to reach Rs 1,800 crore in revenue this fiscal year and aims to add 1.5 to 2 million square feet of office space annually.  Operating in seven cities with 50 locations, WeWork India manages more than 6.5 million square feet, over 90,000 desks, and serves more than 70,000 members. About 80% of its client base consists of enterprises, with the rest comprising SMBs, startups, and entrepreneurs.  Flexible office space is increasingly popular in India as companies seek efficiency with distributed work models. Industry data shows a notable increase in leasing of flexible workspaces from FY22 to FY23, particularly in Bengaluru, Pune, and Delhi NCR.  Globally, WeWork has faced significant challenges, including losses and unfavorable investments that led to its bankruptcy filing in the US and Canada. Nevertheless, WeWork India reports continued growth and resilience, operating separately from the parent company’s financial difficulties.  In related business news: Indian tax authorities are probing Apple, Google, and Amazon’s local units for potential tax issues, Indians top Dubai’s real estate buyers, and Razorpay is planning to relocate its parent company to India, a move that might trigger substantial US tax costs.

L’Embassy Group, che detiene il 73%, è ancora in trattativa con WeWork Inc. e un’intesa potrebbe concretizzarsi nei prossimi trimestri se i colloqui procederanno senza intoppi.  WeWork India, segmento redditizio e in rapida crescita del business internazionale dell’azienda, opera in modo indipendente, pur beneficiando del brand globale WeWork grazie all’accordo con la casa madre. Da quando WeWork Inc. ha richiesto la protezione dal fallimento (Chapter 11) negli Stati Uniti, WeWork India ha dichiarato che le proprie attività non sono state influenzate dall’insolvenza della società madre.  Nel 2020 WeWork Inc. ha investito 100 milioni di dollari per acquisire il 27% di WeWork India, valutando l’azienda oltre 500 milioni di dollari. Questo investimento ha permesso a WeWork India di consolidare la propria posizione sul mercato e di crescere in un settore coworking molto competitivo.  Ad aprile-settembre 2023, WeWork India ha registrato ricavi per 831 crore di rupie (un aumento del 40% su base annua) e un EBITDA di 532 crore di rupie (in crescita del 90% rispetto all’anno precedente). L’azienda prevede di raggiungere ricavi per 1.800 crore quest’anno fiscale e punta ad aggiungere annualmente da 1,5 a 2 milioni di piedi quadrati di spazi ufficio.  Presente in sette città con 50 sedi, WeWork India gestisce oltre 6,5 milioni di piedi quadrati, più di 90.000 postazioni e serve oltre 70.000 membri. Circa l’80% della clientela è costituita da grandi aziende, mentre il resto comprende PMI, startup e imprenditori.  Gli spazi di lavoro flessibili sono sempre più richiesti in India, poiché le aziende cercano maggiore efficienza con modelli distribuiti. I dati del settore mostrano una crescita significativa negli affitti di spazi flessibili tra l’anno finanziario 2022 e il 2023, soprattutto a Bengaluru, Pune e Delhi NCR.  A livello globale, WeWork ha affrontato grandi difficoltà, con perdite e investimenti sfavorevoli che hanno portato al fallimento negli Stati Uniti e in Canada. Altre notizie di business: le autorità fiscali indiane stanno indagando sulle filiali locali di Apple, Google e Amazon per possibili questioni fiscali, gli indiani sono ora i principali acquirenti nel mercato immobiliare di Dubai, e Razorpay intende riportare la sua società madre in India, operazione che potrebbe comportare rilevanti tasse negli Stati Uniti.

article_content: A group of tourists who ran up the iconic 'Rocky' steps at the Philadelphia Museum of Art received a memorable surprise at the top—a selfie with Sylvester Stallone, the actor who played Rocky. Peter Rowe said he and his two friends had just finished climbing the famous staircase on Saturday when they encountered Stallone. “He said to us, 'Man, you guys are fast. You're making me look bad!'” Rowe recalled. Rowe (right) captured a selfie with friends Jacob Kerstan (left), Andrew Wright (third from left), and Stallone on the renowned steps. Stallone posed with his fist raised, telling the trio, “Look tough, guys!” according to Rowe. The steps became famous after Stallone’s character, Rocky Balboa, used them for a training montage in the original 'Rocky' film. Thousands of people now visit the steps yearly to recreate the run and take pictures with the Rocky statue, which originally appeared as a prop in 'Rocky III.' Rowe’s friends, Jacob Kerstan and Andrew Wright, were visiting from Azusa Pacific University in the Los Angeles area. Rowe recently graduated from the university and moved to Lancaster, Pennsylvania, about 60 miles west of Philadelphia. Despite all their time in Los Angeles, Rowe said they had never seen a celebrity before. “What are the chances of meeting him, that celebrity, right there?” he said about spotting Stallone, calling it “an unreal experience.” Stallone is in Philadelphia filming 'Creed,' the latest installment in the Rocky series, starring Michael B. Jordan as the grandson of Apollo Creed. A representative for the Stallone film did not immediately respond to questions about the photo on Tuesday.

article_content: World champion Jorge Lorenzo narrowed Dani Pedrosa's MotoGP championship lead with his second consecutive victory on Sunday, overcoming scorching heat in Spain. Pedrosa had set a lap record during Saturday's qualifying for the Catalunya Grand Prix but was outpaced by fellow Spaniard Lorenzo from the start and finished second, holding off persistent attacks from rookie teammate Marc Marquez. Lorenzo, who also triumphed in Italy two weeks ago, brought his Yamaha within seven points of Pedrosa after claiming his third win in the sixth of 18 races on the 2013 calendar. The 26-year-old from Mallorca previously won at Montmelo in 2012 and 2010—the latter leading to his first world title. “To be honest, I didn’t expect to win,” said Lorenzo after earning his 26th career victory, placing him seventh on the all-time list. “I knew I had some chance, but not like in Mugello where I was more confident. Physically, it was extremely tough as it was the hottest race of the year. I had to push 100% the whole race, as any mistake would have been costly. Because I stayed mentally strong and never gave up, I managed to open a small gap in the last five laps, which was enough to win.” Pedrosa, from Sabadell in Catalonia, has now finished runner-up three times in his home race, which he last won in 2008. “I had to ride defensively most of the race as Marc kept attacking,” Pedrosa commented. “I was never close enough to Jorge to attempt a pass. It wasn’t my ideal race, but I’m relieved to still lead overall.” Marquez, who started sixth, bounced back from his crash at Mugello to secure his fifth podium of the season, maintaining third place in the championship—30 points behind Pedrosa. Seven-time world champion Valentino Rossi finished fourth, returning to form after not finishing the previous race in Italy and coming twelfth in France. “Race by race, aside from some bad luck, especially like at Mugello, we’re improving and I can ride the bike better,” Rossi said. “We still have challenges, particularly early in the race where the bike setup isn’t perfect yet.” Germany’s Stefan Bradl finished fifth on a Honda, ahead of Britain’s Bradley Smith, who achieved a career-best sixth for Monster Yamaha Tech 3, and Ducati’s Andrea Dovizioso in seventh. Spain’s Aleix Espargaro took eighth on an Aprilia, with U.S. veteran Colin Edwards ninth for Kawasaki, and Italy’s Michele Pirro completing the top ten on a Ducati. Cal Crutchlow, who started second, crashed out on lap 10, along with Ducati’s former world champion Nicky Hayden—among eight riders who did not finish.
