Il ventiseienne di Maiorca aveva già vinto a Montmelo nel 2012 e nel 2010—l’ultima vittoria gli valse il suo primo titolo mondiale. “A dire il vero, non mi aspettavo di vincere,” ha detto Lorenzo dopo la sua 26ª vittoria in carriera, che lo pone settimo nella classifica di tutti i tempi. “Sapevo di avere qualche chance, ma non come a Mugello dove ero più sicuro. article_content: Dr. Ed Allen, a 32-year-old general practitioner, describes the past 15 months living with severe long Covid as 'the greatest challenge of his life.' Before becoming ill in February 2022, Dr. Allen was an avid fitness enthusiast, but during his worst days, he struggled to walk even 500 steps. Although he reports gradual improvement, he still worries he may never fully recover. Dr. Allen, who works at Birstall Medical Practice near Leicester, shared his story with the BBC to raise awareness about long Covid. He first tested positive for Covid-19 in February 2022, initially experiencing mild symptoms. However, after a second infection later that year, his illness persisted. 'I had muscle aches and felt feverish, with flu-like symptoms. The unbearable fatigue lasted for weeks and then months,' he said. 'Most days were intolerable—I couldn’t keep my eyes open and spent most of my time on the sofa. The brain fog was unlike anything I’d previously experienced.' Most people recover from Covid-19 within a few days or weeks, and usually within 12 weeks. For some, symptoms can last longer. Long Covid is a relatively new condition still being studied. Its symptoms most commonly include fatigue, shortness of breath, and brain fog, though some experience additional problems, according to the NHS. Dr. Allen became so unwell that he was forced to take six months off work. He is now able to return to work part-time, working the equivalent of two or three days a week at the surgery, but says he has made 'limited progress' and is still not as he was before. He explained: 'Eighteen months ago, before long Covid, I could do anything I wanted. Exercise was like a drug for me. I’d push myself to my limits—a two-hour walk after a gym session would have been nothing. Now, walking is slow and difficult.' 'There were dark times when I felt trapped and unable to function as I had before. I’m proud to have found my way out of that. Long Covid isn’t just physical—it affects you psychologically too. It has impacted me on many levels. This is the biggest challenge I’ve ever faced, without a doubt. I wouldn’t wish it on anyone.' Dr. Allen is among about 6,000 people who have received help from a long Covid clinic at Leicester’s Glenfield Hospital, established in June 2020. He is now able to walk more than 6,000 steps. Dr. Sanjay Bhandari, a consultant cardiologist who runs the clinic, said: 'Long Covid is a real and debilitating condition. We see patients like Ed who were previously very active and are now struggling to manage daily activities. These are genuine symptoms. Recovery mainly happens through rehabilitation, supporting patients to gradually increase exercise without overexertion.' article_content: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has called for a review of the powers granted to judges to annul elections in Nigeria, stating that it undermines the will of millions of voters. He described as unacceptable a situation where a small group of judges—three or four—determine the nation’s leadership after citizens have voted. Obasanjo made the remarks on Monday during a high-level consultation he organized titled 'Rethinking Western Liberal Democracy in Africa' at the Green Legacy Resorts within the Olusegun Obasanjo Presidential Library in Abeokuta. The event was attended by notable figures from academia and politics, including former governors Kayode Fayemi (Ekiti), Sule Lamido (Jigawa), Liyel Imoke (Cross River), and Aminu Tambuwal (Sokoto). "Whatever system of government we have, it should not be possible for three or four individuals in the judiciary to overturn the choices of millions of voters. We must find a way to address this. It's unacceptable that millions might vote one way, but the final decision rests with a small group of judges whose rulings cannot be challenged. That should not stand," Obasanjo said. "If we call for new elections, what happens to the initial one? I don’t have all the answers, but we need to address this issue in our democracy." Obasanjo also expressed reservations about the phrase 'Nigerian factor,' arguing that it often serves to excuse unethical conduct. He recounted that in 1998, his party lost local government elections because they refused to offer money to police and Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) officials, as was customarily done. He opposed these payments, insisting that such officials are government employees who are already salaried. He said, "When things go wrong, people call it the 'Nigerian factor.' In 1998, during the first local government election, party leaders gathered in my office in Abeokuta and suggested funds should be given to INEC and police. I said, 'What nonsense! Aren’t they already paid?' They replied, 'That’s how it’s done,' but I refused to approve it. Predictably, we lost all the local governments. Afterwards, party members told me, 'If you had let us do it our way, we would have won.' I felt guilty." "For the following state assembly election, I stayed out of the process completely—the outcome did not change. Even the person who took the money didn’t distribute it as intended," Obasanjo added.

Obasanjo ha rilasciato queste dichiarazioni lunedì durante una consultazione di alto livello da lui organizzata intitolata 'Ripensare la democrazia liberale occidentale in Africa', tenutasi al Green Legacy Resorts presso la Olusegun Obasanjo Presidential Library ad Abeokuta. All’evento hanno partecipato personalità di spicco del mondo accademico e politico, tra cui gli ex governatori Kayode Fayemi (Ekiti), Sule Lamido (Jigawa), Liyel Imoke (Cross River) e Aminu Tambuwal (Sokoto). "In qualunque sistema di governo adottiamo, non dovrebbe essere possibile per tre o quattro membri della magistratura ribaltare le scelte di milioni di elettori. Dobbiamo trovare un modo per affrontare questa questione. È inaccettabile che milioni votino in un modo e che la decisione finale spetti a pochi giudici con sentenze che non possono essere contestate. Questo non dovrebbe essere accettato," ha dichiarato Obasanjo. "Se si decide di ripetere le elezioni, che fine fa la precedente? Non ho tutte le risposte, ma dobbiamo discutere questa problematica nella nostra democrazia." Obasanjo ha anche espresso riserve sull’espressione 'fattore nigeriano', sostenendo che troppo spesso viene usata per giustificare comportamenti non etici. Ha raccontato che nel 1998 il suo partito perse le elezioni amministrative locali perché si rifiutò di offrire denaro a poliziotti e funzionari della Commissione Elettorale Nazionale Indipendente (INEC), come invece era consuetudine. Si oppose a questi pagamenti, ritenendo che tali funzionari statali fossero già remunerati dal governo. Ha detto: "Quando le cose vanno male, la gente parla del 'fattore nigeriano'. Nel 1998, durante la prima elezione locale, i leader di partito si riunirono nel mio ufficio ad Abeokuta e suggerirono di stanziare fondi per INEC e la polizia. Dissi: 'Che assurdità! Non sono già pagati?' Loro replicarono: 'Così si fa', ma io mi rifiutai. Come previsto, abbiamo perso tutti i governi locali. In seguito, i membri del partito mi dissero: 'Se ci avessi lasciato fare come sempre, avremmo vinto.' Mi sono sentito in colpa." "Per le successive elezioni dell’assemblea statale mi sono completamente tirato fuori dal processo—ma il risultato non è cambiato. Persino chi ricevette il denaro non lo distribuì come previsto," ha aggiunto Obasanjo.

article_content: Hungary's Prime Minister Viktor Orban maintains that Ukraine is unlikely to achieve a military victory over Russia and encourages the European Union to pursue alternative solutions to the ongoing war. In an interview with Hungarian state radio, Orban—known for his nationalist policies—criticized the EU’s approach to Ukraine, saying, 'Everyone knows, but few admit, that this strategy is failing. Ukrainians won’t win on the battlefield,' and questioned whether Hungary should continue allocating public funds to support Ukraine. Though Western support is seen as vital to Ukraine’s defense, patience is reportedly waning among some European and American political leaders. Orban, an Oxford graduate often characterized as close to Russian President Vladimir Putin, has blocked EU funding for Ukraine following Kyiv’s decision to label Hungary’s OTP Bank as an international sponsor of war. On the diplomatic front, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda sharply criticized Orban for engaging with Russia, citing Orban’s meeting with Putin in October. Speaking in Brussels, Nausėda stated, 'It’s more than strange for us to start connecting with a regime that commits severe atrocities in Ukraine. This sends the wrong message internationally, especially to Ukraine.' The United States is monitoring the battlefield closely. National Security Council spokesperson John Kirby reported on Thursday that Russian forces have incurred heavy losses during intensified attacks near Avdiivka, in eastern Ukraine’s Donetsk region, losing more than 125 armored vehicles and substantial equipment. Kirby further noted that low morale prevails among Russian soldiers. Nonetheless, US officials caution that Russia retains offensive capacity and may achieve tactical gains in the coming months. Also on Thursday, Russia’s parliament endorsed a draft budget for 2024–2026 featuring a 68% surge in military spending, placing defense expenditures above social spending by over 25% for the first time. Meanwhile, Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko has called for an immediate end to hostilities and urged negotiations on both territory and peace. He highlighted concerns about potentially limited US aid to Ukraine as a reason to commence talks without any preconditions. Recently, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a decree that rules out dialogue with Putin specifically, but leaves open the possibility of talking with Russia under certain terms. Despite 18 months of conflict, a majority of Ukrainians remain determined to fight until victory. An October Gallup poll found that 60% support continued resistance, but 31% would prefer a negotiated end to the war.

article_content: Three brothers from Morenci, Michigan—Tanner Skelton (5 years old), Alexander William Skelton (7), and Andrew Skelton (9)—have been missing since the Thanksgiving holiday weekend. Local residents came together for a candlelight vigil in support of the boys, who were last seen at their father John's home on Thanksgiving Day. John Skelton was arrested last Tuesday following his release from a mental health facility, where he had been treated after a suicide attempt, according to Morenci Police Chief Larry Weeks. He faces a parental kidnapping charge and is resisting extradition from Ohio, with a hearing set for December 14. Despite efforts from both local and federal authorities, the boys' whereabouts remain unknown. Investigators have found several items but have not determined what happened to the children. Authorities remain skeptical of the information John Skelton has provided. Skelton says he left the boys with a woman named Joann Taylor on the morning before his suicide attempt, claiming this was to prevent them from seeing his actions. He stated that Taylor was supposed to take the boys home to Morenci on November 26, but they never arrived. Officials say Skelton had no known relationship with Taylor and they are not sure she exists. Authorities are asking for the public’s help, especially in spotting Skelton’s blue 2000 Dodge Caravan, which may have carried the boys along the 25-mile route between Morenci and Holiday City, Ohio. The last confirmed non-family sighting of the brothers was at 5 p.m. on November 25. Descriptions of the boys are as follows: Tanner is 3 feet 6 inches tall, with strawberry-blond hair, blue eyes, and weighing about 40 pounds; Alexander is 3 feet 9 inches, with brown hair and eyes, about 45 pounds, and has scars on his hairline and chin; Andrew, the oldest, is 4 feet 1 inch tall, with brown hair and eyes, weighing about 57 pounds.

article_content: A recent study led by scientists at UC San Diego’s Scripps Institution of Oceanography reveals that meltwater flowing out to sea from beneath Antarctic glaciers—known as subglacial discharge—may be causing these glaciers to lose ice more rapidly. According to their advanced modeling, this mechanism could significantly contribute to global sea-level rise, especially under high greenhouse gas emissions scenarios. Importantly, this subglacial discharge effect is not currently considered in the major projections used by organizations like the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). If this process is widespread across Antarctica, global sea-level rise may be underestimated in existing models. Lead author Tyler Pelle explained, ‘Knowing when and how much global sea-level will rise is critical to the welfare of coastal communities. Millions of people live in low-lying areas and we need accurate projections to prepare adequately.’ Published on October 27 in Science Advances, the research focused on Denman and Scott glaciers in East Antarctica, modeling their retreat through the year 2300 under various greenhouse gas scenarios. This new model uniquely accounts for subglacial discharge—the flow of meltwater from beneath glaciers into the sea. Denman and Scott glaciers combined hold enough ice to raise global sea levels by about 1.5 meters (5 feet) if completely melted. In a high emissions scenario (IPCC’s SSP5-8.5), the study found subglacial discharge increased their sea-level contribution by 15.7%, from 19 millimeters (0.74 inches) to 22 millimeters (0.86 inches) by 2300. These neighboring glaciers are located above a more-than-two-mile-deep continental trench. The new model showed that with subglacial discharge included, the glaciers reach this trench’s steep slope—and thus accelerate retreat—about 25 years earlier than expected. Co-author Jamin Greenbaum noted, ‘This paper is a wake-up call for the modeling community. We can’t model these systems accurately without including subglacial discharge.’ The study also highlights the critical role of future emissions. In its low-emissions scenario, the glaciers did not reach the trench’s steep slope and avoided dramatic sea-level contributions. As Greenbaum put it, ‘The real doomsday story is still emissions, and humanity still controls that outcome.’ Subglacial meltwater arises from friction and geothermal heat at the base of the ice. Prior research suggests such meltwater exists beneath many glaciers worldwide, including major Antarctic glaciers like Thwaites Glacier. When this subglacial discharge flows out, it’s thought to accelerate melting of the floating ice shelf attached to glaciers, mainly by increasing ocean mixing and delivering more heat beneath the ice. This leads to faster upstream glacier movement and further sea-level rise. Although this effect is scientifically recognized, it hasn’t been factored into sea-level rise models because its impact was believed to be localized. Pelle became focused on subglacial discharge after observing unexpectedly rapid melting at Denman Glacier compared to neighboring Scott Glacier, despite similar ocean conditions. Model results showed this was due to a stronger subglacial discharge channel draining across Denman’s grounding line. The team’s simulations modeled three scenarios: a control (no extra ocean warming), a low emissions pathway (SSP1-2.6), and a high emissions pathway (SSP5-8.5), both with and without subglacial discharge. In high emissions, subglacial discharge raised projected sea-level rise from these glaciers by around 16%. Under the high emissions scenario including subglacial discharge, Denman and Scott Glaciers retreated into the deep trench about 25 years sooner, and their annual contribution to sea-level rise quickly intensified to about 0.33 millimeters per year—approximately half of the current annual contribution from the entire Antarctic ice sheet. As the glacier retreats down the trench's steep slope, called a retrograde slope, the ice shelf loses increasingly large slabs of ice, a process known as Marine Ice Sheet Instability. This can drive rapid, runaway ice loss, outpacing new accumulation. Such retrograde slopes also exist beneath other significant glaciers, like Thwaites, raising concerns about broader Antarctic ice sheet instability. ‘Subglacial meltwater has been inferred beneath most, if not all, Antarctic glaciers,’ Pelle said. ‘It’s urgent to model these glaciers and understand the impact of subglacial discharge on sea-level rise.’ The team is now seeking funding to expand their model to the entire Antarctic ice sheet, and future work aims to allow for a dynamic response of the subglacial environment to climate. Present models treat subglacial meltwater as constant. Allowing it to dynamically interact with the ice and ocean systems could reveal even stronger effects, suggests Greenbaum. ‘Our results may be conservative estimates of subglacial discharge’s impact.’ Greenbaum’s upcoming fieldwork in Antarctica, in partnership with NSF, NASA, the Australian Antarctic Division, and Korea Polar Research Institute, aims to collect direct evidence of subglacial freshwater discharge beneath Antarctic ice shelves. Co-authors on this study are Christine Dow (University of Waterloo), Adrian Jenkins (Northumbria University), and Mathieu Morlighem (Dartmouth College).
translated_content: Un recente studio guidato da scienziati della Scripps Institution of Oceanography dell’Università della California, San Diego, rivela che l’acqua di fusione che scorre sotto i ghiacciai antartici fino al mare—detta scarico subglaciale—potrebbe far perdere ghiaccio a questi ghiacciai più rapidamente. Secondo i loro avanzati modelli, questo meccanismo potrebbe contribuire in modo significativo all’innalzamento globale del livello del mare, soprattutto in scenari di alte emissioni di gas serra. È importante sottolineare che l’effetto dello scarico subglaciale non è attualmente considerato nelle principali proiezioni utilizzate da organizzazioni come il Gruppo intergovernativo sul cambiamento climatico (IPCC). Se questo processo fosse diffuso in tutta l’Antartide, l’innalzamento globale del mare potrebbe essere sottostimato nei modelli attuali. Il primo autore Tyler Pelle ha spiegato: «Sapere quando e quanto si innalzerà il livello globale del mare è fondamentale per il benessere delle comunità costiere. Milioni di persone vivono in aree a bassa quota e abbiamo bisogno di proiezioni accurate per prepararci adeguatamente». Pubblicata il 27 ottobre su Science Advances, la ricerca si è concentrata sui ghiacciai Denman e Scott nell’Antartide Orientale, modellando il loro ritiro fino al 2300 secondo diversi scenari di emissioni di gas serra. Questo nuovo modello tiene conto in modo innovativo dello scarico subglaciale, cioè del flusso d’acqua di fusione da sotto i ghiacciai verso il mare. Denman e Scott insieme contengono abbastanza ghiaccio da far salire il livello del mare di circa 1,5 metri (5 piedi) se si sciogliessero completamente. In uno scenario di alte emissioni (SSP5-8.5 dell’IPCC), lo studio ha rilevato che lo scarico subglaciale ha aumentato il contributo all’innalzamento del livello del mare del 15,7%, da 19 millimetri (0,74 pollici) a 22 millimetri (0,86 pollici) entro il 2300. Questi ghiacciai, vicini tra loro, si trovano sopra una fossa continentale profonda più di tre chilometri. Il nuovo modello mostra che, includendo lo scarico subglaciale, i ghiacciai raggiungono il ripido pendio della fossa—accelerando così il ritiro—circa 25 anni prima del previsto. Il coautore Jamin Greenbaum ha dichiarato: «Questo studio è una sveglia per la comunità dei modellatori. Non possiamo modellare accuratamente questi sistemi senza includere lo scarico subglaciale». Lo studio evidenzia anche l’importanza cruciale delle emissioni future. Nello scenario a basse emissioni, i ghiacciai non raggiungono il pendio ripido della fossa ed evitano contributi drammatici al livello del mare. Come ha affermato Greenbaum, «La vera storia da fine del mondo sono ancora le emissioni, e l’umanità ha ancora quel pulsante in mano». L’acqua di fusione subglaciale nasce da attrito e calore geotermico alla base del ghiaccio. Ricerche precedenti suggeriscono che tale acqua sia presente sotto molti ghiacciai nel mondo, inclusi ghiacciai antartici importanti come il Thwaites. Quando questa acqua fluisce fuori, si pensa che acceleri lo scioglimento della piattaforma galleggiante, soprattutto aumentando la miscelazione oceanica e portando più calore sotto il ghiaccio. Questo porta a un movimento più rapido del ghiacciaio a monte e a ulteriore innalzamento del mare. Sebbene l’effetto sia riconosciuto scientificamente, non era stato incluso nei modelli perché si credeva fosse localizzato. Pelle si è focalizzato sullo scarico subglaciale dopo aver osservato uno scioglimento inaspettatamente rapido al ghiacciaio Denman rispetto al vicino Scott, nonostante condizioni oceaniche simili. I risultati dei modelli indicano che ciò era dovuto a un canale di scarico subglaciale più forte sotto la linea di galleggiamento del Denman. Le simulazioni del gruppo hanno considerato tre scenari: uno di controllo (senza ulteriore riscaldamento oceanico), uno a basse emissioni (SSP1-2.6) e uno ad alte emissioni (SSP5-8.5), sia con che senza scarico subglaciale. Nelle alte emissioni, lo scarico subglaciale ha aumentato il contributo all’innalzamento del mare di circa il 16%. Con alte emissioni e scarico subglaciale, Denman e Scott sono arretrati nella fossa profonda circa 25 anni prima, e il loro contributo annuo all’innalzamento del mare è aumentato rapidamente fino a circa 0,33 millimetri l’anno—pari a circa metà del contributo attuale dell’intero ghiaccio antartico. Mentre il ghiacciaio arretra lungo il ripido pendio della fossa, chiamato pendio retrogrado, la piattaforma glaciale perde lastre di ghiaccio sempre più spesse, un processo noto come ‘instabilità della calotta glaciale marina’. Ciò può portare a rapida perdita di ghiaccio, superando l’accumulo nell’entroterra. Pendii simili si trovano anche sotto altri grandi ghiacciai come il Thwaites, alimentando timori di una più ampia instabilità della calotta antartica. «L’acqua di fusione subglaciale è stata individuata sotto la maggior parte dei ghiacciai antartici», ha spiegato Pelle. «È urgente modellare questi ghiacciai e capire quanto influisce lo scarico subglaciale sull’innalzamento del mare». Il gruppo cerca ora finanziamenti per estendere il modello e, in futuro, permettere una risposta dinamica dell’ambiente subglaciale al clima. Gli attuali modelli trattano l’acqua di fusione subglaciale come costante. Permetterle di interagire dinamicamente con ghiaccio e oceano potrebbe mostrare effetti ancora più forti, suggerisce Greenbaum. «I nostri risultati potrebbero essere una stima prudente dell’impatto dello scarico subglaciale». I prossimi lavori di Greenbaum in Antartide, con NSF, NASA, la Divisione Antartica Australiana e il Korea Polar Research Institute, mirano a raccogliere prove dirette dello scarico di acqua dolce subglaciale sotto le piattaforme antartiche. Tra gli autori dello studio ci sono anche Christine Dow (University of Waterloo), Adrian Jenkins (Northumbria University) e Mathieu Morlighem (Dartmouth College).

article_content: An 8-year-old Bangladeshi boy, Noshat Nahian, was fatally struck by a tractor-trailer in Queens, New York, while walking to school on the last day before the holiday break. Noshat, a third-grader at Public School 152, was walking with his 11-year-old sister around 8 a.m., carrying a red gift bag for his teacher, when driver Mauricio Osorio-Palominos hit him with the back wheels of his truck. Police arrested 51-year-old Osorio-Palominos of Newark, New Jersey, after discovering he was driving with a suspended license. The accident happened half a block from the school, as Osorio-Palominos was turning left onto Northern Boulevard from Sixty-first Street. Noshat's mother usually walked her children to school but stayed home that morning. Witness Maria Humala reported seeing Noshat wearing a hood and looking down just before the collision. Noshat's sister was in shock beside him. After the accident, Noshat's sister ran home to get their mother, who was able to be with her son at Elmhurst Hospital before he died. Osorio-Palominos had received his commercial driving license in 1985 and has had it suspended and reinstated three times. He has 17 prior violations, including failing to comply with police instructions, ignoring traffic signals, seat belt violations, and speeding. He owns Gamosse Transportation, operating as the sole employee. Noshat's father, 40-year-old Mohammed Osma Miah, works for a rice wholesaler, and his mother works at a store in Jackson Heights. The family had moved to the U.S. from Bangladesh just months earlier because Noshat liked the neighborhood. Mr. Miah expressed deep grief and regret, mentioning he was saving up to buy Noshat a laptop. Local residents noted that the intersection where the accident happened is particularly dangerous, as there is typically no crossing guard stationed across the six-lane boulevard. School administrators at P.S. 152 have brought in crisis counselors for students needing support during the holiday break.

Leszek Balcerowicz, Poland’s former finance minister, recently described Poland as enjoying its ‘best period in 300 years.’ This article examines how Poland transitioned from communism to become one of Eastern Europe’s most stable and thriving democracies.

In 1918, modern Poland gained independence, only to be invaded by Germany and the Soviet Union during the Second World War. Nearly six million Poles, including most of the country’s large Jewish population, died in the conflict. After World War II, Poland became a Soviet satellite state under communist rule for the next four decades, facing periodic revolts against the authoritarian regime in Warsaw.

A turning point came in 1980 at the Lenin Shipyard in Gdansk, where widespread economic dissatisfaction led to worker strikes. Led by electrician Lech Walesa, the workers secured the right to strike and form trade unions, marking the birth of the Solidarity movement. Solidarity grew into a powerful force, with support from the Catholic Church and the influence of Polish-born Pope John Paul II, who had visited Poland in 1979.

Despite efforts by Soviet-backed authorities—including the imposition of martial law by General Wojciech Jaruzelski in 1981, which banned Solidarity—the movement persisted. Poland’s deepening economic struggles eventually forced the government to negotiate with Walesa and Solidarity, leading to partially free elections in 1989. Solidarity won a significant victory, gaining major influence over the new government. Tadeusz Mazowiecki became prime minister, and Lech Walesa was elected president in 1990.

Under finance minister Leszek Balcerowicz, Poland initiated extensive economic reforms, moving away from a centrally planned system. While this transformation brought increased unemployment and infrastructure challenges, deregulation of banking and lending, privatization of state assets, and stronger domestic competition fueled dynamic growth. By the mid-1990s, Poland was known as the ‘Tiger of Europe.’

Poland also liberalized trade, made the zloty convertible, and entered new markets, particularly in the EU and U.S. Joining NATO in 1999 and the European Union in 2004 aligned Poland further with the West. Although many Poles initially left for jobs in other EU countries, this trend slowed as Poland experienced robust economic growth after 2008.

Politically, Poland has established itself as a fully democratic country. Since 1991, all parliamentary and four presidential elections have been free and fair, with smooth and constitutional transfers of power between governments.

Claims management firms have taken as much as £5 billion from the compensation paid to victims of the PPI mis-selling scandal. Many of these companies used nuisance texts or cold calls to gather a database of potential claimants, later charging up to 25% in fees to recover payment protection insurance (PPI) premiums—often without making the charges clear.

As a result, people mis-sold unnecessary insurance by major UK banks were financially exploited a second time by these claims firms. The banks have set aside over £22 billion for refunds after what is considered the biggest scandal in British retail banking.

While anyone mis-sold PPI can claim a refund themselves for free using a standard complaints letter, many banks made the process difficult. This allowed claims management firms to step in and offer paid help, taking a significant portion of the compensation returned to consumers.

New findings from Citizens Advice reveal almost one in three people using claims management companies felt pressured to pursue a refund, and 27% said the fees were not properly explained. In some cases, successful claimants may have ended up in debt to these firms, since if an individual owes money to their bank, the lender can use the PPI compensation to pay off the balance—leaving the customer responsible for paying the claims firm's fees.

Citizens Advice research found 39% of customers did not know they could make a claim for free. The organization is calling for a ban on cold calls from claims firms, aiming to reduce nuisance calls and protect consumers from predatory practices.

Gillian Guy, chief executive of Citizens Advice, criticized both banks and claims management firms, highlighting the need for stricter regulation and improved customer treatment. She emphasized that some claims companies operate below expected standards and that the regulator should revoke licenses from underperforming firms. Guy also argued banks should focus on helping customers save money, rather than mis-selling products.

In addition, the City regulator, the Financial Conduct Authority, found that despite some improvements, one in ten financial firms with sales teams were still failing to manage staff bonus schemes properly, increasing the risk of new mis-selling scandals.

Le società di gestione dei reclami hanno prelevato fino a 5 miliardi di sterline dai risarcimenti destinati alle vittime dello scandalo della vendita impropria delle assicurazioni PPI. Molte di queste aziende hanno utilizzato messaggi indesiderati o chiamate a freddo per creare un database di potenziali clienti, addebitando poi fino al 25% di commissioni per il recupero dei premi delle assicurazioni sulla protezione dei pagamenti (PPI), spesso senza spiegare chiaramente questi costi.

Di conseguenza, le persone a cui le principali banche britanniche avevano venduto polizze inutili sono state sfruttate una seconda volta da queste società di gestione dei reclami. Le banche hanno stanziato oltre 22 miliardi di sterline per i rimborsi in seguito a quello che è considerato il più grande scandalo nella storia della banca al dettaglio britannica.

Sebbene chiunque sia stato vittima di una vendita impropria di PPI possa richiedere gratuitamente un rimborso utilizzando una lettera di reclamo standard, molte banche hanno reso il processo complicato. Ciò ha permesso alle società di gestione dei reclami di intervenire e offrire assistenza a pagamento, trattenendo gran parte dei risarcimenti restituiti ai consumatori.

Secondo una nuova ricerca di Citizens Advice, quasi una persona su tre che si è rivolta a queste società si è sentita sotto pressione per richiedere un rimborso, mentre il 27% ha dichiarato che le commissioni non sono state adeguatamente spiegate. In alcuni casi, chi ha ottenuto con successo il rimborso potrebbe essersi indebitato con queste aziende, poiché se una persona ha debiti con la propria banca, la banca può utilizzare il risarcimento PPI per saldare il saldo, lasciando al cliente la responsabilità di pagare la commissione alla società di gestione dei reclami.

Dalla ricerca di Citizens Advice emerge che il 39% dei clienti non era a conoscenza di poter richiedere un rimborso gratuitamente. L’organizzazione chiede un divieto alle chiamate promozionali da parte delle società di gestione dei reclami, per ridurre le chiamate indesiderate e proteggere i consumatori da comportamenti predatori.

Gillian Guy, amministratrice delegata di Citizens Advice, ha criticato sia le banche che le società di gestione dei reclami, sottolineando la necessità di una regolamentazione più severa e di un miglior trattamento dei clienti. Ha ribadito che alcune società operano al di sotto degli standard previsti e che l’ente regolatore dovrebbe revocare la licenza alle aziende non conformi. Guy ha anche affermato che le banche dovrebbero concentrarsi sull’aiutare i clienti a risparmiare denaro, anziché vendere loro prodotti non necessari.

article_content: Louise Whitby, a pregnant employee at the recruitment firm A4e in Kirkby, Merseyside, missed out on a share of a £28.8 million EuroMillions jackpot after being absent from work due to morning sickness. Ten of her colleagues, who participated in the workplace lottery syndicate, divided the jackpot, with each receiving about £2.8 million. Whitby, aged 31, claims she had consistently contributed to the syndicate for two years and attempted to pay her weekly £2 share prior to the winning draw but was turned down. As a result, she has hired a solicitor to pursue her share of the winnings, arguing she was excluded because she was unable to attend work due to pregnancy-related illness. Had she been included, each syndicate member's portion would have been just over £2.5 million. The ten winners requested anonymity from the National Lottery organisers and are reported to have quit their jobs following the win. Whitby expressed feelings of disappointment and betrayal, stating she considered her colleagues friends but could no longer speak with them. The winning numbers were 16, 18, 31, 38, 49, and Lucky Stars 4 and 10. Other staff at the industrial park confirmed most employees did not report for work after the draw, and that new people had to be brought in to cover their roles. A social media post from another A4e employee, later deleted, referenced the sudden staff departures following the win. A4e is currently advertising new positions at its Kirkby office, including adviser and administrator roles. An A4e spokesperson declined to comment on the situation. The ticket holder became the 16th largest National Lottery winner in UK history. A National Lottery spokesperson confirmed the prize had been claimed and praised the UK's ongoing success in EuroMillions.

article_content: Venugopal Garre, Managing Director at Bernstein, believes that top private banks should be a priority for investors at present, citing low regulatory risk in this segment. He remains cautious on NBFCs (Non-Banking Financial Companies), particularly larger ones, and prefers to gain exposure to small and midcap financials (SMIDs) via specific allocations. Garre highlights the remarkable growth in the US tech sector, mentioning the soaring valuations of companies like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Apple. He notes it's challenging for Indian investors to participate in such growth via Indian IT largecaps, as these do not offer exposure to global high-tech trends. He suggests that if Indian investors are able to invest directly in leading global tech companies, it may be the most effective route. According to Garre, Indian IT services function as a core, cross-industry utility business with moderate growth. While the sector continues to adopt new technologies like AI, such innovations represent incremental opportunity rather than transformative growth. He proposes that an alternative strategy may lie in India's growing manufacturing sector, especially as tech supply chains diversify and assembly operations expand locally. Discussing the impact of AI, Garre remains optimistic about the Indian IT sector's adaptability, referencing its successful evolution through several major technological shifts over the past decades. He believes AI will not be an existential threat to the Indian IT industry, but rather an opportunity to enhance efficiency and service offerings. Garre points out a valuation gap in Indian markets, where IT companies often trade at much lower multiples than sectors with similar or lower growth rates, such as FMCG. Regarding portfolio strategy, Garre includes a small allocation to cryptocurrencies such as Ethereum, based on a global outlook favoring risk assets. He also mentions a shift out of fixed deposits after benefitting from favorable interest rates earlier in the year. Separate news highlights the Income Tax Department's detection of approximately ₹10,000 crore in tax evasion by e-tailers selling via social media platforms, such as Instagram and Facebook. The GST Department has issued over 20,000 notices since 2022, causing Indian companies to reassess their tax liabilities before engaging in mergers, acquisitions, or other major transactions. A separate report includes allegations from Nawaz Modi, the estranged wife of Raymond managing director Gautam Singhania, who claims Singhania assaulted her and their daughter two months ago.

article_content: Venice will introduce a trial system involving an admission fee and daily cap on visitor numbers in its crowded city center starting next April. The city's mayor, Luigi Brugnaro, described the scheme as the first of its kind in the world, aiming to manage tourist flows at peak times. Under the plan, visitors will need to reserve online and pay a €5 ($5.45) entry fee to access the city center between 8:30am and 4pm during peak tourist season from April 25 to May 5. The fee will also be active on weekends in May and June, and during the first two weekends of July. Visitors must obtain a QR code with their booking, which will be checked at designated entry points to access Venice's historic quarters. The restriction does not apply to smaller lagoon islands such as Murano, renowned for its glass-making. For years, authorities have debated, but not acted, on how to regulate the millions of people visiting Venice's fragile lagoon and landmarks like St Mark’s Square and the Rialto Bridge. With a permanent population of about 51,000 and frequent flooding, many residents are concerned the city cannot cope with mounting tourist pressure. Repeated delays in implementing the ticketing plan stemmed from concerns over reduced tourist revenue and restrictions on movement. However, the city moved forward following a UNESCO warning that Venice could be placed on the list of at-risk world heritage sites. Residents, Venetian natives, students, workers, and homeowners will be exempt from the scheme. Children under 14 can enter free of charge upon registration. Non-compliant visitors risk fines ranging from €50 to €310 ($54 to $340). Mayor Brugnaro stated the system could be adjusted to ensure its effectiveness, and hopes it may serve as a model for other vulnerable cities in need of protection.

Secondo il piano, i visitatori dovranno prenotare online e pagare un biglietto d'ingresso di 5 euro ($5,45) per accedere al centro città tra le 8:30 e le 16:00 durante l'alta stagione turistica, dal 25 aprile al 5 maggio. La tariffa sarà attiva anche nei weekend di maggio e giugno e durante i primi due fine settimana di luglio. I visitatori dovranno ottenere un codice QR con la prenotazione, che verrà controllato nei punti di accesso designati per entrare nei quartieri storici di Venezia. La restrizione non si applica alle isole minori della laguna, come Murano, famosa per la lavorazione del vetro. Le autorità hanno discusso per anni, senza agire, su come regolare i milioni di persone che visitano la fragile laguna e i simboli cittadini come Piazza San Marco e il Ponte di Rialto. Con una popolazione residente di circa 51.000 persone e frequenti episodi di allagamento, molti temono che la città non possa reggere la crescente pressione turistica. I ripetuti ritardi nell'attuazione del piano sono dovuti a dubbi sull'impatto sugli introiti turistici e sulle libertà di movimento. Tuttavia, il Comune ha deciso di procedere dopo l'avvertimento dell'UNESCO che Venezia potrebbe essere inserita tra i siti patrimonio mondiale a rischio. Saranno esentati dal sistema residenti, nativi veneziani, studenti, lavoratori e proprietari di abitazioni. L'ingresso sarà gratuito per i minori di 14 anni previa registrazione. article_content: Mohamed Salah inspired Fiorentina to a 3-1 victory over Sassuolo in Serie A on Saturday, keeping their hopes alive for Champions League qualification. Salah, who joined Fiorentina on loan from Chelsea in a deal that sent Juan Cuadrado to Stamford Bridge, opened the scoring with help from Khouma Babacar, who netted Fiorentina's other two goals. Domenico Berardi, who had hit the post earlier, scored a consolation goal for Sassuolo. Salah contributed one goal and one assist as Fiorentina beat Sassuolo 3-1. Khouma Babacar scored twice and celebrated with his teammates. Fiorentina temporarily closed the gap to third place down to four points, with Napoli facing Palermo later, hoping to move within a point of second-placed Roma. The win provides a timely boost for Fiorentina ahead of their Europa League round of 32 match against Tottenham Hotspur on Thursday. Sassuolo stayed 12th, suffering only their second home defeat of the season. Vincenzo Montella gave Salah his first start, and the Egyptian winger scored his first Fiorentina goal at the half-hour mark, sprinting onto Babacar's back-heel pass and shooting into the bottom left corner. Two minutes later, Salah returned the favor with a through ball, allowing Babacar to go past Paolo Cannavaro and beat Andrea Consigli from close range. Berardi nearly pulled Sassuolo back into the match just before halftime, but his curling shot hit the left post. Babacar doubled his tally in the 62nd minute, beating the offside trap to control David Pizarro's long ball. Berardi reduced the deficit five minutes later with a looping header over Fiorentina goalkeeper Ciprian Tatarusanu.

article_content: The friendly football match between Brazil and Argentina in Beijing, China, is in jeopardy due to severe air pollution. Stars including Neymar, Lionel Messi, and Angel di Maria are scheduled to play at the Bird's Nest stadium in the Chinese capital on Saturday, but the fixture may be cancelled. Currently, all players are confined to their hotels after Chinese authorities issued an orange pollution alert, advising people to stay indoors. On Thursday, the air quality index was reportedly 18 times higher than the recognized safety level. Regarding the situation, Brazil's team doctor Rodrigo Lasmar said, 'One of the recommendations from pollution control officials is to stay indoors, and that is what we have done. Our athletes only leave the hotel for training and spend about 22 out of every 24 hours inside.' Should the match go ahead, it would be the first time Brazil and Argentina have met since November 2012. Brazil coach Dunga urged his players to remain focused, expressing that there is little they can do about the difficult conditions at the Bird's Nest stadium. He stated, 'It is there. It is like when we played at altitude. We have to face the match. Nobody has the power to change it.' Robinho, the Santos forward, added, 'It is difficult to breathe. The throat remains dry. It feels like being near a bonfire, with heavy smoke. We cannot escape it. Those who cope best will have an advantage on the field.' The Bird's Nest was the main stadium for the 2008 Olympics, where Usain Bolt notably starred. Security measures have been increased to protect players, including Neymar, during their movements in the stadium, and coach Dunga continues to direct training sessions amidst the smog.

article_content:
The 45th edition of France’s Festival des 3 Continents will feature a retrospective dedicated to iconic Indian actor Amitabh Bachchan, organizers announced on Monday. Running in Nantes from November 24 to December 3, the festival segment, titled 'Amitabh Bachchan, Big B Forever', will showcase nine of Bachchan’s films from the 1970s and 1980s: Trishul, Amar Akbar Anthony, Satte Pe Satta, Sholay, Don, Kabhi Kabhie, Deewaar, Kaala Patthar, and Abhimaan.

This retrospective is organized in partnership with the Film Heritage Foundation (FHF) and with support from the French Embassy in India. Bachchan expressed his pleasure that FHF is co-presenting the selection of his early films at one of the oldest and most reputed film festivals. He noted that many of these movies gave him the opportunity to play a range of roles and work with significant filmmakers, including Hrishikesh Mukherjee, Manmohan Desai, Yash Chopra, and Ramesh Sippy. Although he will not attend in person, Bachchan shared that his daughter Shweta will represent him at the festival.

Shivendra Singh Dungarpur, director of FHF, said the foundation is proud to partner on the 'Amitabh Bachchan, Big B Forever' retrospective. The organization had previously hosted a four-day national event, 'Bachchan Back To The Beginning', for Bachchan’s 80th birthday last year. Dungarpur thanked festival artistic director Jerome Baron for the chance to showcase nine films from a period when Bachchan was at his career peak, from 1973 to 1982.

Jerome Baron commented that the Festival des 3 Continents seeks inspiration by connecting contemporary cinema with the classics. He called Bachchan a living icon, uniquely blending the past and present of popular Hindi cinema, and a truly unique performer.

Additionally, the festival will host the world premiere of 'The Real Superstar', a 68-minute experimental documentary on Bachchan by French filmmaker Cedric Dupire.

article_content: Nissan is investing $1.4 billion to modernize its Sunderland factory in northeast England, enabling production of new electric versions of the Qashqai and Juke, two of its top-selling vehicles. This initiative is seen as significant support for the UK government’s push to strengthen the economy. Currently producing gasoline and hybrid Qashqai and Juke models with a workforce of 6,000, the Sunderland plant will benefit from advances in manufacturing and the construction of a new gigafactory for electric vehicle batteries, according to both Nissan and government statements. Prime Minister Rishi Sunak described the move as a strong show of faith in the UK automotive sector, which reportedly adds £71 billion to the economy each year. To celebrate the news, Sunak and Chancellor Jeremy Hunt toured the plant, met with employees, and posed for photos. Nissan aims to transition its entire European passenger vehicle portfolio to electric power by 2030. The Sunderland facility will also manufacture the next generation Leaf. Battery production is already underway on the site by AESC, part of the Chinese group Envision; the new plans include building a third battery factory. The announcement comes as the UK faces economic sluggishness and steady inflation, but brings optimism. However, auto manufacturers remain apprehensive about incoming post-Brexit tariffs in January. These would raise costs for EVs if sufficient components aren’t sourced from either the UK or the EU—a challenge, since European battery production lags behind Asia. Nissan’s on-site battery facility could give it an advantage. Nissan joins other major companies increasing UK EV investment: BMW is investing £600 million in its Oxford Mini plant, Tata Sons is developing a £4 billion battery facility for Jaguar Land Rover, and Stellantis has allocated £100 million for electric vehicles at its Vauxhall factory. CEO Makoto Uchida underscored that electrification is essential to Nissan’s vision for carbon neutrality. With more electric models forthcoming, the company says it's accelerating rapidly into a new era.

article_content: Olawale Adetula, co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of TNC Africa, describes the new series ‘Ololade’ as a tribute to classic Nollywood television. This Netflix original, produced by TNC Africa, boasts a star-studded cast, including Femi Adebayo, Mercy Aigbe, Mide Martins, Adebowale Adedayo (Mr Macaroni), Liz Da-Silva, Jaiye Kuti, Kunle Idowu (Frank Donga), Debby Felix, Damilola Oni, Oluwatobi Olubiyi (Oli Ekun), and Olanrewaju Ayanwale. In a statement to Saturday Beats, Adetula said, “TNC Africa is dedicated to telling original African stories through TV series. ‘Ololade’ is our way of honoring Nollywood TV classics that many of us grew up watching. As a tech- and data-driven company, our research shows a growing demand for authentic TV drama. We believe a well-told story can resonate with anyone, regardless of their background or language. Our hope is that 'Olóládé' will encourage even more high-quality, original content in Nigeria’s indigenous languages.” Directed by Adeniyi Omobulejo, also known as TAJ, the series is set to premiere on November 24, 2023. Omobulejo stated, “Watching ‘Ololade’ brings back nostalgia—it’s all about strong storytelling, engaging characters, and dramatic developments, which are the essence of great television.” ‘Ololade’ follows the story of two friends who unexpectedly become wealthy, only to find themselves entangled in a risky money laundering scheme. TNC Africa is also behind ‘Little Black Book’ and ‘My Name Is A-zed’, both nominated for the 2022 Africa Magic Viewers Choice Awards.

article_content: Mobile security threats are sharply rising, with Android devices accounting for most malware incidents, as revealed by NQ Mobile. Headquartered in both the U.S. and China, the company estimated that 33 million Android devices were compromised by malware in 2012—over three times the number affected in the previous year. Omar Khan, Co-CEO of NQ Mobile, told CNN that Android’s open-source model allows for creative app development, but also opens the door to cybercriminals who exploit this openness to spread malicious apps. The report details that malware often infiltrates phones through apps designed to look genuine but are actually harmful, through phony websites, and through text scams called 'smishing,' which aim to steal private data like credit card or email details. Some threats extend beyond data theft; a German hacker and licensed pilot recently demonstrated an Android app that could, in theory, hijack an airplane remotely, adding a new layer of concern. Security firm Blue Coat identified that 25% of mobile malware originates from pornography websites. Studies from McAfee and NQ Mobile also indicate that 30% to 50% of users don’t secure their smartphones with passwords, making them more vulnerable. Khan recommended simple measures like enabling passwords, installing security software, and connecting only to trusted Wi-Fi or Bluetooth networks to safeguard devices. He noted that users often connect to unsafe sources without caution. NQ Mobile’s report showed that China, India, and Russia top the list of countries with infected devices, suggesting that heavy dependence on smartphones for internet makes users there especially vulnerable to attack.

Omar Khan, Co-CEO di NQ Mobile, ha dichiarato alla CNN che il modello open source di Android favorisce lo sviluppo di app innovative, ma apre anche la strada ai cybercriminali che sfruttano questa apertura per diffondere applicazioni malevoli. Il rapporto spiega che il malware spesso penetra nei telefoni tramite app che sembrano affidabili ma sono in realtà dannose, attraverso siti web fasulli e tramite truffe via SMS chiamate 'smishing', che puntano a rubare dati privati come dettagli di carte di credito o email. Alcune minacce vanno oltre il furto di dati; di recente, un hacker tedesco e pilota commerciale ha dimostrato un'app Android che, in teoria, potrebbe dirottare un aereo da remoto, suscitando nuove preoccupazioni. Khan ha raccomandato alcune semplici misure come attivare una password, installare software di sicurezza e connettersi solo a reti Wi-Fi o Bluetooth affidabili per proteggere i dispositivi. Il rapporto di NQ Mobile ha mostrato che Cina, India e Russia sono i paesi con più dispositivi infettati, suggerendo che la forte dipendenza dagli smartphone per l’accesso a Internet rende gli utenti in queste aree particolarmente vulnerabili agli attacchi.

article_content: A mother from Nottingham is upset after discovering her eight-year-old daughter's KFC meal was served in a takeaway box covered in green mold. Cherie Williams, 26, found the moldy residue after pouring her daughter Charleigh's food onto a plate. The meal, purchased for £1.99 from KFC in Bulwell by Charleigh's grandmother Mandy, was initially dismissed by staff as grease, despite the green color. When Mandy, 52, returned to complain the next day, she said the supervisor laughed and did not take her seriously. She attempted to contact KFC customer service, but waited on hold for 45 minutes without success. Only after media involvement did KFC apologize, saying this was an unprecedented incident that would be thoroughly investigated. The company promised to contact Ms. Williams with a goodwill gesture.

A court has heard that Manas Kapoor, a 35-year-old product controller at Morgan Stanley and a gambling addict, is accused of killing his wife Shivani in a fit of rage on the day he was due to attend a disciplinary meeting after losing the bank millions of pounds. Kapoor reportedly feared he would lose his job after an accounting error and had asked Shivani, also 35, to accompany him for support. Prosecutors allege that on July 10, 2013, Kapoor strangled Shivani at their Northwood, Middlesex home, then attempted to cover it up by claiming she had fallen off a stool. She died in the hospital two days later.

In the months preceding her death, Shivani discovered Kapoor had accrued £8,000 of gambling debt and had been borrowing from friends and family to pay it off. Jewelry and cash had also gone missing from their home, and when confronted, Kapoor denied involvement and became aggressive. The day before her death, Shivani told a friend she was considering calling the police and leaving Kapoor, but was reluctant due to their one-year-old daughter, Vania.

On the afternoon of July 10, Kapoor called emergency services, claiming to have found Shivani unconscious on the bedroom floor, suggesting she had fallen while reaching for something. Kapoor said Shivani suffered from blackouts, but friends and family contended that she had only ever fainted after missing a meal post-childbirth. Paramedics noticed a red mark on Shivani’s neck and found additional injuries, including bruises consistent with being restrained and evidence of force applied to her face and neck. Kapoor had fresh scratches on his face.

Prosecutor Duncan Atkinson told the court that the physical findings and timing indicated murder rather than accident. Kapoor’s financial troubles and stress over his job were presented as contributing factors. The court heard Shivani and Kapoor had experienced a strained marriage, with testimony from friends and family about Shivani’s unhappiness and the couple’s financial disputes. Kapoor maintains his innocence, alleging the death was accidental and that scratches on his face were from his daughter. The trial continues.

article_content: Dorking Museum unknowingly displayed live World War II explosives for almost twenty years. The dangerous items—an old cannon shell and a military flare—were only found during a recent stock assessment. After sending photos to the Imperial War Museum, staff were informed of the potential risks and immediately contacted local police. The bomb squad from Aldershot was called in, and Army specialists safely detonated the explosives. Museum representative Kathy Atherton suggested that the munitions were likely donated years ago by war-era collectors, possibly having been forgotten in storage until recently. The revelation came just two months before the museum's three-year refurbishment was set to finish. The Ministry of Defence reported that the Royal Logistic Corps removed and destroyed a two-inch illumination mortar round and a 20mm cannon shell. These had been displayed alongside a 1940s map marking bomb sites, plane crashes, and parachute landings from the war.

Dopo aver inviato delle foto all'Imperial War Museum, lo staff è stato avvisato dei potenziali rischi e ha subito contattato la polizia locale. È stato chiamato il reparto artificieri di Aldershot e gli specialisti dell'Esercito hanno fatto brillare gli esplosivi in sicurezza. Kathy Atherton, portavoce del museo, ha ipotizzato che i manufatti siano probabilmente stati donati anni fa da collezionisti dell’epoca bellica, forse lasciati dimenticati in magazzino fino a oggi. article_content: Matthew White, a key suspect in the racist murder of Stephen Lawrence, committed a violent assault on black security guard Bethel Ikpeze in 2015. The incident took place at a Lidl store in Eltham, southeast London, where White tried to stab Ikpeze with a used syringe while shouting racist abuse and referring to his involvement in the Lawrence case. White claimed to have killed before and felt immune from consequences. Although White was arrested and sentenced to four months in prison for this attack, he was only convicted of possessing a syringe in public, theft, and making threats, rather than attempted assault or racial abuse. Ikpeze’s account, which included explicit threats and racist remarks, was reported to Metropolitan Police officers, but the information was not pursued in connection to the Lawrence investigation. The charges filed did not reflect the racial element or the attempted violence. Former prisoners later stated that White, while incarcerated, confessed to being present at the attack on Stephen Lawrence and criticized police for failing to investigate him properly. BBC investigative reporting recently brought these details to light, with testimonies from independent witnesses and descriptions matching the assailant noted at the 1993 crime scene. White, who was known for drug abuse and repeat offenses, continued to target black individuals, notably with another racist assault reported in 2020. Victims often only learned of White’s ties to the Lawrence case years later via media coverage. Failures in the initial Metropolitan Police investigation into Lawrence’s murder led to findings of institutional racism, and new revelations highlight persistent investigative gaps and missed chances to prosecute all those involved. Individuals like Ikpeze voiced shock at the lack of action on reported racism and violence. There was a notable gap between the details given to police and the court charges, pointing to ongoing systemic challenges. The BBC continues to encourage information sharing regarding the Lawrence murder, providing secure ways for individuals to come forward. The ongoing investigation underscores the need for accountability and reform in handling racially motivated crime in the UK.

Sergeant Adam Johnson of the Austin Police Department received widespread recognition for stopping an armed gunman during a pre-dawn attack in downtown Austin, Texas. At around 2:33 AM, Johnson was on mounted patrol, leading a 12-member team and holding the reins of two horses, when 49-year-old Larry McQuilliams began firing more than 100 rounds at multiple buildings with AK-47 and .22-caliber rifles.

Amid the chaos, Johnson fired a single shot from his Smith & Wesson M&P .40 pistol from 312 feet away, striking McQuilliams. The gunman, who possessed multiple firearms and a detailed map marking 34 downtown targets—including the Mexican consulate, the federal courthouse, and a bank—was pronounced dead at the scene. A postmortem examination was planned to determine if Johnson's shot was fatal.

Army Major John Plaster, an expert in long-range shooting, called Johnson's action 'extraordinary,' especially under such challenging circumstances. Austin Police Chief Art Acevedo commended Johnson's composure and professionalism, emphasizing the high standard of training within the department.

article_content: After a protracted legal struggle, Abu Qatada—a figure associated with extremist activity in Europe—was deported by UK authorities to Jordan. His wife and five children have now joined him there, with their government-funded flight marking the end of their time in Britain. Over their stay since the early 1990s, the family received more than £500,000 in welfare. This move is seen as a significant achievement for then-Home Secretary Theresa May, who led the costly legal proceedings to remove Qatada at a cost of £3 million. Although there were uncertainties due to two children’s British citizenship, the family members not born in the UK relinquished their rights to remain. The Home Office has indicated the family might be prevented from returning, though the British citizenship of the youngest children could pose challenges. Conservative MP Dominic Raab welcomed the family’s departure and suggested the need for policy reforms to avoid future repeats.

article_content: The Republican Party finds itself at a pivotal moment, debating its future role in immigration reform. Should the GOP consider supporting a path to citizenship for approximately 11 million unauthorized immigrants to appeal to the rapidly growing Hispanic voter demographic? Or should it reinforce its opposition to reform, aiming to maintain loyalty among its existing, predominantly white voter base? While attention has primarily focused on the U.S.-Mexico border, the Republican Party might benefit from looking north. In Canada, the Conservative Party—once consistently defeated by the Liberals—transformed its electoral fortunes by embracing immigration and connecting with immigrant communities. Having lived in Canada as an American immigrant and journalist, I observed that the Liberal Party historically garnered robust support from immigrants, largely through successful coalitions built in major urban centers like Toronto and Vancouver. In contrast, the Conservatives, dominated by white voters from central Canada, were often relegated to the political sidelines. Under Prime Minister Stephen Harper, the Conservatives reversed this trend. In the 2011 federal election, they surpassed the Liberals among voters born outside Canada—a dramatic turnaround shaped by proactive outreach in the 2000s. Initiatives included reducing immigration fees, apologizing and compensating for historic injustices like the Chinese 'head tax,' and targeting immigrant families with specific tax relief. The party also ran more minority candidates than rivals and invested in multilingual campaign ads. Of the 23 seats the Conservatives gained in 2011, 20 were in the diverse Toronto area, and each had significant immigrant populations. By comparison, in the 2000 election, the Liberals received over 60% of the immigrant vote. Crucial to this shift was Jason Kenney, Canada’s Minister of Citizenship, Immigration, and Multiculturalism. Kenney dedicated years to engaging directly with immigrant communities, attending events and places of worship, and making personal connections. Kenney also championed policy innovation, adopting a more market-driven, decentralized immigration system inspired by Australia and New Zealand. The reformed process uses third-party assessments of skills and language ability, linking prospective immigrants with job offers before arrival. Provinces gained a greater role, encouraging regional economic development through immigration. To balance concerns among long-time Conservative voters about system integrity, the party also tightened refugee policies and other immigration rules, demonstrating that strong border controls could coexist with a welcoming attitude towards immigrants. This approach led to greater diversity within the Conservative voter base. As Kenney noted, Canadians were drawn to the party for its values of freedom, enterprise, hard work, personal responsibility, and respect for law and tradition. While the GOP could learn from Canada, it has so far focused on restrictive measures, such as 'self-deportation,' which hurt support among immigrant communities. Still, the Canadian experience illustrates that it is possible to welcome immigrants and maintain a message rooted in traditional values. The views expressed in this commentary are those of Edward Alden.

Dovrebbe sostenere un percorso verso la cittadinanza per circa 11 milioni di immigrati senza documenti, nel tentativo di conquistare l’elettorato ispanico in rapida crescita? Oppure dovrebbe rafforzare la sua opposizione alla riforma, puntando a mantenere la lealtà dell’attuale base elettorale, prevalentemente bianca? Mentre l’attenzione si è concentrata soprattutto sul confine tra Stati Uniti e Messico, forse il Partito Repubblicano dovrebbe guardare anche a nord. In Canada, il Partito Conservatore—un tempo regolarmente sconfitto dai Liberali—ha cambiato le proprie sorti elettorali abbracciando l’immigrazione e costruendo rapporti con le comunità di immigrati. Avendo vissuto in Canada come immigrato americano e giornalista, ho osservato che il Partito Liberale tradizionalmente raccoglieva largo sostegno dagli immigrati, grazie a coalizioni di successo nelle grandi città come Toronto e Vancouver. Al contrario, i Conservatori, sostenuti soprattutto da elettori bianchi del centro del Canada, erano spesso ai margini della politica. Con il primo ministro Stephen Harper, i Conservatori hanno invertito questa tendenza. Nelle elezioni federali del 2011, hanno superato i Liberali tra gli elettori nati fuori dal Canada, grazie a una strategia proattiva avviata negli anni 2000. Le iniziative comprendevano la riduzione delle tasse per gli immigrati, le scuse e i risarcimenti per ingiustizie storiche come la famigerata 'head tax' cinese, e misure fiscali mirate alle famiglie immigrate. Il partito ha inoltre candidato più rappresentanti delle minoranze rispetto agli avversari e investito in spot elettorali multilingue. Nel 2000, per confronto, i Liberali avevano ottenuto oltre il 60% del voto degli immigrati. Figura chiave di questo cambiamento è stato Jason Kenney, ministro canadese per la Cittadinanza, l’Immigrazione e il Multiculturalismo. Kenney ha dedicato anni a coinvolgere direttamente le comunità di immigrati, partecipando a eventi, visite a luoghi di culto e instaurando rapporti personali. Kenney ha anche promosso innovazioni politiche, adottando un sistema d’immigrazione più flessibile e orientato al mercato, ispirato ai modelli di Australia e Nuova Zelanda. Il nuovo processo prevede valutazioni indipendenti delle competenze e della conoscenza linguistica, collegando i potenziali immigrati alle offerte di lavoro prima dell’arrivo. Le province hanno acquisito un ruolo maggiore, favorendo lo sviluppo economico regionale tramite l'immigrazione. Per rassicurare l’elettorato più tradizionalista, il partito ha anche irrigidito le norme sull’asilo e altre regole d’immigrazione, dimostrando che controlli severi possono convivere con un atteggiamento aperto verso gli immigrati. Questo approccio ha condotto a una maggiore diversità tra gli elettori conservatori. Come ha sottolineato Kenney, i canadesi sono attratti dal partito proprio per valori come libertà, impresa, lavoro, responsabilità personale e rispetto delle leggi e della tradizione. article_content:
Australia is preparing for a pivotal referendum to decide if Indigenous peoples will be formally recognized in the country's constitution through the creation of a new parliamentary advisory body called the 'Voice to Parliament.' This body would enable voices from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities to independently advise lawmakers on relevant issues.

The campaign ahead of the vote has exposed deep societal divisions, driven by an increase in racism and abuse, often amplified by misinformation on social media. Indigenous Australians, who comprise about 3.8% of the population (approximately 980,000 people in 2021), continue to face significant disparities, including shorter life expectancy, higher suicide and incarceration rates, and reduced access to healthcare compared to non-Indigenous citizens.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has made the referendum a key priority, but the debate has generated mixed reactions. Academic voices like Dani Linder from the University of Queensland note a growing sense of distress among Indigenous communities as public rhetoric becomes more polarized.

The vote involves a single question—whether to approve a constitutional amendment acknowledging Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people by establishing the Voice. Voting is compulsory, with early voting turnout surpassing 2.2 million. Polls are open nationwide from 8am to 6pm, and results will be updated online. For the amendment to pass, it must receive a majority of national votes and majorities in at least four of the six states. Historically, only eight out of 44 referendums have succeeded in Australia since 1901.

The concept originated with a national meeting of 250 Indigenous representatives at Uluru. Members of the Voice would be chosen by their own communities, serving fixed terms, and would advise parliament and government, although they would not have legislative or veto power. Advocates believe this will help close the gap in health, education, employment, and housing outcomes for Indigenous Australians, and improve government responsiveness.

Internationally, countries like Finland, Norway, and Sweden have established Indigenous advisory bodies (Sami Parliaments) to give guidance on community-specific issues. Nonetheless, objections to the Voice persist. The opposition, led by Liberal leader Peter Dutton, argues there is insufficient clarity about the Voice's structure and legal standing and warns of potential lasting divisions. They campaign under the slogan ‘If you don’t know, vote no.’ Some Indigenous critics—referred to as 'progressive no' voters—feel the Voice falls short of delivering practical change and advocate for a treaty or formal recognition of sovereignty instead.

The referendum will not only decide the fate of the Voice but also reflect how Australians view reconciliation and constitutional recognition of Indigenous peoples.

Gli indigeni australiani rappresentano circa il 3,8% della popolazione (980.000 persone secondo il censimento del 2021) e continuano a subire gravi disuguaglianze: aspettativa di vita inferiore, tassi di suicidio e incarcerazione più alti e minore accesso ai servizi sanitari rispetto al resto dei cittadini.

Alcuni critici indigeni—detti 'progressive no'—ritengono che la Voice sia insufficiente e chiedono, invece, un trattato o il riconoscimento formale della sovranità.

L'esito del referendum non deciderà solo il futuro della Voice, ma sarà anche un segnale del grado di riconciliazione e del livello di riconoscimento costituzionale che l'Australia è disposta ad accordare ai suoi popoli indigeni.

article_content: British Transport Police have recovered a rare Stradivarius violin, crafted over 300 years ago and worth more than $1 million, along with two bows valued at more than $105,000. Stolen near a London train station in late 2010, these items were found in a house in central England following an extensive investigation. The violin suffered only minor damage. Detective Chief Inspector Simon Taylor, who led the effort, credited the successful recovery to cooperation between various police forces, an insurance company, and antique dealers. Violinist Min Jin Kym, the owner, reported the theft after discovering her case missing. She expressed immense relief and happiness at the news of the violin's recovery, having thought about the loss every day. In 2011, two teenagers were caught and sentenced for stealing the violin. Created in 1696 by Antonio Stradivari from Cremona, Italy, Stradivarius violins are among the most revered instruments in the world. Stradivari made approximately 1,116 instruments, of which over 600—spanning violas, cellos, mandolins, and guitars—still survive. In the 18th century, his work was highly coveted by royalty, nobility, clergy, and top musicians, prized for their exceptional sound. Stradivari continued crafting instruments until 1737, when he died at age 92.

article_content: Nikolai Patrushev, a senior Russian official and close ally of President Vladimir Putin, has cautioned that the confrontational approaches of the United States and its allies are raising the likelihood of nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons being deployed. His comments come in the wake of Russia’s large-scale offensive in Ukraine, which has pushed Moscow's relations with Western countries to their most tense since the Cold War. The post-Cold War array of arms control agreements has largely collapsed. Western nations interpret the Ukraine conflict as a Russian bid for territorial expansion, while Russian authorities argue the dispute is part of a larger challenge against a waning Western-dominated order—one they accuse of stirring instability to maintain influence. Citing TASS, Patrushev suggested US supremacy on the global stage is declining, directly tying recent security deterioration to American policies. Patrushev underscored that dangers associated with nuclear, chemical, and biological arms are rising, particularly as arms control systems break down. While he did not identify locations at risk, he criticized US actions in the Middle East and its support for Ukraine, maintaining these have aggravated global security issues. A former KGB officer, Patrushev occupies a critical position in Russia’s national security circles and has increasingly represented hardline viewpoints within the Kremlin. He made these statements shortly after the US condemned Russia’s withdrawal from an important European arms treaty, interpreting it as a sign Moscow is abandoning arms control obligations. US representatives have raised the possibility of Russia using tactical nuclear arms in the Ukraine conflict, though President Putin has sought to allay such fears. Patrushev further alleged that Western powers—particularly Anglo-Saxon nations—are losing sway and actively destabilizing independent countries. He reiterated claims, again without presenting evidence, that Ukraine was prepared for conflict by the West and had used drones to attack Russian nuclear facilities, specifically naming an incident at the Kursk nuclear station. These assertions remain unverified, and Ukrainian officials have yet to comment. In other, unrelated news items: Tata Group has acquired Wistron’s iPhone manufacturing plant in India; India leads in the QS Asia university rankings; and Religare Enterprises is contesting a takeover by the Burman family amid fraud allegations.

A shell casing thought to be from a bullet was found in a rental car used by former NFL player Aaron Hernandez on the day Odin Lloyd was killed. Keelia Smyth, manager of an Enterprise branch in North Attleborough, testified that she discovered the casing attached to chewed blue gum and a child’s drawing after Hernandez returned a damaged Nissan Altima on June 17, 2013. She recalled Hernandez offered her blue gum before leaving.

According to Smyth, Hernandez returned the car on June 18, made no attempt to hide his identity, and requested an SUV; he ended up with a Chrysler 300 since no SUVs were available. After learning of Hernandez’s arrest, Smyth reported her findings to the police. Officers subsequently found the .45-caliber shell casing, gum, and drawing in a dumpster.

During the trial, both prosecution and defense criticized police for storing evidence in the bed of a regular pickup truck, raising concerns about proper preservation and chain of custody. Smyth's testimony opened the trial, and Hernandez’s uncle also testified about Hernandez’s distress over lost endorsements following the arrest.

Hernandez, who was on a $41 million contract at the time, was released by the New England Patriots hours after being charged with murder and firearms offenses. The victim, Odin Lloyd—who dated the sister of Hernandez’s fiancée—was found shot to death in an industrial park.

The murder weapon remains missing, complicating efforts for both the prosecution and defense. Judge Susan Garsh ruled that Robert Paradis, a friend of Hernandez, cannot testify about allegedly knowing of a .45-caliber gun linked to Hernandez, stating his comments were inconclusive about whether Hernandez ever possessed the weapon.

In preparation for South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol's state visit, King Charles III explored the vibrant Korean community in London this week. President Yoon and his wife, Kim Keon Hee, will be welcomed with full royal honors, including traditional British ceremonies, during their stay from November 20 to 23. Their program also honors British soldiers who served in the Korean War.

On November 21, Charles and Queen Camilla will give the official welcome at Horse Guards Parade, allowing President Yoon to inspect a guard of honor. The president and first lady will participate in two wreath-laying ceremonies: first at the Korean War Memorial, marking 70 years since the war's end, and then at the grave of the Unknown Warrior in Westminster Abbey.

President Yoon's itinerary features an address to Parliament, attendance at a Buckingham Palace state banquet, a business forum on November 22, and a meeting with Prime Minister Rishi Sunak at 10 Downing Street.

Prior to these events, King Charles visited New Malden, a London district home to one of Europe’s largest Korean populations. Greeted by children waving British and Korean flags, he enjoyed a Korean choir and spoke with locals about K-pop music. He received kimchi—a well-known Korean dish—as a gift in honor of his upcoming 75th birthday on November 14. Charles joked with residents about the dish's spiciness and mentioned his interest in seeing a live K-pop performance. Local resident Sunny Lee shared that the king enjoyed the cultural experience. President Yoon and the first lady will be in the UK from November 20 to 23.
