article_content:
CNN’s documentary 'Our Nixon' provides viewers with a rare, candid glimpse into one of America’s most complex presidents. Having served on Nixon’s White House staff for over three years, I can confirm that this film, while not capturing the full picture, offers revealing, firsthand insights into Nixon’s character seldom seen by the public.

For younger generations, it’s difficult to appreciate just how dominant Nixon was in American politics for more than four decades. Apart from Franklin Roosevelt, no other 20th-century leader was nominated in five national elections by their party. From his rapid ascent as a young congressman to his passing, Nixon was featured on the cover of Time magazine 56 times, reflecting both deep respect and intense criticism. He achieved a landslide re-election victory, only to resign from office in disgrace following Watergate — a trajectory unlike any other.

Why do profoundly powerful leaders sometimes bring about their own downfall? I asked myself this, especially as someone who entered the Nixon White House by chance after leaving the Navy in the early 1970s. My mentor, Raymond Price, head of the speechwriting team, invited me to work with him, granting me a close-up view of Nixon’s leadership, particularly during high-level meetings.

The film employs home movies captured by Bob Haldeman (chief of staff), John Ehrlichman (top domestic adviser), and Dwight Chapin (aide-de-camp), highlighting Nixon’s enjoyment of presidential ceremonies—convention balloon drops, large crowds on foreign trips, his visit to China’s Great Wall, and diplomatic toasts with Zhou Enlai. Nixon relished the grandeur of the role.

Yet, these films don’t capture Nixon’s profound private discussions. In my experience, Nixon was a strategic thinker, often able to project far into the future to advance the national interest. Like Winston Churchill, whom he admired, Nixon believed that understanding history provided insight into what lay ahead. While many Americans recognized Nixon’s capacity for meanness and duplicity, they also saw him as shrewd and tough—qualities they trusted to confront the Soviet Union during tense times.

My early impressions of Nixon were positive: he read deeply, discussed history and politics with advisers like Pat Moynihan and Henry Kissinger, and showed intellectual curiosity. Later, as I gained more access, I became aware of a darker side. The documentary incorporates secret recordings that exposed Nixon’s mistrust and insecurities—including his belief that the media and even his own cabinet were often against him. Only a few insiders knew about the taping system, and hearing the contents came as a shock to the rest of us.

Nixon’s defensive attitude, partly rooted in his real and imagined enemies, led him to embrace a “jungle” mentality: attack or be attacked. According to Leonard Garment, a close legal adviser, Nixon’s desire for control amid the Vietnam War’s turmoil fueled actions like wiretapping journalists and staff and creating the “plumbers” to stop leaks. These efforts escalated into the political operations connected to Watergate. While this view is persuasive, I also believe that Nixon’s personal struggles—his inability to manage his darker impulses, as Carl Jung theorized—contributed to his downfall.

I sometimes feel sympathy for Nixon. As counselor Bryce Harlow observed, we may never know what shaped him as a young man, but it must have been consequential. The three men behind the documentary’s cameras—Haldeman, Ehrlichman, and Chapin—did not set out as henchmen, but as insiders excited by history in the making. Caught up in the intrigue, they became participants in the administration’s deceits, dirty tricks, and crimes. Over time, feelings were damaged: Ehrlichman felt betrayed by Nixon; Haldeman believed critics misunderstood the president; Chapin, creative and loyal, paid the price for his devotion with a broken career.

Decades later, Dwight Chapin still seeks to defend Nixon’s reputation, believing the documentary is unfairly one-sided. Among historians and those of us who lived through it, debate over Nixon’s legacy—his achievements and his ultimate self-destruction—remains unresolved. I believe Nixon possessed greatness, but he was ultimately undone by his own ungoverned inner turmoil. For the country’s sake, he had to step down.

The opinions expressed are solely those of David Gergen.
translated_content:
Il documentario della CNN “Our Nixon” offre agli spettatori uno sguardo raro e autentico su uno dei presidenti più complessi d’America. Dopo oltre tre anni nello staff della Casa Bianca di Nixon, posso confermare che il film, pur non restituendo il quadro completo, rivela aspetti inediti e sinceri del carattere di Nixon, raramente visti dal pubblico.

Per le nuove generazioni, è difficile capire quanto Nixon sia stato centrale nella politica americana per oltre quarant’anni. A parte Franklin Roosevelt, nessun altro leader del Novecento è stato candidato cinque volte a elezioni nazionali dal proprio partito. Dalla sua rapida ascesa come giovane deputato fino alla sua scomparsa, Nixon è apparso 56 volte sulla copertina di Time, simbolo di rispetto e critica. Ottenne una storica rielezione, solo per dimettersi poi in disgrazia dopo il Watergate: un percorso unico.

Perché leader così potenti finiscono per causare la propria rovina? Me lo sono chiesto spesso, soprattutto entrando per caso nello staff di Nixon dopo aver lasciato la Marina nei primi anni Settanta. Il mio mentore, Raymond Price, allora capo dei discorsi, mi invitò a lavorare con lui, permettendomi di osservare da vicino la leadership di Nixon, soprattutto durante incontri di rilievo.

Il film sfrutta i filmati amatoriali di Bob Haldeman (capo di gabinetto), John Ehrlichman (consigliere per la politica interna) e Dwight Chapin (aiutante personale), mostrando quando Nixon apprezzasse la cerimonia presidenziale: voli di palloncini alle convention, folle immense durante i viaggi all’estero, la camminata sulla Grande Muraglia cinese, brindisi diplomatici con Zhou Enlai. Nixon si gustava la grandezza del ruolo.

Tuttavia, questi filmati non mostrano le conversazioni private e riflessive di Nixon. Per esperienza, era uno stratega capace di guardare molto avanti per il bene del Paese. Come Churchill, che ammirava, Nixon credeva che conoscere la storia aiutasse a prevedere il futuro. Molti americani vedevano il suo lato duro e ambiguo, ma lo consideravano abbastanza tenace da tenere testa all’URSS nei momenti delicati.

Le mie prime impressioni di Nixon erano positive: leggeva molto, dibatteva con Pat Moynihan e Henry Kissinger, era curioso. Successivamente, gli ho visto anche il lato oscuro. Il documentario include registrazioni segrete che rivelano la sua diffidenza e insicurezza—persino verso i suoi collaboratori. Solo pochi conoscevano il sistema di registrazione; scoprirlo fu scioccante per tutti noi.

L’attitudine difensiva di Nixon, alimentata da nemici veri o presunti, lo spinse a una visione della politica come “giungla”: o mangi o sei mangiato. Secondo Leonard Garment, suo fidato avvocato, il desiderio di controllo sul caos del Vietnam portò alle intercettazioni e alla creazione dei “plumbers” contro le fughe di notizie. Questi atti degenerarono poi nelle operazioni che portarono al Watergate. Pur trovando questa analisi convincente, credo che anche i conflitti interiori di Nixon—come illustrato da Carl Jung—abbiano giocato un ruolo nella sua caduta.

Talvolta provo empatia per Nixon. Come diceva il consigliere Bryce Harlow, forse non sapremo mai cosa lo abbia segnato da giovane, ma doveva essere qualcosa di profondo. I tre dietro la cinepresa—Haldeman, Ehrlichman e Chapin—non si consideravano scagnozzi, ma spettatori privilegiati della storia. Coinvolti negli intrighi, finirono col partecipare anche a imbrogli e illeciti. I rapporti si deteriorarono: Ehrlichman si sentì tradito; Haldeman pensava che i critici si sbagliassero; Chapin, creativo e leale, pagò un caro prezzo.

Ancora oggi, Dwight Chapin difende la memoria di Nixon, credendo che il documentario sia troppo parziale. Tra storici e testimoni dell’epoca, il dibattito sull’eredità di Nixon è aperto. Credo che avesse una sua grandezza, ma fu infine sconfitto dai suoi demoni interiori. Per il bene del Paese, dovette dimettersi.

Le opinioni espresse sono solo quelle di David Gergen.

article_content: Senator Eyinanya Abararibe, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Power, has identified poverty as a primary factor fueling child labour in Nigeria. He made these remarks at the 'Stakeholders 2.0 Consultation on Child Protection' organized by the Child Solidarity Group in partnership with the Almajiri Child Rights Initiative, held at American Corners, Ikeja, Lagos. Abararibe highlighted that girls are particularly at risk, often facing sexual exploitation, child marriage, and domestic violence. He noted, 'Many of these children can be seen selling items on the street, yet some do not view this as a violation of the Child Rights Act. Poverty forces many parents to send their children out to work. We must confront these harmful beliefs and directly address children's vulnerability to ensure their protection.' Mohammed Sabo, founder of the Almajiri Child Rights Initiative (ACRI), commented that Nigeria's failure to resolve issues facing children demonstrates the inefficiency of current laws and a lack of accountability. He said, 'Child marriage remains prevalent in northern Nigeria, while child trafficking and child labour are common in the south. The country's laws have not been properly implemented or are simply ineffective. At the root, the problem lies in a lack of accountable governance.' Emediong Akpabio, CEO of the Child Solidarity Group (CSG), urged stakeholders in child rights to prioritize children when planning interventions. Akpabio stressed the need for precise data on vulnerable groups, stating, 'Without specific information on the number of vulnerable children, they will continue to be overlooked in intervention and implementation efforts.'

Abararibe ha sottolineato che le bambine sono particolarmente a rischio, spesso soggette a sfruttamento sessuale, matrimoni precoci e violenza domestica. Ha osservato: 'Molti di questi bambini sono visti vendere prodotti per strada, ma alcuni non considerano questo una violazione del Child Rights Act. La povertà costringe molti genitori a mandare i figli a lavorare. Dobbiamo sfidare queste convinzioni dannose e affrontare direttamente la vulnerabilità dei bambini per garantirne la protezione.' Mohammed Sabo, fondatore dell’Almajiri Child Rights Initiative (ACRI), ha affermato che il fallimento della Nigeria nell’affrontare i problemi che riguardano i bambini dimostra l’inefficienza delle leggi attuali e una mancanza di responsabilità. Ha dichiarato: 'I matrimoni precoci sono diffusi nel nord della Nigeria, mentre il traffico di minori e il lavoro minorile sono problematiche comuni al sud. Le leggi del Paese non sono state applicate correttamente o risultano inefficaci. Alla radice vi è la mancanza di governance responsabile.' Emediong Akpabio, CEO del Child Solidarity Group (CSG), ha invitato chi lavora nel settore dei diritti dell'infanzia a mettere i bambini al centro di ogni intervento. Akpabio ha evidenziato l’importanza di dati precisi sui gruppi vulnerabili, affermando: 'Senza informazioni specifiche sul numero di minori vulnerabili, questi continueranno a essere esclusi da interventi e iniziative.'

article_content: Katie Sheppard, a 20-year-old footballer for West Ham Ladies, was found dead by hanging at her home in Sidcup, south-east London, earlier this year. Her death occurred just hours before she was due to begin pre-season training with her club. An inquest at Croydon Coroner’s Court revealed details of a recent disagreement between Sheppard and her girlfriend, Nancy Richardson. Text messages showed that Sheppard expressed frustration toward Richardson, particularly over Richardson’s reluctance to disclose their relationship to her parents. Sheppard’s body was discovered on July 2 by Nathaniel Hall, her mother’s partner. Police officer PC Alex Giacomazzi described concerns that there may have been a suicide pact, but investigations did not support this theory. A handwritten note was found in Sheppard’s diary reading, 'God forgive me, I sacrifice myself to you and to your kingdom,' next to a drawing of a coffin marked with the initial 'K.' Sheppard had been prescribed antidepressants the previous year, although none were found at her home. Post-mortem examinations confirmed her cause of death as asphyxia by hanging and ruled out foul play. The coroner, Dr Adela Williams, recorded an open verdict, stating that the precise reasons for Sheppard’s death were unclear and that there was no definitive evidence of intent. article_content:
Arsenal Football Club continues to face a challenging season. The club's long-serving chairman, Peter Hill-Wood, is recovering in hospital after suffering a heart attack, which occurred the day before Arsenal's 2-0 home defeat against Swansea City. This loss left Arsenal in 10th place out of 20 teams in the English Premier League after 15 matches, marking the club's worst start to a season since 1994. Hill-Wood, 76, who has served as chairman since 1982, had been battling pneumonia and was taken ill at home on Friday, according to the club's website. A statement from Arsenal wished him a full and speedy recovery, extending thoughts to him and his family. Peter Hill-Wood follows a family legacy, as his father, Denis, and grandfather, Samuel, also held the role.

Supporters and public figures have shared well-wishes for Hill-Wood, with fans and former players expressing frustration about the club’s recent direction. Some are unhappy about the departure of leading players such as Robin van Persie and Cesc Fabregas in the past few years. Ex-player Emmanuel Eboue, now with Galatasaray, posted his dissatisfaction on Twitter after the Swansea loss, criticizing the board and questioning the team’s current spirit and quality. He suggested that pressure on the board might only come from decreased match attendance.

Prominent Arsenal supporter and CNN presenter Piers Morgan also criticized manager Arsene Wenger, who has managed the club since 1996 and won 11 trophies, but none since 2005. Morgan described Arsenal’s recent performance as among the worst of Wenger’s tenure and publicly called for him to step down, using the hashtag #WengerOut.

Despite difficulties in the league, Arsenal have already qualified for the last 16 of the UEFA Champions League. Wenger is aiming for a morale boost in their upcoming match against Olympiakos. He observed that the team’s home performances have not met expectations and suggested there may be psychological factors at play.

Arsenal's major sponsor, Emirates, recently renewed its partnership with the club, agreeing to a $240 million deal covering shirt sponsorship until 2019 and stadium naming rights until 2028. However, funds from this agreement will not be available for squad strengthening until later next year. When asked about the upcoming transfer window, Wenger stated that the board is willing to invest if suitable players are found but did not confirm any specific plans.

Another Premier League manager under scrutiny is Sunderland’s Martin O'Neill, whose team remains just above the relegation zone following a 2-1 loss to Norwich. O'Neill expressed frustration with his team’s performance, lamenting missed opportunities for better results.

article_content: A recent study from Norway challenges conventional perceptions of physical attractiveness and body satisfaction. Conducted by researchers Mari Rysst and Ingun Grimstad Klepp at the National Institute for Consumer Research, the study involved in-depth interviews with 20 Norwegian men and women. Half of the participants were described as 'bodily deviant,' meaning they had lived with obesity, burn injuries, or physical disabilities. Contrary to popular belief, the study found that individuals whose bodies differ from mainstream ideals—often depicted as slim and athletic—can be just as, or even more, content with their appearance as those who meet such standards. In fact, those considered to have 'good-looking' bodies often reported feeling more self-conscious about their looks. Many participants not fitting the conventional ideal emphasized that personality, charm, and charisma are more significant in determining attractiveness. For example, one obese woman described men who cared for others as 'sexy' and felt that a good-looking body could just as easily be chubby as thin. The participant identified as the 'most obese informant' noted that a person's personality strongly influences how attractive they appear. According to Rysst, some overweight individuals downplayed the importance of physical appearance, potentially as a way to normalize and feel better about their own bodies. One participant, Storm, a 30-year-old man with severe skin damage from a fire, expressed acceptance of his scars but noted he still had insecurities about other aspects of his body. Another obese woman reported she had learned to ignore concerns about her appearance, allowing her to live confidently and enjoy her professional life. The researchers concluded that those who fall outside societal 'norms' often accept their bodies, recognizing that certain features may be difficult or impossible to change. Conversely, participants with average or 'good-looking' bodies tended to feel less satisfied with their appearances. Rysst commented, 'It was surprising to us that those who were rather fit and slim were dissatisfied with their looks. I think people are influenced by the images they see in media, advertisements, and public spaces—often without realizing it. Our sense of the perfect body is shaped by these exposures, regardless of our personal preferences. Ultimately, this reflects the society we live in—you can't be too good-looking.'

Condotto dalle ricercatrici Mari Rysst e Ingun Grimstad Klepp presso il National Institute for Consumer Research, lo studio ha previsto interviste approfondite con 20 uomini e donne norvegesi. La metà dei partecipanti è stata definita “deviante corporeo”, ossia persone che convivono con obesità, ustioni o disabilità fisiche. Contrariamente alle convinzioni comuni, lo studio ha rilevato che chi si discosta dagli ideali estetici dominanti—spesso legati a corpi magri e atletici—può essere altrettanto, se non più, soddisfatto del proprio aspetto rispetto a chi si conforma a tali standard. In effetti, coloro considerati fisicamente 'belli' hanno spesso riferito maggiore autoconsapevolezza e insicurezza riguardo al proprio aspetto. Molti partecipanti che non rientravano nei canoni convenzionali hanno sottolineato come personalità, fascino e carisma siano elementi più importanti nell’attrattività. Ad esempio, una donna obesa ha descritto come attraenti gli uomini premurosi, sostenendo che un corpo bello può essere sia rotondo che magro. L’informatrice identificata come 'la più obesa' ha osservato che la personalità conta molto nell’essere percepiti come attraenti. Secondo Rysst, alcune persone in sovrappeso tendevano a minimizzare l’importanza dell’aspetto fisico, forse per normalizzare la propria forma e sentirsi meglio. Un partecipante, Storm, un uomo di 30 anni con gravi cicatrici da ustioni, ha dichiarato di aver accettato le proprie cicatrici, pur avendo insicurezze su altri aspetti del suo corpo. Un’altra donna obesa ha riferito di aver imparato a ignorare la propria immagine corporea, raggiungendo così sicurezza e soddisfazione lavorativa. I ricercatori hanno concluso che chi si trova al di fuori delle “norme” sociali tende ad accettare il proprio corpo, riconoscendo che certi tratti sono difficili o impossibili da cambiare. Al contrario, i partecipanti con corpi nella media o 'belli' sembravano meno soddisfatti del proprio aspetto. Rysst ha commentato: 'Ci ha sorpreso che proprio chi era piuttosto in forma e snello fosse insoddisfatto del suo aspetto. Credo che le persone siano influenzate dalle immagini che vedono nei media, nelle pubblicità e negli spazi pubblici—spesso senza rendersene conto. La nostra idea di corpo perfetto è modellata da queste esposizioni, indipendentemente dalle preferenze personali. In fondo, questo riflette la società in cui viviamo—non si può essere troppo belli.'

article_content: According to a recent report by the Project Management Institute (PMI), project managers in Nigeria with Project Management Professional (PMP) certification earn, on average, 60% more than those without it. This finding comes from the 13th edition of PMI's Earning Power: Project Management Salary Survey, which reviewed data from more than 20,000 project professionals in 21 countries. Globally, PMP-certified project managers receive median salaries that are 33% higher than their non-certified counterparts. In Nigeria, this gap is even wider, showcasing the certification's strong impact on earning potential and career advancement. The report states that project professionals in Nigeria earn a median salary of $23,370. Additionally, about two-thirds (66%) of survey respondents experienced an increase in total compensation—including salary, bonuses, and other cash incentives—over the past year. George Asamani, Managing Director for PMI Sub-Saharan Africa, highlighted the value of PMP certification. He described it as a key driver for increasing earning power and advancing careers, emphasizing PMI's commitment to offering globally recognized credentials to project professionals at all career stages. Survey results also indicate that the benefits of PMP certification extend beyond just higher salaries, also fostering career development and professional standing. Asamani noted that Africa's progress relies on factors such as policy frameworks, infrastructure, technology, and capacity building, emphasizing that skilled project management is crucial for success in these areas. He pointed out that, in today's volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous (VUCA) business landscape, hiring PMP-certified project managers has become a strategic priority for organizations. According to Asamani, certified professionals demonstrate expertise in strategic decision-making, risk management, and adapting to change—traits essential for thriving in dynamic environments. He added that earning PMP certification reflects a dedication to lifelong learning and ongoing professional development.

article_content: UPDATED: Universal and Blumhouse’s ‘Five Nights at Freddy’s’ is set for an impressive estimated $130.6 million global opening, exceeding earlier estimates as it targets a $52.6 million debut from 64 international box office markets. Domestically, the film opened at $78 million, a remarkable figure especially considering its simultaneous release on Peacock. In international markets, where the film is playing exclusively in theaters, it has set numerous records. Globally, this is the largest horror film opening of 2023, surpassing ‘The Nun II,’ and it marks the best opening ever for Blumhouse, beating out ‘Halloween.’ Internationally, Latin America strongly supported ‘FNAF,’ with Mexico leading at $10.8 million (65% market share and the largest post-pandemic horror opening). Other major markets included the UK ($6.3M; 3rd biggest horror launch), Australia ($3.8M), Brazil ($3.9M), and Germany ($2.6M). Argentina ($2.3M) and Chile ($1.9M) also contributed notable numbers. This initial wave of markets performed comparably to genre hits like ‘The Conjuring 2,’ ‘Annabelle Comes Home,’ and ‘Insidious: The Red Door,’ and more than doubled the numbers of ‘M3GAN’ in the same regions. Highlights include the biggest horror opening day of all time in Chile, Peru, and Uruguay; Blumhouse’s best debut ever in 16 markets (including Germany, Brazil, Australia, Argentina, Netherlands, New Zealand, Bolivia, Chile, Central America, Colombia, Uruguay, Peru, Saudi Arabia, Finland, Sweden, and Norway), and the second-best in Mexico. 2023’s strongest opening day was recorded in Ukraine. The current weekend estimates indicate the largest horror opening weekend ever in Peru, Chile, Poland, Ukraine, and Finland, and the top horror start of 2023 in markets such as Mexico, UK, Australia, Chile, Poland, Saudi Arabia, Peru, New Zealand, Ecuador, Netherlands, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Ukraine, and Denmark. ‘Freddy’s’ is projected to be Blumhouse’s biggest opening weekend ever in Mexico, Australia, Brazil, Chile, Poland, Saudi Arabia, Peru, New Zealand, Ecuador, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Ukraine, and Denmark. The film will open in Spain and Italy this week, in France and Korea later this November, and in Japan in February next year. In holdover business, ‘Killers of the Flower Moon’ from Apple, Paramount, and Imperative Entertainment added $14.1 million in 64 markets, only a 36% decline in its second weekend. The film’s overseas total is $47.4 million, with a global sum of $88 million. India debuted with $330,000 at 188 locations, marking Martin Scorsese’s biggest opening there. The UK leads with $6.8 million, followed by France ($5.3M), Germany ($3.6M), Spain ($2.9M), and Australia ($2.7M). IMAX shows contributed $9 million globally, with $3.6 million from overseas. Universal and DreamWorks Animation’s ‘Trolls Band Together’ expanded to 17 more markets ahead of its US release. Mexico debuted at $1.5 million, opening third behind ‘Five Nights at Freddy’s’ and local film ‘Radical.’ Spain opened at No. 1, as ‘Freddy’s’ had not yet opened there. Top markets to date: UK ($10.8M), France ($5.3M), Brazil ($3.3M), Germany ($3.1M), and Netherlands ($1.8M). Italy, Australia, and Korea will open in the coming weeks. Paramount, Nickelodeon, and Spin Master’s ‘Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie’ has surpassed $100 million overseas, reaching $107.2 million internationally and $166.4 million globally. This frame saw $9.7 million (down just 23%). The film is now out in nearly all markets, with Japan to come on December 15. China leads with $17.1 million, followed by France ($10.8M), Germany ($9M), UK ($7.4M), and Mexico ($6.6M). ‘Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour’ added $6.7 million from 96 reported markets in 4,143 theaters in its third weekend. The film’s estimated international total is now $53.7 million and $203 million globally, making it the first pure concert film to cross the $200 million mark. Thirteen more markets will add IMAX screens this upcoming weekend. Individual market breakdowns have yet to be provided. ‘Oppenheimer’ has now surpassed ‘Tenet’s lifetime box office in China, ranking as the third biggest Christopher Nolan movie there (behind ‘Interstellar’ and ‘Inception’). Upcoming in China is Maoyan’s ‘Last Suspect,’ while Japan will see Toho’s ‘Godzilla Minus One’ later this week. A young couple received a bizarre early-morning wake-up call when a sealed can of baked beans exploded in their kitchen. Ben Leo and his girlfriend Rhian Wade were startled awake by a sudden loud noise at around 3am, initially fearing that a bomb had detonated somewhere in their home. Despite searching late that night, the pair were unable to identify the source of the bang.

The following day, as Ben prepared lunch, he discovered the culprit: a can of baked beans, purchased recently from Lidl, had burst open inside their kitchen cupboard, spraying beans everywhere. Ben, 24, from Worthing, West Sussex, explained, "We had no idea what had happened, and at 3am we were very confused and tired. It sounded like a small bomb had gone off. The next day I opened the cupboard to find beans everywhere—the can had expanded and blown its top. Instead of beans on toast, I ended up cleaning them up."

Ben noted the can was still within its expiration date and had only just been bought from a local store. He expressed concern about what could have happened if someone had been nearby during the explosion: "It's scary to think what might have occurred if I had been looking into the cupboard when the tin exploded. The metal edges were extremely sharp and could have left me badly injured. You would not expect this from something as harmless as a can of baked beans. Luckily, we're both safe, but we'll definitely reconsider where we buy our baked beans in the future."

A Lidl spokesperson stated, "We have strict quality control processes in place with our suppliers and take these matters extremely seriously. We ask that the packaging be returned to us so we may begin a thorough investigation, in collaboration with our supplier."

article_content: Tensions continue to escalate along the Lebanon-Syria border as the Syrian civil war spills into neighboring Lebanon. On Tuesday, two rockets fired from Syria landed in and near the Lebanese city of Hermel, a Hezbollah stronghold, according to Lebanon’s state news agency NNA. No injuries were reported. The identity of those who fired the rockets was not immediately clear. Hezbollah, the Shiite militant group, has been supporting the Syrian government in its conflict against anti-government rebels. Earlier on the same day, three Lebanese soldiers were killed when unidentified gunmen attacked a military checkpoint near the Syrian border, in the town of Arsal. Former Lebanese Prime Minister Saad Hariri described the attack as a 'heinous crime,' urging unity among political groups to support the army and prevent Lebanon from being drawn into the Syrian conflict. Arsal, a northeastern border town with significant Sunni population, is known for links to rebel sympathizers; some residents are reportedly fighting with the radical al-Nusra Front. This week’s attack on Lebanese soldiers was the second such incident in Arsal, where some locals accuse the army of siding with Hezbollah against Sunni rebels due to Arsal’s strategic role as a supply route for Syrian opposition forces. The Free Syrian Army’s chief of staff, Gen. Salam Idris, threatened to retaliate against Hezbollah unless it stopped supporting the Syrian government within 24 hours, warning of severe consequences if intervention continued. In March, two Syrian jets fired rockets near Arsal, and just a day before the recent Hermel incident, rocket attacks from Syria killed a 17-year-old girl and wounded two others in Hermel, according to NNA. This week, the European Union voted to lift its embargo on arming Syrian rebels, a move that Britain’s Foreign Secretary William Hague said aimed to pressure President Bashar al-Assad to negotiate a diplomatic solution to the crisis. The Syrian National Coalition criticized the EU’s decision as insufficient, warning of increased violence. Syria’s government, Iran, and Russia condemned the EU’s decision. Iran warned it would encourage terrorism in Europe, and Russia claimed the move undermined peace efforts. Russia announced it would proceed with a previously signed contract to deliver S-300 surface-to-air missiles to Syria, arguing this could deter further escalation. Israeli Defense Minister Moshe Yaalon voiced concern, stating Israel would take action if necessary. Since unrest erupted in March 2011, over 80,000 people—most of them civilians—have died in Syria, according to United Nations estimates. Opposition activists accuse government forces of indiscriminate attacks, while President Assad maintains he is fighting terrorism. The United States and European nations remain divided on whether to arm Syrian rebels, with concerns that weapons could fall into extremist hands such as al-Nusra Front, designated by the U.S. as a terrorist group. U.S. Defense Secretary Chuck Hagel recently stated that options were being reconsidered but no final decisions had been made. On Monday, U.S. Senator John McCain made an unannounced visit to Syria, meeting Free Syrian Army commanders. Rebel leaders stressed the urgent need for arms, expressing confidence in their ability to control weapon distribution. McCain also voiced concerns about rising extremism among opposition ranks. CNN contributors Holly Yan, Salma Abdelaziz, Hamdi Alkhshali, and Elise Labott contributed to this report.

article_content: David Cameron has been called upon to halt what critics describe as 'dangerous' cuts to Britain's defence budget. According to a report by the UK National Defence Association, a group made up of former senior military officials, reducing the country's armed forces during a period of global instability could pose significant risks. The report warns that Britain could become 'irrelevant' unless it increases defence spending beyond the current level of 2% of national output. Air Commodore Andrew Lambert, the report's author who served in Bosnia, Iraq, and the Falklands, expressed concerns that Argentina might take advantage of perceived UK weakness to potentially invade the Falkland Islands. The report references the term 'Guilty Men', drawing on a 1940 book by Michael Foot and others, which criticized earlier Prime Ministers Stanley Baldwin and Neville Chamberlain for failing to adequately prepare the military before the Second World War. UKNDA highlights current global threats, pointing to increased military spending by China and Russia, instability in the Middle East, piracy near Somalia, and a reduction in the United States' commitment to European defence. Historian Andrew Roberts, contributing to the report, described the government's approach as 'illogical, dangerous, and ultimately self-defeating'. He expressed concern that current ministers could be judged by history as the 'Guilty Men' of their time. Meanwhile, Defence Secretary Phillip Hammond is set to announce major reductions to Ministry of Defence civil servant bonuses, after criticism over their size. This year, payouts will be reduced by £13 million, with bonuses reserved for employees showing 'genuinely outstanding performance'. Under the new scheme, total bonus payments are expected to fall by a third to around £30 million, with the average award at £430 and top bonuses at £860, restricted to staff below the Senior Civil Service level. This move comes as thousands of frontline troops face job cuts and pay freezes, while civil servants continued to receive sizable bonuses—amounting to over £40 million in 2010-2011. In comparison, by 2008-09, bonuses peaked at £47.5 million, up from £24.1 million in 2003-04.

article_content: Akasa Air announced on Thursday the addition of Port Blair to its growing network. The airline will operate daily through flights between Bengaluru and Port Blair, with a stop in Chennai but no aircraft change required in Chennai. Bookings are now open on Akasa Air’s website, its Android and iOS app, and several leading online travel agencies. Praveen Iyer, Co-Founder and Chief Commercial Officer at Akasa Air, stated, 'The launch of operations in the Andamans is another step in our ongoing network expansion. Port Blair is renowned for its natural beauty and strong tourism demand. This addition reflects Akasa Air's commitment to providing seamless travel options and top-tier service for our passengers.' Since its launch in August 2022, Akasa Air has served over 5.9 million passengers and now connects 16 Indian cities: Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kochi, Delhi, Guwahati, Agartala, Pune, Lucknow, Goa, Hyderabad, Varanasi, Bagdogra, Bhubaneswar, and Kolkata. The airline has placed an order for 76 Boeing 737 MAX aircraft, powered by CFM’s LEAP-1B fuel-efficient engines. According to Akasa Air, 'The 737 MAX family delivers superior efficiency, reducing fuel consumption and carbon emissions, and supports our commitment to maintaining the youngest and greenest fleet in Indian aviation.' In market news, India's IPO sector is experiencing a boom. Three of four IPOs—Tata Technologies, Flair Writing Industries, and Gandhar Oil Refinery—were fully subscribed within hours of their opening. IndiGo, India’s largest airline, is reportedly considering the introduction of a premium class, hot meals, and a loyalty program by the end of 2024 to attract business travelers and compete with Air India on international routes. Since the implementation of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), creditors have withdrawn 26,518 insolvency cases involving defaults totaling up to ₹9.33 lakh crore before these applications were formally admitted.

article_content: Nearly 50 people have been rescued and five are confirmed dead as emergency services continue an international operation to save passengers from the burning Norman Atlantic ferry in the Adriatic Sea. The Greek coast guard confirmed that four bodies were found on Monday, including a man who died after becoming stuck in a lifeboat chute and another who jumped overboard to escape the fire. About 149 passengers are still believed to be trapped, while 391 have been rescued, having been airlifted from the sea and transferred to other vessels for transport to shore. The Norman Atlantic, flying the Italian flag, caught fire off the Greek island of Corfu while traveling from Patras, Greece, to Ancona, Italy. Italian prosecutors have launched an inquiry to determine the cause of the disaster and whether criminal negligence was involved. Greek maritime minister Miltiadis Varvitsioti confirmed the recovery of four bodies from the water. Two Australians traveling on Turkish passports were among those trapped on board, but it is unclear if they have been rescued. On Monday, the first large group of 49 rescued passengers, including four children, arrived at the port of Bari aboard the Spirit of Piraeus, according to Sky News. The fire broke out on the car deck of the Norman Atlantic on Sunday. Rescue operations have been hindered by gale-force winds and rough seas. Passengers became stranded on the upper decks as crews worked overnight to airlift them from the ferry. The Italian navy ship San Giorgio took 89 passengers by 9pm AEST, and at least one person was hospitalized due to heart disease. Over ten merchant vessels participated in the rescue, providing blankets and support to evacuees. Helicopters made at least 34 trips between shore and the ferry, airlifting seven people, according to USA Today. Greek Prime Minister Antonis Samaras hailed the 'massive and unprecedented operation' that saved hundreds of lives under extremely difficult conditions, The New York Times reported. Italian coast guard Admiral Giovanni Pettorino emphasized that rescue teams worked throughout the night despite the challenging weather and darkness. Italian navy Captain Riccardo Rizzotto stated that passenger safety was their top priority. Passenger lists included individuals from Austria, Turkey, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Greece, and the United Kingdom. Nick Channing-Williams, a British show jumper, and his fiancée Regina Theoffili, were among those initially stranded. One British woman and her two children were airlifted to safety, while her husband reportedly remained on board. Some passengers were stranded for over eight hours on the upper decks, unable to reach lifeboats due to high seas. Some called TV stations for help, describing severe heat, melted shoes, dense smoke, and the pervasive smell of burning plastic. Helicopters continued evacuating passengers, including women and children, in tough weather conditions of rain, thunder, and lightning. Vassiliki Tavrizelou, a rescued passenger, recounted being stranded for hours in the cold and rain, witnessing fire and explosions onboard. Italian and Greek authorities continue rescue efforts as the vessel is being towed in difficult conditions. An investigation is underway into the cause of the fire, with initial reports suggesting burning olive oil in trucks may have contributed to its spread.

Il capitano della marina italiana Riccardo Rizzotto ha dichiarato che la sicurezza dei passeggeri era la loro massima priorità. Le liste passeggeri comprendevano persone provenienti da Austria, Turchia, Francia, Germania, Paesi Bassi, Grecia e Regno Unito. Nick Channing-Williams, fantino britannico, e la sua fidanzata Regina Theoffili erano tra i primi rimasti bloccati. Una donna britannica e i suoi due figli sono stati portati in salvo in elicottero, mentre il marito sarebbe rimasto a bordo. Alcuni passeggeri sono rimasti bloccati per più di otto ore sui ponti superiori, impossibilitati a raggiungere le scialuppe a causa del mare agitato. Alcuni hanno chiamato stazioni televisive per chiedere aiuto, descrivendo il calore intenso, le scarpe sciolte, il fumo denso e il persistente odore di plastica bruciata. Gli elicotteri hanno continuato a evacuare passeggeri, comprese donne e bambini, sotto pioggia, tuoni e fulmini. Vassiliki Tavrizelou, una passeggera salvata, ha raccontato di essere rimasta bloccata per ore al freddo e sotto la pioggia, assistendo a incendi ed esplosioni a bordo. Le autorità italiane e greche continuano i soccorsi mentre la nave viene rimorchiata in condizioni difficili. È in corso un'indagine sulle cause dell'incendio, con le prime ipotesi che indicano come causa la combustione di olio d'oliva trasportato nei camion.

article_content: Two months after American journalist James Foley was killed by Islamic State militants, his parents, Diane and John Foley, took part in a moving tribute in Bayeux, France. The ceremony remembered journalists who lost their lives in conflict zones in 2014 and featured the unveiling of a new commemorative stone. Alongside Maryvonne Lepage—whose daughter, Camille Lepage, was killed as a photojournalist in the Central African Republic—the Foleys joined others in honoring James and the 51 journalists killed that year. Diane Foley spoke passionately about the importance of truthful information and expressed hope that her son’s death would inspire change. The event occurred during the Bayeux-Calvados journalism awards, honoring reporters in war zones since 1994. Christophe Deloire of Reporters Without Borders noted that 2014 had already seen an especially high number of journalists killed. James Foley, who was murdered at age 40, began his career teaching literacy in prison before moving into journalism, later working in Iraq, Afghanistan, Libya, and Syria. He was kidnapped in Syria in 2012, and the Islamic State later released a video of his killing. While held captive, Foley and other hostages passed their time talking and playing improvised games. Diane Foley later criticized US officials for inadequate communication and urgency in trying to free her son, saying her family felt they were left to manage alone. She hoped that the tragedy would shed light on the risks journalists take and the need to protect them. Foley’s death was followed by similar executions of American journalist Steven Sotloff and British aid workers David Haines and Alan Henning. At the ceremony, media leaders such as AFP’s editor-in-chief, Philip Chetwynd, stressed the escalating dangers for journalists, particularly in conflict areas like Syria, and honored the courage of reporters like Foley.

article_content: Following the Hamas attack on southern Israel in October 2023 and subsequent Israeli airstrikes on Gaza, the West Bank saw a rapid escalation in violence and movement restrictions. Israeli authorities imposed closures, curfews, regular raids, and made numerous arrests across Palestinian areas. According to reports from Palestinian residents and rights organizations, violent actions by Israeli settlers have risen sharply—these include killings, the destruction of olive trees and agricultural land, and intimidation that has forced entire communities to evacuate. UN and Palestinian officials state that over 900 Palestinians were displaced from 15 hamlets, with more than 3,000 olive trees destroyed during this year's harvest. Palestinian Health Ministry data records nine Palestinian deaths from settler attacks during this period. Many in the West Bank describe living in constant fear and compare their situation to imprisonment. The Israeli military has intensified its operations in the West Bank, including more frequent raids and some airstrikes. Since the conflict began, over 200 Palestinians have died due to Israeli military actions. One significant incident happened at the Jenin refugee camp on November 9, where 14 Palestinians were killed—mostly militants—making it the deadliest raid since the early 2000s. Despite international condemnation, such as from U.S. President Joe Biden, rights groups including Yesh Din claim that Israeli authorities rarely hold settlers accountable for violence. Reportedly, only one settler has been arrested and subsequently released, with few others placed in preventive detention. The Israeli military says it is tasked with preventing violence and acting against unlawful behavior but has not commented on specific incidents. There are approximately 700,000 Israeli settlers in the West Bank, and they now enjoy strong political backing within the government. Recent appointments, like that of Zvi Sukkot—a settler previously barred for alleged violence—reflect this support. Advocacy groups argue that incidents attributed to settlers are exaggerated or involve self-defense. Since the onset of the conflict, many settlers have joined military reserve units, sometimes replacing regular army personnel in West Bank security roles, which rights groups say fuels a sense of impunity and increases violence directed at Palestinians. Palestinian daily life has become even more restricted: extensive curfews, school closures, checkpoints, and severe limitations on movement are now routine. Many Palestinian workers lost their permits to work in Israel, with only a small number allowed to return. Daily commutes and access to essential services have grown arduous, while families cope with trauma from continuous threats and displacement. Communities such as Hebron are subjected to especially strict measures, including heavy military presence and frequent night-time actions by settlers. In towns like Qusra and Hawara, both settler and military operations have resulted in further casualties and forced departures. Reports from human rights groups detail instances of intimidation, property damage, and alleged physical abuse. Many Palestinians and human rights organizations believe that recent settler violence aims to force Palestinians off land desired for settlement expansion. Some Israeli political leaders have openly called for harsh action against Palestinian towns. The unrest has undermined essential cultural and economic activities, notably the olive harvest season—crucial for many families' incomes. The Israeli military states that it reviews reports of violence and takes disciplinary steps when warranted, though details are rarely shared. Palestinians and activists continue to express frustration at the lack of accountability and warn that conditions could further deteriorate if present trends continue.

In città come Qusra e Hawara, sia le azioni dei coloni che le operazioni militari hanno causato vittime e nuove ondate di sfollamento. Report delle organizzazioni umanitarie parlano di intimidazioni, danni a proprietà e presunti abusi fisici. Molti palestinesi e organizzazioni per i diritti umani credono che la violenza recente dei coloni abbia l’obiettivo di cacciare i palestinesi da terre destinate all’espansione degli insediamenti. Alcuni leader politici israeliani hanno pubblicamente invocato misure drastiche contro paesi palestinesi. Le tensioni hanno compromesso attività culturali ed economiche fondamentali, come la raccolta delle olive, cruciale per il reddito di molte famiglie. L’esercito israeliano dichiara di esaminare i rapporti sulle violenze e di prendere provvedimenti disciplinari quando necessario, ma i dettagli restano pochi. I palestinesi e gli attivisti continuano a lamentare la mancanza di responsabilità e avvertono che le condizioni potrebbero peggiorare ulteriormente se la situazione dovesse continuare così.

A recent study claims to have resolved the long-standing question of why penguins cannot fly. Researchers report that penguins are such effective swimmers that their wings evolved into flippers specialized for diving, resulting in the loss of flight. This evolutionary tradeoff means that no bird can be fully adapted for both efficient swimming and flying.

To reach this conclusion, scientists studied guillemots, seabirds that both swim and fly. Research conducted on Coats Island, Northern Canada, revealed that guillemots expend much less energy diving than other birds, while their energy expenditure in flight was the highest recorded—31 times greater than at rest. This supports the theory that wings optimized for swimming make flight energetically unsustainable.

Currently, there are 18 penguin species, with 13 experiencing population declines and five classified as endangered. While penguins are often associated with Antarctica, they also inhabit regions such as South America, South Africa, Australia, New Zealand, and several southern Pacific islands. In the water, penguins employ 'porpoising'—leaping in shallow arcs to reduce friction and swim up to 20 miles per hour. Their distinctive black-and-white countershading camouflages them from predators both above and below.

Penguins possess excellent underwater vision, aiding in effective hunting even in low-visibility waters. Depending on species, wild penguins typically live 15–20 years and spend up to 75% of their life at sea.

Professor John Speakman of Aberdeen University noted that while penguins’ lack of flight was previously enigmatic, the current findings support biomechanical models showing that enhanced swimming adaptations increased the energy required for flight, ultimately making flight impossible. The benefits of energy-efficient diving outweighed disadvantages like being slower on land or vulnerable to predators near the ocean.

Guillemots, resembling penguin ancestors, are capable divers and efficient swimmers, but flight is extremely energy-intensive for them. The study suggests that penguin ancestors transitioned to denser bones for diving, losing the hollow bones that aid flight in most birds, thus becoming better suited for aquatic life.

Kyle Elliott, a zoologist at the University of Manitoba, emphasized that adaptations for swimming come at a cost to flying ability. The research was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

Uno studio recente afferma di aver finalmente risolto il vecchio quesito sul perché i pinguini non possono volare. Secondo i ricercatori, i pinguini sono nuotatori così straordinari che le loro ali si sono trasformate in pinne specializzate per l’immersione, portando così alla perdita della capacità di volo. Questo compromesso evolutivo comporta che nessun uccello possa essere completamente adattato sia al volo sia al nuoto efficiente.

Per arrivare a questa conclusione, gli scienziati hanno studiato le urie, uccelli marini che sanno sia nuotare che volare. Ricerche condotte sull’Isola di Coats, nel nord del Canada, hanno rivelato che le urie consumano molta meno energia nuotando sott’acqua rispetto ad altri uccelli, ma il loro consumo energetico mentre volano è il più alto mai registrato: ben 31 volte superiore rispetto allo stato di riposo. Questo conferma la teoria secondo cui ali adattate al nuoto rendono il volo insostenibile dal punto di vista energetico.

Oggi esistono 18 specie di pinguino, di cui 13 in declino e cinque classificate come in pericolo. Anche se li associamo soprattutto all’Antartide, i pinguini abitano anche Sud America, Sud Africa, Australia, Nuova Zelanda e molte isole dell’Oceano Pacifico meridionale. In acqua i pinguini attuano il “porpoising”, saltando in archi poco profondi per ridurre l’attrito e raggiungere velocità fino a 32 km/h. Il loro piumaggio nero e bianco, detto controombreggiatura, li mimetizza dai predatori sia dall’alto che dal basso.

I pinguini hanno anche una vista subacquea eccellente, che permette loro di cacciare efficacemente anche in acque torbide. A seconda delle specie, possono vivere dai 15 ai 20 anni e trascorrono in mare fino al 75% della loro vita.

Il professor John Speakman dell’Università di Aberdeen ha osservato che, sebbene la mancanza di volo dei pinguini avesse a lungo suscitato domande, questi risultati supportano i modelli biomeccanici che dimostrano come le ali ottimizzate per il nuoto abbiano reso il volo sempre meno sostenibile dal punto di vista energetico. Così, il vantaggio evolutivo dell’efficienza in acqua ha superato gli svantaggi, come la minor agilità a terra o il rischio di predatori vicino alle acque.

Le urie, simili agli antenati dei pinguini, sono ottime tuffatrici e nuotatrici, ma spendono moltissima energia per volare. Lo studio suggerisce che gli antenati dei pinguini abbiano sviluppato ossa più dense per facilitare le immersioni, perdendo quelle cave che aiutano il volo nella maggior parte degli uccelli, diventando così più adatti alla vita acquatica.

Kyle Elliott, zoologo all’Università di Manitoba, ha evidenziato che ogni adattamento per il nuoto comporta un compromesso nella capacità di volare. La ricerca è stata pubblicata su Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

article_content: A drug offering hope to late-stage breast cancer patients was approved by the government yesterday. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Kadcyla, which is said to act as a 'smart bomb' against a form of the disease believed to affect about one fifth of patients. Kadcyla combines the well-known drug Herceptin with a chemotherapy agent called DM1. On Friday, the FDA approved Kadcyla, a new breast cancer drug that is expected to extend the lives of people with advanced stages of the disease. DM1 is too potent to be administered directly but, when combined with Herceptin, it is delivered straight to cancer cells. The drug has been shown effective in treating HER2-positive breast cancer—a type in which the HER2 protein promotes cancer growth—adding several months to the lives of many patients who were facing terminal diagnoses. Kadcyla was tested in clinical trials on 991 women with advanced HER2-positive breast cancer, resulting in an average life extension of 5.8 months compared to standard chemotherapy. According to the FDA, 20 percent of breast cancer patients have HER2-positive cancer. Breast cancer is the second most deadly cancer among American women; this year it's estimated that 232,340 will be diagnosed with breast cancer, and 39,620 are expected to die from the disease. Genentech, the maker of Kadcyla, stated that the drug will be available in two weeks, though it comes with a high price tag—$94,000 for a ten-month course. The company announced assistance programs for patients unable to afford treatment, stating, 'People without health insurance or who have exceeded their insurance limits might qualify to receive Kadcyla free of charge.' Genentech says Kadcyla is the first in a series of cancer drugs using the 'smart bomb' approach currently in development. Hal Barron, Chief Medical Officer and Head of Global Product Development at Genentech, said: 'Kadcyla is an antibody-drug conjugate representing an entirely new way to treat HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, and it helped patients live nearly six months longer. We currently have more than 25 antibody-drug conjugates in development and hope this promising approach will lead to more medicines for other cancers in the future.'

article_content: A lakeside cabin cherished by five lifelong friends—who became famous on CNN.com for taking the same group photo every five years over three decades—was recently burglarized. John Wardlaw, who owns the cabin near the California–Oregon border through a trust established by his grandfather, expressed anger and disbelief over the break-in. The cabin, which gained worldwide attention as the backdrop for the friends' regular photos, suffered losses including an $8,500 boat and family heirlooms like an antique oil lamp, duck calls, mountain goat horns, and a .410 shotgun. Thankfully, the house wasn't damaged during the burglary. The theft is under investigation by the Siskiyou County Sheriff’s Department, but so far there are no suspects, and the stolen items remain missing. Allison Giannini from the sheriff’s department described Copco Lake as a peaceful, rarely trafficked area, making the crime especially surprising for locals. Wardlaw, based in Santa Barbara and a filmmaker by profession, discovered the burglary through neighbors who noticed the boat and trailer were gone. Along with his wife Tricia, he visits the cabin about five times a year to unwind and fish. The property also acts as a base for exploring outdoor attractions like Crater Lake, the Oregon Caves, and the Rogue River. Wardlaw personally maintains the three-bedroom home, making repairs and upgrades since it was built in 1970, such as replacing windows and siding. He recalls finding old smoke bombs and acorns hidden by wildlife during renovations, often thinking back to the time his friend John Dickson threw a smoke bomb to drive out birds, not realizing the risk involved. Dickson, who appears in the friends' recurring photos, said the theft was deeply upsetting. He emphasized that the cabin has been their sanctuary for more than thirty years. The incident has saddened the group, for whom the cabin symbolizes a lasting friendship.

article_content: A family narrowly escaped harm after their newly purchased VW Golf Cabriolet burst into flames during a school run in Cheam, Surrey—just a day after acquiring the vehicle on eBay for £810. Nicky Keefe, a primary school teacher, had driven her partner Kevin Keogh and their three children only a quarter of a mile from home when smoke was noticed inside the car. The alarm was first raised by her 14-year-old son, James, who felt his trainers melting and alerted his mother by shouting that his feet were on fire. Realizing the seriousness, the family quickly exited the vehicle. The convertible, a 19-year-old model with under 95,000 miles and MOT valid until next year, had been collected from a private seller in Hampshire. The seller described the vehicle on eBay as having 'a few dings' but 'lots of years left in it', and highlighted features such as heated seats. On the morning of the incident, Mrs Keefe noticed smoke from the car's grills but assumed it might be typical for an older vehicle. She turned on the heater to clear the windscreen, only for her son to realize his shoes were melting due to extreme heat. Mrs Keefe's partner and younger children, Harry (12) and Mia (10), were also in the car but escaped unscathed. The family informed motorists behind them about the fire before the vehicle was quickly engulfed in flames. Firefighters responded to the scene around 8:20 am, and police closed Lower Morden Lane while the car was removed. No injuries were reported. Mrs Keefe expressed her shock but relief that her family was safe. She stated that she would check her insurance and contact eBay about the situation.

article_content: PARIS: After years of debate, rugby's administrators have announced significant changes they hope will address the sport's long-standing imbalance favoring its traditional powers. On Tuesday (Oct 24), World Rugby (WR) unveiled a set of sweeping reforms described as the most significant since rugby turned professional in 1995. Since then, the largest nations have become increasingly dominant, while promising to expand the game worldwide. WR chairman Sir Bill Beaumont recalled past struggles to reform the international calendar, highlighting how self-interest and financial dependency have hindered change. Major unions, such as England's RFU, rely on substantial profits from home internationals at Twickenham—over £12 million (US$14.59m) per match—to fund their operations, making fixtures against Tier Two nations less attractive financially. This pattern repeats among the top teams, who tend to play each other in June and November with only occasional matches against emerging countries. The Six Nations has not adopted promotion or relegation to encourage aspiring teams like Georgia, despite including Italy since 2000. As a result, coaches and players from Tier Two nations often call for more competitive opportunities during the World Cup cycle. The complexity is compounded by the interests of leading club leagues, the British & Irish Lions, and ongoing concerns about player welfare and match schedules. These factors have made broad-based agreement difficult. WR CEO Alan Gilpin admitted achieving consensus required considerable compromise and collaboration among many stakeholders. The new structure includes a biennial Nations League beginning in 2026 that brings together Six Nations and Rugby Championship teams in two conferences, culminating in a grand final in Europe. A second division of 12 teams will give Tier Two countries regular matches against each other. WR also committed to increasing matches between Tier One and Tier Two teams in off years, although actual promotion and relegation will not occur until the 2030 competition. This means players from Samoa, Georgia, Portugal, or Uruguay might not regularly face top teams until after the 2027 and even 2031 World Cups. Gilpin explained that the extended timeline was necessary to balance the concerns and interests of all involved, noting: 'It might seem like a long time away, but it's a significant improvement on the current situation.'

article_content: Beneath the French-Swiss border, the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is about to become the world’s most advanced instrument for exploring nature at the smallest scales. As the largest particle accelerator ever built, the LHC seeks to unravel how the universe began by smashing particles together and studying the outcomes. ALICE, CMS, and the collider’s other experiments are set to answer fundamental questions—from investigating the origin of mass via the hypothetical Higgs boson to searching for evidence of extra dimensions. Scientists hope to mimic the extreme conditions just after the Big Bang, less than a millionth of a second into the universe’s history. Though some members of the public have raised concerns—including legal efforts to stop the project over fears about black holes—researchers consistently stress the safety of the experiment. They clarify that any black holes produced would be extremely small and disappear almost instantly, posing zero risk. Based at CERN near Geneva, construction of the LHC and its scientific infrastructure has cost about $10 billion and spanned decades. On September 10, scientists will conduct a crucial test: circulating protons along the entire 17-mile underground tunnel for the first time. This milestone could set the stage for transformative discoveries about the laws of physics. The LHC’s advanced magnets and detectors are technological marvels—CMS alone contains more iron than the Eiffel Tower. These intricate systems must operate flawlessly deep underground with little human intervention. Previous tests revealed how powerful the equipment is, occasionally shifting heavy parts with strong magnetic forces. Excitement is building across the global scientific community as the LHC approaches full operation. Collaborators at places like Fermilab in the United States are marking the event and hope this first attempt succeeds. Yet even if there are initial setbacks, researchers are eager to tackle and overcome challenges after decades of anticipation. Physicists point out that, just as the discovery of the electron led to technologies that changed the world, unexpected results from the LHC may revolutionize our understanding of nature. The knowledge gained could answer basic questions about our universe and ourselves.

Gli scienziati sperano di ricreare le condizioni estreme che si verificarono subito dopo il Big Bang, meno di un milionesimo di secondo dopo la nascita dell’universo. Nonostante alcune preoccupazioni pubbliche—incluse azioni legali per fermare il progetto a causa dei timori sui buchi neri—i ricercatori ribadiscono costantemente la sicurezza dell'esperimento. article_content:
Elon Musk is under criticism from the business community after appearing to endorse an antisemitic post on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter. On Wednesday, Musk responded, 'you have said the actual truth,' to a post making sweeping claims about Jewish people, which echoed the 'great replacement' conspiracy theory—a theory frequently cited by white supremacists. This conspiracy posits that Jewish people are attempting to reduce the white population in the US by supporting nonwhite immigration, and it has been referenced in previous hate crimes, including the Pittsburgh synagogue shooting in 2018 and the Buffalo mass shooting last year.

Public backlash grew quickly after the exchange became widely known on Thursday. Among the critics were Tesla investors and technology leaders, who took to social media to denounce Musk's comment, with some calling for his resignation and others stating they would no longer support Tesla. Dustin Moskowitz, cofounder of Asana and Facebook, publicly called for Musk to resign from his leadership roles. Marc Bodnick, a tech entrepreneur, said he found Musk’s comments shockingly antisemitic, while investor Andrew Left stated he would return his Tesla, adding it was inferior to a BMW.

Despite these criticisms, Tesla stock remained resilient, gaining roughly 0.75% in mid-afternoon trading on Friday and rising over 9% across the previous five days. Some long-standing investors, like Ross Gerber, announced plans to replace their Tesla vehicles due to the controversy, though Gerber stated he intends to keep his company shares. Gary Black, whose Future Fund invests in Tesla, reported inquiries from clients about the situation, but said his fund will remain invested.

Kristin Hull, CEO of Nia Impact Capital, called for Tesla’s board to censure or otherwise address Musk, arguing that a CEO's erratic or prejudiced statements can directly harm a company’s reputation and financial performance.

In addition, several companies—including IBM and Apple—are suspending or removing advertising from X after reports by Media Matters revealed that ads from major brands were placed alongside pro-Nazi posts. X’s CEO Linda Yaccarino issued a statement reaffirming the platform’s commitment to fighting antisemitism, but it remains uncertain whether these efforts will be enough to address the ongoing fallout.
